# sage

<!-- GUILDOS-SKILL name="sage" -->

<!-- GUILDOS-DESC -->
The reality gate. Two actions cover the whole turn lifecycle: `preflight` (before any action — registry scan + no-scratch rule) and `askSage` (before any user-facing message — WWCD question gate + success-claim reality gate). Both are also enforced via .claude hooks. Also owns the plan gate for reusable abstractions, the concurrent-session branch lock, and the canonical Quest Report / BCS reporting standard.
<!-- /GUILDOS-DESC -->

```markdown
# Sage

> **Index only.** This skill is a discovery pointer. The full procedure for each
> action lives in the single content source `libs/skill_book/sage/index.js`. Load it on demand:
> `node libs/adventurer/run-action.mjs --howto sage <action>` (or read the source directly).

## Actions

- **askSage** — Vet a would-be user-facing message. For a QUESTION: PROCEED (most-aggressive reversible option) or ESCALATE (genuine irreversible/business-damaging decision). For a SUCCESS/DONE report: SHIP (real, visually verified if applicable, artifact cataloged + where-to-review stated) or REJECT (go actually do/verify/point it first). Call before surfacing ANY question OR any success claim. When the gate passes, an output-format gate also fires: execution/research turns with multiple items MUST be formatted as a Quest Report (sage.questReport); discussion / single-item turns stay plain prose.
- **BCS** — Alias of `questReport` — the two names are fully synonymous (BCS = "Briefing CJ Style", the report's original name). `sage.BCS`, the bare word `BCS`, and any 3-letter B/C/S permutation all resolve to the same Quest Report standard. Canonical content lives in `questReport`; see it for the six-component spec.
- **branchLock** — Concurrent-session branch-lock guard (PreToolUse hook on Bash; adopted SIO 2026-07-03). Blocks `git checkout <branch>` / `git switch` when the worktree is SHARED with other LIVE Claude sessions (pid registry ~/.claude/sessions/, pid-alive-verified); solo sessions are never blocked, and file-restore forms (`git checkout -- <path>`) always pass. When blocked: stay on the current branch, EnterWorktree for a private checkout, or (only on explicit user instruction) prefix BRANCH_LOCK_OVERRIDE=1. Logic: libs/skill_book/sage/branchLock.mjs; shim: .claude/hooks/branch-lock.mjs.
- **planGate** — Run BEFORE executing a quest whose `deliverable` is `reusable` (skill book / weapon / shared infra). Forces a plan-shape decision BEFORE work, not after — because a reusable abstraction is expensive to re-shape post-hoc. Returns PROCEED (plan is concrete enough — steps named, deliverable shape locked, registry slot identified) or RESHAPE (the abstraction shape is still ambiguous — go align with the user on shape FIRST). For `feature` / `one-off` quests this gate is a no-op (PROCEED immediately).
- **preflight** — Run BEFORE any action (writing code, running a tool, dispatching, deciding to decline). Forces: (1) scan libs/skill_book/ + libs/weapon/ for an existing capability; (2) if a fit exists, USE it — never hand-roll; (3) never decline ("I can't / no tool for that") without naming the scanned skill books that don't cover it; (4) never create files/scripts outside libs/skill_book/<name>/ or libs/weapon/<name>/ unless the user explicitly asks. Returns USE_SKILL_BOOK / USE_WEAPON / ADD_SKILL_BOOK / INLINE_OK / ESCALATE.
- **preflightSlim** — The 2-3 line preflight variant injected instead of the full gate in STRATEGY/TRACKING threads (butlerPlanning; adopted SIO 2026-07-03). Role detection = user declaration ('strategy thread' etc. in the prompt or the transcript's opening message), persisted per session in .claude/hooks/.state/; saying 'full preflight' flips the session back. Same rules bind — slim is a reminder, not an exemption. Logic: libs/skill_book/sage/sessionRole.mjs; shim: .claude/hooks/preflight.mjs.
- **questReport** — Quest Report — the canonical managerial-decision reporting standard. The required output SHAPE whenever askSage passes on an execution- or research-type turn with multiple items to communicate (discussion / single-item turns stay plain prose). Six components: `Health:` line · `Re:` context-recap line · Item|Progress|Δ|Status table · question list (surviving ESCALATE-class only) · closing line containing `100%` · `User actions:` line. **`BCS` is a full synonym** — `sage.BCS` === `sage.questReport`; invoked by `questReport`, `BCS`, or any 3-letter B/C/S permutation (BCS/CBS/…). Read this action verbatim before producing one — do not free-style.
```

```js
// Branch-lock guard (adopted SIO, 2026-07-03) — logic for the thin shim
// .claude/hooks/branch-lock.mjs (PreToolUse on Bash).
//
// Failure this kills: two live Claude Code sessions share one working dir; one
// runs `git checkout <branch>` / `git switch` and moves the shared checkout
// under the sibling's feet (observed 2026-07-03: a sibling's just-made commit
// appeared lost mid-session; reflog showed the checkout switch).
//
// Design: SIBLING-AWARE, not always-on. Branch switching is blocked ONLY when
// at least one OTHER live Claude session (per the pid registry
// ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json, pid-alive-verified) shares this session's cwd.
// A solo session never feels the guard. When blocked, the alternatives are:
// stay on the current branch, EnterWorktree (private worktree), or a
// user-instructed BRANCH_LOCK_OVERRIDE.

import { readdirSync, readFileSync, existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { homedir } from "node:os";

// Env override exists ONLY so the selftest can point the guard at a fixture
// registry; production always reads ~/.claude/sessions/.
function sessionsDir() {
  return process.env.CLAUDE_SESSIONS_DIR || join(homedir(), ".claude", "sessions");
}

function normCwd(p) {
  return String(p || "").replace(/\//g, "\\").replace(/\\+$/, "").toLowerCase();
}

function pidAlive(pid) {
  if (!pid) return false;
  try {
    process.kill(pid, 0);
    return true;
  } catch (e) {
    return e && e.code === "EPERM"; // exists but not ours — still alive
  }
}

/**
 * Other LIVE Claude sessions sharing `cwd`. Reads the harness pid registry
 * (~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json: { pid, sessionId, cwd, name, ... }); stale
 * records (dead pid) are ignored, so a crashed sibling never wedges the guard.
 */
export function listLiveSiblings({ sessionId, cwd }) {
  const dir = sessionsDir();
  const out = [];
  let files = [];
  try {
    files = readdirSync(dir).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".json"));
  } catch {
    return out;
  }
  for (const f of files) {
    let rec;
    try {
      rec = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(dir, f), "utf8"));
    } catch {
      continue;
    }
    if (!rec || !rec.sessionId || rec.sessionId === sessionId) continue;
    if (normCwd(rec.cwd) !== normCwd(cwd)) continue;
    if (!pidAlive(rec.pid)) continue;
    out.push({ pid: rec.pid, sessionId: rec.sessionId, name: rec.name || "" });
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Returns the switch target if `command` would change the checked-out branch
 * of the current worktree, else null. Non-switching git forms pass:
 * file restores (`git checkout -- <path>`, `git checkout <ref> -- <path>`,
 * `git checkout <existing-path>`), commits, fetches, and all non-git commands.
 */
export function branchSwitchTarget(command, cwd) {
  const cmd = String(command || "");
  if (/BRANCH_LOCK_OVERRIDE/.test(cmd)) return null; // explicit, user-instructed escape
  // `git` must sit at a command boundary (start / ; & | ( or newline) — a bare
  // substring match also fires on commands that merely MENTION a checkout in
  // quoted text (echo/grep/commit messages), observed live 2026-07-03.
  const re = /(?:^|[;&|(\n])\s*git\s([^|;&\n]*?)\b(switch|checkout)\b([^|;&\n]*)/gi;
  let m;
  while ((m = re.exec(cmd))) {
    const verb = m[2].toLowerCase();
    const args = m[3].trim();
    if (!args) continue;
    if (/(^|\s)--(\s|$)/.test(` ${args} `)) continue; // pathspec form — file restore
    const parts = args.split(/\s+/);
    if (parts.includes("-")) return "-"; // `git switch -` / `git checkout -`
    // -b/-B (checkout) and -c/-C (switch) create AND switch — target follows the flag
    const bi = parts.findIndex((p) => /^-[bBcC]$/.test(p));
    if (bi >= 0 && parts[bi + 1]) return parts[bi + 1];
    const first = parts.find((p) => !p.startsWith("-"));
    if (!first) continue;
    // `git checkout <existing path>` restores a file; `git switch` never takes paths
    if (verb === "checkout" && cwd) {
      try {
        if (existsSync(join(cwd, first))) continue;
      } catch {}
    }
    return first;
  }
  return null;
}

/**
 * The hook entrypoint. { block:false } or { block:true, target, siblings, message }.
 */
export function checkBranchLock({ command, sessionId, cwd }) {
  const target = branchSwitchTarget(command, cwd);
  if (!target) return { block: false };
  const siblings = listLiveSiblings({ sessionId, cwd });
  if (!siblings.length) return { block: false };
  const names = siblings.map((s) => s.name || s.sessionId.slice(0, 8)).join(", ");
  return {
    block: true,
    target,
    siblings,
    message: `<branch-lock-block>
BLOCKED: this command would switch the checked-out branch (→ ${target}) of a worktree SHARED with ${siblings.length} other live Claude session(s): ${names}.
Switching a shared checkout moves HEAD under the siblings' feet (this exact failure lost sight of a sibling's fresh commit on 2026-07-03).

Pick one instead:
  • Stay on the current branch — commit/push here if that satisfies the task.
  • EnterWorktree — get a private worktree, then switch branches freely inside it.
  • Act on the other branch WITHOUT switching: git fetch / git log <branch> / git merge <branch> / git push origin HEAD:<branch>.
  • Only if the user EXPLICITLY instructed this checkout switch: re-run with BRANCH_LOCK_OVERRIDE=1 prefixed to the command and state that instruction in your reply.
</branch-lock-block>
`,
  };
}
```

```markdown
# Engineering Decisions — sage skill book

Load-bearing "why", not API docs. See root `CLAUDE.md` §6.

## 2026-07-03 · Branch-lock is sibling-aware (pid registry), not always-on and not a lock file

**Decision.** The concurrent-session branch-lock (`branchLock.mjs` + the
`.claude/hooks/branch-lock.mjs` shim) blocks branch switches ONLY when another
LIVE Claude session — per `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`, pid-alive-verified —
shares the same cwd. No lock file is written, ever.

**Rejected alternatives.** (a) A branch-lock FILE that sessions write/honor
before checkout — rejected because lock files go stale on crash (the writer
dies, the lock wedges every future session) and require write-side discipline
from every session. (b) Mandatory EnterWorktree for any git-mutating session —
rejected as high-friction: the common case (one session, or siblings that never
switch branches) would pay a worktree tax for a failure that only occurs on
concurrent SWITCHING. The harness already maintains the pid registry; reading
it costs nothing and self-heals (dead pid = ignored record).

**Why.** The observed failure (2026-07-03) was specifically a checkout switch
under a live sibling's feet. Guarding exactly that — switch commands, live
siblings, same cwd — gives zero friction in every other case and needs no new
state or discipline from any session.

**Consequence if violated.** Replacing this with a lock file reintroduces
stale-lock wedging; making it always-on trains agents to reflexively
BRANCH_LOCK_OVERRIDE (alarm fatigue); removing it re-exposes the lost-commit
failure mode.

## 2026-07-03 · Slim preflight triggers on user DECLARATION, not on inference or an env var

**Decision.** The strategy-thread slim preflight (`sessionRole.mjs` +
`preflightSlim`) classifies a session "strategy" ONLY when the user declares it
("this is a/my … strategy/tracking/planning thread") in the current prompt or
the transcript's opening message. The verdict is persisted per session under
`.claude/hooks/.state/`; "full preflight" in any prompt flips back.

**Rejected alternatives.** (a) Env var / launch flag — the user starts threads
from the desktop app and won't set per-session env; silent misconfiguration
would strip the full gate from execution threads. (b) Behavioral inference
(e.g. "no Write/Edit in N turns → strategy") — flapping and wrong on
read-heavy execution turns. (c) Keyword MENTION matching — rejected after two
live false positives during implementation: this very execution session's
brief contains both "the main strategy thread" and "Slim preflight", and a
mention-based regex classified it as strategy. Declaration form only.

**Why.** Strategy threads already open with an explicit declaration by
convention (butlerPlanning); matching that exact convention costs nothing and
cannot silently degrade an execution thread's gate — the failure mode of every
rejected alternative. Fail-safe direction: any miss = full gate (only cost is
tokens), never a missing gate.

**Consequence if violated.** Loosening back to keyword mentions strips the
full preflight from execution threads that merely reference the strategy
thread in their briefs — the exact sessions the gate exists to police.

## 2026-07-03 · Aggressive-default hedging tripwires live in askSage, NOT in a CLAUDE.md GM section

**Decision.** The "aggressive defaults" ruleset (dimensional default table +
anti-rationalization phrase list + "state the pick as an overridable
assumption") was folded into the `askSage` question gate as the
*Hedging-phrase tripwires* block — not added as a standalone CLAUDE.md section.
Only the two architecture-neutral merits were ported: (1) sentence-level hedging
tripwires ("If you want X, I'll do Y" → "Doing X; override if you want Y"), and
(2) proceed-transparently (name the aggressive pick as a one-line overridable
assumption, never re-convert it into a question).

**Rejected alternative.** Reviving the orphaned `awesome-aryabhata` branch's
CLAUDE.md addition verbatim — the full 7-row dimensional table + the GM
triage-cascade / OCS hardening (mandatory SA-AO-match / SA-SMART-scan dispatch,
5-field OCS).

**Why.** askSage is the *stably-triggered* gate (harness `Stop` hook, every
turn); a CLAUDE.md prose section is not enforced. The ruleset's core ("pick the
bolder reversible default, don't ask") is already askSage's WWCD rule, so a
separate section is redundant. Crucially, 4 of the 7 table rows and ALL of the
cascade/OCS hardening are tied to the **BCS / OCS / AO GM architecture retired
2026-06-12** (see memory `feedback_bcs_default`) — porting them would resurrect
dead concepts (create-AO, Quick Action Index alias, MA-SMART-advisor →
MA-runner). The 3 neutral rows (scope→broad, rigor→full-verify,
tooling→skill-book-over-raw) are already implicit in "most aggressive," so they
were compressed into one clarifier line rather than a table.

**Consequence if violated.** Re-adding the aggressive-defaults table to
CLAUDE.md (a) duplicates a rule the enforced gate already carries, and (b) drags
retired BCS/OCS/AO vocabulary back into live guidance, where a future agent will
try to honor `create-AO` / `SMART plan via MA-runner` steps that no longer
exist. Keep the default-bias logic in `askSage`; keep it architecture-neutral.
```

```js
 *

 *   - `askSage` (turn END / pre-message): vet every would-be question (WWCD) and
 *     every would-be success claim (reality gate). Kills manufactured stops and
 *     unverified "done" reports. When the gate passes, an output-format gate
 *     also fires: execution/research turns with multiple items are surfaced as a
 *     Quest Report (see the `questReport` action; legacy name "BCS"); discussion
 *     stays prose.

 * Both gates are also wired as harness hooks in `.claude/settings.json` so the

  preflight: `
You are Sage's preflight gate. An agent is about to take an action (write code, run a tool, dispatch a sub-agent, create a file, or decline a request). Route it here first. Goal: kill three failure modes BEFORE they happen.

## The three failures this gate prevents

1. **Hand-rolling when a skill book / weapon already exists.** GuildOS has ~40 skill books and ~40 weapons. The probability the registry already covers the ask is high. Skipping the scan and writing ad-hoc code (a bespoke node snippet, an inline curl, a one-off scraper) is the #1 regression.
2. **Declining a capability that exists.** Phrases like "I can't", "I'm unable to", "I don't have access", "you'll have to do that manually", "there's no tool for that" are RED FLAGS. They almost always mean the registry scan was skipped. Do not surface a decline without naming the scanned skill books that genuinely don't cover the ask.
3. **Leaving unmanaged scratch artifacts.** New .js / .mjs / .py / .sh / .sql files OUTSIDE libs/skill_book/<name>/ or libs/weapon/<name>/ accumulate as dead scripts. If the logic should persist → add it as a skill book or weapon action. If it's truly disposable → run it inline (node -e, sql query in tool result) without writing a file. Files in repo root, /scripts at the top level, or /_tmp are forbidden unless the user explicitly asked.

## The procedure

1. **Scan.** Read libs/skill_book/<name>/index.js TOC entries and libs/weapon/<name>/ exports for anything matching the ask's verb + noun. Use the registry summary the harness injects at prompt start.
2. **Decide.**
   - **USE_SKILL_BOOK** — a skill book action matches. Use it. Name the \`<skillBookId>.<actionId>\`.
   - **USE_WEAPON** — a weapon function matches (typically for external integrations). Use it.
   - **ADD_SKILL_BOOK** — no match but the logic should persist (will be needed again, has a verb-noun shape that fits the registry). Add the new skill book/weapon FIRST, then use it.
   - **INLINE_OK** — truly disposable (a single inspection query, a one-shot calculation, debugging a specific file). Run inline; do not write a new file.
   - **ESCALATE** — genuinely no fit AND the user must decide between adding a new skill book vs a different approach.
3. **Block decline-without-scan.** If the would-be action is "tell the user I can't / no tool exists / they have to do it" — do NOT surface that until you have named the specific skill books you checked and why none fit.

## Output

\`\`\`
{ "verdict": "USE_SKILL_BOOK", "use": "<skillBookId>.<actionId>", "why": "<one line>" }
{ "verdict": "USE_WEAPON", "use": "<weaponId>.<fn>", "why": "<one line>" }
{ "verdict": "ADD_SKILL_BOOK", "proposed_id": "<id>", "why": "<one line: why this should persist>" }
{ "verdict": "INLINE_OK", "why": "<one line: why it's truly disposable, no file created>" }
{ "verdict": "ESCALATE", "why": "<one line: the genuine architectural fork>" }
\`\`\`

Default bias: USE_SKILL_BOOK / USE_WEAPON. ESCALATE is rare. A decline is NEVER the default verdict — if you reached "I can't" without a scan, the verdict is to scan first.
`.trim(),

  preflightSlim: `
Strategy/tracking thread — slim sage gate (full text: sage.preflight; the rules bind unchanged, only the per-turn reminder is compressed).
Track & discuss only — delegate scans/digests to cheap leaves (butlerPlanning); registry-first before ANY action or decline (scan skill books/weapons: node libs/weapon/skillBooks/cli.mjs "<action>"); no new script files outside libs/skill_book/ + libs/weapon/.
Say "full preflight" to restore the full gate for this session.
`.trim(),

  askSage: `
You are Sage — the reality gate. An agent is about to surface a message to the user. Route it here first. Two kinds of message, two decisions:
- **A would-be QUESTION** → PROCEED (agent answers its own question with the most aggressive reversible option and keeps working) or ESCALATE (the question genuinely needs the user). See "The rule (solidified WWCD)".
- **A would-be SUCCESS / DONE / "verified" / "converged" report** → SHIP (it is real and the user can act on it now) or REJECT (it is not actually done/verified/findable — send the agent back to really do it, really verify it visually, and state where to review it). See "Success-claim reality gate".

## The rule (solidified WWCD)

If the would-be question is a **pick-between-options** choice, and the **most aggressive option is cheap to reverse** — no real business damage — then **auto-select the most aggressive option and return PROCEED**. The user is NOT asked. "Most aggressive" = the option that makes the most forward progress / does the most work / commits hardest to the obvious intent.

"Cheap to reverse / no real business damage" means ALL of:
- reversible via git / undo / re-edit (working-tree or local changes)
- no production data loss, no dropped/destroyed records without backup
- no money moved, no order placed, no transaction
- no irreversible external communication (email/Slack/post/PR-merge to a third party)
- no destructive op on shared infra without a backup
- no business-damaging external commitment

If the most aggressive option is cheap to reverse → PROCEED with it. If it isn't → consider the next-most-aggressive option that IS cheap to reverse and PROCEED with that. Only when EVERY forward option carries genuine irreversibility / business damage, OR the decision is a true architectural fork only the user can own → return ESCALATE.

## What is NOT a valid escalation (these are the wrench — always PROCEED)

- "I'm low on context / running out of tokens." Irrelevant to whether the work is reversible. PROCEED.
- "This session has run long / let me check in." Session length is not a business risk. PROCEED.
- "Let me confirm before I continue" when continuing is reversible. PROCEED.
- "Should I do A or B?" when both A and B are cheap to reverse — pick the more aggressive one. PROCEED.
- "Should I defer X until later?" when X is reversible and there's clearly more to do now. Do X. PROCEED.
- "Status check / does this look right?" — that is a report, not a question. PROCEED (deliver the report, keep going).
- Re-asking a choice the user already effectively decided. PROCEED with their evident intent.

These are the LLM behavior of finding an excuse to stop. Sage's whole job is to return PROCEED on them so the agent keeps doing the obviously-needed reversible work without making the user push it forward.

## Hedging-phrase tripwires (the wrench, at the sentence level)

The wrench list above catches bad *reasons* to stop. This catches the *phrasings* that smuggle a manufactured stop into a drafted message even when the reason is unstated. If the would-be message contains any of these shapes, you have rationalized away from the aggressive reversible default — rewrite and PROCEED:

- **"If you want X, I'll do Y"** / **"Let me know if you'd like X"** / **"unless you want X"** — when X is the bolder reversible default, this is hedging. Replace with: **"Doing X (aggressive default); tell me if you'd rather Y."** Then actually do X.
- **"Should I proceed / continue / go ahead?"** on reversible work — the answer is always yes. Drop the question, do it.
- **"no recurrence implied" / "just this once" / "one-off"** as a *reason to pick the smaller option* — if the broader/recurring/verified option is reversible, pick it and note it as an overridable assumption.

**Proceed transparently, not silently.** When you PROCEED on an aggressive reversible default the user didn't explicitly ask for, name the pick as a one-line, overridable assumption ("Assuming broad scope / full verify / skill-book path — say so to narrow it") and keep going. Surfacing the pick for override is NOT the same as asking permission — never convert it back into a question. "Most aggressive" resolves per axis to: scope → broad (filter after, not before); rigor → full verification over fast-path; tooling → skill book / weapon over a raw one-off call.

## Genuine escalations (return ESCALATE — these actually reach the user)

- Production schema/data destruction without a backup; dropping a real customer table; mass external side effects.
- Moving money, placing an order, sending an irreversible external message on the user's behalf.
- Merging/force-pushing to a shared protected branch; deleting a remote others depend on.
- A true product/architecture fork with lasting consequences the user must own and that is NOT cheaply reversible.
- A decision whose aggressive option WOULD cause real business damage and no cheap-to-reverse forward option exists.
- **A required credential is missing.** When execution hits an unset credential/auth env var (a weapon throws \`<VAR> not set\`, an OAuth scope 403s, an auth bundle is stale, a login wall blocks the path) and no other capability can complete the task, that is a genuine ESCALATE — the agent cannot self-supply a secret. The escalation MUST name (1) the exact \`VAR_NAME\` (or scope/bundle) that is missing, and (2) the acquisition path — where/how the operator supplies it (which formulary key, which \`.env\` var, "run \`scripts/auth-capture.mjs --upload\`", "generate a PAT at <url>"). Never surface a vague "I need credentials" — name the var and the fix. (Skills carry NO literal secrets; they reference env vars by design, so an unset var is the expected failure and this named escalation is the expected response — see \`skillExchange\` ED.)

## Success-claim reality gate (Sage's second job)

When the message reports success ("done", "complete", "verified", "converged", "shipped", "PASS", "it works"), Sage interrogates it BEFORE it reaches the user. Ask, literally:

1. **Is this REAL success, verified VISUALLY if applicable, THROUGH THE USER'S OWN CHANNEL?** Did the thing actually happen against the real substrate (real DB row / real stage / real file / real deploy), or is this a description of intended behavior, a sim, a fixture, or "the code looks right"? If the deliverable has any visual/observable surface, was it actually opened and LOOKED AT? **And critically — was it observed through the USER's real channel (their connected browser / CIC / their actual environment, session, host), or through an AGENT-SIDE PROXY (\`Claude_Preview\`/preview_screenshot, a headless/sandbox render, an agent-side dev server the user can't reach, a node/puppeteer screenshot, curl/HTML)?** An agent-side render is NOT the user's channel — it runs in a different environment and systematically deviates (the SE judge once declared a sandbox \`Claude_Preview\` screenshot "visual path proven" while the user's Chrome errored on the same URL — canonical anti-pattern). If verification was via an agent-side proxy, or if a proxy succeeded while the user's real channel failed/differs → REJECT (the divergence IS the finding). "Verified code" / "the weapon would return ok" / "I screenshotted the sandbox preview" / an agent's say-so is NOT user-channel verification.
2. **Is the artifact cataloged / stored where the user can view it?** A real URL, a quest page, a committed file path, a storage-bucket link, a screenshot in the carousel — something persistent the user can actually open. "It exists in my context / I described it" does not count.
3. **Is the instruction for WHERE to review it clearly in the response?** The user must be told exactly where to look (the URL, the quest link, the file path, the tab). A success report with no "see it here: …" is incomplete.
4. **The litmus:** will the user, in ANY circumstance, come back and say *"where is it?"* or *"you didn't actually do it"*? If there is a plausible path to either reaction, the claim is NOT ready.

If all four pass → **SHIP** (the success report is real and actionable; the user can act on it in one click). If ANY fails → **REJECT**: do not surface the success claim. Send the agent back to (a) actually do/finish the real action, (b) actually verify it visually if applicable, (c) catalog the artifact somewhere viewable, and (d) put the explicit where-to-review pointer in the response. A premature/“self-attested” success report is worse than no report — it burns user trust and guarantees a "where is it / you didn't do it" round-trip.

This gate is the success-side mirror of the WWCD question gate: the question gate stops manufactured stops; the success gate stops manufactured/unverified "done"s. Both default to protecting the user from a wasted round-trip.

## Output

Return one of (questions use PROCEED/ESCALATE; success reports use SHIP/REJECT):

\`\`\`
{ "verdict": "PROCEED", "chosen_option": "<the most aggressive cheap-to-reverse option>", "why": "<one line: why it's reversible / no business damage>" }
{ "verdict": "ESCALATE", "why": "<one line: the specific irreversibility or business damage that forces a real user decision>" }
{ "verdict": "SHIP", "why": "<one line: real + visually verified if applicable + artifact cataloged + where-to-review stated>" }
{ "verdict": "REJECT", "missing": ["real-execution" | "visual-verification" | "artifact-not-cataloged" | "no-where-to-review"], "fix": "<what the agent must actually do/verify/point before this can be surfaced>" }
\`\`\`

For questions: default is PROCEED; ESCALATE is the rare genuine-irreversible exception (never token/length/"let me check in"). For success reports: REJECT is NOT rare — apply the four checks honestly; a claim that cannot survive "where is it? / you didn't actually do it" is REJECT.

## Output format gate — Quest Report for execution/research turns

The verdict decides WHETHER the message ships. This gate decides its SHAPE. It fires only AFTER the verdict resolves to a pass (SHIP, or PROCEED/ESCALATE that still surfaces a final message) — a REJECT goes back to work and produces no user-facing report yet.

The user reads these reports as a manager making decisions, not as a reader following a journey. Big paragraphs of thinking-process with the conclusion buried (or absent) are the failure this gate kills. So once the verdict passes, classify the turn:

- **Execution** — you did / built / changed / fixed / deployed / ran something. Multiple deliverables, files, status lines, or steps to report.
- **Research** — you investigated and have findings: multiple results, sources, measurements, or recommendations to report.
- **Discussion** — a conversational answer, an explanation, advice, a single-thread reply, or a single trivial item. No multi-item rundown.

Decision (2026-06-12 — Quest Report mandate RETIRED for chat responses; structured reporting moved fully to QUEST OBJECTIVES):
- **The Quest Report is NO LONGER required at the end of a response.** The durable managerial record now lives on the **quest** — its \`objectives\` (status / progress / delta / notes) and \`quest_comments\` are what a manager reads. A chat reply may be **plain prose**. Keep the discipline that matters regardless of format: lead with the conclusion (don't bury it under thinking-process), answer the user's questions directly first, and surface only genuinely-blocking decisions.
- **The Quest Report shape is now a TOOL, not a mandate.** Reach for it when it genuinely helps a multi-deliverable execution/research turn (a manager scanning many status lines). Its canonical components live in \`sage.questReport\` (Health · Re · Item|Progress|Δ|Status table · Answers · Questions · a 100% closing line · User actions) — use them verbatim *when you choose the shape*. For most turns, prose is fine.
- The verdict block (the \`{ "verdict": … }\` JSON) is internal gate bookkeeping, not part of the briefing — keep it out of any Quest Report you do write.

**Enforcement (2026-06-12):** the Stop hook (\`.claude/hooks/stop-gate.mjs\`) NO LONGER enforces Quest Report shape (the Health / Re / table / 100% / User-actions markers) or the 🔴-Need-Attention-row coherence rule — both retired. What the Stop hook STILL enforces: the verdict block must be present and coherent, success language requires \`verdict=SHIP\` + an artifact/where-to-review pointer (the success-claim reality gate), and no scratch \`.mjs/.js/.py/.sh/.sql\` may be created outside the skill-book / weapon / hooks registry.
`.trim(),

  planGate: `
You are Sage's plan gate for reusable abstractions. A quest is about to enter the execute stage. If \`quest.deliverable === "reusable"\` (a new skill book, weapon, or shared piece of infra), the abstraction shape must be locked BEFORE work begins — re-shaping a reusable after the fact is the most expensive mistake the system makes (downstream consumers, registry entries, docs all drift).

## When this gate is a no-op (return PROCEED immediately)

- \`deliverable\` is \`"feature"\` (one-app change) → PROCEED, the existing execute → purrview → review chain handles iteration.
- \`deliverable\` is \`"one-off"\` (single ticket, no reuse) → PROCEED.
- \`deliverable\` is missing or unspecified → PROCEED (treat as one-off).

## When this gate actually runs (deliverable === "reusable")

Check ALL of:

1. **Registry slot identified.** Does the quest name the target \`libs/skill_book/<id>/\` or \`libs/weapon/<id>/\` path? If "we'll figure out where it lives" → RESHAPE.
2. **Action shape locked.** For a skill book: are the TOC actions named (verb-noun, input keys, output keys)? For a weapon: are the exported functions named with signatures? If shape is still "something like X" → RESHAPE.
3. **Consumer named.** Which existing skill book / quest / endpoint will use this on day one? A reusable with no day-one consumer is over-abstracted speculation → RESHAPE.
4. **Reversibility scoped.** Is the new surface \`local\` (read-only / pure), \`shared\` (writes to shared infra), or \`irreversible\` (external side effects)? Tag it now so sage and the preflight hook can mechanically reference it later.

If all four pass → **PROCEED** (the quest is concrete enough to execute without re-shape thrash). If ANY fails → **RESHAPE** (the quest goes back to questmaster/user for shape alignment FIRST — work does not start).

## Mid-run drift check (the second firing)

planGate ALSO fires mid-run when the worker has touched files and you are about to dispatch the next sub-agent step. Compute drift:

  drift_pct = (out-of-plan files touched) / (total files touched in this quest)

Where "out-of-plan" = a file whose path is not in any step's \`_Boundary:_ May write\` allow-list AND not in the quest's high-level \`description\` scope.

- **drift_pct < 25%** → PROCEED. Normal exploration / adjacent fixes are fine.
- **25% ≤ drift_pct < 50%** → WARN (verdict still PROCEED, but surface the drift in the next sub-agent dispatch's context so it self-corrects).
- **drift_pct ≥ 50%** → RESHAPE. The quest's actual scope has diverged from its plan; pause for re-scoping rather than letting the divergence compound. (autonomous-dev's 50% threshold — empirically the inflection where "I'm extending the plan" becomes "I'm doing a different quest now".)

Mid-run output adds one verdict shape:

\`\`\`
{ "verdict": "WARN", "drift_pct": <n>, "out_of_plan": ["<paths>"], "why": "<one line>" }
\`\`\`

## Output

\`\`\`
{ "verdict": "PROCEED", "deliverable": "feature|one-off|reusable", "why": "<one line>" }
{ "verdict": "RESHAPE", "missing": ["registry-slot" | "action-shape" | "consumer" | "reversibility"], "fix": "<what to align with the user before execution starts>" }
\`\`\`
`.trim(),

  questReport: `
You are producing a **Quest Report** — the canonical managerial-decision report. (**"BCS" is a full synonym, not a deprecated name**: Quest Report and BCS / "Briefing CJ Style" name the exact same standard interchangeably — \`sage.BCS\` resolves here. Earlier name "sit rep", renamed 2026-04-26; re-homed into the sage skill book and tied to askSage's output-format gate on 2026-06-09. Invoked by "questReport", "BCS", or any 3-letter B/C/S permutation — BCS / CBS / CSB / BSC / SBC / SCB.)

The Quest Report is an honest accounting of the turn's true state — fitting Sage's reality-gate identity. The user reads it as a manager making decisions, not as a reader following the journey that produced them. Output exactly the six components below, in this order, and **nothing else** — no preamble, no commentary, no narration, no journey recap, no transition prose between sections. If a thought doesn't fit one of the six components, it doesn't go in the Quest Report. The askSage verdict block is internal bookkeeping — keep it out of the six components.

1. **Self health assessment** (one line, BEFORE the table). Format: \`Health: <0-100>% — <one-sentence situation summary>.\` Reflect actual execution confidence, blocker severity, and operational momentum — not morale, not optimism, not encouragement. If the work is genuinely stuck, the score is low; do not default to 80–90% as background noise.
2. **Context recap** (one line, immediately AFTER Health and BEFORE the table). Format: \`Re: <1-2 line summary of what the user asked / what this turn is about>\`. Keep it to **1-2 lines max**. It exists so the user, scanning this report later out of context, instantly re-remembers the request that prompted it. Paraphrase the user's most recent request in your own words — do not quote it verbatim, do not narrate your process.
3. **The table** with exactly four columns: **Item | Progress | Δ | Status**.
4. **Answers to your questions** (only if the user asked one or more questions THIS turn; omit if none). A short \`Answers:\` block that directly answers each question the user raised this turn, before any question of yours. This goes immediately before the Question list. Direct answers, no narration.
5. **Question list** (pending questions FOR the user — only surviving ESCALATE-class questions; omit the section entirely if none). Always comes AFTER your answers to them.
6. **Closing line** — must contain the literal substring \`100%\`.
7. **User actions line** (last line of reply, always present). Format: \`User actions: <≤20 words>\` or \`User actions: no actions needed\`.

**Ordering rule (LOCKED 2026-06-10):** the message must END with, in this order: (a) Answers to the user's questions this turn, then (b) the Question list of pending questions for the user, then the 100% closing line, then User actions. Answers-to-them always precede questions-for-them.

**Table column spec — all four required, in this order:**
- **Item** — the action item / quest / initiative name.
- **Progress** — concrete progress signal. For quest-monitoring use \`X/Y\` (Y = total items rows, X = items with \`url IS NOT NULL\`); for other rundowns use a short anchored phrase (e.g. "phase 2 of 4", "draft sent", "PR open #482"). Use "—" only if there is genuinely no progress signal yet.
- **Δ** (delta) — what changed since the last Quest Report / last mention. "new" on first appearance. **Never write "—" or "no change" for an Active row** — see Active check below.
- **Status** — exactly one of three labels: ✅ **Done** / 🔵 **Active** / 🔴 **Need Attention**.

**Anti-BS clause (the load-bearing rule).** A Δ counts only if it describes concrete observable movement: an implementation, a migration step, a decision recorded, a test result, an artifact created, a blocker discovered, a code change, a validated finding, or a measurable execution-progress fact. The following phrasings are **banned** and will be treated as empty deltas during Active-check: "continued refinement", "ongoing work", "additional testing", "further improvements", "continued investigation", "additional iteration", "further review", "good progress", "moving forward", or any equivalent vague-momentum wording. If you cannot point to a concrete event, the Δ is empty — apply the Active check.

**Row sort order (mandatory):** all ✅ Done rows first, then all 🔵 Active rows, then all 🔴 Need Attention rows. Within a group, preserve incoming order unless the user explicitly requests reprioritization.

**Active check (mandatory before labeling any row Active):** if a row would be Active but its Δ is empty (literally absent OR a banned vague-momentum phrase per the anti-BS clause), it is NOT Active. Investigate why it stalled (read the quest, check cursor session state, scan recent commits/comments, run a smoke test if applicable) and reclassify:
- If the work is actually finished → ✅ Done.
- If something is blocking forward motion → 🔴 Need Attention, and add a corresponding entry to the Question list.

A row that is genuinely Active will always have a non-empty, concrete Δ describing the latest forward motion.

**Question list format** (after the table; one entry per surviving question). Every question here has already cleared askSage's WWCD gate — the Quest Report surfaces the surviving ESCALATE-class questions, it is NOT a second place to manufacture stops. Questions must be **self-contained enough to review later out of context** — include the minimum context to make the decision intelligible cold. Each entry has three parts in this order:
1. **Brief context** — one or two sentences with the minimum facts needed to decide.
2. **Why I can't do it myself** — one sentence (the WWCD justification; if it doesn't survive WWCD, the question doesn't belong here).
3. **Question line** — exactly: \`Question: <the question>?\` (literal leading word "Question:", trailing "?").

If there are no surviving questions, omit the question list entirely.

**Context recap line** is the line directly below Health, before the table, always: \`Re: <1-2 line paraphrase of the user's request / what this turn is about>\`. It is the manager's "what was this again?" anchor — 1-2 lines max, in your own words, no verbatim quoting and no process narration. The Stop hook greps for a leading \`Re:\` (or \`Recap:\`) on \`verdict === "SHIP"\`; a Quest Report without it is refused.

**Required closing line:** every Quest Report must contain the literal substring \`100%\` somewhere. The user greps for it; a Quest Report without \`100%\` is rejected unread. Natural fits: "100% of N items captured", "Everything 100% on track", "100% blocked, awaiting user". Whatever fits the actual state honestly — but the substring must be present.

**User actions line** is the last line of the reply, always: \`User actions: <≤20 words>\` or \`User actions: no actions needed\`.

Named interaction protocols like the Quest Report and WWCD are domain terms with defined contracts. **Before producing one, read this section verbatim — do not free-style. Do not infer missing protocol behavior.**

## YUNOQR / YUNOBCS (Why you no Quest Report) shortphrase
When the user says YUNOQR or YUNOBCS: compare your last output to the Quest Report standard above and produce a requirement-by-requirement analysis of how it differed. Report only the differences (skip compliant items). Output a table with 3 columns: a number, "What I did", "What I will do instead". Then produce a fresh Quest Report, and end with exactly: "This new round of Quest Report addressed xx out of yy issues identified above, and I think it is [OK/not ok, I will try again]".
`.trim(),
};

// `BCS` is a full synonym of `questReport` — the report's original name
// ("Briefing CJ Style"). Alias the runtime action so `sage.BCS` returns the
// same gate text as `sage.questReport` (the toc lists both; loadSageGate
// normalizes B/C/S permutations to questReport for hook/CLI lookups).
skillBook.BCS = skillBook.questReport;

export default skillBook;
```

<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: libs/skill_book/sage/sessionRole.mjs -->
```js
// Session-role detection for the slim-preflight gate (adopted SIO, 2026-07-03).
// Called by the thin shim .claude/hooks/preflight.mjs each UserPromptSubmit.
//
// Problem this solves: the full sage preflight (~12KB gate text + registry) was
// injected EVERY turn even in tracking-only strategy threads (butlerPlanning),
// where the model takes no execution actions. A strategy thread gets the 2-3
// line `preflightSlim` variant instead; execution threads keep the full gate.
//
// Detection = declaration, not inference: a thread is "strategy" only when the
// user SAYS so — in the current prompt or in the transcript's opening user
// message ("this is a main strategy thread…"). The verdict is persisted per
// session in .claude/hooks/.state/ so later turns cost one small file read.
// "full preflight" in a prompt flips the session back to execution.

import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, existsSync, openSync, readSync, closeSync } from "node:fs";
import { join } from "node:path";

// DECLARATION form required ("this is a/my … strategy thread"), not a mere
// MENTION — execution threads routinely reference the strategy thread in their
// briefs ("tracked from the main strategy thread") and must keep the full gate.
const STRATEGY_RE =
  /\bthis (is|session is|thread is) (a |the |my )?(main )?(strategy|tracking|planning|objective[- ]tracking|butler[- ]?planning)[- ]?(thread|session)\b|\btracking-only thread\b/i;
const FULL_RE = /\b(full preflight|execution mode|exit strategy mode)\b/i;

function stateFile(repoRoot, sessionId) {
  const safe = String(sessionId || "default").replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, "_");
  return join(repoRoot, ".claude", "hooks", ".state", `session-role-${safe}.json`);
}

function persist(sf, role, why) {
  try {
    mkdirSync(join(sf, ".."), { recursive: true });
  } catch {}
  try {
    writeFileSync(sf, JSON.stringify({ role, why, at: new Date().toISOString() }));
  } catch {}
}

// First user text of the transcript, from its first 64KB only — the strategy
// declaration is by convention the thread's opening message; never read more.
function readOpening(transcriptPath) {
  if (!transcriptPath || !existsSync(transcriptPath)) return "";
  let buf;
  try {
    const fd = openSync(transcriptPath, "r");
    buf = Buffer.alloc(65536);
    const n = readSync(fd, buf, 0, buf.length, 0);
    closeSync(fd);
    buf = buf.subarray(0, n);
  } catch {
    return "";
  }
  const texts = [];
  for (const line of buf.toString("utf8").split("\n")) {
    let rec;
    try {
      rec = JSON.parse(line);
    } catch {
      continue;
    }
    if (rec?.type === "queue-operation" && typeof rec.content === "string") texts.push(rec.content);
    const msg = rec?.message;
    if (msg?.role === "user") {
      if (typeof msg.content === "string") texts.push(msg.content);
      else if (Array.isArray(msg.content)) {
        for (const b of msg.content) if (b?.type === "text" && b.text) texts.push(b.text);
      }
    }
    if (texts.length >= 3) break;
  }
  return texts.join("\n");
}

/**
 * @returns {{ role: "strategy"|"execution", source: string }}
 * Precedence: prompt "full preflight" escape > prompt declaration > persisted
 * verdict > transcript-opening declaration > default execution. The default is
 * ALSO persisted so a settled session never re-reads its transcript; a later
 * in-prompt declaration still upgrades it (checked before the state file).
 */
export function detectSessionRole({ sessionId, prompt = "", transcriptPath = "", repoRoot = process.cwd() }) {
  const sf = stateFile(repoRoot, sessionId);
  if (FULL_RE.test(prompt)) {
    persist(sf, "execution", "user requested full gate");
    return { role: "execution", source: "prompt-escape" };
  }
  if (STRATEGY_RE.test(prompt)) {
    persist(sf, "strategy", "declared in prompt");
    return { role: "strategy", source: "prompt" };
  }
  try {
    if (existsSync(sf)) {
      const rec = JSON.parse(readFileSync(sf, "utf8"));
      if (rec?.role === "strategy" || rec?.role === "execution") return { role: rec.role, source: "state" };
    }
  } catch {}
  if (STRATEGY_RE.test(readOpening(transcriptPath))) {
    persist(sf, "strategy", "declared in transcript opening");
    return { role: "strategy", source: "transcript" };
  }
  persist(sf, "execution", "no strategy declaration found");
  return { role: "execution", source: "default" };
}
```

<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: libs/weapon/GuildOS2QuestUpdate/engineering_decisions.md -->
```markdown
# GuildOS2QuestUpdate — engineering decisions

## 2026-07-06 · A dedicated, explicitly-named weapon for GuildOS2 write-back — NOT questMutator, NOT a generic "questUpdate"

**Decision.** The weapon a local leaf uses to report progress on a *GuildOS2*
quest is its own folder, named `GuildOS2QuestUpdate`, and its `description` +
SKILL.md lead with "GuildOS2, not this repo's native quest lifecycle."

**Rejected alternatives.**
- *Reuse `questMutator`.* It is GuildOS's native write-back and speaks a different
  wire shape (`POST /api/quest/update`, `mutations:[{type,action,ref_id,values}]`)
  against THIS repo's DB. GuildOS2's endpoint is `PATCH localhost:3007/api/quest`
  with `ops:[{table,id,mode,fields}]`. Same verb ("update a quest"), incompatible
  payloads and target — routing a GuildOS2 update through questMutator 400s.
- *Name it the generic `questUpdate`.* In a repo that already owns a full native
  quest lifecycle (questmaster, questMutator, questDesign, questExecution,
  questReview, questPurrview), a bare `questUpdate` reads as "the update step of OUR
  quests." A leaf scanning the registry would grab it for a native quest and corrupt
  cross-app state. The name must carry the cross-app boundary.

**Why.** GuildOS is the *worker guild* of GuildOS2 (see `app/api/guildos2worker`).
The two apps have separate databases; nothing but this weapon's wire call crosses
the boundary. The single highest-probability drift is an agent conflating "update a
quest" here with "update a quest there." The explicit name + the SCOPE banner in
`index.js` + the SKILL.md description exist solely to make that conflation impossible.

**Consequence if violated.** Fold this into questMutator, or rename it to a generic
`questUpdate`, and a future leaf will point native quest-lifecycle machinery at a
GuildOS2 quest (or vice-versa) — silent cross-app writes that fail the schema check
or, worse, mutate the wrong app's row. Keep the boundary in the name.

## 2026-07-06 · Weapon speaks GuildOS2's REAL `ops` shape; `stage`/`description` are the only sugar

**Decision.** `update()` forwards `ops:[{table,id,mode,fields}]` verbatim to
GuildOS2 (the exact shape `libs/quest/write.js TABLES` validates over there), and
adds just two convenience params — `stage` and `description` — folded into one
`quest`-update op.

**Rejected alternative.** Inventing a friendlier local schema (e.g. the
`subitem_ops`/`type` shape that appears in GuildOS2's `how_to_respond` prompt stub)
and translating it here. Rejected: a second shape that must track GuildOS2's real
`TABLES` whitelist is a drift trap. The endpoint is the source of truth; this weapon
stays a thin, honest passthrough so it can't silently diverge from what GuildOS2
accepts. (The prompt stub in GuildOS2 is illustrative; the endpoint's `ops` shape is
authoritative — reconcile the stub toward the endpoint, never the reverse.)

## 2026-07-08 · Live PATCH field-whitelist is NARROWER than `index.js`'s header comment — trust the server's 400, not the docstring

**Decision.** When building `ops[]`, use the field sets the running `/api/quest`
validator enforces, NOT the (stale) `API CONTRACT` list in `index.js`'s header.
Verified live 2026-07-08 against a real batch:
- `objectives` writable fields = **`n, description, status, notes`** — there is **no
  `name`, `progress`, or `delta`**. The objective label goes in `description`
  (the header comment's `name/progress/delta` are wrong).
- `comments` writable fields = **`source, summary, detail, resolved, stage`** — there
  is **no `action`, `actor_name`, `position`, or `verdict`** despite the header
  listing them.

**Rejected alternative.** Trusting the header's field lists — they 400 the *entire*
batch (`payload validation failed — op[i]: unknown field(s) for "<table>"`), no
partial write.

**Why.** The header `API CONTRACT` was mirrored from an older GuildOS2
`libs/quest/write.js TABLES` map and drifted. GuildOS2 is a separate repo we don't
control; its schema moves without this weapon noticing. The running validator is the
only source of truth.

**Consequence if violated.** Whole-batch HTTP 400 and zero writes — the failure is
loud, but it costs a round-trip every time until the payload matches the live schema.

## 2026-07-08 · Creating a NEW GuildOS2 quest is `POST /api/quest/seed`, not this weapon

**Decision.** This weapon only PATCHes *existing* quests (GuildOS2's `quest` table is
update-only). To create one: `POST http://localhost:3007/api/quest/seed
{title, assignee?, description?}` (machine-key-gated → `ownerId`) creates at
`stage=plan`, then PATCH here to attach objectives/deliverables/comments.

**Rejected alternative.** Looking for a create verb on `POST /api/quest` — that route
is **lease**, not create (`leaseQuest`).

**Why / consequence.** `seed` **deletes any prior same-title quest for the owner**
before inserting (replace-by-name). Idempotent for re-seeds, but if two genuinely
distinct quests share a title, seeding one destroys the other. Use unique titles, or
PATCH an existing quest instead of re-seeding.
```

```js
/**
 * @file GuildOS2QuestUpdate — write-back weapon for quests owned by the SEPARATE
 * GuildOS2 app (http://localhost:3007), NOT this repo's native quest lifecycle.
 *
 * ⚠️ SCOPE — READ THIS FIRST. GuildOS is the WORKER GUILD of GuildOS2. When a
 * local leaf leases a GuildOS2 quest (via app/api/guildos2worker) and finishes a
 * chunk of work, it reports progress back to GuildOS2 through THIS weapon. This is
 * the "local skill" the lease's how-to-respond instruction tells the worker to look
 * for first.
 *
 * This weapon is DELIBERATELY DISTINCT from GuildOS's OWN quest machinery
 * (questMutator / questDesign / questExecution / questReview / questPurrview and the
 * questmaster skill book). Those mutate quests in THIS repo's database via THIS
 * repo's routes. GuildOS2 is a different app, different DB, different route, and a
 * DIFFERENT payload shape:
 *   - GuildOS  native write-back (questMutator): POST /api/quest/update
 *       { quest_id, mutations:[{ type, action:"add|update|remove", ref_id, values }] }
 *   - GuildOS2 write-back (THIS weapon):         PATCH http://localhost:3007/api/quest
 *       { questId,  ops:[{ table, id, mode:"new|update|delete", fields }] }
 * Do NOT point this weapon at a GuildOS quest, and do NOT reach for questMutator to
 * update a GuildOS2 quest — the shapes are incompatible and the write will 400.
 *
 * API CONTRACT (GuildOS2, mirrored from GuildOS2 libs/quest/write.js TABLES):
 *   PATCH {baseUrl}/api/quest
 *   Authorization: Bearer <GUILDOS2_API_KEY>
 *   Body: { questId:"<uuid>", ops:[ { table, id, mode, fields } ] }
 *   Logical tables + writable fields:
 *     quest        (update-only; id = the quest id): title, description, stage,
 *                  assignee, assignee_id, due_date, active_worker
 *     objectives:  n, name, status, notes, progress, delta
 *     questions:   qtype, direction, body, answer, answered, unblocks_objective_ids, actor_name
 *     deliverables:name, kind, ref, status, verify_screenshot_ref, instruction, acceptance_criteria
 *     assets:      label, ref, kind, source, actor_name, detail, resolved
 *     comments:    source, action, summary, detail, actor_name, resolved, position, verdict
 *   Per op: id:"" (or omitted) + mode:"new" inserts; existing id + mode:"update"|"delete".
 */

import { provingGroundsLog } from "@/libs/proving-grounds";

export const description =
  "Write-back to a quest in the SEPARATE GuildOS2 app (PATCH localhost:3007/api/quest). " +
  "This is GuildOS-as-worker-guild reporting progress to GuildOS2 — NOT this repo's native " +
  "quest lifecycle (that is questMutator/questmaster). Different app, DB, route, and payload shape.";

export const toc = {
  update: {
    description:
      "Apply a mutation batch to a GuildOS2 quest (progress notes, objective/deliverable " +
      "status, stage advance). Targets GuildOS2, not the native GuildOS quest system.",
    input: {
      questId: "GuildOS2 quest uuid (required)",
      ops: 'array of { table, id, mode:"new"|"update"|"delete", fields } — the real GuildOS2 batch shape',
      stage: 'optional sugar — advance the quest to this stage (becomes a quest-update op)',
      description: "optional sugar — set the quest description (becomes a quest-update op)",
      baseUrl: "optional override, default http://localhost:3007",
      apiKey: "optional override, default env GUILDOS2_API_KEY",
    },
    output: { ok: "boolean", results: "per-op results from GuildOS2", status: "HTTP status" },
  },
};

const DEFAULT_BASE = "http://localhost:3007";
const VALID_TABLES = new Set(["quest", "objectives", "questions", "deliverables", "assets", "comments"]);

/**
 * update — PATCH a GuildOS2 quest. Passes `ops` straight through to GuildOS2's
 * uniform mutation endpoint; `stage`/`description` are convenience sugar folded into
 * a single quest-update op so the common "advance + leave a note" case is one call.
 */
export async function update({ questId, ops = [], stage, description, baseUrl, apiKey } = {}) {
  if (!questId) return { ok: false, error: "questId is required (the GuildOS2 quest uuid)" };
  const key = apiKey || process.env.GUILDOS2_API_KEY;
  if (!key) return { ok: false, error: "no GUILDOS2_API_KEY (env or opts.apiKey)" };

  const batch = Array.isArray(ops) ? [...ops] : [];
  // Fold stage/description sugar into a quest-update op (merge if one already exists).
  if (stage !== undefined || description !== undefined) {
    const fields = {};
    if (stage !== undefined) fields.stage = stage;
    if (description !== undefined) fields.description = description;
    const existing = batch.find((o) => o.table === "quest" && o.mode === "update");
    if (existing) existing.fields = { ...existing.fields, ...fields };
    else batch.push({ table: "quest", id: questId, mode: "update", fields });
  }
  if (!batch.length) return { ok: false, error: "nothing to write: provide ops[] and/or stage/description" };

  const bad = batch.find((o) => !VALID_TABLES.has(o?.table));
  if (bad) {
    return { ok: false, error: `unknown table "${bad?.table}" (valid: ${[...VALID_TABLES].join(", ")}). Note: GuildOS2 uses ops[{table,...}], NOT the questMutator mutations[{type,...}] shape.` };
  }

  const base = baseUrl || process.env.GUILDOS2_BASE || DEFAULT_BASE;
  const url = `${base}/api/quest`;
  const body = { questId, ops: batch };

  // [proving-grounds step 9] the CALL side — GuildOS2 logs step 10/11 on receive+write.
  provingGroundsLog(
    "9. worker-update-call",
    `GuildOS worker → GuildOS2 update — quest ${questId}, ${batch.length} op(s)`,
    { questId, ops: batch.map((o) => ({ table: o.table, mode: o.mode, id: o.id || null })) }
  );

  let res, json;
  try {
    res = await fetch(url, {
      method: "PATCH",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", Authorization: `Bearer ${key}` },
      body: JSON.stringify(body),
    });
    json = await res.json().catch(() => ({}));
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, error: `PATCH ${url} failed: ${e.message}`, hint: "is the GuildOS2 dev server up on this base?" };
  }

  if (!res.ok) {
    return { ok: false, status: res.status, error: json?.error || `GuildOS2 rejected the write (HTTP ${res.status})`, detail: json };
  }
  return { ok: true, status: res.status, results: json?.results || json };
}
```

```js
/**
 * Asana weapon — unified Asana REST API connector.
 *
 * Auth: ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN from profiles.env_vars or process.env.
 */

export const toc = {
  searchWorkspaces: "Search visible Asana workspaces for the authenticated user.",
  searchProjects: "Search Asana projects by name or workspace.",
  readProject: "Read a single Asana project by id.",
  writeProject: "Update an Asana project's name and/or notes (description).",
  searchTasks: "Search Asana tasks across projects with filters.",
  readTask: "Read full details of one Asana task.",
  writeTask: "Create or update an Asana task (upsert).",
  deleteTask: "Delete an Asana task.",
  readSections: "Read sections of an Asana project.",
  readComments: "Read stories/comments on an Asana task.",
  writeComment: "Post a comment on an Asana task.",
  editComment: "Edit the text of an existing comment story (only the author can edit).",
  deleteComment: "Delete a comment story by its GID (only the author can delete).",
};
import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";

const API_BASE = "https://app.asana.com/api/1.0";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Auth
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async function getToken(userId) {
  if (process.env.ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN) return process.env.ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN;
  if (!userId) return null;
  const db = await database.init("service");
  const { data } = await db
    .from("profiles")
    .select("env_vars")
    .eq("id", userId)
    .single();
  return data?.env_vars?.ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN ?? null;
}

async function asanaFetch(path, opts = {}, userId) {
  const token = await getToken(userId);
  if (!token) throw new Error("Missing ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN");
  const url = path.startsWith("http") ? path : `${API_BASE}${path}`;
  const res = await fetch(url, {
    ...opts,
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      ...opts.headers,
    },
  });
  if (!res.ok) {
    const body = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`Asana API ${res.status}: ${body.slice(0, 500)}`);
  }
  const json = await res.json();
  return json.data !== undefined ? json : json;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Workspaces
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * List all workspaces the token has access to.
 * @param {object} [input]
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function searchWorkspaces(input = {}, userId) {
  const res = await asanaFetch("/workspaces?limit=100", {}, userId);
  return { workspaces: res.data || [] };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Projects
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Search projects by name or list all in a workspace.
 * @param {{ workspace_id?: string, query?: string, limit?: number }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function searchProjects({ workspace_id, query, limit = 100 } = {}, userId) {
  if (workspace_id) {
    const res = await asanaFetch(
      `/projects?workspace=${workspace_id}&opt_fields=name,archived,color&limit=${limit}`,
      {},
      userId,
    );
    let projects = res.data || [];
    if (query) {
      const q = query.toLowerCase();
      projects = projects.filter((p) => p.name.toLowerCase().includes(q));
    }
    return { projects };
  }
  // Search all workspaces
  const { workspaces } = await searchWorkspaces({}, userId);
  const all = [];
  for (const ws of workspaces) {
    const res = await asanaFetch(
      `/projects?workspace=${ws.gid}&opt_fields=name,archived,color&limit=${limit}`,
      {},
      userId,
    );
    let projects = res.data || [];
    if (query) {
      const q = query.toLowerCase();
      projects = projects.filter((p) => p.name.toLowerCase().includes(q));
    }
    all.push(...projects);
  }
  return { projects: all };
}

/**
 * Read a single project by GID.
 * @param {{ project_id: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function readProject({ project_id } = {}, userId) {
  if (!project_id) throw new Error("project_id is required");
  const res = await asanaFetch(
    `/projects/${project_id}?opt_fields=name,notes,archived,color,created_at,modified_at,owner.name,members.name`,
    {},
    userId,
  );
  return res.data || res;
}

/**
 * Update an Asana project (name and/or notes/description).
 * @param {{ project_id: string, name?: string, notes?: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function writeProject({ project_id, name, notes } = {}, userId) {
  if (!project_id) throw new Error("project_id is required");
  const body = {};
  if (name !== undefined) body.name = name;
  if (notes !== undefined) body.notes = notes;
  if (!Object.keys(body).length) throw new Error("Nothing to update — provide name and/or notes");
  const res = await asanaFetch(
    `/projects/${project_id}`,
    { method: "PUT", body: JSON.stringify({ data: body }) },
    userId,
  );
  return res.data || res;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Tasks
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Search tasks in a project or by assignee.
 * @param {{ project_id?: string, assignee?: string, workspace_id?: string, completed?: boolean, limit?: number }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function searchTasks({ project_id, assignee, workspace_id, completed, limit = 100 } = {}, userId) {
  const optFields = "name,notes,completed,assignee.name,memberships.section.name,tags.name,due_on,created_at,modified_at";

  if (project_id) {
    const params = new URLSearchParams({ opt_fields: optFields, limit: String(limit) });
    if (completed === false) params.set("completed_since", "now");
    const allTasks = [];
    let offset = null;
    do {
      if (offset) params.set("offset", offset);
      const res = await asanaFetch(`/projects/${project_id}/tasks?${params}`, {}, userId);
      if (res.data) allTasks.push(...res.data);
      offset = res.next_page?.offset || null;
    } while (offset && allTasks.length < limit);
    return { tasks: allTasks.slice(0, limit) };
  }

  if (assignee && workspace_id) {
    const params = new URLSearchParams({
      assignee,
      workspace: workspace_id,
      opt_fields: optFields,
      limit: String(limit),
    });
    if (completed === false) params.set("completed_since", "now");
    const res = await asanaFetch(`/tasks?${params}`, {}, userId);
    return { tasks: res.data || [] };
  }

  throw new Error("Either project_id or both assignee + workspace_id are required.");
}

/**
 * Read a single task by GID.
 * @param {{ task_id: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function readTask({ task_id } = {}, userId) {
  if (!task_id) throw new Error("task_id is required");
  const res = await asanaFetch(
    `/tasks/${task_id}?opt_fields=name,notes,completed,assignee.name,memberships.section.name,tags.name,due_on,created_at,modified_at,parent.name,custom_fields`,
    {},
    userId,
  );
  return res.data || res;
}

/**
 * Create or update a task.
 * @param {{ task_id?: string, project_id?: string, name?: string, notes?: string, assignee?: string, due_on?: string, completed?: boolean }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function writeTask({ task_id, project_id, name, notes, assignee, due_on, completed } = {}, userId) {
  const body = {};
  if (name != null) body.name = name;
  if (notes != null) body.notes = notes;
  if (assignee != null) body.assignee = assignee;
  if (due_on != null) body.due_on = due_on;
  if (completed != null) body.completed = completed;

  if (task_id) {
    // Update existing task
    const res = await asanaFetch(
      `/tasks/${task_id}`,
      { method: "PUT", body: JSON.stringify({ data: body }) },
      userId,
    );
    return res.data || res;
  }

  // Create new task
  if (!project_id && !body.projects) {
    throw new Error("project_id is required when creating a new task");
  }
  if (project_id) body.projects = [project_id];
  const res = await asanaFetch(
    "/tasks",
    { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ data: body }) },
    userId,
  );
  return res.data || res;
}

/**
 * Delete a task.
 * @param {{ task_id: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function deleteTask({ task_id } = {}, userId) {
  if (!task_id) throw new Error("task_id is required");
  await asanaFetch(`/tasks/${task_id}`, { method: "DELETE" }, userId);
  return { ok: true, deleted: task_id };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Sections
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Read sections in a project.
 * @param {{ project_id: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function readSections({ project_id } = {}, userId) {
  if (!project_id) throw new Error("project_id is required");
  const res = await asanaFetch(`/projects/${project_id}/sections?opt_fields=name`, {}, userId);
  return { sections: res.data || [] };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Comments / Stories
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Read comments on a task.
 * @param {{ task_id: string, limit?: number }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function readComments({ task_id, limit = 20 } = {}, userId) {
  if (!task_id) throw new Error("task_id is required");
  const res = await asanaFetch(
    `/tasks/${task_id}/stories?opt_fields=created_by.name,text,created_at,resource_subtype&limit=${limit}`,
    {},
    userId,
  );
  const comments = (res.data || [])
    .filter((s) => s.resource_subtype === "comment_added")
    .map((s) => ({
      author: s.created_by?.name || "unknown",
      text: (s.text || "").slice(0, 1000),
      created_at: s.created_at,
    }));
  return { comments };
}

/**
 * Write a comment on a task.
 * @param {{ task_id: string, text: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function writeComment({ task_id, text } = {}, userId) {
  if (!task_id) throw new Error("task_id is required");
  if (!text) throw new Error("text is required");
  const res = await asanaFetch(
    `/tasks/${task_id}/stories`,
    { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ data: { text } }) },
    userId,
  );
  return res.data || res;
}

/**
 * Edit the text of an existing comment story. Only the original author can edit.
 * @param {{ story_id: string, text: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function editComment({ story_id, text } = {}, userId) {
  if (!story_id) throw new Error("story_id is required");
  if (text == null) throw new Error("text is required");
  const res = await asanaFetch(
    `/stories/${story_id}`,
    { method: "PUT", body: JSON.stringify({ data: { text } }) },
    userId,
  );
  return res.data || res;
}

/**
 * Delete a comment story by its GID. Only the original author can delete.
 * @param {{ story_id: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function deleteComment({ story_id } = {}, userId) {
  if (!story_id) throw new Error("story_id is required");
  await asanaFetch(`/stories/${story_id}`, { method: "DELETE" }, userId);
  return { ok: true, deleted: story_id };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Credential check
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export async function checkCredentials(userId) {
  try {
    const token = await getToken(userId);
    if (token) {
      return { ok: true, msg: "ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN is set" };
    }
    return {
      ok: false,
      msg: "Missing ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN — add it to profile env_vars or process.env.",
    };
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, msg: `Error: ${e.message}` };
  }
}
```

<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: libs/weapon/assemblePackage/index.js -->
```js
/**
 * assemblePackage weapon — deterministic SA prompt assembly.
 *
 * Replaces the MA's practice of reading skill book howTos itself and
 * improvising SA prompts. Instead, this script retrieves the relevant
 * howTo sections and stitches them into a ready-to-dispatch SA prompt.
 *
 * This is the retrieval layer in the RAG architecture:
 *   triage (MA classifies) → assemblePackage (retrieves howTos) → SA executes
 *
 * Source-map: every result includes which sections were included, from
 * which source, and any warnings. Failures are never silent.
 *
 * Build order (per plan): bcs → compliance_nudge → direct_action → quest
 * self_update is a placeholder until path allowlist rules are defined.
 */

import { skillBook as guildmasterSkillBook } from "@/libs/skill_book/guildmaster/index.js";
import { WEAPONS } from "@/libs/weapon/registry.js";
import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";

/**
 * @typedef {Object} AssembleResult
 * @property {string} prompt        - Assembled SA prompt, ready to dispatch
 * @property {string[]} sections    - Section names included (e.g. ['bcs_spec'])
 * @property {string[]} sources     - Skill book / weapon paths read
 * @property {string[]} warnings    - Missing services, unresolved refs, etc.
 */

/**
 * Assemble an SA prompt for a given situation.
 *
 * @param {Object} opts
 * @param {'bcs'|'compliance_nudge'|'direct_action'|'quest'|'self_update'} opts.situation
 * @param {string[]} [opts.services]    - For direct_action: weapon ids to include
 * @param {string}   [opts.questId]    - For quest: the quest id to fetch from DB
 * @param {string}   [opts.targetFile] - For self_update: reserved / unused until allowlist exists
 * @returns {Promise<AssembleResult>}
 */
export async function assemblePackage({ situation, services = [], questId, targetFile }) {
  const toc = guildmasterSkillBook.toc;

  switch (situation) {

    // ── ① BCS (static) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    case "bcs": {
      const howTo = toc?.bcs?.howTo;
      if (!howTo) {
        return {
          prompt: "",
          sections: [],
          sources: ["guildmaster"],
          warnings: ["guildmaster.bcs.howTo not found — skill book may be stale"],
        };
      }
      return {
        prompt: [
          "## BCS Spec (read verbatim before producing a BCS response)",
          "",
          howTo.trim(),
        ].join("\n"),
        sections: ["bcs_spec"],
        sources: ["guildmaster.toc.bcs"],
        warnings: [],
      };
    }

    // ── ② Compliance nudge (static) ───────────────────────────────────────
    case "compliance_nudge": {
      const howTo = toc?.complianceNudge?.howTo;
      const bcsHowTo = toc?.bcs?.howTo; // YUNOBCS handler references the BCS spec
      if (!howTo) {
        return {
          prompt: "",
          sections: [],
          sources: ["guildmaster"],
          warnings: ["guildmaster.complianceNudge.howTo not found — skill book may be stale"],
        };
      }
      const parts = [
        "## Compliance Nudge Handler (WWCD / DSY / SW / YUNOBCS)",
        "",
        howTo.trim(),
      ];
      const sections = ["compliance_nudge_spec"];
      const sources = ["guildmaster.toc.complianceNudge"];
      const warnings = [];

      // Include BCS spec for YUNOBCS sub-flow
      if (bcsHowTo) {
        parts.push("\n## BCS Spec (referenced by YUNOBCS sub-flow)", "", bcsHowTo.trim());
        sections.push("bcs_spec");
        sources.push("guildmaster.toc.bcs");
      } else {
        warnings.push("guildmaster.bcs.howTo not found — YUNOBCS sub-flow may be incomplete");
      }

      return { prompt: parts.join("\n"), sections, sources, warnings };
    }

    // ── ③ Direct Action (dynamic services) ────────────────────────────────
    case "direct_action": {
      const howTo = toc?.packageDirect?.howTo;
      if (!howTo) {
        return {
          prompt: "",
          sections: [],
          sources: ["guildmaster"],
          warnings: ["guildmaster.packageDirect.howTo not found — skill book may be stale"],
        };
      }

      const parts = [
        "## Direct Action / Discussion Rules",
        "",
        howTo.trim(),
      ];
      const sections = ["direct_action_rules"];
      const sources = ["guildmaster.toc.packageDirect"];
      const warnings = [];

      // Append weapon toc entries for each requested service
      for (const svc of services) {
        const weapon = WEAPONS.find((w) => w.id === svc);
        if (!weapon) {
          warnings.push(`unknown service: ${svc} — not found in weapon registry`);
          continue;
        }
        // Build a compact weapon summary from registry metadata
        const weaponSummary = [
          `### Weapon: ${weapon.title} (id: ${weapon.id})`,
          `**Tagline:** ${weapon.tagline}`,
          `**Summary:** ${weapon.summary}`,
          weapon.description?.length ? `**Details:** ${weapon.description.join(" ")}` : "",
        ].filter(Boolean).join("\n");

        parts.push("", weaponSummary);
        sections.push(`weapon:${svc}`);
        sources.push(`weapon/registry.js[${svc}]`);
      }

      return { prompt: parts.join("\n"), sections, sources, warnings };
    }

    // ── ④ Quest (dynamic DB) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    case "quest": {
      const howTo = toc?.packageQuest?.howTo;
      if (!howTo) {
        return {
          prompt: "",
          sections: [],
          sources: ["guildmaster"],
          warnings: ["guildmaster.packageQuest.howTo not found — skill book may be stale"],
        };
      }

      const parts = [
        "## Quest Dispatch Rules",
        "",
        howTo.trim(),
      ];
      const sections = ["quest_rules"];
      const sources = ["guildmaster.toc.packageQuest"];
      const warnings = [];

      if (questId) {
        try {
          const db = await database.init("service");
          const { data: quest, error } = await db
            .from("quests")
            .select("id, title, description, stage, priority, assigned_to")
            .eq("id", questId)
            .single();

          if (error || !quest) {
            warnings.push(`quest:${questId} — DB fetch failed: ${error?.message ?? "no data"}`);
          } else {
            const { data: deliverables } = await db
              .from("deliverables")
              .select("item_key, expectation, url, caption")
              .eq("quest_id", questId)
              .order("item_key");

            const deliverableLines = (deliverables ?? []).map((it) =>
              `  - ${it.item_key}: ${it.expectation ?? "(no expectation)"} [url: ${it.url ?? "pending"}]`
            ).join("\n");

            parts.push(
              "",
              "## Quest Data",
              `**ID:** ${quest.id}`,
              `**Title:** ${quest.title}`,
              `**Stage:** ${quest.stage}`,
              `**Priority:** ${quest.priority}`,
              `**Assigned to:** ${quest.assigned_to ?? "unassigned"}`,
              "",
              "**Description:**",
              quest.description ?? "(none)",
              "",
              "**Deliverables:**",
              deliverableLines || "  (no deliverables rows yet)",
            );
            sections.push(`quest_data:${questId}`);
            sources.push(`supabase:quests[${questId}]`);
          }
        } catch (err) {
          warnings.push(`quest:${questId} — DB exception: ${err.message}`);
        }
      } else {
        warnings.push("questId not provided — quest data not injected");
      }

      return { prompt: parts.join("\n"), sections, sources, warnings };
    }

    // ── ⑤ Self Update (blocked — path allowlist required) ─────────────────
    case "self_update": {
      return {
        prompt: "",
        sections: [],
        sources: [],
        warnings: [
          "self_update not yet implemented — path allowlist required before file-content injection is safe",
        ],
      };
    }

    default: {
      return {
        prompt: "",
        sections: [],
        sources: [],
        warnings: [`unknown situation: ${situation} — expected one of: bcs, compliance_nudge, direct_action, quest, self_update`],
      };
    }
  }
}

export const toc = {
  assemblePackage: "Build a ready-to-dispatch SA prompt from skill book howTos and weapon registry for a given situation. Returns {prompt, sections, sources, warnings}.",
};
```
