```js
/**
 * Calendly weapon — Calendly v2 REST API connector.
 *
 * Auth: CALENDLY_ACCESS_TOKEN (Personal Access Token) from profiles.env_vars or process.env.
 *
 * Scope split (read the tradeshow.closeCalendlyAvailability howTo before using):
 * - The public Calendly v2 REST API is READ-ONLY for availability. There is NO
 *   public endpoint to block a date / mark a day unavailable / add a date override.
 *   The WRITE path for closing availability is the Calendly MCP server
 *   (mcp__calendly__*, OAuth) or, when MCP is not yet authed, CIC on calendly.com.
 * - This weapon owns the READ + VERIFY half: prove a day is open/closed, list event
 *   types + scheduled events, cancel a scheduled event. `readAvailabilityClosure`
 *   is the API-level verification that the close actually took effect.
 */

export const toc = {
  readUser: "Read the authenticated Calendly user (uri, organization, scheduling_url, timezone).",
  searchEventTypes: "Search the user's Calendly event types (active by default).",
  searchScheduledEvents: "Search scheduled events for the user within a time window.",
  readAvailabilitySchedules: "Read the user's availability schedules (rules + name; read-only).",
  readAvailableTimes: "Read bookable slots for one event type over a future date range (<=7 days).",
  readBusyTimes: "Read the user's busy intervals over a time window.",
  readAvailabilityClosure: "Verify a set of dates are CLOSED (zero bookable slots) for an event type — the API-side close verification.",
  deleteScheduledEvent: "Cancel a scheduled event by its UUID.",
};

import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";

const API_BASE = "https://api.calendly.com";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Auth
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async function getToken(userId) {
  if (process.env.CALENDLY_ACCESS_TOKEN) return process.env.CALENDLY_ACCESS_TOKEN;
  if (!userId) return null;
  try {
    const db = await database.init("service");
    const { data } = await db
      .from("profiles")
      .select("env_vars")
      .eq("id", userId)
      .single();
    return data?.env_vars?.CALENDLY_ACCESS_TOKEN ?? null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

async function calendlyFetch(path, opts = {}, userId) {
  const token = await getToken(userId);
  if (!token) throw new Error("Missing CALENDLY_ACCESS_TOKEN");
  const url = path.startsWith("http") ? path : `${API_BASE}${path}`;
  const res = await fetch(url, {
    ...opts,
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      ...opts.headers,
    },
  });
  if (!res.ok) {
    const body = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`Calendly API ${res.status}: ${body.slice(0, 500)}`);
  }
  if (res.status === 204) return {};
  return res.json();
}

// Resolve the caller's user URI (most endpoints require it). Cheap; cached per call chain.
async function resolveUserUri(userUri, userId) {
  if (userUri) return userUri;
  const me = await calendlyFetch("/users/me", {}, userId);
  return me.resource?.uri;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// User
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Read the authenticated user.
 * @param {object} [input]
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function readUser(input = {}, userId) {
  const res = await calendlyFetch("/users/me", {}, userId);
  const r = res.resource || {};
  return {
    uri: r.uri,
    name: r.name,
    email: r.email,
    scheduling_url: r.scheduling_url,
    timezone: r.timezone,
    current_organization: r.current_organization,
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Event types
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Search the user's event types.
 * @param {{ userUri?: string, active?: boolean, count?: number }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function searchEventTypes({ userUri, active = true, count = 100 } = {}, userId) {
  const uri = await resolveUserUri(userUri, userId);
  const params = new URLSearchParams({ user: uri, count: String(count) });
  if (active != null) params.set("active", String(active));
  const res = await calendlyFetch(`/event_types?${params}`, {}, userId);
  return {
    event_types: (res.collection || []).map((e) => ({
      uri: e.uri,
      name: e.name,
      slug: e.slug,
      active: e.active,
      duration: e.duration,
      scheduling_url: e.scheduling_url,
    })),
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Scheduled events
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Search scheduled events for the user in a window.
 * @param {{ userUri?: string, minStart?: string, maxStart?: string, status?: string, count?: number }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function searchScheduledEvents(
  { userUri, minStart, maxStart, status = "active", count = 100 } = {},
  userId,
) {
  const uri = await resolveUserUri(userUri, userId);
  const params = new URLSearchParams({ user: uri, count: String(count) });
  if (minStart) params.set("min_start_time", minStart);
  if (maxStart) params.set("max_start_time", maxStart);
  if (status) params.set("status", status);
  const res = await calendlyFetch(`/scheduled_events?${params}`, {}, userId);
  return {
    events: (res.collection || []).map((e) => ({
      uri: e.uri,
      uuid: (e.uri || "").split("/").pop(),
      name: e.name,
      status: e.status,
      start_time: e.start_time,
      end_time: e.end_time,
    })),
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Availability (read-only)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Read the user's availability schedules.
 * @param {{ userUri?: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function readAvailabilitySchedules({ userUri } = {}, userId) {
  const uri = await resolveUserUri(userUri, userId);
  const res = await calendlyFetch(
    `/user_availability_schedules?user=${encodeURIComponent(uri)}`,
    {},
    userId,
  );
  return {
    schedules: (res.collection || []).map((s) => ({
      uri: s.uri,
      name: s.name,
      default: s.default,
      timezone: s.timezone,
      rules: s.rules,
    })),
  };
}

/**
 * Read bookable slots for one event type over a date range.
 * Calendly constraint: start_time must be in the future and the range <= 7 days.
 * @param {{ eventTypeUri: string, start: string, end: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function readAvailableTimes({ eventTypeUri, start, end } = {}, userId) {
  if (!eventTypeUri) throw new Error("eventTypeUri is required");
  if (!start || !end) throw new Error("start and end (ISO timestamps) are required");
  const params = new URLSearchParams({
    event_type: eventTypeUri,
    start_time: start,
    end_time: end,
  });
  const res = await calendlyFetch(`/event_type_available_times?${params}`, {}, userId);
  const slots = res.collection || [];
  return {
    count: slots.length,
    times: slots.map((s) => s.start_time),
  };
}

/**
 * Read the user's busy intervals in a window.
 * @param {{ userUri?: string, start: string, end: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function readBusyTimes({ userUri, start, end } = {}, userId) {
  if (!start || !end) throw new Error("start and end (ISO timestamps) are required");
  const uri = await resolveUserUri(userUri, userId);
  const params = new URLSearchParams({ user: uri, start_time: start, end_time: end });
  const res = await calendlyFetch(`/user_busy_times?${params}`, {}, userId);
  return {
    busy: (res.collection || []).map((b) => ({
      type: b.type,
      start_time: b.start_time,
      end_time: b.end_time,
    })),
  };
}

/**
 * VERIFY that each given calendar date is CLOSED (zero bookable slots) for an
 * event type. This is the API-side proof that a close-availability action took
 * effect — call it after the MCP/CIC write path closes the days.
 *
 * @param {{ eventTypeUri: string, dates: string[], timezone?: string }} input
 *   dates: array of YYYY-MM-DD strings (the travel/show days to assert closed).
 * @param {string} [userId]
 * @returns {{ allClosed: boolean, perDay: Array<{date,slotCount,closed,sample}> }}
 */
export async function readAvailabilityClosure({ eventTypeUri, dates = [] } = {}, userId) {
  if (!eventTypeUri) throw new Error("eventTypeUri is required");
  if (!dates.length) throw new Error("dates[] (YYYY-MM-DD) is required");
  const perDay = [];
  for (const d of dates) {
    // Query the full UTC day. event_type_available_times needs start in the
    // future; a same-day re-check just before the window is fine.
    const start = `${d}T00:00:00.000000Z`;
    const end = `${d}T23:59:59.000000Z`;
    let slotCount = 0;
    let sample = [];
    let error = null;
    try {
      const r = await readAvailableTimes({ eventTypeUri, start, end }, userId);
      slotCount = r.count;
      sample = r.times.slice(0, 3);
    } catch (e) {
      error = e.message;
    }
    perDay.push({
      date: d,
      slotCount,
      closed: error ? null : slotCount === 0,
      sample,
      ...(error ? { error } : {}),
    });
  }
  const allClosed = perDay.every((p) => p.closed === true);
  return { allClosed, perDay };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Scheduled-event cancellation
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Cancel a scheduled event by UUID.
 * @param {{ uuid: string, reason?: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function deleteScheduledEvent({ uuid, reason = "Booth staff unavailable — tradeshow travel." } = {}, userId) {
  if (!uuid) throw new Error("uuid is required");
  const res = await calendlyFetch(
    `/scheduled_events/${uuid}/cancellation`,
    { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ reason }) },
    userId,
  );
  return { ok: true, cancelled: uuid, resource: res.resource || null };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Credential check
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export async function checkCredentials(userId) {
  try {
    const token = await getToken(userId);
    if (!token) {
      return {
        ok: false,
        msg: "Missing CALENDLY_ACCESS_TOKEN — add it to .env.local or profile env_vars.",
      };
    }
    const me = await readUser({}, userId);
    if (me?.uri) {
      return { ok: true, msg: `CALENDLY_ACCESS_TOKEN valid — ${me.email || me.name}` };
    }
    return { ok: false, msg: "Token set but /users/me returned no resource." };
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, msg: `Error: ${e.message}` };
  }
}
```

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// CLI for the ccSessions weapon.
//   node libs/weapon/ccSessions/cli.mjs                       → all records (compact)
//   node libs/weapon/ccSessions/cli.mjs "<query>" [--cwd <p>] → matching records (full JSON)
// <query> = ccd id (local_<uuid> or bare uuid), transcript uuid, a >=6-hex-char
// short id (objectives-table form), or a title substring.

import { listSessionRecords, resolveSession } from "./index.js";

const args = process.argv.slice(2);
const cwdIdx = args.indexOf("--cwd");
const cwd = cwdIdx >= 0 ? args[cwdIdx + 1] : undefined;
const query = args.filter((a, i) => i !== cwdIdx && i !== (cwdIdx >= 0 ? cwdIdx + 1 : -1))[0];

if (!query) {
  const rows = listSessionRecords().map(
    (r) =>
      `${r.ccdSessionId}  →  ${r.cliSessionId}  [${r.isArchived ? "archived" : "live"}] ${JSON.stringify(r.title)}  (${r.cwd})${r.transcriptExists ? "" : "  ⚠ transcript missing"}`,
  );
  process.stdout.write(rows.join("\n") + "\n");
  process.exit(0);
}

const idLike = /^(local_)?[0-9a-f]{6,}(-[0-9a-f-]+)?$/i.test(query);
const hits = idLike
  ? resolveSession({ sessionId: query, cwd })
  : resolveSession({ title: query, cwd });

if (!hits.length) {
  process.stderr.write(`no session record matched ${JSON.stringify(query)}\n`);
  process.exit(1);
}
process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(hits, null, 2) + "\n");
```

```markdown
# Engineering Decisions — ccSessions weapon

## 2026-07-03 — Read the desktop app's private session store; no maintained index, no mtime heuristic

**Decision:** sessionId↔transcript resolution reads the Claude desktop app's own
store (`%APPDATA%\Claude\claude-code-sessions\<org>\<user>\<ccdSessionId>.json`,
field `cliSessionId` = transcript filename) fresh on every call.

**Rejected alternatives:** (a) A GuildOS-maintained index file mapping ids —
requires write-side discipline from every session and goes stale the moment one
forgets; the app's store is already authoritative and always current. (b) The
prior mtime heuristic ("newest transcript that isn't me") — guesswork that
breaks with ≥2 concurrently-active siblings, exactly the multi-session case
this weapon exists for.

**Why:** the store is the only place the ccd id (`local_<uuid>`) and the CLI
transcript id coexist; reading it is O(store size) and needs zero cooperation
from other sessions.

**Consequence-if-violated:** re-introducing mtime guessing silently mis-attributes
digests across concurrent threads. NOTE the accepted risk: the store is an
UNDOCUMENTED app internal — if a desktop update changes its shape, this weapon
degrades to no-matches (never wrong-matches); the documented fallback is mtime
ordering per butlerPlanning.digestOtherThread step 2.
```

```js
/**
 * ccSessions weapon — deterministic ccd sessionId ↔ transcript mapping
 * (adopted SIO, 2026-07-03).
 *
 * THE FACT THIS WEAPON ENCODES (verified 2026-07-03): the Claude desktop app
 * keeps one JSON record per Claude Code session at
 *   %APPDATA%\Claude\claude-code-sessions\<org-uuid>\<user-uuid>\<ccdSessionId>.json
 * whose `sessionId` field is the ccd id (`local_<uuid>`) that
 * ccd_session_mgmt.list_sessions returns, and whose `cliSessionId` field IS
 * the transcript filename under
 *   ~/.claude/projects/<cwd-slug>/<cliSessionId>.jsonl
 * (cwd-slug = cwd with every non-alphanumeric char replaced by "-").
 * So a title or ccd sessionId resolves to its transcript path with zero
 * mtime guessing.
 *
 * CLI: node libs/weapon/ccSessions/cli.mjs "<local_<uuid> | transcript-uuid |
 *      8-char short id | title substring>"
 */

export const toc = {
  listSessionRecords:
    "Scan the desktop app's claude-code-sessions store; returns [{ccdSessionId, cliSessionId, title, cwd, isArchived, lastActivityAt, model, transcriptPath, transcriptExists}] sorted by lastActivityAt desc.",
  resolveSession:
    "Resolve {sessionId (ccd 'local_<uuid>', bare uuid, transcript uuid, or a >=6-hex-char prefix like the objectives-table short id), title (substring, case-insensitive), cwd (optional filter)} to matching session record(s) incl. transcriptPath. CLI: node libs/weapon/ccSessions/cli.mjs \"<id-or-title>\"",
};

import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, existsSync } from "node:fs";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { homedir } from "node:os";

// Env override exists ONLY for tests; production reads the real store.
function storeDir() {
  return (
    process.env.CCD_SESSIONS_STORE ||
    join(
      process.env.APPDATA || join(homedir(), "AppData", "Roaming"),
      "Claude",
      "claude-code-sessions",
    )
  );
}

/** cwd → the ~/.claude/projects/ directory slug ("C:\Users\x\GuildOS" → "C--Users-x-GuildOS"). */
export function projectSlug(cwd) {
  return String(cwd || "").replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, "-");
}

export function transcriptPathFor(cwd, cliSessionId) {
  return join(homedir(), ".claude", "projects", projectSlug(cwd), `${cliSessionId}.jsonl`);
}

function collectJsonFiles(dir, depth, out) {
  let entries = [];
  try {
    entries = readdirSync(dir);
  } catch {
    return;
  }
  for (const name of entries) {
    const full = join(dir, name);
    let s;
    try {
      s = statSync(full);
    } catch {
      continue;
    }
    if (s.isDirectory()) {
      if (depth > 0) collectJsonFiles(full, depth - 1, out);
    } else if (name.endsWith(".json")) {
      out.push(full);
    }
  }
}

/**
 * All session records in the desktop store, newest activity first.
 * Records are ~10-100KB each (embedded MCP config) but parsing stays cheap at
 * the store's real scale (tens of sessions).
 */
export function listSessionRecords() {
  const files = [];
  collectJsonFiles(storeDir(), 3, files);
  const out = [];
  for (const f of files) {
    let rec;
    try {
      rec = JSON.parse(readFileSync(f, "utf8"));
    } catch {
      continue;
    }
    if (!rec || !rec.sessionId || !rec.cliSessionId) continue;
    const transcriptPath = transcriptPathFor(rec.cwd, rec.cliSessionId);
    out.push({
      ccdSessionId: rec.sessionId,
      cliSessionId: rec.cliSessionId,
      title: rec.title || "",
      cwd: rec.cwd || "",
      isArchived: !!rec.isArchived,
      lastActivityAt: rec.lastActivityAt || 0,
      model: rec.model || "",
      transcriptPath,
      transcriptExists: existsSync(transcriptPath),
    });
  }
  return out.sort((a, b) => (b.lastActivityAt || 0) - (a.lastActivityAt || 0));
}

/**
 * @param {{ sessionId?: string, title?: string, cwd?: string }} q
 *   sessionId: 'local_<uuid>', bare ccd uuid, transcript (cli) uuid, or a
 *   >=6-hex-char prefix of either (the objectives-table short id form).
 *   title: case-insensitive substring. cwd: optional exact-project filter.
 * @returns {Array<ReturnType<typeof listSessionRecords>[number]>}
 */
export function resolveSession(q = {}) {
  let hits = listSessionRecords();
  if (q.cwd) {
    const slug = projectSlug(q.cwd).toLowerCase();
    hits = hits.filter((r) => projectSlug(r.cwd).toLowerCase() === slug);
  }
  if (q.sessionId) {
    const want = String(q.sessionId).replace(/^local_/i, "").toLowerCase();
    hits = hits.filter((r) => {
      const ccd = String(r.ccdSessionId).replace(/^local_/i, "").toLowerCase();
      const cli = String(r.cliSessionId).toLowerCase();
      return ccd === want || cli === want || (want.length >= 6 && (ccd.startsWith(want) || cli.startsWith(want)));
    });
  } else if (q.title) {
    const t = String(q.title).toLowerCase();
    hits = hits.filter((r) => r.title.toLowerCase().includes(t));
  }
  return hits;
}
```

```js
/**
 * cc_cost weapon — offline JSONL transcript analyzer.
 *
 * Adopted from rohitg00/awesome-claude-code-toolkit's cc-cost. Parses Claude
 * Code session transcripts (JSONL) and reports:
 *   - cache hit rate (% turns reading from prompt cache vs cold)
 *   - top-expensive turns (tokens consumed)
 *   - tool-call distribution
 *
 * No external deps. Runs against the user's Claude Code project transcript
 * dir, defaulting to:
 *   C:/Users/xsj70/.claude/projects/C--Users-xsj70-GuildOS/
 *
 * Usage (from a skill book or directly):
 *   const { analyzeTranscripts } = await import("@/libs/weapon/cc_cost/index.js");
 *   const report = await analyzeTranscripts({ limit: 5 });
 */

import { readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
import { join } from "node:path";

const DEFAULT_DIR = "C:/Users/xsj70/.claude/projects/C--Users-xsj70-GuildOS/";

export function checkCredentials() {
  try {
    statSync(DEFAULT_DIR);
    return { ok: true };
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, reason: `Transcript dir not found: ${DEFAULT_DIR}` };
  }
}

/**
 * @param {{ dir?: string, limit?: number, sinceMs?: number }} opts
 * @returns {Promise<{
 *   sessions_total: number,
 *   sessions_analyzed: number,
 *   total_input_tokens: number,
 *   total_output_tokens: number,
 *   total_cache_read_tokens: number,
 *   total_cache_creation_tokens: number,
 *   cache_read_pct: number,
 *   tool_use_counts: Record<string, number>,
 *   top_expensive_turns: Array<{ session: string, turn: number, total_tokens: number }>
 * }>}
 */
export async function analyzeTranscripts(opts = {}) {
  const dir = opts.dir || DEFAULT_DIR;
  const limit = opts.limit || 50;
  const sinceMs = opts.sinceMs || 0;

  let files = [];
  try {
    files = readdirSync(dir)
      .filter((f) => f.endsWith(".jsonl"))
      .map((f) => ({ name: f, path: join(dir, f), mtime: statSync(join(dir, f)).mtimeMs }))
      .filter((f) => f.mtime >= sinceMs)
      .sort((a, b) => b.mtime - a.mtime)
      .slice(0, limit);
  } catch (e) {
    return { error: `cannot read transcript dir: ${e.message}`, sessions_total: 0, sessions_analyzed: 0 };
  }

  let totalInput = 0, totalOutput = 0, totalCacheRead = 0, totalCacheCreate = 0;
  const toolUse = {};
  const turns = [];

  for (const f of files) {
    let lines;
    try {
      lines = readFileSync(f.path, "utf8").split("\n").filter(Boolean);
    } catch { continue; }
    let turnIdx = 0;
    for (const line of lines) {
      let rec;
      try { rec = JSON.parse(line); } catch { continue; }

      const usage = rec?.message?.usage || rec?.usage;
      if (usage) {
        turnIdx++;
        const inp = usage.input_tokens || 0;
        const out = usage.output_tokens || 0;
        const cRead = usage.cache_read_input_tokens || 0;
        const cCreate = usage.cache_creation_input_tokens || 0;
        totalInput += inp;
        totalOutput += out;
        totalCacheRead += cRead;
        totalCacheCreate += cCreate;
        turns.push({ session: f.name, turn: turnIdx, total_tokens: inp + out + cRead + cCreate });
      }

      // Tool-call counting from assistant content blocks.
      const content = rec?.message?.content;
      if (Array.isArray(content)) {
        for (const block of content) {
          if (block?.type === "tool_use" && block?.name) {
            toolUse[block.name] = (toolUse[block.name] || 0) + 1;
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }

  const totalReadable = totalCacheRead + totalInput;
  const cacheReadPct = totalReadable ? Math.round((totalCacheRead / totalReadable) * 1000) / 10 : 0;

  turns.sort((a, b) => b.total_tokens - a.total_tokens);

  return {
    sessions_total: files.length,
    sessions_analyzed: files.length,
    total_input_tokens: totalInput,
    total_output_tokens: totalOutput,
    total_cache_read_tokens: totalCacheRead,
    total_cache_creation_tokens: totalCacheCreate,
    cache_read_pct: cacheReadPct,
    tool_use_counts: toolUse,
    top_expensive_turns: turns.slice(0, 10),
  };
}
```

```js
/**
 * cicHealth — CIC (Claude-in-Chrome) liveness precondition gate.
 *
 * Distinct from `cicVerify` (a vision CONTENT verifier). This weapon answers
 * one question: "is the substrate that user-channel visual verification
 * depends on actually up?" — the SCRIPTABLE half only:
 *
 *   checkServer({ url }) → is the GuildOS dev server actually serving?
 *
 * Why only this half: the CIC screenshot itself is an MCP tool
 * (`mcp__Claude_in_Chrome__*`) available ONLY to the agent, not callable
 * from a Node weapon. So this weapon does the deterministic server-reachable
 * check; the agent-side CIC screenshot + the hard escalation-on-failure gate
 * live in the `browsercontrol.validateCIC` skill-book action, which calls
 * this first. Split is intentional and documented so it is not "fixed" into
 * a fake all-in-one.
 *
 * A 3xx / 401 / 403 still means the server is UP (auth redirect etc.). Only
 * connection-refused / timeout / DNS = DOWN.
 */

import { logWeaponCall } from "../weaponLog/index.js";

const DEFAULT_URL = "http://localhost:3002";

/**
 * @param {{ url?: string, timeoutMs?: number, agent?: string }} [opts]
 * @returns {Promise<{ ok: boolean, reachable: boolean, status: number|null, url: string, reason: string }>}
 */
export async function checkServer({ url = DEFAULT_URL, timeoutMs = 6000, agent = "SA" } = {}) {
  const input = { url, timeoutMs };
  const ctrl = new AbortController();
  const t = setTimeout(() => ctrl.abort(), timeoutMs);
  try {
    const res = await fetch(url, { method: "GET", redirect: "manual", signal: ctrl.signal });
    clearTimeout(t);
    // Any HTTP status = the server answered = UP (incl. 3xx auth redirects, 401/403).
    const out = {
      ok: true,
      reachable: true,
      status: res.status,
      url,
      reason: `server answered HTTP ${res.status} — UP`,
    };
    logWeaponCall({ weapon: "cicHealth", fn: "checkServer", agent, input, output: out, status: "ok" });
    return out;
  } catch (e) {
    clearTimeout(t);
    const aborted = e?.name === "AbortError";
    const out = {
      ok: false,
      reachable: false,
      status: null,
      url,
      reason: aborted
        ? `no response within ${timeoutMs}ms — server DOWN or not started`
        : `connection failed (${e?.message || e}) — server DOWN, refused, or wrong port`,
    };
    logWeaponCall({ weapon: "cicHealth", fn: "checkServer", agent, input, output: out, status: "ok" });
    return out;
  }
}

export const toc = {
  checkServer:
    "Deterministic half of the CIC liveness gate: is the GuildOS dev server actually serving? Input {url?='http://localhost:3002', timeoutMs?, agent?}. Any HTTP status (incl. 3xx/401) = UP; only refused/timeout = DOWN. Returns {ok, reachable, status, url, reason}. The agent-side CIC screenshot + escalation gate is browsercontrol.validateCIC, which calls this first.",
};

export const definition = { checkServer, toc };
export default definition;
```

```js
/**
 * cicVerify — CIC screenshot verification via OpenAI vision.
 *
 * SA calls verify() after taking a CIC screenshot (saved to disk).
 * This weapon:
 *   1. Reads the image file
 *   2. Calls OpenAI vision to extract visible text (OCR equivalent)
 *   3. Passes image + OCR text + objective to a sandboxed verifier (separate OpenAI call)
 *   4. Returns { pass: boolean, ocrText, verdict, reason }
 *   5. Logs the call via weaponLog
 *
 * The verifier is sandboxed: it sees ONLY the image, OCR text, and objective.
 * No conversation history. No motivation to please the MA. Just a boolean.
 *
 * Failure signatures that auto-fail without calling the verifier:
 *   - OCR text is empty or < 10 chars → blank/white page
 *   - OCR text contains "404", "not found", "error", "localhost refused" → bad page
 */

import { readFileSync } from "fs";
import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";
import { logWeaponCall } from "../weaponLog/index.js";
import { screenshotUrl } from "../leafBrowser/index.js";

const OPENAI_BASE = "https://api.openai.com/v1";

async function getApiKey() {
  try {
    const db = await database.init("service");
    const { data } = await db.from("profiles").select("env_vars").limit(1).single();
    return data?.env_vars?.OPENAI_API_KEY || process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY;
  } catch {
    return process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY;
  }
}

async function callVision(apiKey, base64Image, prompt) {
  const res = await fetch(`${OPENAI_BASE}/chat/completions`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}` },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      model: "gpt-4o",
      max_tokens: 500,
      messages: [{
        role: "user",
        content: [
          { type: "image_url", image_url: { url: `data:image/jpeg;base64,${base64Image}`, detail: "low" } },
          { type: "text", text: prompt },
        ],
      }],
    }),
  });
  const data = await res.json();
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(data.error?.message || `OpenAI error ${res.status}`);
  return data.choices[0].message.content.trim();
}

/**
 * Take a screenshot of a URL, returning base64 PNG. Delegates to the single
 * browser substrate (leafBrowser.screenshotUrl) — no local chromium.launch.
 * Viewport-only shot (not full-page) to match this weapon's vision-OCR use.
 * @internal
 */
async function screenshotFromUrl(url) {
  const res = await screenshotUrl({
    url, fullPage: false, viewport: { width: 1280, height: 800 }, timeoutMs: 15000, encoding: "base64",
  });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(res.error);
  return res.base64;
}

/**
 * Verify a page against an objective via vision.
 *
 * Accepts either:
 *   { imagePath, url, objective, agent? }  — read image from disk
 *   { url, objective, agent? }             — take screenshot via Playwright
 *
 * @returns {Promise<{ pass: boolean, ocrText: string, verdict: string, reason: string }>}
 */
export async function verify({ imagePath, url, objective, agent = "SA" }) {
  const input = { imagePath: imagePath || "(playwright)", url, objective: objective?.slice(0, 100) };

  try {
    let base64Image;
    if (imagePath) {
      // Caller provided a pre-saved image
      const imageBuffer = readFileSync(imagePath);
      base64Image = imageBuffer.toString("base64");
    } else {
      // No image path — take screenshot from the URL via Playwright
      if (!url) throw new Error("cicVerify.verify requires either imagePath or url");
      base64Image = await screenshotFromUrl(url);
    }


    const apiKey = await getApiKey();
    if (!apiKey) throw new Error("OPENAI_API_KEY not found in profiles or env");

    // Step 1: OCR — extract visible text from the screenshot
    const ocrText = await callVision(apiKey, base64Image,
      "Extract all visible text from this screenshot exactly as it appears. Include headings, body text, error messages, URLs, button labels. If the page is blank or shows only whitespace, respond with 'BLANK_PAGE'. If it shows an error, respond with 'ERROR: ' followed by the error text."
    );

    // Auto-fail checks on OCR text
    const ocrLower = ocrText.toLowerCase();
    const autoFailReasons = [
      ocrLower.length < 10 && "OCR returned < 10 characters — page appears blank",
      ocrText === "BLANK_PAGE" && "Page is blank/white — nothing rendered",
      ocrLower.includes("404") && "Page shows 404 error",
      ocrLower.includes("not found") && ocrLower.length < 100 && "Page shows Not Found",
      ocrLower.includes("refused to connect") && "Browser refused to connect",
      ocrLower.includes("err_connection_refused") && "Connection refused",
    ].filter(Boolean);

    if (autoFailReasons.length) {
      const result = { pass: false, ocrText, verdict: "FAIL", reason: autoFailReasons[0] };
      logWeaponCall({ weapon: "cicVerify", fn: "verify", agent, input, output: { pass: false, reason: result.reason, ocrLength: ocrText.length }, status: "ok" });
      return result;
    }

    // Step 2: Sandboxed verifier — does the page content match the objective?
    const verdictRaw = await callVision(apiKey, base64Image,
      `You are a QA verifier. You have no context about this task beyond what is provided here.

OBJECTIVE: ${objective}

OCR TEXT EXTRACTED FROM SCREENSHOT:
${ocrText}

Does the screenshot show a page that satisfies the objective?
Answer with exactly: PASS or FAIL
Then on the next line, one sentence explaining why.`
    );

    const lines = verdictRaw.split("\n").map(l => l.trim()).filter(Boolean);
    const pass = lines[0]?.toUpperCase().startsWith("PASS");
    const reason = lines[1] || verdictRaw;

    const result = { pass, ocrText, verdict: pass ? "PASS" : "FAIL", reason };
    logWeaponCall({ weapon: "cicVerify", fn: "verify", agent, input, output: { pass, verdict: result.verdict, ocrLength: ocrText.length }, status: "ok" });
    return result;

  } catch (e) {
    const result = { pass: false, ocrText: "", verdict: "ERROR", reason: `cicVerify failed: ${e.message}` };
    logWeaponCall({ weapon: "cicVerify", fn: "verify", agent, input, output: result, status: "error" });
    return result;
  }
}

export const toc = {
  verify: "Verify a page against an objective via OpenAI vision. Input: {url, objective, agent?, imagePath?}. If imagePath omitted, takes screenshot via Playwright. Returns {pass:boolean, ocrText, verdict, reason}. Auto-fails on blank/404/error. Sandboxed verifier has no conversation context.",
};
```

```markdown
# Engineering Decisions — CJGEO Weapon

## 2026-06-16: v1 API paths, not legacy /api/articles

**Decision:** The weapon uses `/api/v1/articles/...` paths exclusively, NOT the `/api/articles/...` paths documented in `libs/skill_book/cjgeo/index.js refApiActions`.

**Rejected alternative:** Using the `/api/articles/{articleId}` action-based endpoints (get_assets, get_html, set_main_keyword via action field).

**Why:** The `/api/articles/...` routes are LEGACY internal routes without x-api-key auth support on production (they return 404 for the collection endpoint and rely on session-based auth). The `/api/v1/articles/...` routes are the external API surface: they use x-api-key → external_api_keys table lookup, enforce per-user ownership, and have dedicated endpoints per action (not action-field dispatching). Discovered empirically: `/api/articles` POST → 404 on cjgeoai.com; `/api/v1/articles` POST → 201.

**Consequence if violated:** All weapon API calls would 404 or 403 on production. The skill book's `refApiActions` is stale/wrong for external API consumers.

## 2026-06-16: Supabase direct reads for article data

**Decision:** `readArticleDirect` reads from CJGEO's Supabase (ref `<REDACTED-PROJECT-REF>`) using the service role key from `C:/Users/xsj70/cjgeo/.env.local`, because the v1 API doesn't expose read-only get_assets/get_html endpoints.

**Rejected alternative:** Adding get_assets/get_html to the v1 API routes in the CJGEO codebase.

**Why:** The v1 API is intentionally action-oriented (write operations only: create, set keyword, research, generate, adopt). Read operations go through the CJGEO Supabase directly with service role key. The key is loaded from the cjgeo repo's .env.local at runtime (fallback from CJGEO_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY env var).

**Consequence if violated:** No way to read article assets/content for gate checks or publishing adapters. The publishing adapters depend on content_html reads.

## 2026-06-16: Draft generation works on production only (CONFIRMED)

**Decision:** Use production cjgeoai.com (not localhost:3000) as the base URL for draft generation.

**Rejected alternative:** Running draft generation against the local dev server.

**Why:** CJGEO's draft generation uses a v0 AI engine that fires async after the API call. The local dev server accepts the request but the generation worker fails ("Generation failed" after ~1min). Production (cjgeoai.com on Vercel) successfully processes: queued → rendering → completed. Confirmed 2026-06-16: production draft reached "rendering" status within 2 minutes of the API call.

**Consequence if violated:** Draft generation will always fail on the local dev server, blocking the pipeline at step 6. The weapon's CJGEO_BASE_URL must default to https://cjgeoai.com (production), not localhost.
```

```js
/**
 * CJGEO weapon — wraps the CJGEO Content Magic v1 REST API for programmatic
 * full-auto article pipeline execution.
 *
 * Auth: CJGEO_API_KEY env var (x-api-key header on every request).
 * Base URL: CJGEO_BASE_URL env var, defaults to https://cjgeoai.com.
 *
 * v1 API routes (verified from cjgeo codebase 2026-06-16):
 *   POST /api/v1/articles                          — create article
 *   POST /api/v1/articles/{id}/main-keyword        — set main keyword
 *   POST /api/v1/articles/{id}/research/keywords   — keyword research
 *   POST /api/v1/articles/{id}/research/topics     — topic benchmark
 *   POST /api/v1/articles/{id}/draft               — draft generation (fire-and-forget)
 *   GET  /api/v1/articles/{id}/draft/status        — poll draft status
 *   POST /api/v1/articles/{id}/adopt               — adopt draft into content_html
 *
 * NOTE: The skill book cjgeo.refApiActions documents /api/articles/{id} action-based
 * endpoints (get_assets, get_html, etc.) — those are the LEGACY internal routes at
 * /api/articles/[articleId]/route.ts, NOT the v1 API. Both coexist; the v1 routes
 * are the external-API-key path. Assets/HTML reads go through CJGEO Supabase direct
 * when needed (the v1 API doesn't expose read-only get_assets/get_html endpoints).
 */

export const toc = {
  writeArticle:
    "Create a new CJGEO article via the v1 API. Returns article_id.",
  writeMainKeyword:
    "Commit the main keyword on an article. Required before research stages.",
  runKeywordResearch:
    "Run SEO keyword research on an article (5-min chain).",
  runTopicBenchmark:
    "Run competitor topic benchmark on an article (5-min chain).",
  writeDraftGenerate:
    "Kick off async draft generation (fire-and-forget). Poll via readDraftStatus.",
  readDraftStatus:
    "Poll draft generation status (GET). Returns queued/sending/rendering/completed/failed.",
  writeDraftAdopt:
    "Adopt the completed draft into content_html. 409 if draft not completed.",
  readArticleDirect:
    "Read article fields directly from CJGEO Supabase (bypasses API for reads).",
  runFullAutoPipeline:
    "Run the complete no-gating pipeline: create -> keyword -> research -> draft -> poll -> adopt.",
  publishToCjgeoai:
    "cjgeoai.com adapter: verify article is adopted and return the live URL.",
  publishToBosterbio:
    "bosterbio.com adapter: fetch CJGEO content, sanitize for Magento, POST to CMS mutation endpoint.",
  checkCredentials:
    "Check that CJGEO API credentials are configured.",
};

/* ── Internals ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

// Redacted from source — set CJGEO_SUPABASE_URL in .env.local (see .env.example).
const CJGEO_SUPABASE_URL = process.env.CJGEO_SUPABASE_URL;

function loadConfig() {
  const apiKey = process.env.CJGEO_API_KEY;
  const baseUrl = (process.env.CJGEO_BASE_URL || "https://cjgeoai.com").replace(/\/+$/, "");
  if (!apiKey) throw new Error("CJGEO_API_KEY not set");
  return { apiKey, baseUrl };
}

import { readFileSync } from "fs";
import { homedir } from "os";
import { join } from "path";

function loadCjgeoSupabaseKey() {
  const key = process.env.CJGEO_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY;
  if (key) return key;
  try {
    const envPath = process.env.CJGEO_ENV_FILE || join(homedir(), "cjgeo", ".env.local");
    const envContent = readFileSync(envPath, "utf8");
    const match = envContent.match(/^SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=(.+)$/m);
    if (match) return match[1].trim();
  } catch { /* ignore */ }
  throw new Error("CJGEO Supabase service role key not available");
}

async function apiPost(path, body = {}) {
  const { apiKey, baseUrl } = loadConfig();
  const url = `${baseUrl}${path}`;
  const res = await fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      "x-api-key": apiKey,
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  });
  const text = await res.text();
  let json;
  try { json = JSON.parse(text); } catch { json = { raw: text }; }
  if (!res.ok) {
    const msg = json?.error || `HTTP ${res.status}`;
    throw new Error(`CJGEO API ${path}: ${msg}`);
  }
  return json;
}

async function apiGet(path) {
  const { apiKey, baseUrl } = loadConfig();
  const url = `${baseUrl}${path}`;
  const res = await fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers: { "x-api-key": apiKey },
  });
  const text = await res.text();
  let json;
  try { json = JSON.parse(text); } catch { json = { raw: text }; }
  if (!res.ok) {
    const msg = json?.error || `HTTP ${res.status}`;
    throw new Error(`CJGEO API GET ${path}: ${msg}`);
  }
  return json;
}

async function supabaseRead(table, select, filter = "") {
  if (!CJGEO_SUPABASE_URL) throw new Error("CJGEO_SUPABASE_URL not set — configure it in .env.local (see .env.example).");
  const key = loadCjgeoSupabaseKey();
  const url = `${CJGEO_SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/${table}?select=${encodeURIComponent(select)}${filter ? "&" + filter : ""}`;
  const res = await fetch(url, {
    headers: { apikey: key, Authorization: `Bearer ${key}` },
  });
  if (!res.ok) {
    const text = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`CJGEO Supabase read ${table}: ${text}`);
  }
  return res.json();
}

function sleep(ms) { return new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms)); }

/* ── Exports ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

export async function writeArticle({ title, mainKeyword } = {}) {
  if (!title) throw new Error("title is required");
  const body = { title };
  if (mainKeyword) body.main_keyword = mainKeyword;
  const res = await apiPost("/api/v1/articles", body);
  return { article_id: res.article_id || res.id, reused: false };
}

export async function writeMainKeyword({ articleId, mainKeyword } = {}) {
  if (!articleId || !mainKeyword) throw new Error("articleId and mainKeyword required");
  return apiPost(`/api/v1/articles/${articleId}/main-keyword`, { main_keyword: mainKeyword });
}

export async function runKeywordResearch({ articleId, keyword } = {}) {
  if (!articleId) throw new Error("articleId required");
  const body = keyword ? { keyword } : {};
  return apiPost(`/api/v1/articles/${articleId}/research/keywords`, body);
}

export async function runTopicBenchmark({ articleId, keyword } = {}) {
  if (!articleId) throw new Error("articleId required");
  const body = keyword ? { keyword } : {};
  return apiPost(`/api/v1/articles/${articleId}/research/topics`, body);
}

export async function writeDraftGenerate({ articleId, skipResearch = false } = {}) {
  if (!articleId) throw new Error("articleId required");
  return apiPost(`/api/v1/articles/${articleId}/draft`, { skip_research: skipResearch });
}

export async function readDraftStatus({ articleId } = {}) {
  if (!articleId) throw new Error("articleId required");
  return apiGet(`/api/v1/articles/${articleId}/draft/status`);
}

export async function writeDraftAdopt({ articleId } = {}) {
  if (!articleId) throw new Error("articleId required");
  return apiPost(`/api/v1/articles/${articleId}/adopt`, {});
}

/**
 * Read article fields directly from CJGEO Supabase (bypasses API for reads).
 */
export async function readArticleDirect({ articleId, fields = "id,title,status,assets,content_html" } = {}) {
  if (!articleId) throw new Error("articleId required");
  const rows = await supabaseRead("content_magic_articles", fields, `id=eq.${articleId}`);
  if (!rows.length) throw new Error(`Article ${articleId} not found in CJGEO Supabase`);
  return rows[0];
}

/**
 * Run the complete no-gating full-auto pipeline.
 * @param {object} opts
 * @param {string} opts.title - Article title
 * @param {string} opts.mainKeyword - The main keyword/topic
 * @param {number} [opts.pollIntervalMs=60000] - Poll interval (default 1min)
 * @param {number} [opts.pollTimeoutMs=1200000] - Poll timeout (default 20min)
 */
export async function runFullAutoPipeline({ title, mainKeyword, pollIntervalMs = 60_000, pollTimeoutMs = 1_200_000 } = {}) {
  if (!title || !mainKeyword) throw new Error("title and mainKeyword required");

  const stages = [];
  const log = (name, result) => { stages.push({ stage: name, result, ts: new Date().toISOString() }); };

  // 1. Create article
  const created = await writeArticle({ title, mainKeyword });
  log("writeArticle", created);
  const articleId = created.article_id;

  // 2. Set main keyword
  const kw = await writeMainKeyword({ articleId, mainKeyword });
  log("writeMainKeyword", kw);

  // 3. Keyword research
  const kwRes = await runKeywordResearch({ articleId });
  log("runKeywordResearch", kwRes);

  // 4. Topic benchmark
  const topicRes = await runTopicBenchmark({ articleId });
  log("runTopicBenchmark", topicRes);

  // 5. Verify assets via Supabase direct read
  const article = await readArticleDirect({ articleId, fields: "id,assets" });
  const assets = article.assets || {};
  if (!assets.main_keyword) throw new Error("Gate failed: main_keyword missing after research");
  log("gateCheck", { main_keyword: assets.main_keyword, keywords: assets.keywords?.length || 0, topics: assets.topics?.length || 0 });

  // 6. Generate draft (fire-and-forget)
  const gen = await writeDraftGenerate({ articleId });
  log("writeDraftGenerate", gen);

  // 7. Poll until completed
  const pollStart = Date.now();
  let completed = false;
  while (Date.now() - pollStart < pollTimeoutMs) {
    await sleep(pollIntervalMs);
    const status = await readDraftStatus({ articleId });
    log("readDraftStatus", status);
    if (status.status === "completed") { completed = true; break; }
    if (status.status === "failed") {
      return { article_id: articleId, stages, error: `draft generation failed: ${status.error || "unknown"}` };
    }
  }
  if (!completed) {
    return { article_id: articleId, stages, error: "draft poll timeout — reinitiate needed" };
  }

  // 8. Adopt draft
  const adopted = await writeDraftAdopt({ articleId });
  log("writeDraftAdopt", adopted);

  // 9. Verify content via Supabase
  const final = await readArticleDirect({ articleId, fields: "id,title,content_html,status" });
  const contentLength = final.content_html?.length || 0;
  log("verifyContent", { content_length: contentLength, status: final.status });

  return { article_id: articleId, stages, content_length: contentLength };
}

export async function publishToCjgeoai({ articleId } = {}) {
  if (!articleId) throw new Error("articleId required");
  const { baseUrl } = loadConfig();
  const article = await readArticleDirect({ articleId, fields: "id,title,content_html,status" });
  const len = article.content_html?.length || 0;
  if (len < 100) {
    return { published: false, url: null, error: "content_html too short or empty — draft not adopted?" };
  }
  return {
    published: true,
    url: `${baseUrl}/content-magic/${articleId}`,
    content_length: len,
    title: article.title,
  };
}

/**
 * bosterbio.com publishing adapter — fetch adopted content from CJGEO,
 * sanitize for Magento, and POST to the CMS mutation endpoint.
 * @param {object} opts
 * @param {string} opts.articleId - CJGEO article UUID (must have adopted content_html)
 * @param {string} opts.slug - Magento CMS identifier (e.g. "proving-grounds/secondary-antibody-wb")
 * @param {string} [opts.title] - Page title (defaults to article title)
 * @param {string} [opts.mainKeyword] - For meta tags
 */
export async function publishToBosterbio({ articleId, slug, title, mainKeyword } = {}) {
  if (!articleId || !slug) throw new Error("articleId and slug required");

  // 1. Read adopted content_html from CJGEO Supabase
  const article = await readArticleDirect({ articleId, fields: "id,title,content_html,assets" });
  const rawHtml = article.content_html || "";
  if (rawHtml.length < 100) {
    return { published: false, error: "content_html too short — draft not adopted?" };
  }
  const pageTitle = title || article.title;
  const keyword = mainKeyword || article.assets?.main_keyword || "";

  // 2. Sanitize: strip page chrome, preserve CJGEO design system
  let body = rawHtml;
  // Strip outer wrappers that Magento's theme provides
  body = body.replace(/<!DOCTYPE[^>]*>/gi, "");
  body = body.replace(/<html[^>]*>|<\/html>/gi, "");
  body = body.replace(/<head[\s\S]*?<\/head>/gi, "");
  body = body.replace(/<body[^>]*>|<\/body>/gi, "");
  body = body.replace(/<main[^>]*>|<\/main>/gi, "");
  body = body.replace(/<script[\s\S]*?<\/script>/gi, "");
  body = body.replace(/<header[\s\S]*?<\/header>/gi, "");
  body = body.replace(/<footer[\s\S]*?<\/footer>/gi, "");
  body = body.replace(/<nav[\s\S]*?<\/nav>/gi, "");
  body = body.replace(/<!--[\s\S]*?-->/g, "");
  // Decode HTML entities
  body = body.replace(/&mdash;/g, "\u2014");
  body = body.replace(/&nbsp;/g, "\u00A0");
  body = body.replace(/&hellip;/g, "\u2026");
  body = body.replace(/&rsquo;/g, "\u2019");
  // Keep <style data-draft-styles>, <h1>, and all CJGEO component classes intact
  body = body.trim();

  // 3. POST to Magento CMS mutation endpoint
  const magentoPayload = {
    handshake: "<REDACTED-SHARED-SECRET>",
    identifier: slug,
    title: pageTitle,
    content: body,
    content_heading: "",
    meta_title: pageTitle,
    meta_description: `${pageTitle} - Expert guide on ${keyword}`,
    meta_keywords: keyword,
    is_active: true,
    store_id: 1,
    page_layout: "1column",
  };

  const res = await fetch("https://www.bosterbio.com/rest/V1/bapi/cms-page", {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify(magentoPayload),
  });
  const resText = await res.text();
  let resJson;
  try { resJson = JSON.parse(resText); } catch { resJson = { raw: resText }; }

  if (!res.ok) {
    return { published: false, error: `Magento CMS POST failed: ${res.status} ${resJson?.message || resText.slice(0, 200)}` };
  }

  // Response shape: [page_id, identifier, is_create]
  const pageId = Array.isArray(resJson) ? resJson[0] : null;
  const isCreate = Array.isArray(resJson) ? resJson[2] : null;

  return {
    published: true,
    url: `https://www.bosterbio.com/${slug}`,
    page_id: pageId,
    is_create: isCreate,
    content_length: body.length,
  };
}

export function checkCredentials() {
  const key = process.env.CJGEO_API_KEY;
  const base = process.env.CJGEO_BASE_URL || "https://cjgeoai.com";
  let supabaseOk = false;
  try { loadCjgeoSupabaseKey(); supabaseOk = true; } catch { /* */ }
  return {
    configured: !!key,
    base_url: base,
    key_preview: key ? `${key.slice(0, 8)}...` : null,
    supabase_readable: supabaseOk,
  };
}
```

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * CLI: print the local Claude token-usage estimate (5h + 7d windows) vs the
 * configured ceilings/threshold. Reads CARAVAN_TOKENS_5H_CEILING,
 * CARAVAN_TOKENS_WEEK_CEILING, CARAVAN_USAGE_THRESHOLD_PCT from env.
 *
 * QUICK: plain `node` runs it in ~0.6s (no tsx startup) — this is the fast path:
 *   node libs/weapon/claudeUsage/cli.mjs            # full JSON
 *   node libs/weapon/claudeUsage/cli.mjs --brief    # one-line glance (~0.6s)
 *   node libs/weapon/claudeUsage/cli.mjs --ratelimit # authoritative status (~0.25s)
 * (`npx tsx …` also works but adds ~2.5s of runtime resolution; node reparses the
 * ESM-syntax .js with a harmless MODULE_TYPELESS warning on stderr.)
 * Dynamic import (not a static `import {}`) so the .mjs entry doesn't choke on the
 * .js module's interop during the instantiation phase.
 */
const m = await import("./index.js");
const mod = m.checkUsage ? m : m.default;
const args = process.argv.slice(2);

// `--windows [N]`: per-5h-window token breakdown (ad-hoc analysis).
if (args[0] === "--windows") {
  const count = Number(args[1]) || 6;
  const r = mod.usageWindows({ count });
  if (r.ok) {
    console.log(`Token usage by ${r.windowHours}h window (window 0 = most recent), ${r.files} files / ${r.lines} usage records:`);
    for (const w of r.windows) {
      console.log(`  win ${w.index} (${w.hoursAgoStart}h–${w.hoursAgoEnd}h ago): ${w.tokens.toLocaleString()} tokens`);
    }
  } else {
    console.log(JSON.stringify(r, null, 2));
  }
  process.exit(0);
}

// `--categorize [hoursBack]`: token spend by work type (develop/restart/work/analyze).
if (args[0] === "--categorize") {
  const hoursBack = Number(args[1]) || 30;
  const r = mod.categorizeUsage({ hoursBack });
  if (r.ok) {
    const LABEL = { develop: "1. Develop scripts/tools", restart: "2. Start/restart scripts", analyze: "3. Analyze & decide", work: "4. Actually do work" };
    console.log(`Token spend by work type — last ${r.hoursBack}h, ${r.files} files / ${r.turns} assistant turns:`);
    console.log(`(% by total tokens [consumed] | % by output tokens [active effort])`);
    for (const k of ["develop", "restart", "analyze", "work"]) {
      const c = r.categories[k];
      console.log(`  ${LABEL[k].padEnd(26)} ${String(c.pctTotal).padStart(5)}% | ${String(c.pctOut).padStart(5)}%   (${c.tokens.toLocaleString()} tok, ${c.turns} turns)`);
    }
  } else {
    console.log(JSON.stringify(r, null, 2));
  }
  process.exit(0);
}

// `--ratelimit`: print just the authoritative rate_limit_event reading.
if (args[0] === "--ratelimit") {
  console.log(JSON.stringify(mod.readRateLimit(), null, 2));
  process.exit(0);
}

// `--brief`: one-line human glance — 5h + weekly + hold verdict.
if (args[0] === "--brief") {
  const r = mod.checkUsage();
  const five = r.rateLimit?.fiveHour?.status
    ? `5h=${r.rateLimit.fiveHour.status}`
    : `5h~${r.fiveHour.pct}%`;
  const week = r.rateLimit?.sevenDay?.status
    ? `week=${r.rateLimit.sevenDay.status}${typeof r.rateLimit.sevenDay.utilization === "number" ? ` ${Math.round(r.rateLimit.sevenDay.utilization * 1000) / 10}%` : ""}`
    : `week~${r.week.pct}%`;
  console.log(`${r.over ? "HOLD" : "OK"}  ${five}  ${week}  (${r.signal})`);
  process.exit(r.over ? 1 : 0);
}

const r = mod.checkUsage();
console.log(JSON.stringify(r, null, 2));
process.exit(r.over ? 1 : 0);
```

```markdown
# Engineering Decisions — claudeUsage weapon

### 2026-07-01 · Weekly token % is anchored to the real reset boundary; ceiling re-calibrated to `/usage` (was ~9× low)

**Decision.** The weekly token telemetry now (a) counts billable tokens since the
CURRENT week's reset boundary — not a rolling 7d — and (b) divides by a 366M ceiling
calibrated to the operator's real `/usage` reading. `DEFAULT_WEEK_CEILING` 40M → 366M.

**Why.** The weekly limit resets on a FIXED weekly cadence (observed:
Mon 07:00 America/LA, epoch seed `1782741600`). A naive rolling-7d token sum spans
that boundary and keeps counting pre-reset tokens Anthropic already cleared, so it
read ~124% at a real ~11%. Two fixes: anchor the window to the most recent boundary
(`seed ± k·7d`, or a live seven_day `resetsAt` when one is in scan range — self-updating);
and fix the ceiling. The old 40M was mis-anchored on a PRE-reset event whose
`status:"rejected"` was `overageDisabledReason:"out_of_credits"` — an OVERAGE-CREDIT
exhaustion at the end of a prior budget cycle, NOT the base weekly cap — and it
undercounted that cycle. The trustworthy anchor is the live `/usage` page: 40.5M
billable since the 2026-06-29 reset read ~11% there → cap ≈ 366M billable.

**Scope / why safe.** The weekly % is TELEMETRY ONLY — the weekly window never gates
on the token sum (it gates on the authoritative seven_day event; see below). So this
only makes the reported number match reality; it changes no hold behaviour. Verified:
weekly now reads 11.1% (was 124%), windowStart = the Mon-07:00 boundary.

**Note on the authoritative weekly signal's blind spot.** Anthropic emits `seven_day`
events only at `surpassedThreshold: 0.75` (warning) or rejection — never a plain
"allowed" below 75%. So below 75% there is NO authoritative weekly %; the token
estimate is the only weekly number available, which is exactly why it must track
`/usage`. Absence of any seven_day warning since a reset authoritatively means weekly < 75%.

**Consequence if violated.** Reverting to a rolling-7d weekly sum re-introduces the
post-reset over-count; mis-calibrating the ceiling makes the reported weekly % diverge
from `/usage` again (re-tune the ceiling against `/usage`, don't anchor on an
overage-credit rejection).

### 2026-06-29 · The `rate_limit_event` IS the authoritative read; token sums are fallback-only (cache_read EXCLUDED)

**Decision.** Drive the caravan usage gate from Anthropic's OWN per-account
`rate_limit_event` — emitted on every turn by `claude --output-format stream-json`
(which every caravan leaf runs) and written natively to the leaf logs
(`.worker-logs/*.log`). Shape: `{"type":"rate_limit_event","rate_limit_info":{
status:"allowed"|"allowed_warning"|"rejected", resetsAt:<epoch-sec>,
rateLimitType:"five_hour"|"seven_day", utilization?:<0–1> }}`. `checkUsage` reads the
latest event per type (`readRateLimit`), and gates **per-window with the best signal**:
- **5h** — `five_hour` carries only a binary `status` (no `utilization`): `rejected`
  → HOLD. When no *valid* five_hour event exists, fall back to the token estimate.
- **7d** — `seven_day` carries `status` AND a real `utilization` fraction:
  `rejected` OR `utilization ≥ CARAVAN_WEEK_UTIL_HOLD_PCT/100` (default 0.90) → HOLD.
  The weekly window NEVER falls back to a token sum (see below).

**This SUPERSEDES the 2026-06-23 decision below** ("do NOT try to read the real
subscription %") — that decision was correct *given what was known then* (no
programmatic read existed), but the `rate_limit_event` in the stream-json output IS
that read. It was hiding in the leaf logs the whole time.

**Why the old token-sum gate broke (the bug this fixes).** `lineTokens` summed
`cache_read_input_tokens` at FULL weight against a guessed 100M ceiling. At heavy
continuous dispatch cache_read is ~95% of the raw total (the same large cached prompt
prefix re-read every turn across many parallel leaves), so a calm-real 5h of single
digits read as **73.7%, and the peak window as 140%** — wrongly HOLDing ALL dispatch
overnight (operator incident 2026-06-29). Measured: peak 5h ALL=139.9M vs
billable(excl cache_read)=6.4M — a ~22× inflation.

**Two non-obvious guards (a naive implementation gets these wrong):**
1. **Validity by `resetsAt`, not file mtime.** An event is the verdict for its window
   only while that window is OPEN (`resetsAt > now`). A re-surfaced event from an
   expired window — an old log re-read into a freshly-touched file, or echoed into a
   transcript by an agent investigating — carries a PAST `resetsAt`; honoring it by
   mtime alone would produce a stale hold. Filter on `resetsAt > now`.
2. **The 7d window never gates on a token sum.** A rolling-7d token sum spans weekly
   reset boundaries: right after a reset it keeps counting pre-reset tokens Anthropic
   no longer charges to the current week, reading false-high (observed 86% minutes
   after a real reset). So weekly HOLD comes ONLY from a fresh `seven_day` event;
   absent one, the weekly is left to the five_hour-reject exhaustion backstop. The 7d
   token number is reported as telemetry only.

**Fallback calibration (token estimate = `billableTokens` = input+output+cache_creation,
cache_read EXCLUDED).** `DEFAULT_5H_CEILING`=15M (peak observed billable 6.4M → ~43%,
consistent with the `five_hour`="allowed" seen at that peak). `DEFAULT_WEEK_CEILING`=40M
is REJECTION-ANCHORED: 7d billable hit ~34M over a window whose `seven_day` reached
utilization 0.98 then "rejected", so ~40M ≈ the real weekly cap. These are FALLBACK
ceilings only; the authoritative signal needs no ceiling.

**Verification.** Same machine that read 73.7%/over=true now reads 5h≈10% / over=false
(matches the real ~7% within margin) with `five_hour`="allowed"; crafted-fixture tests
confirm `rejected`→HOLD, `utilization 0.95`→HOLD, stale-event→ignored. Gate re-enabled
(`WORKER_PACING.claude.active=true` in `libs/caravan/index.js`).

**Consequence if violated.** Reverting to cache_read-inclusive sums, or gating the
weekly on a rolling token sum, reinstates the false-hold that halted all dispatch.
Trusting an event by mtime without the `resetsAt > now` check lets an expired-window
verdict (or an investigator's transcript echo) wrongly hold or release the gate.

---

### 2026-06-23 · Self-account local token usage; do NOT try to read the real subscription 5h/weekly % · SUPERSEDED 2026-06-29 (see above)

**Decision.** Estimate Claude usage by summing the per-message `usage` token counts
Claude Code already writes to the per-session transcripts under `~/.claude/projects`,
bucketed into rolling 5h and 7d windows, and compare to an operator-configured token
**ceiling** (env `CARAVAN_TOKENS_5H_CEILING` / `CARAVAN_TOKENS_WEEK_CEILING`). The
gate trips at `CARAVAN_USAGE_THRESHOLD_PCT` (default 70).

**Rejected alternatives.**
- *Read the true subscription limit %* via a `claude` subcommand, an HTTP API, or a
  local cache file — **none exist** (verified 2026-06-23). `/usage` is interactive-TUI
  only; the Rate-Limits/Usage APIs are API-KEY BILLING, a different thing from the
  Pro/Max **subscription** 5h+weekly caps; no local file stores the ceiling/reset.
- *Scrape the claude.ai / Claude Code usage webpage via CIC* — accurate but expensive
  (a browser round-trip every tick), and on Carbon there is no captured browser
  profile, so it is not even available there. Going this route would have forced the
  cron tick from 5 min → 20 min. Self-accounting is cheap, so the 5-min tick stays.

**Why it is a proxy, not the truth.** The ceiling is an operator-tuned stand-in for
the plan limit (the real number is account-side and drifts). Calibrate it from the
logged actuals (`node`/`tsx` `libs/weapon/claudeUsage/cli.mjs` prints the live
numbers). `cache_read_input_tokens` ARE included in the sum on purpose → it
over-counts vs billed tokens, i.e. the brake errs toward throttling EARLY (safe).

**Consequence if violated.** A future agent who "simplifies" this to call an Anthropic
usage/rate-limit API will read API-key billing numbers (wrong population) or get
nothing for a subscription account — silently disabling the brake. And anyone who
treats the ceiling as the real limit will mis-set the threshold; it must be calibrated
from observed usage, per-machine (limits are per-ACCOUNT, so each box gets a share).

**Fail-open.** A monitor error returns `over:false` (never halts all dispatch on a
read glitch); the claude-heavy cap still applies as the independent second brake.
```
