```js
/**
 * claudeUsage weapon — local, on-demand read of Claude Code SUBSCRIPTION usage in
 * the rolling 5-hour and 7-day windows, for PACING the caravan dispatch against the
 * Pro/Max rate limits.
 *
 * TWO SIGNALS, AUTHORITATIVE-FIRST (non-native — see engineering_decisions.md):
 *
 *   1. AUTHORITATIVE — `rate_limit_event` (primary gate). `claude --output-format
 *      stream-json` (which every caravan leaf runs) emits, on each turn, a
 *      `{"type":"rate_limit_event","rate_limit_info":{ status, resetsAt,
 *      rateLimitType, utilization? }}` line carrying Anthropic's OWN per-account
 *      verdict. `five_hour` gives a binary status ("allowed"|"rejected"); `seven_day`
 *      gives status PLUS a real `utilization` fraction (0–1). These land natively in
 *      the leaf stream-json logs (`.worker-logs/*.log`). This is the true limit — no
 *      ceiling guessing — so when present-and-fresh it drives the gate directly.
 *
 *   2. FALLBACK — token self-accounting (only when no fresh rate_limit_event exists,
 *      e.g. a box that hasn't dispatched a stream-json leaf recently). Sum the
 *      per-message `usage` BILLABLE tokens (input + output + cache_creation) Claude
 *      Code writes to `~/.claude/projects`, in rolling windows, vs a CALIBRATED
 *      ceiling. `cache_read_input_tokens` is EXCLUDED — at heavy continuous dispatch
 *      it is ~95% of the raw total (the same large cached prefix re-read every turn
 *      across many leaves), and including it made the old gate read ~140% of a 100M
 *      ceiling when the real subscription 5h was single digits → it wrongly HELD all
 *      dispatch. The fallback is still a proxy; the authoritative signal is the truth.
 *
 * This counts ALL Claude usage on the local machine (operator session + every leaf),
 * which is exactly the right signal for "how much of THIS account's Claude budget is
 * spent" (limits are per-ACCOUNT). With several machines on one account, the
 * authoritative rate_limit_event is account-wide and identical everywhere; only the
 * token fallback is per-machine.
 */

import { readdirSync, statSync, openSync, readSync, closeSync } from "fs";
import { join } from "path";
import { homedir } from "os";

export const toc = {
  checkUsage:
    "Read Claude SUBSCRIPTION usage for the rolling 5h + 7d windows — AUTHORITATIVE rate_limit_event status (from leaf stream-json logs) first, billable-token estimate as fallback; returns {over, fiveHour, week, rateLimit}. Used to pace caravan dispatch.",
  readRateLimit:
    "Read Anthropic's own per-account rate_limit_event (status/resetsAt/utilization for five_hour + seven_day) from the latest leaf stream-json logs — the authoritative subscription-limit signal, no token-ceiling guessing.",
  usageWindows:
    "Break local Claude token usage into the last N consecutive 5h windows (ad-hoc analysis: is pacing reducing consumption over time?).",
  categorizeUsage:
    "Classify local Claude token spend into develop / restart-scripts / analyze-decide / do-work buckets by per-turn tool-use heuristic (fuzzy: 'start a script' vs 'work' blur).",
};

const HOUR_MS = 3600 * 1000;
const DAY_MS = 24 * HOUR_MS;
const WEEK_MS = 7 * DAY_MS;
/** Observed weekly-reset boundary (epoch ms): Mon 2026-06-29 07:00 America/LA. The
 *  weekly cap resets on this fixed 7-day cadence, so ANY boundary = seed ± k·7d.
 *  Used to align the weekly token window to the current week when no live seven_day
 *  event is in scan range; a live event's resetsAt supersedes it. */
const WEEKLY_ANCHOR_SEED_MS = 1782741600 * 1000;

/** Env-driven ceilings — BILLABLE-token (cache_read-excluded) proxies for the plan
 *  limit, mapping the token sums to a %. Calibrated from logged actuals:
 *   - 5h = 15M: peak observed 5h billable 6.4M while `five_hour` stayed "allowed"
 *     → ~43% (consistent with allowed). Used as the gate FALLBACK when no valid
 *     five_hour event exists (else the authoritative status gates).
 *   - week = 366M: anchored to the operator's real `/usage` weekly reading
 *     (2026-07-01: 40.5M billable since the reset read ~11% there → 366M). The
 *     earlier 40M was mis-anchored on a pre-reset OVERAGE-credit exhaustion, not the
 *     base weekly cap, and read ~124% at a real ~11%. The weekly % is TELEMETRY only
 *     (the weekly window never gates on the token sum — it gates on the authoritative
 *     seven_day event), so this ceiling just makes the reported number track reality.
 *  Re-tune from `cli.mjs` against `/usage` if they drift. */
export const DEFAULT_5H_CEILING = Number(process.env.CARAVAN_TOKENS_5H_CEILING) || 15_000_000;
export const DEFAULT_WEEK_CEILING = Number(process.env.CARAVAN_TOKENS_WEEK_CEILING) || 366_000_000;
export const DEFAULT_THRESHOLD_PCT = Number(process.env.CARAVAN_USAGE_THRESHOLD_PCT) || 70;
/** seven_day `utilization` fraction at/above which the authoritative weekly signal
 *  HOLDs (real %, not a proxy). 0.90 leaves headroom for the operator's interactive
 *  session below the hard reject. Env-tunable. */
export const DEFAULT_WEEK_UTIL_HOLD = Number(process.env.CARAVAN_WEEK_UTIL_HOLD_PCT) / 100 || 0.9;
/** A rate_limit_event older than this is "stale" → fall back to the token estimate.
 *  6h > the 5h window, so a still-current 5h verdict is never treated as stale. */
const RATE_LIMIT_MAX_AGE_MS = Number(process.env.CARAVAN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_AGE_MS) || 6 * HOUR_MS;

/** BILLABLE tokens on one usage object — input + output + cache_creation. EXCLUDES
 *  cache_read_input_tokens on purpose (the dominant inflator: ~95% of the raw total
 *  at heavy load; see file header). This is the gate's fallback metric. */
function billableTokens(u) {
  if (!u || typeof u !== "object") return 0;
  return (
    (u.input_tokens || 0) +
    (u.output_tokens || 0) +
    (u.cache_creation_input_tokens || 0)
  );
}

/** TOTAL tokens incl. cache_read — the raw "consumed" figure. Used by the ad-hoc
 *  analysis fns (usageWindows / categorizeUsage), NOT the gate. */
function lineTokens(u) {
  if (!u || typeof u !== "object") return 0;
  return billableTokens(u) + (u.cache_read_input_tokens || 0);
}

/** Read the last `maxBytes` of a file as utf8 (transcripts can be large; the lines
 *  we care about are appended at the end, within the window). */
function readTail(path, maxBytes) {
  let fd;
  try {
    fd = openSync(path, "r");
    const size = statSync(path).size;
    const want = Math.min(maxBytes, size);
    const buf = Buffer.alloc(want);
    if (want > 0) readSync(fd, buf, 0, want, size - want);
    return buf.toString("utf8");
  } catch {
    return "";
  } finally {
    if (fd !== undefined) try { closeSync(fd); } catch { /* ignore */ }
  }
}

/** Pull every `rate_limit_event` object out of a chunk of text. Handles the NATIVE
 *  form (a top-level stream-json line in a leaf log) AND the ESCAPED form (a
 *  stream-json line captured inside a transcript string field, where `"` became
 *  `\"`). Returns the parsed `rate_limit_info` objects in file order. */
function extractRateLimitInfos(text) {
  const infos = [];
  if (!text || text.indexOf("rate_limit_event") < 0) return infos;
  // Match a brace-balanced JSON object starting at "type":"rate_limit_event",
  // in either the native or backslash-escaped quoting.
  const re = /\{\\?"type\\?":\\?"rate_limit_event\\?".*?\\?"rate_limit_info\\?":\s*(\{.*?\})/g;
  let m;
  while ((m = re.exec(text))) {
    let frag = m[1];
    // Un-escape the escaped form (\" → ", \\ → \) so JSON.parse accepts it.
    if (frag.indexOf('\\"') >= 0) frag = frag.replace(/\\"/g, '"').replace(/\\\\/g, "\\");
    try {
      const info = JSON.parse(frag);
      if (info && typeof info === "object") infos.push(info);
    } catch { /* skip a fragment we can't parse */ }
  }
  return infos;
}

/**
 * Read Anthropic's OWN per-account rate-limit verdict — the authoritative
 * subscription-limit signal — from the most recent leaf stream-json logs (and, as a
 * secondary source, the captured transcripts). Returns the latest event per
 * `rateLimitType`, chosen by (file mtime, then resetsAt) so the current window wins.
 *
 * @param {{ workerLogsDir?:string, projectsDir?:string, maxAgeMs?:number, maxFiles?:number, tailBytesPerFile?:number }} [opts]
 * @returns {{ ok:boolean, fiveHour:{status:string,resetsAt:number|null}|null, sevenDay:{status:string,utilization:number|null,resetsAt:number|null}|null, latestMs:number, ageMs:number|null, source:string, error?:string }}
 */
export function readRateLimit(opts = {}) {
  const workerLogsDir = opts.workerLogsDir || join(process.cwd(), ".worker-logs");
  const projectsDir = opts.projectsDir || join(homedir(), ".claude", "projects");
  const maxAgeMs = opts.maxAgeMs || RATE_LIMIT_MAX_AGE_MS;
  const maxFiles = opts.maxFiles || 40;
  const tailBytes = opts.tailBytesPerFile || 256 * 1024; // events sit near the file end
  const now = Date.now();
  const cutoff = now - maxAgeMs;

  // best[type] = { resetsAt, mtime, info } — most-recent by (mtime, resetsAt).
  const best = {};
  let latestMs = 0;
  let source = "none";

  /** Scan one flat dir of files, newest-mtime first, for rate_limit_event lines. */
  const scanDir = (dir, label, recurse) => {
    let entries;
    try { entries = readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }); } catch { return; }
    const files = [];
    for (const e of entries) {
      const fp = join(dir, e.name);
      if (e.isDirectory()) { if (recurse) scanDir(fp, label, false); continue; }
      let mtime;
      try { mtime = statSync(fp).mtimeMs; } catch { continue; }
      if (mtime < cutoff) continue;
      files.push({ fp, mtime });
    }
    files.sort((a, b) => b.mtime - a.mtime);
    for (const { fp, mtime } of files.slice(0, maxFiles)) {
      const infos = extractRateLimitInfos(readTail(fp, tailBytes));
      for (const info of infos) {
        const type = info.rateLimitType || "unknown";
        const resetsAt = Number(info.resetsAt) || 0;
        const cur = best[type];
        if (!cur || mtime > cur.mtime || (mtime === cur.mtime && resetsAt >= cur.resetsAt)) {
          best[type] = { resetsAt, mtime, info };
          if (mtime > latestMs) { latestMs = mtime; source = label; }
        }
      }
    }
  };

  // Worker-logs are the PRIMARY source (native stream-json lines, always fresh while
  // the caravan dispatches). Only fall through to the transcripts if they yield nothing.
  try {
    scanDir(workerLogsDir, "worker-logs", false);
    if (!Object.keys(best).length) scanDir(projectsDir, "transcripts", true);
  } catch (err) {
    return { ok: false, error: err?.message || String(err), fiveHour: null, sevenDay: null, latestMs: 0, ageMs: null, source: "none" };
  }

  const five = best.five_hour?.info || null;
  const seven = best.seven_day?.info || null;
  return {
    ok: true,
    fiveHour: five ? { status: five.status || "unknown", resetsAt: Number(five.resetsAt) || null } : null,
    sevenDay: seven
      ? { status: seven.status || "unknown", utilization: typeof seven.utilization === "number" ? seven.utilization : null, resetsAt: Number(seven.resetsAt) || null }
      : null,
    latestMs,
    ageMs: latestMs ? now - latestMs : null,
    source,
  };
}

/**
 * Read 5h + 7d subscription usage and decide whether the caravan should HOLD.
 *
 * AUTHORITATIVE-FIRST: when a fresh `rate_limit_event` is present (a leaf has run
 * stream-json within `RATE_LIMIT_MAX_AGE_MS`), Anthropic's OWN verdict drives the
 * gate — `five_hour`/`seven_day` "rejected" HOLDs, and `seven_day` utilization at/above
 * the hold fraction HOLDs (a real %, headroom below the hard reject). No ceiling
 * guessing. The BILLABLE-token estimate (cache_read-excluded) is computed alongside
 * for telemetry, and becomes the GATE only as a FALLBACK when no fresh event exists.
 *
 * @param {{ fiveHourCeiling?:number, weekCeiling?:number, thresholdPct?:number, weekUtilHold?:number, projectsDir?:string, workerLogsDir?:string, tailBytesPerFile?:number }} [opts]
 * @returns {{ ok:boolean, over:boolean, reason:string, signal:"rate_limit"|"token_fallback"|"error", rateLimit:object, fiveHour:{tokens:number,ceiling:number,pct:number}, week:{tokens:number,ceiling:number,pct:number}, error?:string }}
 */
export function checkUsage(opts = {}) {
  const fiveHourCeiling = opts.fiveHourCeiling || DEFAULT_5H_CEILING;
  const weekCeiling = opts.weekCeiling || DEFAULT_WEEK_CEILING;
  const thresholdPct = opts.thresholdPct || DEFAULT_THRESHOLD_PCT;
  const weekUtilHold = opts.weekUtilHold || DEFAULT_WEEK_UTIL_HOLD;
  // Read at most this many trailing bytes per file (a week of one session is well
  // under this; bounds the per-tick cost regardless of total transcript size).
  const tailBytes = opts.tailBytesPerFile || 8 * 1024 * 1024;
  const root = opts.projectsDir || join(homedir(), ".claude", "projects");

  const now = Date.now();
  const cut5 = now - 5 * HOUR_MS;
  let tok5 = 0, tok7 = 0;

  // ── AUTHORITATIVE signal — Anthropic's own rate_limit_event ────────────────
  // Read FIRST so its resetsAt can anchor the weekly token window (below).
  // VALIDITY by resetsAt, NOT just file mtime: an event is the verdict for its
  // window only while that window is still OPEN (resetsAt in the future). A
  // re-surfaced event from an expired window (e.g. an old log re-read into a fresh
  // file, or echoed into a transcript) carries a PAST resetsAt and is correctly
  // ignored — so it can never produce a stale hold.
  let rl;
  try { rl = readRateLimit({ workerLogsDir: opts.workerLogsDir, projectsDir: root }); }
  catch (e) { rl = { ok: false, error: e?.message || String(e), fiveHour: null, sevenDay: null, ageMs: null, source: "none" }; }
  const nowSec = now / 1000;

  // WEEKLY WINDOW START — anchor to Anthropic's real reset boundary, NOT a naive
  // rolling 7d. The weekly limit resets on a FIXED weekly cadence (observed:
  // Mon 07:00 America/LA); a seven_day event's `resetsAt` is one such boundary, so
  // the current window began at the most recent boundary ≤ now (anchor ± k·7d). This
  // makes the weekly token number reflect the CURRENT week (usage since the last
  // reset) instead of double-counting pre-reset tokens Anthropic already cleared.
  // Prefer a live seven_day resetsAt (self-updating); else the observed seed below.
  const weeklyResetMs = rl.sevenDay?.resetsAt ? rl.sevenDay.resetsAt * 1000 : WEEKLY_ANCHOR_SEED_MS;
  let weekStart = weeklyResetMs;
  while (weekStart + WEEK_MS <= now) weekStart += WEEK_MS; // forward to the boundary ≤ now
  while (weekStart > now) weekStart -= WEEK_MS;            // (or back, if the anchor is future)
  const tokFileCut = Math.min(cut5, weekStart);

  // ── billable-token estimate (telemetry always; gate only on fallback) ──────
  try {
    const dirs = readdirSync(root, { withFileTypes: true });
    for (const d of dirs) {
      if (!d.isDirectory()) continue;
      const sub = join(root, d.name);
      let files;
      try { files = readdirSync(sub); } catch { continue; }
      for (const name of files) {
        if (!name.endsWith(".jsonl")) continue;
        const fp = join(sub, name);
        let mtime;
        try { mtime = statSync(fp).mtimeMs; } catch { continue; }
        if (mtime < tokFileCut) continue; // nothing in either window
        const text = readTail(fp, tailBytes);
        let nl = text.indexOf("\n"); // skip a possibly-truncated first line
        const body = nl >= 0 ? text.slice(nl + 1) : text;
        for (const ln of body.split("\n")) {
          if (ln.indexOf('"usage"') < 0) continue;
          let o;
          try { o = JSON.parse(ln); } catch { continue; }
          const ts = Date.parse(o.timestamp || "");
          if (!ts) continue;
          const u = o.message && typeof o.message === "object" ? o.message.usage : o.usage;
          const t = billableTokens(u);
          if (!t) continue;
          if (ts >= weekStart) tok7 += t;
          if (ts >= cut5) tok5 += t;
        }
      }
    }
  } catch (err) {
    // Fail-OPEN: a broken monitor must not silently halt all dispatch (the
    // claude-heavy cap still applies). Surface the error so it is visible.
    return {
      ok: false,
      error: err?.message || String(err),
      signal: "error",
      rateLimit: { ok: false, fiveHour: null, sevenDay: null },
      fiveHour: { tokens: 0, ceiling: fiveHourCeiling, pct: 0 },
      week: { tokens: 0, ceiling: weekCeiling, pct: 0 },
      over: false,
      reason: `usage monitor error (fail-open): ${err?.message || err}`,
    };
  }

  const pct5 = fiveHourCeiling > 0 ? Math.round((tok5 / fiveHourCeiling) * 1000) / 10 : 0;
  const pct7 = weekCeiling > 0 ? Math.round((tok7 / weekCeiling) * 1000) / 10 : 0;
  const tokenBlock = {
    fiveHour: { tokens: tok5, ceiling: fiveHourCeiling, pct: pct5 },
    week: { tokens: tok7, ceiling: weekCeiling, pct: pct7, windowStart: new Date(weekStart).toISOString(), anchor: rl.sevenDay?.resetsAt ? "live" : "seed" },
  };

  const fiveValid = !!(rl.ok && rl.fiveHour && rl.fiveHour.resetsAt && rl.fiveHour.resetsAt > nowSec);
  const sevenValid = !!(rl.ok && rl.sevenDay && rl.sevenDay.resetsAt && rl.sevenDay.resetsAt > nowSec);

  // PER-WINDOW best signal:
  //   • 5h  — authoritative status when valid; else the calibrated token estimate
  //           (the 5h token sum is reliable: short window, cache_read-excluded).
  //   • 7d  — authoritative status/utilization ONLY. The 7d token sum is NEVER a
  //           hold trigger: a rolling-7d sum spans weekly reset boundaries (it keeps
  //           counting pre-reset tokens Anthropic no longer charges to the current
  //           week), so it false-reads high right after a reset. The weekly limit is
  //           caught authoritatively whenever a fresh seven_day event exists (active
  //           dispatch emits them), with the five_hour reject as the exhaustion backstop.
  const fiveSig = fiveValid ? `5h=${rl.fiveHour.status}` : `5h~token ${pct5}%`;
  const fiveOver = fiveValid ? rl.fiveHour.status === "rejected" : pct5 >= thresholdPct;

  const sevenUtil = sevenValid && typeof rl.sevenDay.utilization === "number" ? rl.sevenDay.utilization : null;
  const sevenOver = sevenValid && (rl.sevenDay.status === "rejected" || (sevenUtil != null && sevenUtil >= weekUtilHold));
  const weekSig = sevenValid
    ? `wk=${rl.sevenDay.status}${sevenUtil != null ? ` util ${Math.round(sevenUtil * 1000) / 10}%` : ""}`
    : `wk~unmetered (token est ${pct7}%)`;

  const over = fiveOver || sevenOver;
  const signal = fiveValid || sevenValid ? "rate_limit" : "token_fallback";
  const reason = `usage ${over ? "gate HOLD" : "OK"} (${signal}) — ${fiveSig}, ${weekSig}`;
  return { ok: true, over, signal, rateLimit: rl, ...tokenBlock, reason };
}

/**
 * Bucket local Claude token usage into `count` consecutive `windowHours` windows
 * back from now (window 0 = most recent). Ad-hoc analysis (NOT the per-tick gate) —
 * lets you see whether pacing is bending the consumption curve over time. Uses a
 * generous tail read per file to bound cost while covering the lookback.
 *
 * @param {{ windowHours?:number, count?:number, projectsDir?:string, tailBytesPerFile?:number }} [opts]
 * @returns {{ ok:boolean, windowHours:number, count:number, files:number, lines:number, windows:Array<{index:number, hoursAgoStart:number, hoursAgoEnd:number, tokens:number}>, error?:string }}
 */
export function usageWindows({ windowHours = 5, count = 6, projectsDir, tailBytesPerFile } = {}) {
  const root = projectsDir || join(homedir(), ".claude", "projects");
  const tailBytes = tailBytesPerFile || 32 * 1024 * 1024;
  const now = Date.now();
  const cutoff = now - count * windowHours * HOUR_MS;
  const buckets = new Array(count).fill(0);
  let files = 0, lines = 0;
  try {
    for (const d of readdirSync(root, { withFileTypes: true })) {
      if (!d.isDirectory()) continue;
      const sub = join(root, d.name);
      let names;
      try { names = readdirSync(sub); } catch { continue; }
      for (const name of names) {
        if (!name.endsWith(".jsonl")) continue;
        const fp = join(sub, name);
        let mtime;
        try { mtime = statSync(fp).mtimeMs; } catch { continue; }
        if (mtime < cutoff) continue;
        files++;
        const text = readTail(fp, tailBytes);
        const nl = text.indexOf("\n");
        const body = nl >= 0 ? text.slice(nl + 1) : text;
        for (const ln of body.split("\n")) {
          if (ln.indexOf('"usage"') < 0) continue;
          let o;
          try { o = JSON.parse(ln); } catch { continue; }
          const ts = Date.parse(o.timestamp || "");
          if (!ts || ts < cutoff || ts > now) continue;
          const u = o.message && typeof o.message === "object" ? o.message.usage : o.usage;
          const t = lineTokens(u);
          if (!t) continue;
          const idx = Math.floor((now - ts) / (windowHours * HOUR_MS));
          if (idx >= 0 && idx < count) { buckets[idx] += t; lines++; }
        }
      }
    }
  } catch (err) {
    return { ok: false, error: err?.message || String(err), windowHours, count, files, lines, windows: [] };
  }
  const windows = buckets.map((tokens, i) => ({
    index: i,
    hoursAgoStart: (i + 1) * windowHours,
    hoursAgoEnd: i * windowHours,
    tokens,
  }));
  return { ok: true, windowHours, count, files, lines, windows };
}

/** The 4 work categories (operator's taxonomy 2026-06-23). */
const CATS = ["develop", "restart", "work", "analyze"];
const CODE_RE = /\.(js|mjs|cjs|ts|tsx|py|sh|sql)$/i;
const RESTART_RE = /(schtasks|taskkill|npm run|\btsx\b|\bnode\b|start-process|stop-process|restart-|restart\b|pg_ctl|enable-scheduledtask|start-scheduledtask|\/run\b|\/end\b|\bstart\b)/i;
const MUTATE_RE = /(insert\s|update\s|delete\s|upsert|merge\s|-x\s*(post|patch|put|delete)|prefer:\s*return|\.from\([^)]*\)\.(insert|update|delete))/i;

/**
 * Classify ONE assistant turn into a work category by the tools it invoked.
 * Priority: code-write → develop; start/restart a script → restart; data mutation
 * or non-code file output → work; read/query/reason → analyze (the catch-all,
 * incl. tool-less "deciding" turns). The restart-vs-work split is inherently fuzzy
 * (both are exec calls; the real work is non-LLM), so treat those two as a blend.
 * @param {Array|string} content message.content
 * @returns {"develop"|"restart"|"work"|"analyze"}
 */
function classifyTurn(content) {
  const blocks = Array.isArray(content) ? content : [];
  let codeWrite = false, otherWrite = false, restart = false, mutate = false, readQuery = false;
  for (const b of blocks) {
    if (!b || b.type !== "tool_use") continue;
    const name = (b.name || "").toLowerCase();
    const inp = b.input || {};
    if (name.includes("write") || name.includes("edit") || name.includes("notebook")) {
      if (CODE_RE.test(String(inp.file_path || ""))) codeWrite = true;
      else otherWrite = true;
    } else if (name === "bash" || name.includes("powershell") || name.includes("exec") || name.includes("shell")) {
      const cmd = String(inp.command || "");
      if (MUTATE_RE.test(cmd)) mutate = true;
      else if (RESTART_RE.test(cmd)) restart = true;
      else readQuery = true; // select / get-content / findstr / ls / git status / cat …
    } else if (name.includes("read") || name.includes("grep") || name.includes("glob") || name.includes("search")) {
      readQuery = true;
    } else {
      readQuery = true; // TodoWrite, web fetch, misc → lump into analyze
    }
  }
  if (codeWrite) return "develop";
  if (restart) return "restart";
  if (mutate || otherWrite) return "work";
  return "analyze"; // reads/queries, or a tool-less reasoning/deciding turn
}

/**
 * Categorize local Claude token spend into develop / restart / work / analyze by
 * per-assistant-turn tool-use heuristic. Attributes each assistant message's usage
 * tokens to the category of the tools it called. % is reported BOTH by total tokens
 * (cache-read-inclusive — what's consumed) and by OUTPUT tokens (active generation,
 * less cache-dominated, a cleaner "effort" signal).
 *
 * @param {{ hoursBack?:number, projectsDir?:string, tailBytesPerFile?:number }} [opts]
 * @returns {{ ok:boolean, hoursBack:number, files:number, turns:number, totalTokens:number, totalOut:number, categories:Object, error?:string }}
 */
export function categorizeUsage({ hoursBack = 30, projectsDir, tailBytesPerFile } = {}) {
  const root = projectsDir || join(homedir(), ".claude", "projects");
  const tailBytes = tailBytesPerFile || 32 * 1024 * 1024;
  const now = Date.now();
  const cutoff = now - hoursBack * HOUR_MS;
  const acc = {}; for (const c of CATS) acc[c] = { tokens: 0, out: 0, turns: 0 };
  let files = 0, turns = 0;
  try {
    for (const d of readdirSync(root, { withFileTypes: true })) {
      if (!d.isDirectory()) continue;
      const sub = join(root, d.name);
      let names; try { names = readdirSync(sub); } catch { continue; }
      for (const name of names) {
        if (!name.endsWith(".jsonl")) continue;
        const fp = join(sub, name);
        let mtime; try { mtime = statSync(fp).mtimeMs; } catch { continue; }
        if (mtime < cutoff) continue;
        files++;
        const text = readTail(fp, tailBytes);
        const nl = text.indexOf("\n");
        const body = nl >= 0 ? text.slice(nl + 1) : text;
        for (const ln of body.split("\n")) {
          if (ln.indexOf('"usage"') < 0) continue;
          let o; try { o = JSON.parse(ln); } catch { continue; }
          const ts = Date.parse(o.timestamp || "");
          if (!ts || ts < cutoff || ts > now) continue;
          const msg = o.message;
          if (!msg || typeof msg !== "object" || msg.role !== "assistant") continue;
          const t = lineTokens(msg.usage);
          if (!t) continue;
          const cat = classifyTurn(msg.content);
          acc[cat].tokens += t;
          acc[cat].out += (msg.usage.output_tokens || 0);
          acc[cat].turns += 1;
          turns++;
        }
      }
    }
  } catch (err) {
    return { ok: false, error: err?.message || String(err), hoursBack, files, turns, categories: acc };
  }
  const totalTokens = CATS.reduce((s, c) => s + acc[c].tokens, 0) || 1;
  const totalOut = CATS.reduce((s, c) => s + acc[c].out, 0) || 1;
  const categories = {};
  for (const c of CATS) {
    categories[c] = {
      tokens: acc[c].tokens,
      pctTotal: Math.round((acc[c].tokens / totalTokens) * 1000) / 10,
      outTokens: acc[c].out,
      pctOut: Math.round((acc[c].out / totalOut) * 1000) / 10,
      turns: acc[c].turns,
    };
  }
  return { ok: true, hoursBack, files, turns, totalTokens, totalOut, categories };
}

export default { checkUsage, readRateLimit, usageWindows, categorizeUsage, toc };
```

```markdown
# Engineering decisions — `libs/weapon/claudecli`

Rationale layer (per CLAUDE.md §6). The WHY behind the leaf-invocation subprocess.
Append; supersede in place when a decision changes.

---

## 2026-06-13 — the full dispatch prompt is persisted into the worker log, delimited

**Decision.** In the streaming path (`logPath` set), `invoke()` writes the full
`taskPrompt` into the log immediately after the start marker, wrapped in
`# ===PROMPT_BEGIN===` / `# ===PROMPT_END===`. The quest-detail worker-log viewer
(`formatWorkerLog`) renders that block whole, untruncated.

**Rejected alternative.** Rely on `claude --print --output-format stream-json` to
echo the input prompt back (it does NOT), or just remove the UI's clip.

**Why.** stream-json does not echo the input prompt, and the prompt temp file is
deleted after the run — so without an explicit write there is **no record of what
the leaf was actually told**, which the operator needs to audit dispatches. A
delimited block is parser-safe (the JSON-per-line `formatWorkerLog` skips
non-JSON lines, so an undelimited multi-line prompt would be silently dropped).

**Consequence if violated.** Worker logs lose the prompt entirely (the symptom:
the operator could only see a 600-char clip of it, sourced inconsistently from
stream-json events that don't reliably contain it).

---

## 2026-06-13 — leaf invocations run `node --no-warnings` (don't flip package.json type)

**Decision.** Leaf-prompt invocations of `run-action.mjs` use `node --no-warnings`
to suppress `MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON`.

**Rejected alternative.** Add `"type":"module"` to `package.json`.

**Why.** This is a mixed CommonJS/ESM repo (Next app); flipping `package.json` to
`module` risks breaking `require`-based `.js` files. Suppressing the cosmetic
warning at the call site is the low-risk fix.

**Consequence if violated.** Either warning noise floods every worker
transcript/tool-result, or a global `type` flip breaks CJS modules.
```

```js
/**
 * claudeCLI weapon — invokes `claude --print --dangerously-skip-permissions` and returns
 * stdout. Uses exec() with a temp file for the prompt to avoid shell escaping issues
 * and environment quirks in the Next.js dev server.
 */

export const toc = {
  invoke: "Invoke Claude Code CLI as a subprocess with a prompt; returns stdout / raw output.",
};
import { exec, spawn } from "child_process";
import { writeFileSync, unlinkSync, mkdirSync, createWriteStream } from "fs";
import { join, dirname } from "path";
import { tmpdir } from "os";
import { randomUUID } from "crypto";

const TIMEOUT_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000; // 30 minutes — real Tier-2/quest-creation GM cascades exceed 5m

/**
 * Invoke `claude --print`. Two modes:
 *  - Default (no opts): buffered exec, returns final stdout. Used by GM cascades.
 *  - Streaming (opts.logPath set): spawn + tee stdout/stderr LIVE into a log file
 *    so a UI can tail a leaf worker's transcript. opts.streamJson adds
 *    `--verbose --output-format stream-json` for a per-event (tool-call) log.
 * @param {string} taskPrompt
 * @param {{ logPath?: string, streamJson?: boolean, mcpConfigPath?: string }} [opts]
 *   mcpConfigPath: path to an --mcp-config JSON (e.g. leafBrowser.prepareLeafBrowser's
 *   output) injecting extra MCP servers for THIS invocation only — used to hand a
 *   leaf an authenticated Playwright browser. Omitted ⇒ leaf inherits only the
 *   config-declared servers, exactly as before.
 * @returns {Promise<{ ok: boolean, html: string, rawOutput: string, error?: string }>}
 */
export async function invoke(taskPrompt, opts = {}) {
  // Support object-style input from run-action.mjs (fn(input) calling convention):
  //   claudeCLI invoke '{"taskPrompt":"...","mcpConfigPath":"..."}'
  if (taskPrompt && typeof taskPrompt === "object" && !Array.isArray(taskPrompt)) {
    opts = { ...opts, ...taskPrompt };
    taskPrompt = taskPrompt.taskPrompt;
  }
  if (!taskPrompt || typeof taskPrompt !== "string" || !taskPrompt.trim()) {
    return { ok: false, html: "", rawOutput: "", error: "taskPrompt is required" };
  }
  const { logPath = null, streamJson = false, mcpConfigPath = null } = opts || {};

  // Write prompt to a temp file so we don't have to shell-escape it
  const tmpFile = join(tmpdir(), `claudecli-${randomUUID()}.txt`);
  try {
    writeFileSync(tmpFile, taskPrompt.trim(), "utf8");
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, html: buildErrorHtml(`Failed to write temp file: ${e.message}`, ""), rawOutput: "", error: e.message };
  }

  // Use `type` (Windows) or `cat` (Unix) to pipe the prompt file into claude --print
  const cat = process.platform === "win32" ? "type" : "cat";
  const fmt = streamJson ? " --verbose --output-format stream-json" : "";
  // Per-invocation MCP injection (e.g. an authenticated Playwright browser for a
  // browser-tagged leaf). --dangerously-skip-permissions already auto-allows the
  // injected tools, so no --allowedTools allowlist is needed (and adding one would
  // wrongly RESTRICT the leaf to only those tools).
  const mcp = mcpConfigPath ? ` --mcp-config "${mcpConfigPath}"` : "";
  const cmd = `${cat} "${tmpFile}" | claude --print --dangerously-skip-permissions${fmt}${mcp}`;

  // Strip ANTHROPIC_API_KEY so claude CLI uses OAuth login (Max subscription) instead of API credits
  const env = { ...process.env };
  delete env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY;

  // ── Streaming path — tee a leaf worker's live transcript into logPath ──
  if (logPath) {
    try { mkdirSync(dirname(logPath), { recursive: true }); } catch { /* ignore */ }
    let ws;
    try { ws = createWriteStream(logPath, { flags: "w" }); } catch { ws = null; }
    if (ws) ws.write(`# worker log — started ${new Date().toISOString()}\n`);
    // Persist the FULL dispatch prompt at the top of the log. `claude --print
    // --output-format stream-json` does NOT echo the input prompt back, and the
    // prompt temp file is deleted after the run — so without this the operator
    // has no record of what the leaf was actually told. Delimited so the log
    // viewer (formatWorkerLog) can render it whole, untruncated.
    if (ws) ws.write(`# ===PROMPT_BEGIN===\n${taskPrompt.trim()}\n# ===PROMPT_END===\n`);
    return new Promise((resolve) => {
      let out = "";
      const child = spawn(cmd, { cwd: process.cwd(), env, shell: true, windowsHide: true });
      // Decode as UTF-8 at the stream level (not per-chunk) so multibyte chars
      // (em-dash, →, β, emoji) split across a pipe-buffer boundary aren't mangled
      // into U+FFFD �. Node's StringDecoder buffers partial sequences across chunks.
      child.stdout?.setEncoding("utf8");
      child.stderr?.setEncoding("utf8");
      const killer = setTimeout(() => { try { child.kill(); } catch { /* ignore */ } }, TIMEOUT_MS);
      child.stdout?.on("data", (d) => { const s = d.toString(); out += s; if (ws) ws.write(s); });
      child.stderr?.on("data", (d) => { const s = d.toString(); if (ws) ws.write(s); });
      child.on("error", (e) => {
        clearTimeout(killer);
        if (ws) { try { ws.end(`\n# spawn error: ${e.message}\n`); } catch { /* ignore */ } }
        try { unlinkSync(tmpFile); } catch { /* ignore */ }
        resolve({ ok: false, html: "", rawOutput: out, error: e.message });
      });
      child.on("close", (code) => {
        clearTimeout(killer);
        if (ws) { try { ws.end(`\n# worker log — exited code=${code} at ${new Date().toISOString()}\n`); } catch { /* ignore */ } }
        try { unlinkSync(tmpFile); } catch { /* ignore */ }
        resolve({ ok: code === 0, html: out.trim(), rawOutput: out });
      });
    });
  }

  // ── Default path — buffered exec with retry on transient failure ──
  // A non-zero `claude --print` exit under concurrency (many simultaneous leaf
  // judges) shows up as "Command failed" and was bouncing quests on a flake.
  // Retry transient (non-timeout) failures with linear backoff; the tmpFile is
  // kept until all attempts finish. A real 30-min timeout is NOT retried.
  const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3;
  const runOnce = () =>
    new Promise((res) => {
      exec(cmd, { cwd: process.cwd(), timeout: TIMEOUT_MS, maxBuffer: 10 * 1024 * 1024, env }, (err, stdout, stderr) => {
        res({ err, stdout: stdout || "", stderr: stderr || "" });
      });
    });

  let last;
  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= MAX_ATTEMPTS; attempt++) {
    last = await runOnce();
    if (process.env.NODE_ENV === "development" && last.stderr) {
      process.stderr.write(`[claudecli:stderr] ${last.stderr}`);
    }
    if (!last.err) {
      try { unlinkSync(tmpFile); } catch { /* ignore */ }
      return { ok: true, html: last.stdout.trim(), rawOutput: last.stdout };
    }
    const isTimeout = last.err.killed || last.err.code === "ETIMEDOUT";
    if (isTimeout) break; // a genuine 30-min timeout is not transient — don't retry
    if (attempt < MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
      console.warn(`[claudecli] attempt ${attempt}/${MAX_ATTEMPTS} failed (${last.err.message?.split("\n")[0]}); retrying after backoff`);
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1500 * attempt));
    }
  }
  try { unlinkSync(tmpFile); } catch { /* ignore */ }
  const isTimeout = last.err.killed || last.err.code === "ETIMEDOUT";
  const msg = isTimeout
    ? "Claude CLI timed out after 30 minutes."
    : `Claude CLI error after ${MAX_ATTEMPTS} attempts: ${last.err.message}`;
  return { ok: false, html: buildErrorHtml(msg, last.stdout), rawOutput: last.stdout, error: isTimeout ? "timeout" : last.err.message };
}

/** @param {string} msg @param {string} log */
function buildErrorHtml(msg, log) {
  const escaped = (s) => s.replace(/&/g, "&amp;").replace(/</g, "&lt;").replace(/>/g, "&gt;");
  return `<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>claudeCLI Error</title>
<style>body{font-family:monospace;padding:2rem;background:#1a1a1a;color:#f87171}
pre{white-space:pre-wrap;word-break:break-all;color:#d1d5db;background:#111;padding:1rem;border-radius:6px}</style>
</head><body><h2>claudeCLI Error</h2><p>${escaped(msg)}</p>${log ? `<pre>${escaped(log)}</pre>` : ""}</body></html>`;
}
```

<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: libs/weapon/cloudflare/index.js -->
```js
/**
 * Cloudflare weapon — unified read/search connector for Cloudflare zones.
 *
 * Auth: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN from profiles.env_vars or process.env.
 *
 * Hides always-on plumbing: pagination for DNS, GraphQL scalar nuances
 * (Date=YYYY-MM-DD vs Time=RFC3339), the 1-day window cap on adaptive
 * analytics datasets (Pro), and the sunset legacy REST `/analytics/dashboard`
 * endpoint (GraphQL-only on new zones).
 */

import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";
import { skillActionOk, skillActionErr } from "@/libs/skill_book/actionResult.js";

export const toc = {
  read: "Read a Cloudflare resource by name (zone, zones, dns, firewallRules, accessRules, pageRules, rateLimits, zoneSettings, rulesets, ruleset, botManagement, tokenCapabilities). Input: {resource, zoneName?|zoneId?, rulesetId?}. Resolves zone by name when only zoneName is given.",
  search: "Run a GraphQL analytics query. Datasets: requestsDaily (7d), cacheByHost (24h), cacheByPath (24h), cacheByContentType (24h), firewallEvents (24h — hard cap), bypassedPaths (24h). Input: {resource, zoneName?|zoneId?, limit?, windowHours?}.",
  normalize: "Interpret ambiguous Cloudflare semantics. Kinds: legacyFirewallAction (translates bypass/skip to actual behavior), httpResponse (classifies a fetched response as allow/challenge/block/origin-error using CSP+body tells).",
  audit: "Run a read-only audit of a zone (chains read+normalize): token capabilities → DNS (proxied cPanel-family + staging exposure) → legacy firewall rules (inverted-bypass detection) → page/rate policy → static-asset cache leakage. Returns a skillActionOk envelope { zoneName, findings, scopeMissing, recommendations }. Input: {zoneName} (+ optional userId as first arg).",
};

const API = "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4";
const GRAPHQL = "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/graphql";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Auth
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async function getToken(userId) {
  if (process.env.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN) return process.env.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN;
  const db = await database.init("service");
  if (userId) {
    const { data } = await db.from("profiles").select("env_vars").eq("id", userId).maybeSingle();
    const t = data?.env_vars?.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN;
    if (t) return t;
  }
  // Fallback: any profile carrying the token (convenience for inline CLI use).
  const { data } = await db.from("profiles").select("id,env_vars");
  for (const p of data || []) {
    const t = p.env_vars?.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN;
    if (t) return t;
  }
  return null;
}

async function cfFetch(path, opts = {}, userId) {
  const token = await getToken(userId);
  if (!token) throw new Error("Missing CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN");
  const url = path.startsWith("http") ? path : API + path;
  const res = await fetch(url, {
    ...opts,
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json", ...opts.headers },
  });
  const body = await res.text();
  let json;
  try { json = JSON.parse(body); } catch { json = { raw: body }; }
  return { status: res.status, ok: res.ok, json };
}

async function cfGraphQL(query, variables, userId) {
  const token = await getToken(userId);
  if (!token) throw new Error("Missing CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN");
  const res = await fetch(GRAPHQL, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({ query, variables }),
  });
  const json = await res.json();
  if (json.errors?.length) {
    throw new Error(`Cloudflare GraphQL error: ${JSON.stringify(json.errors).slice(0, 400)}`);
  }
  return json.data;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Zone resolution
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async function resolveZoneId({ zoneId, zoneName }, userId) {
  if (zoneId) return zoneId;
  if (!zoneName) throw new Error("resolveZone: provide zoneId or zoneName");
  const { json } = await cfFetch(`/zones?name=${encodeURIComponent(zoneName)}`, {}, userId);
  if (!json.success || !json.result?.[0]) {
    throw new Error(`Zone "${zoneName}" not found or token lacks access`);
  }
  return json.result[0].id;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// read
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * @param {{resource: string, zoneId?: string, zoneName?: string, rulesetId?: string}} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function read(input = {}, userId) {
  const { resource, rulesetId } = input;
  if (!resource) throw new Error("read: resource required");

  if (resource === "zones") {
    const { json } = await cfFetch("/zones?per_page=50", {}, userId);
    return { zones: json.result || [] };
  }

  if (resource === "tokenCapabilities") {
    return readTokenCapabilities(input, userId);
  }

  // All other resources need a zone.
  const zoneId = await resolveZoneId(input, userId);

  if (resource === "zone") {
    const { json } = await cfFetch(`/zones/${zoneId}`, {}, userId);
    return { zone: json.result || null };
  }

  if (resource === "dns") {
    const all = [];
    let page = 1;
    while (true) {
      const { json } = await cfFetch(`/zones/${zoneId}/dns_records?per_page=200&page=${page}`, {}, userId);
      if (!json.result?.length) break;
      all.push(...json.result);
      const total = json.result_info?.total_pages || 1;
      if (page >= total) break;
      page++;
    }
    return { records: all };
  }

  if (resource === "firewallRules") {
    const { json } = await cfFetch(`/zones/${zoneId}/firewall/rules?per_page=100`, {}, userId);
    return { rules: json.result || [] };
  }

  if (resource === "accessRules") {
    const { json } = await cfFetch(`/zones/${zoneId}/firewall/access_rules/rules?per_page=200`, {}, userId);
    return { rules: json.result || [] };
  }

  if (resource === "pageRules") {
    const { json } = await cfFetch(`/zones/${zoneId}/pagerules`, {}, userId);
    return { rules: json.result || [] };
  }

  if (resource === "rateLimits") {
    const { json } = await cfFetch(`/zones/${zoneId}/rate_limits`, {}, userId);
    return { rules: json.result || [] };
  }

  if (resource === "zoneSettings") {
    const { status, json } = await cfFetch(`/zones/${zoneId}/settings`, {}, userId);
    if (status === 403) throw new Error("Token lacks Zone Settings:Read");
    const flat = {};
    for (const s of json.result || []) flat[s.id] = { value: s.value, editable: s.editable, modified_on: s.modified_on };
    return { settings: flat };
  }

  if (resource === "rulesets") {
    const { status, json } = await cfFetch(`/zones/${zoneId}/rulesets`, {}, userId);
    if (status === 403) throw new Error("Token lacks Zone WAF:Read");
    return { rulesets: json.result || [] };
  }

  if (resource === "ruleset") {
    if (!rulesetId) throw new Error("read ruleset requires rulesetId");
    const { status, json } = await cfFetch(`/zones/${zoneId}/rulesets/${rulesetId}`, {}, userId);
    if (status === 403) throw new Error("Token lacks Zone WAF:Read");
    return { ruleset: json.result || null };
  }

  if (resource === "botManagement") {
    const { status, json } = await cfFetch(`/zones/${zoneId}/bot_management`, {}, userId);
    if (status === 403) throw new Error("Token lacks Account Bot Management:Read");
    return { botManagement: json.result || null };
  }

  throw new Error(`read: unknown resource "${resource}"`);
}

async function readTokenCapabilities({ zoneName, zoneId }, userId) {
  const token = await getToken(userId);
  if (!token) throw new Error("Missing CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN");
  // Verify token first
  const verifyRes = await fetch(API + "/user/tokens/verify", { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
  const verify = await verifyRes.json();
  if (!verify.success) return { valid: false, verify, capabilities: {} };

  let zid = zoneId;
  if (!zid && zoneName) {
    try { zid = await resolveZoneId({ zoneName }, userId); } catch { /* leave null */ }
  }
  const endpoints = zid ? [
    ["zone", `/zones/${zid}`],
    ["dns", `/zones/${zid}/dns_records?per_page=1`],
    ["firewallRules", `/zones/${zid}/firewall/rules?per_page=1`],
    ["accessRules", `/zones/${zid}/firewall/access_rules/rules?per_page=1`],
    ["pageRules", `/zones/${zid}/pagerules`],
    ["rateLimits", `/zones/${zid}/rate_limits`],
    ["zoneSettings", `/zones/${zid}/settings`],
    ["rulesets", `/zones/${zid}/rulesets`],
    ["botManagement", `/zones/${zid}/bot_management`],
  ] : [];
  const capabilities = {};
  for (const [name, p] of endpoints) {
    const r = await fetch(API + p, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
    capabilities[name] = { status: r.status, ok: r.ok };
  }
  return { valid: true, tokenId: verify.result?.id, zoneId: zid || null, capabilities };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// search (GraphQL analytics)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const fmtDate = (d) => d.toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/**
 * @param {{resource: string, zoneId?: string, zoneName?: string, limit?: number, windowHours?: number}} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function search(input = {}, userId) {
  const { resource, limit = 50, windowHours = 24 } = input;
  if (!resource) throw new Error("search: resource required");
  const zoneId = await resolveZoneId(input, userId);
  const now = new Date();
  const startWindow = new Date(now.getTime() - windowHours * 3600 * 1000);

  if (resource === "requestsDaily") {
    // 7-day daily rollup. Uses Date scalar (YYYY-MM-DD).
    const s = new Date(now.getTime() - 7 * 86400 * 1000);
    const q = `query($z:String!,$s:Date!,$e:Date!){viewer{zones(filter:{zoneTag:$z}){
      httpRequests1dGroups(limit:7,filter:{date_geq:$s,date_leq:$e},orderBy:[date_ASC]){
        dimensions{date}
        sum{requests cachedRequests bytes cachedBytes threats}
        uniq{uniques}
      }
    }}}`;
    const d = await cfGraphQL(q, { z: zoneId, s: fmtDate(s), e: fmtDate(now) }, userId);
    return { daily: d.viewer.zones[0]?.httpRequests1dGroups || [] };
  }

  if (resource === "cacheByHost") {
    const q = `query($z:String!,$d1:Time!,$d2:Time!,$n:Int!){viewer{zones(filter:{zoneTag:$z}){
      httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups(limit:$n,filter:{datetime_geq:$d1,datetime_leq:$d2},orderBy:[count_DESC]){
        count dimensions{cacheStatus clientRequestHTTPHost edgeResponseContentTypeName}
        sum{edgeResponseBytes}
      }
    }}}`;
    const d = await cfGraphQL(q, { z: zoneId, d1: startWindow.toISOString(), d2: now.toISOString(), n: limit }, userId);
    return { rows: d.viewer.zones[0]?.httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups || [] };
  }

  if (resource === "cacheByContentType") {
    const q = `query($z:String!,$d1:Time!,$d2:Time!,$n:Int!){viewer{zones(filter:{zoneTag:$z}){
      httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups(limit:$n,filter:{datetime_geq:$d1,datetime_leq:$d2},orderBy:[count_DESC]){
        count dimensions{cacheStatus edgeResponseContentTypeName}
        sum{edgeResponseBytes}
      }
    }}}`;
    const d = await cfGraphQL(q, { z: zoneId, d1: startWindow.toISOString(), d2: now.toISOString(), n: limit }, userId);
    return { rows: d.viewer.zones[0]?.httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups || [] };
  }

  if (resource === "cacheByPath" || resource === "bypassedPaths") {
    const cacheFilter = resource === "bypassedPaths" ? `,cacheStatus_in:["bypass","none","dynamic","miss"]` : "";
    const q = `query($z:String!,$d1:Time!,$d2:Time!,$n:Int!){viewer{zones(filter:{zoneTag:$z}){
      httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups(limit:$n,filter:{datetime_geq:$d1,datetime_leq:$d2${cacheFilter}},orderBy:[count_DESC]){
        count dimensions{cacheStatus edgeResponseContentTypeName clientRequestPath clientRequestHTTPHost}
        sum{edgeResponseBytes}
      }
    }}}`;
    const d = await cfGraphQL(q, { z: zoneId, d1: startWindow.toISOString(), d2: now.toISOString(), n: limit }, userId);
    return { rows: d.viewer.zones[0]?.httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups || [] };
  }

  if (resource === "firewallEvents") {
    // HARD CAP: adaptive firewall dataset rejects windows > 1 day on Pro.
    const clamp = Math.min(windowHours, 24);
    const d1 = new Date(now.getTime() - clamp * 3600 * 1000);
    const q = `query($z:String!,$d1:Time!,$d2:Time!,$n:Int!){viewer{zones(filter:{zoneTag:$z}){
      firewallEventsAdaptiveGroups(limit:$n,filter:{datetime_geq:$d1,datetime_leq:$d2},orderBy:[count_DESC]){
        count dimensions{action source ruleId clientRequestHTTPHost clientCountryName}
      }
    }}}`;
    const d = await cfGraphQL(q, { z: zoneId, d1: d1.toISOString(), d2: now.toISOString(), n: limit }, userId);
    return { events: d.viewer.zones[0]?.firewallEventsAdaptiveGroups || [], windowClampedToHours: clamp };
  }

  throw new Error(`search: unknown resource "${resource}"`);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// normalize (pure interpretation — no network)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * @param {{kind: string, data: unknown}} input
 */
export function normalize({ kind, data } = {}) {
  if (kind === "legacyFirewallAction") {
    // Legacy Firewall Rules action semantics differ from the plain-English names:
    // - "bypass": SKIP Cloudflare security features for matching requests (WAF, Bot Fight, Security Level, Rate Limiting by ID).
    //   NOT a block. A rule labeled "[Blacklist] … action=bypass" is inverted from intent.
    // - "skip": Skip specific downstream products (specified in `products`). Same family as bypass but scoped.
    // - "allow": Allow matching requests through all security products (same end state as bypass for matching traffic, but semantically different in audit trail).
    // - "challenge" / "managed_challenge" / "js_challenge": Interactive challenge.
    // - "block": Drop the request.
    // - "log": Log only, no enforcement.
    const a = String(data || "").toLowerCase();
    const meaning = {
      bypass: "SKIP all WAF/Bot/Security-Level checks for matching traffic (whitelist). NOT a block.",
      skip: "Skip the downstream products specified in the rule (see `products`). Whitelist-ish.",
      allow: "Allow through; bypasses Managed Challenges. Whitelist.",
      challenge: "Interactive CAPTCHA challenge.",
      managed_challenge: "Cloudflare Managed Challenge (JS + non-interactive for humans, fails bots).",
      js_challenge: "JS challenge (deprecated for Managed).",
      block: "Drop the request. Enforcement.",
      log: "Log only. No enforcement.",
    };
    return { action: a, meaning: meaning[a] || `Unknown action "${a}"` };
  }

  if (kind === "httpResponse") {
    // Classify a response object: { status, headers, body }.
    const r = /** @type {{status: number, headers: Record<string,string>, body?: string}} */ (data || {});
    const status = r.status;
    const headers = r.headers || {};
    const body = r.body || "";
    const csp = (headers["content-security-policy"] || headers["Content-Security-Policy"] || "").toLowerCase();
    const server = (headers.server || headers.Server || "").toLowerCase();
    const cfCache = headers["cf-cache-status"] || headers["CF-Cache-Status"] || null;
    const cfMitigated = headers["cf-mitigated"] || headers["CF-Mitigated"] || null;

    // Managed Challenge tell: 403 + CSP referencing challenges.cloudflare.com.
    if (status === 403 && csp.includes("challenges.cloudflare.com")) {
      return { classification: "challenge", reason: "Managed Challenge page (CSP references challenges.cloudflare.com)", cfCache, cfMitigated };
    }
    // cf-mitigated header is the authoritative signal when present.
    if (cfMitigated) {
      return { classification: cfMitigated === "challenge" ? "challenge" : "block", reason: `cf-mitigated=${cfMitigated}`, cfCache, cfMitigated };
    }
    // Cloudflare 1xxx error pages are edge-origin errors, not blocks.
    if (status >= 500 && /cloudflare/.test(body) && /Error code \d{3,4}/i.test(body)) {
      return { classification: "origin-error", reason: "Cloudflare error page (origin unreachable)", cfCache, cfMitigated };
    }
    if (status === 403 && server === "cloudflare") {
      return { classification: "block", reason: "HTTP 403 from Cloudflare edge (likely WAF or firewall block)", cfCache, cfMitigated };
    }
    if (status >= 200 && status < 400) {
      return { classification: "allow", reason: `HTTP ${status}`, cfCache, cfMitigated };
    }
    return { classification: "other", reason: `HTTP ${status}`, cfCache, cfMitigated };
  }

  throw new Error(`normalize: unknown kind "${kind}"`);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// audit — read-only zone audit (orchestrates read + normalize)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function pickInput(a, b) {
  if (b !== undefined && typeof b === "object" && b !== null && !Array.isArray(b)) return b;
  if (a !== undefined && typeof a === "object" && a !== null && !Array.isArray(a)) return a;
  return {};
}

/**
 * Read-only audit of a Cloudflare zone. Agent-facing entry point: chains
 * read() + normalize() into a compiled finding set. Pure reads — no mutation.
 *
 * Calling conventions (both supported, mirroring the adventurer-runtime shape):
 *   audit({ zoneName })            // input as first arg
 *   audit(userId, { zoneName })    // userId as first arg, input as second
 *
 * @param {unknown} [a] userId or input
 * @param {unknown} [b] input when a is userId
 * @returns {Promise<import("@/libs/skill_book/actionResult.js").SkillActionResult>}
 */
export async function audit(a, b) {
  const input = pickInput(a, b);
  const userId = typeof a === "string" ? a : undefined;
  const zoneName = String(input.zoneName ?? "bosterbio.com").trim();

  try {
    const caps = await read({ resource: "tokenCapabilities", zoneName }, userId);
    const scopeMissing = Object.entries(caps.capabilities || {})
      .filter(([, v]) => !v.ok)
      .map(([k]) => k);

    const findings = [];
    const recommendations = [];

    // DNS: cPanel-family proxied, staging exposure
    const { records } = await read({ resource: "dns", zoneName }, userId);
    const adminProxied = records.filter(
      (r) => r.proxied && /^(cpanel|webmail|whm|webdisk|cpcalendars|cpcontacts)\./i.test(r.name || ""),
    );
    if (adminProxied.length) {
      findings.push({
        severity: "critical",
        id: "admin-proxied",
        detail: `${adminProxied.length} cPanel-family records are orange-clouded (proxied). Proxying breaks AutoSSL and risks WAF-rate-limiting admin logins.`,
        records: adminProxied.map((r) => r.name),
      });
      recommendations.push({ id: "unproxy-admin", impact: "hygiene-must-do", effort: "10 min" });
    }

    const stagingHosts = records.filter((r) =>
      /^(dev|stage|staging|jr-staging)\./i.test(r.name || "") || /\.(staging|mobile)\./i.test(r.name || ""),
    );
    if (stagingHosts.length) {
      findings.push({
        severity: "critical",
        id: "staging-exposed",
        detail: `${stagingHosts.length} staging/dev hostnames exist in DNS and may be publicly accessible.`,
        records: stagingHosts.map((r) => r.name),
      });
    }

    // Legacy firewall rules semantic analysis (inverted-bypass detection)
    const { rules: fwRules } = await read({ resource: "firewallRules", zoneName }, userId);
    for (const rule of fwRules) {
      const n = normalize({ kind: "legacyFirewallAction", data: rule.action });
      const desc = rule.description || "";
      const claimsBlock = /\b(blacklist|ban|block)\b/i.test(desc);
      if (claimsBlock && (n.action === "bypass" || n.action === "skip" || n.action === "allow")) {
        findings.push({
          severity: "critical",
          id: "inverted-firewall-rule",
          detail: `Rule "${desc}" is labeled as blacklist but action="${rule.action}" which means ${n.meaning}`,
          ruleId: rule.id,
        });
      }
    }

    // Page rules / rate limits / cache policy
    const [{ rules: pageRules }, { rules: rateLimits }] = await Promise.all([
      read({ resource: "pageRules", zoneName }, userId),
      read({ resource: "rateLimits", zoneName }, userId),
    ]);
    if (pageRules.length === 0 && rateLimits.length === 0) {
      findings.push({
        severity: "material",
        id: "no-cache-or-rate-policy",
        detail: "Zero Page Rules, zero legacy Rate Limits. All cache/rate policy relies on origin headers + Custom Rules.",
      });
    }

    // Cache analytics — find worst cache=bypass content types
    try {
      const { rows: ctRows } = await search({ resource: "cacheByContentType", zoneName, limit: 50, windowHours: 24 }, userId);
      const byType = {};
      for (const row of ctRows) {
        const ct = row.dimensions.edgeResponseContentTypeName || "unknown";
        byType[ct] = byType[ct] || { hit: 0, bypass: 0, miss: 0, none: 0, dynamic: 0, totalBytes: 0 };
        const bucket = row.dimensions.cacheStatus;
        if (byType[ct][bucket] !== undefined) byType[ct][bucket] += row.count;
        byType[ct].totalBytes += row.sum?.edgeResponseBytes || 0;
      }
      const leaky = Object.entries(byType)
        .filter(([ct, v]) => ["css", "js", "pdf", "svg", "bin", "woff", "woff2", "ttf"].includes(ct) && v.bypass + v.none > v.hit)
        .map(([ct, v]) => ({ contentType: ct, ...v }));
      if (leaky.length) {
        findings.push({
          severity: "critical",
          id: "static-cache-bypass",
          detail: `Static asset content types where bypass+none exceeds hit — origin is serving cacheable assets`,
          contentTypes: leaky,
        });
        recommendations.push({ id: "static-cache-rule", impact: "cuts ~30+ GB/day off origin", effort: "20 min" });
      }
    } catch (e) {
      findings.push({ severity: "minor", id: "cache-analytics-failed", detail: String(e.message || e) });
    }

    return skillActionOk({ zoneName, findings, scopeMissing, recommendations });
  } catch (e) {
    return skillActionErr(e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e));
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Credential health — used by the WEAPONS registry.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export async function checkCredentials(userId) {
  try {
    const token = await getToken(userId);
    if (!token) return { ok: false, msg: "No CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN in env or profiles" };
    const r = await fetch(API + "/user/tokens/verify", { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
    const j = await r.json();
    if (!j.success) return { ok: false, msg: `Token invalid: ${JSON.stringify(j.errors).slice(0, 120)}` };
    return { ok: true, msg: `Token ${j.result?.id?.slice(0, 8)}… active` };
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, msg: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e) };
  }
}
```

```js
/**
 * codexCLI weapon — invokes the local OpenAI Codex CLI (`codex exec`) as a
 * subprocess. Mirrors the `claudecli` / `cursorcli` invoke contract so caravan
 * dispatch can route by `adventurers.worker_type`.
 */

export const toc = {
  invoke: "Invoke OpenAI Codex CLI (`codex exec`) as a subprocess with a prompt; returns stdout / raw output.",
};

import { exec, spawn } from "child_process";
import { writeFileSync, unlinkSync, mkdirSync, createWriteStream } from "fs";
import { join, dirname } from "path";
import { tmpdir } from "os";
import { randomUUID } from "crypto";

const TIMEOUT_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;
const CODEX_BIN = process.env.CODEX_CLI_BIN || "npx -y @openai/codex";

function q(s) {
  return `"${String(s).replace(/"/g, '\\"')}"`;
}

function command(tmpFile, { streamJson = false, cwd = process.cwd(), model = process.env.CODEX_MODEL } = {}) {
  const cat = process.platform === "win32" ? "type" : "cat";
  const json = streamJson ? " --json" : "";
  const modelArg = model ? ` --model ${q(model)}` : "";
  return `${cat} ${q(tmpFile)} | ${CODEX_BIN} exec${json}${modelArg} --cd ${q(cwd)} --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust -`;
}

/**
 * @param {string} taskPrompt
 * @param {{ logPath?: string, streamJson?: boolean, cwd?: string, model?: string }} [opts]
 * @returns {Promise<{ ok: boolean, output: string, rawOutput: string, error?: string }>}
 */
export async function invoke(taskPrompt, opts = {}) {
  if (!taskPrompt || typeof taskPrompt !== "string" || !taskPrompt.trim()) {
    return { ok: false, output: "", rawOutput: "", error: "taskPrompt is required" };
  }
  const { logPath = null, streamJson = false, cwd = process.cwd(), model = process.env.CODEX_MODEL } = opts || {};
  const codexPrompt = [
    "CODEX WORKER NOTE: This leaf is running under Codex CLI on Windows PowerShell.",
    "For GuildOS run-action JSON payloads, prefer --input-file with a BOM-free UTF-8 file, or use PowerShell single-quoted JSON carefully.",
    "Do not use Claude-specific shell quoting examples such as --% unless you have verified they work in this shell.",
    "",
    taskPrompt.trim(),
  ].join("\n");
  const tmpFile = join(tmpdir(), `codexcli-${randomUUID()}.txt`);
  try {
    writeFileSync(tmpFile, codexPrompt, "utf8");
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, output: "", rawOutput: "", error: `Failed to write temp file: ${e.message}` };
  }

  const cmd = command(tmpFile, { streamJson, cwd, model });
  const env = { ...process.env };

  if (logPath) {
    try { mkdirSync(dirname(logPath), { recursive: true }); } catch { /* ignore */ }
    let ws;
    try { ws = createWriteStream(logPath, { flags: "w" }); } catch { ws = null; }
    if (ws) {
      ws.write(`# codex worker log - started ${new Date().toISOString()}${model ? ` (model=${model})` : ""}\n`);
      ws.write(`# ===PROMPT_BEGIN===\n${codexPrompt}\n# ===PROMPT_END===\n`);
    }
    return new Promise((resolve) => {
      let out = "";
      const child = spawn(cmd, { cwd, env, shell: true, windowsHide: true });
      // UTF-8 decode at the stream level so multibyte chars split across a pipe
      // boundary aren't mangled into U+FFFD � (see claudecli for the full rationale).
      child.stdout?.setEncoding("utf8");
      child.stderr?.setEncoding("utf8");
      const killer = setTimeout(() => { try { child.kill(); } catch { /* ignore */ } }, TIMEOUT_MS);
      child.stdout?.on("data", (d) => { const s = d.toString(); out += s; if (ws) ws.write(s); });
      child.stderr?.on("data", (d) => { const s = d.toString(); if (ws) ws.write(s); });
      child.on("error", (e) => {
        clearTimeout(killer);
        if (ws) { try { ws.end(`\n# spawn error: ${e.message}\n`); } catch { /* ignore */ } }
        try { unlinkSync(tmpFile); } catch { /* ignore */ }
        resolve({ ok: false, output: out.trim(), rawOutput: out, error: e.message });
      });
      child.on("close", (code) => {
        clearTimeout(killer);
        if (ws) { try { ws.end(`\n# codex worker log - exited code=${code} at ${new Date().toISOString()}\n`); } catch { /* ignore */ } }
        try { unlinkSync(tmpFile); } catch { /* ignore */ }
        resolve({ ok: code === 0, output: out.trim(), rawOutput: out, ...(code === 0 ? {} : { error: `Codex CLI exited with code ${code}` }) });
      });
    });
  }

  const result = await new Promise((resolve) => {
    exec(cmd, { cwd, timeout: TIMEOUT_MS, maxBuffer: 10 * 1024 * 1024, env }, (err, stdout, stderr) => {
      resolve({ err, stdout: stdout || "", stderr: stderr || "" });
    });
  });
  try { unlinkSync(tmpFile); } catch { /* ignore */ }
  if (!result.err) return { ok: true, output: result.stdout.trim(), rawOutput: result.stdout };
  return {
    ok: false,
    output: result.stdout.trim(),
    rawOutput: result.stdout,
    error: result.err.killed || result.err.code === "ETIMEDOUT" ? "timeout" : `${result.err.message}\n${result.stderr}`.trim(),
  };
}
```

```markdown
# Engineering decisions — `libs/weapon/cursor`

Rationale layer (per CLAUDE.md §6). The WHY behind Cursor dispatch + model policy.
Append; supersede in place when a decision changes.

---

## 2026-06-24 — Cursor is a CHEAP worker (Composer only); NEVER a bridge for Claude. Pin the model, never omit it. (operator directive, LOCKED)

**The decision.** We hold a **Claude 20X Max** subscription. Therefore:
- ALL Claude work runs on that flat-rate subscription via `claudecli` (OAuth login,
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` stripped so it uses the Max plan, NOT API credits).
- Cursor is used ONLY as a **cheap worker on its own in-house Composer model**
  (`composer-2.5`). It is a *cheaper-than-Claude* second engine, valued for Composer.
- We **NEVER route a premium frontier model (claude-\*, gpt-\*, gemini-\*, grok-\*)
  THROUGH Cursor.** Doing so ("using Cursor as a bridge for Claude") both (a) bills
  Cursor's metered API-model pool — Pro's "$200 API model usage" — and (b) double-pays
  for Claude we already hold flat-rate. It is the worst of both billing worlds.

**The incident this fixes (2026-06-24).** A process burned **$200** of Cursor's
metered API-model allowance in one cycle by running premium models through Cursor.
Root cause = every cloud-agent creation path **OMITTED the `model` field**, and the
prior LOCKED guidance (`cursorCJGEO` skill book, "OMIT the model; Cursor picks its
current default") actively *taught* that omission. Cursor's configured default for
background agents is a **premium frontier model** (the recommended set from
`GET /v0/models` is `composer-2.5` + `claude-opus-4-8-*`, `gpt-5.5-*`, `gpt-5.3-codex-*`
— only `composer-2.5` is cheap). So every omitted-model dispatch silently ran premium.
The `nudgeCICPolice` cron heartbeat (`writeFollowup` every ~10 min, which makes the
agent RUN on its creation model) kept a premium agent burning around the clock.

**The fix (structural — make the violation impossible, not merely discouraged).**
1. `libs/weapon/cursor/model.js` — single source of truth: `CURSOR_CHEAP_MODEL`
   (`composer-2.5`) + `resolveCheapCursorModel(id)` which returns the cheap default
   when none is given and **THROWS on any non-`composer-*` id** (including `auto`,
   which can route premium) unless `CURSOR_ALLOW_PREMIUM=1` (the audited operator
   escape hatch).
2. Every creation surface now PINS the model via that guard, shape
   `model: { id: "composer-2.5" }` (a `ModelRef` OBJECT per the cloud-agents OpenAPI —
   NOT a top-level string): `cursor.writeAgent`, the local proxy
   `app/api/cloud_agents/route.js` `cursor_setup`, and the `cursorcli` weapon
   (local CLI `--model`).
3. The `cursorCJGEO` "OMIT model" LOCKED note is **superseded** in place — it was the
   discovery-layer substrate that propagated the bug.

**Why pin at CREATION specifically.** A Cursor agent's model is fixed when the agent
is created (`POST /v0/agents`); `followup` calls inherit it and take no model field. So
pinning `writeAgent`/`cursor_setup` is the load-bearing fix — it makes every NEW agent
(and every cron auto-respawn, which goes through `writeAgent`) cheap. Existing agents
created BEFORE this fix keep their premium model until they expire and are recreated.

**Rejected alternatives.**
- *Omit the model and trust Cursor's default* (the prior rule) — that default is
  premium; the omission was the bug.
- *Pass `model` as a top-level string* (the original `composer-2.0` that 400'd) — wrong
  shape AND stale id. The 400 was a shape/staleness bug, never a reason to omit; the
  correct shape is the `{ id }` ModelRef.
- *A doc note saying "use cheap models"* — discouragement is not enforcement; a future
  dispatch would omit the model again. The `resolveCheapCursorModel` throw is the wall.
- *`--model auto` for the CLI* (cursorcli's first default) — `auto` can route to a
  premium frontier model, so it violates "cheap only." Blocked by the guard.

**Consequence if violated.** Re-introduce an omitted/`auto`/premium model on any Cursor
dispatch and the metered API pool burns again (the exact $200 incident), while we keep
paying flat-rate for the same Claude capacity on Max — paying twice to go slower-and-
more-expensive than just using `claudecli`.

**Open follow-ups (NOT a code gap — operational).**
- *Existing premium cloud-agent sessions* (the 8 `cursor_cloud` adventurers created
  pre-fix) still carry a premium creation-model. They are currently halted by the
  account's exhausted budget. They auto-heal to `composer-2.5` when recreated (creation
  is now pinned), but until then the CIC-Police heartbeat would resume premium runs once
  budget returns. Retire/recreate them cheap after the budget resets (or set a spend
  limit) — surfaced to the operator rather than nulling live session handles autonomously.
- *Live re-verify the cloud `model:{id}` shape* once budget allows a real
  `POST /v0/agents` (the shape is OpenAPI-confirmed but could not be live-tested while
  the account was out of usage).
- *Account identity*: the headless `CURSOR_API_KEY` (key name "GuildOS") resolves to
  `<REDACTED-EMAIL>` via `GET /v0/me` — the user's own account, confirmed not a
  wrong-account artifact.
```
