<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: libs/weapon/cursor/index.js -->
```js
/**
 * Cursor weapon — Cursor Cloud Agent dispatch and management via Cursor API.
 *
 * Auth: CURSOR_API_KEY from profiles.env_vars or process.env.
 * Endpoint: https://api.cursor.com/v0/agents
 * Model: PINNED to Cursor's cheap Composer model via resolveCheapCursorModel
 *   (model.js). NEVER omit it — omitting makes Cursor pick its PREMIUM frontier
 *   default (a premium claude or gpt model), which bills the metered API pool and
 *   double-pays for Claude we already hold flat-rate on Claude Max. Burned $200 in one
 *   cycle (2026-06-24). The correct body shape is `model: { id: "composer-2.5" }`
 *   (ModelRef per the cloud-agents OpenAPI), NOT a top-level string (the stale
 *   `composer-2.0` string was the old HTTP-400; that note is now superseded).
 */

export const toc = {
  readAgent: "Read a Cursor cloud agent's status and metadata.",
  readConversation: "Read a Cursor agent's full conversation history.",
  writeFollowup: "Send a followup message to a Cursor agent (push-based dispatch).",
  searchAgents: "Search Cursor agents (wraps readAgent; API has no list endpoint).",
  readQueuedMessages: "Read queued user messages sent after the last assistant reply.",
  writeAgent: "Create a new Cursor cloud agent for a given repository.",
  readEnvSetupInstructions: "Generate an env setup script to bootstrap a fresh Cursor agent session.",
  syncSessionStatus: "Probe an adventurer's upstream Cursor session status and reconcile the adventurers DB row. Returns { upstream_status, alive, dispatch_safe, was_drift }.",
  // --- Agent-facing actions (skillActionOk/Err envelope; (userId, input) signature) ---
  dispatchTask: "Agent-facing: send a task to a Cursor cloud agent via followup. Input { agentId, instructions }. A followup runs the agent on its CREATION model (pinned cheap by writeAgent/cursor_setup) — the model input is inert; choose the model at creation, not here.",
  readStatus: "Agent-facing: check a Cursor cloud agent's status. Input { agentId }.",
  readConversationAction: "Agent-facing: read a Cursor agent's full conversation. Input { agentId }.",
  dispatchPptGeneration: "Agent-facing: dispatch a PowerPoint-generation task to a Cursor cloud agent. Input { agentId, topic, slides?, questId? }.",
};
import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";
import { guildosCredentialsSetupBlock } from "./setupBlock.js";
import { resolveCheapCursorModel } from "./model.js";
import { skillActionOk, skillActionErr } from "@/libs/skill_book/actionResult.js";
import { getAdventurerExecutionContext } from "@/libs/adventurer/advance.js";

const API_BASE = "https://api.cursor.com/v0/agents";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Auth
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async function getApiKey(userId) {
  if (process.env.CURSOR_API_KEY) return process.env.CURSOR_API_KEY;
  if (!userId) return null;
  const db = await database.init("service");
  const { data } = await db
    .from("profiles")
    .select("env_vars")
    .eq("id", userId)
    .single();
  return data?.env_vars?.CURSOR_API_KEY ?? null;
}

function makeAuthHeader(apiKey) {
  return `Basic ${Buffer.from(`${apiKey}:`).toString("base64")}`;
}

async function cursorFetch(path, opts = {}, userId) {
  const key = await getApiKey(userId);
  if (!key) throw new Error("Missing CURSOR_API_KEY");
  const url = path.startsWith("http") ? path : `${API_BASE}${path}`;
  const res = await fetch(url, {
    ...opts,
    headers: {
      Authorization: makeAuthHeader(key),
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      ...opts.headers,
    },
  });
  if (!res.ok) {
    const body = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`Cursor API ${res.status}: ${body.slice(0, 500)}`);
  }
  return res.json();
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Agent management
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Read agent status.
 * @param {{ agentId: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function readAgent({ agentId } = {}, userId) {
  if (!agentId) throw new Error("agentId is required");
  return cursorFetch(`/${agentId}`, {}, userId);
}

/**
 * Read agent conversation history.
 * @param {{ agentId: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function readConversation({ agentId } = {}, userId) {
  if (!agentId) throw new Error("agentId is required");
  return cursorFetch(`/${agentId}/conversation`, {}, userId);
}

/**
 * Send a followup message to an agent (push-based dispatch).
 * @param {{ agentId: string, message: string, model?: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function writeFollowup({ agentId, message, model } = {}, userId) {
  if (!agentId) throw new Error("agentId is required");
  if (!message) throw new Error("message is required");
  return cursorFetch(
    `/${agentId}/followup`,
    {
      method: "POST",
      body: JSON.stringify({
        prompt: { text: message },
      }),
    },
    userId,
  );
}

/**
 * Search for agents by partial ID or metadata.
 * Note: Cursor API doesn't have a list endpoint — this reads a known agent.
 * For now, wraps readAgent. Extend when API adds list support.
 * @param {{ agentId: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function searchAgents({ agentId } = {}, userId) {
  if (!agentId) throw new Error("agentId is required for search (Cursor API has no list endpoint)");
  const agent = await readAgent({ agentId }, userId);
  return { agents: [agent] };
}

/**
 * Read queued (unprocessed) messages — user messages sent after the last assistant response.
 * @param {{ agentId: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function readQueuedMessages({ agentId } = {}, userId) {
  if (!agentId) throw new Error("agentId is required");
  const conv = await readConversation({ agentId }, userId);
  const msgs = conv?.messages || [];
  const lastAssistantIdx = msgs.findLastIndex((m) => m.type === "assistant_message");
  return { queued: msgs.slice(lastAssistantIdx + 1).filter((m) => m.type === "user_message") };
}

/**
 * Create a new Cursor cloud agent.
 * @param {{ repository: string, ref: string, prompt?: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
/**
 * Spawn a new Cursor cloud agent. ALWAYS provisions GuildOS service-role
 * credentials in the spawn prompt as the first action, so the agent never
 * hits the documented "missing GuildOS Supabase credentials" blocker that
 * caused the 2026-04-26 ptglab smoke-test to escalate without bookkeeping.
 *
 * Contract: this is the ONLY supported path for creating an agent. Direct
 * POSTs to the Cursor API that skip the credentials-injection block are a
 * contract violation — agents spawned that way cannot complete GuildOS-
 * side bookkeeping (items rows, quest_comments, submitForPurrview).
 *
 * Credential source: process.env (the Guildmaster running this weapon must
 * have GuildOS env loaded — `--env-file=.env.local` or equivalent).
 *
 * @param {{ repository: string, ref: string, prompt?: string,
 *           skipCredentialsInjection?: boolean }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function writeAgent({ repository, ref, prompt, skipCredentialsInjection = false, model } = {}, userId) {
  if (!repository) throw new Error("repository is required");
  if (!ref) throw new Error("ref is required");
  const key = await getApiKey(userId);
  if (!key) throw new Error("Missing CURSOR_API_KEY");
  // Cheap-worker policy: pin Cursor's Composer model (premium throws unless
  // CURSOR_ALLOW_PREMIUM=1). NEVER omit — omission = Cursor's premium default.
  const modelId = resolveCheapCursorModel(model);

  let finalPrompt = prompt || "Wait for initialization instructions.";

  if (!skipCredentialsInjection) {
    // Prefer the GUILDOS_-prefixed names so the GuildOS project is unambiguous
    // even when the orchestrator's env is also wired to a project's own
    // Supabase. Falls back to the basic names for backward compat.
    const guildosUrl =
      process.env.GUILDOS_NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL ||
      process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL;
    const guildosKey =
      process.env.GUILDOS_SUPABASE_SECRETE_KEY ||
      process.env.GUILDOS_SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY ||
      process.env.SUPABASE_SECRETE_KEY ||
      process.env.SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY;
    if (!guildosUrl || !guildosKey) {
      throw new Error(
        "writeAgent: GuildOS credentials missing from process.env. Required: GUILDOS_NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL + GUILDOS_SUPABASE_SECRETE_KEY (or the basic NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL + SUPABASE_SECRETE_KEY for backward compat). The agent cannot do GuildOS bookkeeping without these. Run with `--env-file=.env.local` or pass `skipCredentialsInjection: true` if you genuinely want a creds-less agent (rare — almost always wrong)."
      );
    }
    finalPrompt = guildosCredentialsSetupBlock({ supabaseUrl: guildosUrl, supabaseKey: guildosKey }) + finalPrompt;
  }

  const res = await fetch(API_BASE, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: makeAuthHeader(key),
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      prompt: { text: finalPrompt },
      source: { repository, ref },
      model: { id: modelId },
    }),
  });
  if (!res.ok) {
    const body = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`Cursor API ${res.status}: ${body.slice(0, 500)}`);
  }
  return res.json();
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Session-health probe — pre-dispatch check that the upstream Cursor session
// matches what the adventurers DB row says, and is in a state that can accept
// a followup. Reconciles drift (DB says idle, upstream says EXPIRED, etc.).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Probe one adventurer's session against the Cursor API and reconcile the DB.
 *
 * Returns:
 *   {
 *     upstream_status: 'RUNNING' | 'FINISHED' | 'EXPIRED' | 'CREATING' | 'ERROR' | <other>,
 *     alive: boolean,            // upstream session exists at all
 *     dispatch_safe: boolean,    // followup is expected to land (FINISHED/RUNNING/CREATING ok; EXPIRED not)
 *     was_drift: boolean,        // db.session_status differed from upstream
 *     adventurer: { id, name, session_id, session_status }, // post-sync row
 *   }
 *
 * Drift handling: if upstream returns a status the local DB doesn't reflect
 * accurately, this updates `adventurers.session_status` to a normalized
 * "idle" (dispatch-safe) or "expired" (needs respawn) value. Does NOT auto-
 * respawn — caller decides.
 *
 * @param {{ adventurerId?: string, adventurerName?: string }} input — pass one
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function syncSessionStatus({ adventurerId, adventurerName } = {}, userId) {
  if (!adventurerId && !adventurerName) {
    throw new Error("syncSessionStatus: pass adventurerId or adventurerName");
  }
  const db = await database.init("service");
  const q = db.from("adventurers").select("id, name, session_id, session_status, worker_type").limit(1);
  const { data: rows } = await (adventurerId ? q.eq("id", adventurerId) : q.eq("name", adventurerName));
  const adv = rows?.[0];
  if (!adv) throw new Error(`syncSessionStatus: adventurer not found (${adventurerId || adventurerName})`);
  if (!adv.session_id) {
    return {
      upstream_status: "no_session",
      alive: false,
      dispatch_safe: false,
      was_drift: false,
      adventurer: adv,
    };
  }

  let upstreamStatus = "unknown";
  let alive = false;
  try {
    const j = await cursorFetch(`/${adv.session_id}`, {}, userId);
    upstreamStatus = String(j?.status || "unknown");
    alive = true;
  } catch (err) {
    // Cursor API returns 404 / 410 for hard-deleted sessions; surface that
    upstreamStatus = "deleted_or_unreachable";
    alive = false;
  }

  // Normalize to DB-friendly status. dispatch_safe: can a followup land?
  const dispatch_safe =
    alive && (upstreamStatus === "RUNNING" || upstreamStatus === "FINISHED" || upstreamStatus === "CREATING");
  const desiredDbStatus = dispatch_safe
    ? "idle"
    : upstreamStatus === "EXPIRED"
      ? "expired"
      : "unreachable";

  const was_drift = adv.session_status !== desiredDbStatus;
  if (was_drift) {
    await db.from("adventurers").update({ session_status: desiredDbStatus }).eq("id", adv.id);
  }

  return {
    upstream_status: upstreamStatus,
    alive,
    dispatch_safe,
    was_drift,
    adventurer: { ...adv, session_status: desiredDbStatus },
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Environment setup helper (for fresh agent sessions)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Generate the env setup instructions for a fresh Cursor agent session.
 * Reads required env vars from profiles and formats them for the agent.
 * @param {{ userId: string, envVarKeys?: string[] }} input
 */
export async function readEnvSetupInstructions({ userId, envVarKeys } = {}) {
  if (!userId) throw new Error("userId is required");
  const db = await database.init("service");
  const { data } = await db
    .from("profiles")
    .select("env_vars")
    .eq("id", userId)
    .single();

  const ev = data?.env_vars || {};
  const keys = Array.isArray(envVarKeys) && envVarKeys.length > 0
    ? envVarKeys
    : [
        "NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL",
        "NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY",
        "SUPABASE_SECRETE_KEY",
        "OPENAI_API_KEY",
        "PIGEON_API_KEY",
        "PIGEON_POST_OWNER_ID",
      ];

  const lines = [];
  for (const k of keys) {
    const val = ev[k] || process.env[k] || "";
    if (val) lines.push(`${k}=${val}`);
  }

  return {
    envFileContent: lines.join("\n"),
    setupScript: [
      "npm install && npx playwright install chromium --with-deps && npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code",
      `cat > .env.local << 'ENVEOF'\n${lines.join("\n")}\nENVEOF`,
    ].join("\n"),
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Credential check
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export async function checkCredentials(userId) {
  try {
    const key = await getApiKey(userId);
    if (key) {
      return { ok: true, msg: "CURSOR_API_KEY is set" };
    }
    return {
      ok: false,
      msg: "Missing CURSOR_API_KEY — add it to your profile env_vars in Council Hall > Formulary.",
    };
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, msg: `Error: ${e.message}` };
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Agent-facing wrappers — (userId, input) signature, skillActionOk/Err envelope.
// These are the methods the `cursor` skill book's toc points at. They were moved
// out of libs/skill_book/cursor/index.js so the skill book stays a pure prompt
// registry. The underlying logic delegates to the weapon functions above.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function resolveUserId(explicitUserId) {
  const ctx = getAdventurerExecutionContext();
  return explicitUserId || ctx?.userId || null;
}

/**
 * Send a task to a Cursor cloud agent via followup message.
 * NOTE: a followup runs the agent on the model it was CREATED with (the API followup
 * body takes no model field), so the `model` input here is inert — model selection
 * happens at creation (writeAgent / cursor_setup), which is PINNED cheap. If the agent
 * was created cheap (post-2026-06-24), the followup runs cheap; a pre-fix premium agent
 * stays premium until recreated. See libs/weapon/cursor/model.js + engineering_decisions.md.
 * @param {string} [_userId]
 * @param {{ agentId?: string, instructions?: string, model?: string }} input
 */
export async function dispatchTask(_userId, input) {
  const inObj = typeof input === "object" && input ? input : {};
  const agentId = String(inObj.agentId || "").trim();
  const instructions = String(inObj.instructions || "").trim();
  const model = String(inObj.model || "").trim() || undefined;

  if (!agentId) return skillActionErr("agentId is required");
  if (!instructions) return skillActionErr("instructions are required");

  const userId = resolveUserId(_userId);
  try {
    const result = await writeFollowup({ agentId, message: instructions, model }, userId);
    return skillActionOk({
      items: {
        result: JSON.stringify(result),
        agentId,
      },
      msg: `Task dispatched to agent ${agentId}`,
    });
  } catch (e) {
    return skillActionErr(`Dispatch failed: ${e.message}`);
  }
}

/**
 * Check the current status of a Cursor cloud agent.
 * @param {string} [_userId]
 * @param {{ agentId?: string }} input
 */
export async function readStatus(_userId, input) {
  const inObj = typeof input === "object" && input ? input : {};
  const agentId = String(inObj.agentId || "").trim();
  if (!agentId) return skillActionErr("agentId is required");

  const userId = resolveUserId(_userId);
  try {
    const agent = await readAgent({ agentId }, userId);
    return skillActionOk({
      items: {
        status: JSON.stringify(agent.status || "unknown"),
        agent: JSON.stringify(agent),
      },
      msg: `Agent ${agentId} status: ${agent.status || "unknown"}`,
    });
  } catch (e) {
    return skillActionErr(`Status check failed: ${e.message}`);
  }
}

/**
 * Read the full conversation history of a Cursor cloud agent.
 * (Named *Action to avoid clashing with the lower-level `readConversation` API wrapper.)
 * @param {string} [_userId]
 * @param {{ agentId?: string }} input
 */
export async function readConversationAction(_userId, input) {
  const inObj = typeof input === "object" && input ? input : {};
  const agentId = String(inObj.agentId || "").trim();
  if (!agentId) return skillActionErr("agentId is required");

  const userId = resolveUserId(_userId);
  try {
    const conv = await readConversation({ agentId }, userId);
    return skillActionOk({
      items: { conversation: JSON.stringify(conv) },
      msg: `Retrieved conversation for agent ${agentId}`,
    });
  } catch (e) {
    return skillActionErr(`Conversation read failed: ${e.message}`);
  }
}

/**
 * Dispatch a PowerPoint-generation task to a Cursor cloud agent. The agent
 * builds the .pptx and uploads it to Supabase Storage under cursor_cloud/.
 * @param {string} [_userId]
 * @param {{ agentId?: string, topic?: string, slides?: string, questId?: string }} input
 */
export async function dispatchPptGeneration(_userId, input) {
  const inObj = typeof input === "object" && input ? input : {};
  const agentId = String(inObj.agentId || "").trim();
  const topic = String(inObj.topic || "").trim();
  const slides = String(inObj.slides || "").trim();
  const questId = String(inObj.questId || "").trim();

  if (!agentId) return skillActionErr("agentId is required");
  if (!topic) return skillActionErr("topic is required");

  const userId = resolveUserId(_userId);
  const instructions = [
    `Generate a PowerPoint presentation about: ${topic}`,
    slides ? `\nSlide content:\n${slides}` : "",
    "",
    "Requirements:",
    "- Use pptxgenjs or python-pptx to create the PPT file",
    "- Upload the final .pptx to Supabase Storage at:",
    questId
      ? `  cursor_cloud/${questId}/${topic.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, "-").toLowerCase()}.pptx`
      : `  cursor_cloud/general/${topic.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, "-").toLowerCase()}.pptx`,
    "- Post the public URL as a quest comment",
    "- Take a screenshot of at least one slide as visual proof",
    "",
    "After generating, git push your changes.",
  ].join("\n");

  try {
    const result = await writeFollowup({ agentId, message: instructions }, userId);
    return skillActionOk({
      items: {
        result: JSON.stringify(result),
        agentId,
      },
      msg: `PPT generation dispatched to agent ${agentId}: "${topic}"`,
    });
  } catch (e) {
    return skillActionErr(`PPT dispatch failed: ${e.message}`);
  }
}
```

```js
/**
 * Cursor model policy — the single source of truth for "Cursor = cheap worker only".
 * Pure module, NO imports, so it is consumable identically from the Next runtime, a
 * Next API route, and a plain-node leaf (cursorcli) without adapter shims.
 *
 * DECISION (2026-06-24, operator directive): we hold a Claude 20X Max subscription,
 * so ALL Claude work runs on that flat-rate subscription via claudecli (OAuth, no API
 * credits). Cursor is used ONLY as a CHEAP worker on its own in-house Composer model.
 * We NEVER route a premium frontier model (Claude/GPT/Gemini/Grok) THROUGH Cursor —
 * Cursor bills those against its metered API-model pool ("$200 API model usage") AND
 * it double-pays for Claude we already have flat-rate ("using Cursor as a bridge for
 * Claude"). Omitting the model on a Cursor dispatch makes Cursor pick its PREMIUM
 * default — that omission is what burned $200 in one cycle (the bug this enforces away).
 * Full rationale: libs/weapon/cursor/engineering_decisions.md.
 */

/** Cursor's cheap in-house worker model id (from GET /v0/models — the only non-premium
 *  entry in the recommended set). Env-overridable, but it must stay a composer-* id. */
export const CURSOR_CHEAP_MODEL = process.env.CURSOR_CHEAP_MODEL || "composer-2.5";

/** Premium = anything that is NOT Cursor's own composer-* model. Everything else in
 *  Cursor's recommended list (claude-*, gpt-*, gemini-*, grok-*, and "auto", which may
 *  route to a frontier model) bills the metered API pool. */
export function isPremiumCursorModel(id) {
  const s = String(id || "").trim().toLowerCase();
  if (!s) return false; // empty/omitted → the caller substitutes the cheap default
  return !s.startsWith("composer");
}

/**
 * Resolve + ENFORCE the model for any Cursor dispatch. Returns the cheap default when
 * none is given; THROWS on a premium id unless `CURSOR_ALLOW_PREMIUM=1` is set — the
 * explicit, auditable operator escape hatch for a deliberate one-off. This is the
 * structural guard that makes "Cursor never bridges to Claude" impossible to violate by
 * accident (an omitted/defaulted/auto model can no longer silently land on a frontier model).
 *
 * @param {string} [id] requested model id (may be undefined/empty)
 * @returns {string} a composer-* model id (or the premium id if the escape hatch is set)
 */
export function resolveCheapCursorModel(id) {
  const chosen = (id && String(id).trim()) || CURSOR_CHEAP_MODEL;
  if (isPremiumCursorModel(chosen) && process.env.CURSOR_ALLOW_PREMIUM !== "1") {
    throw new Error(
      `Cursor model "${chosen}" is a premium (metered) model. POLICY: Cursor runs ONLY its cheap Composer ` +
        `model; Claude work goes through Claude Max (claudecli). Pass a composer-* id, set CURSOR_CHEAP_MODEL, ` +
        `or — for a deliberate, audited one-off — set CURSOR_ALLOW_PREMIUM=1. ` +
        `See libs/weapon/cursor/engineering_decisions.md.`,
    );
  }
  return chosen;
}
```

/**
 * Pure-JS module: builds the GuildOS-credentials shell-setup block that
 * `cursor.writeAgent` prepends to every spawn prompt.
 *
 * Extracted so node scripts (which can't resolve `@/libs/...` Next path
 * aliases) and the Next-runtime weapon both consume the same source.
 * No imports — keep it that way so this module is consumable from any
 * runtime without adapter shims.
 */

/**
 * @param {{ supabaseUrl: string, supabaseKey: string }} input
 * @returns {string} shell-setup block to prepend to a Cursor agent's spawn prompt
 */
export function guildosCredentialsSetupBlock({ supabaseUrl, supabaseKey } = {}) {
  if (!supabaseUrl || !supabaseKey) {
    throw new Error(
      "guildosCredentialsSetupBlock: supabaseUrl + supabaseKey are required. " +
      "Caller is responsible for sourcing them from process.env (NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL + SUPABASE_SECRETE_KEY) " +
      "or profiles.env_vars before invoking the spawn."
    );
  }
  return [
    "═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════",
    "FIRST ACTION — provision GuildOS credentials (do this BEFORE anything else)",
    "═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════",
    "",
    "Set these env vars so GuildOS bookkeeping works regardless of which",
    "project repo you're working on. Both the GUILDOS_-prefixed names",
    "(canonical when working in multi-repo envs) AND the basic names",
    "(backward compat) are exported, so libs that read either form work.",
    "",
    "```bash",
    "mkdir -p ~/guildos",
    "cat > ~/.guildos.env <<'EOF'",
    `export GUILDOS_NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL='${supabaseUrl}'`,
    `export GUILDOS_SUPABASE_SECRETE_KEY='${supabaseKey}'`,
    `export NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL='${supabaseUrl}'`,
    `export SUPABASE_SECRETE_KEY='${supabaseKey}'`,
    "EOF",
    "echo 'source ~/.guildos.env' >> ~/.bashrc",
    "source ~/.guildos.env",
    "test -n \"$GUILDOS_SUPABASE_SECRETE_KEY\" && echo 'GuildOS creds loaded' || echo 'FAILED — escalate'",
    "```",
    "",
    "After that, run housekeeping.initAgent (clones GuildOS, loads skill books, finds your quests). The init step assumes the env is already loaded.",
    "",
    "═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════",
    "TASK PROMPT",
    "═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════",
    "",
  ].join("\n");
}

<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: libs/weapon/cursorcli/engineering_decisions.md -->
```markdown
# Engineering decisions — `libs/weapon/cursorcli`

Rationale layer (per CLAUDE.md §6). The WHY behind the local Cursor-CLI invoke
weapon — the four non-native requirements baked in, and why this is a separate
weapon from `claudecli`. Append; supersede in place when a decision changes.

---

## 2026-06-23 — four non-native invocation requirements are baked into `invoke`, discovered by smoke test

The local Cursor CLI (`cursor-agent --print`) needs four things a Claude leaf
never does. They are NOT discoverable from the CLI's `--help`; each cost a failed
smoke-test run to find (2026-06-23), so they live in code, not in the caller:

1. **`CURSOR_API_KEY` must be in the child env.** `cursor-agent status` reports
   "Login successful" from a stored INTERACTIVE token, but headless `--print` does
   NOT use it — it errors `Authentication required` unless `CURSOR_API_KEY` is set.
   *Rejected:* relying on `cursor-agent login`. *Consequence:* every headless run
   fails auth on a box where only the interactive login was done.

2. **Strip `HTTP(S)_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY` from the child env.** This box has a local
   proxy (`<REDACTED-IP>:7897`, Clash-style) exported in the environment; cursor-agent
   honors it and then `Failed to reach the Cursor API` because the proxy can't
   egress to `api.cursor.com`. The weapon deletes the proxy vars for the child.
   *Rejected:* leaving the inherited env intact (the native default). *Consequence:*
   every run dies at the proxy hop even though direct egress works.

3. **Default to `composer-2.5` (Cursor's cheap Composer), enforced cheap-only.**
   *(SUPERSEDED 2026-06-24 — the original entry said default `--model auto`. That was
   WRONG: `auto` can route to a premium frontier model and bill Cursor's metered API
   pool — the "$200 bridge-for-Claude" burn. See `libs/weapon/cursor/engineering_decisions.md`.)*
   The model now resolves through `resolveCheapCursorModel` (`../cursor/model.js`):
   default `CURSOR_CHEAP_MODEL` (`composer-2.5`), and any non-`composer-*` id
   (including `auto`, `claude-*`, `gpt-*`) **throws** unless `CURSOR_ALLOW_PREMIUM=1`.
   *Why composer is correct even though it once returned "out of usage":* when the
   monthly pool is fully exhausted, ALL models (composer included) report out-of-usage
   — that reflects a drained pool, not composer being expensive. Composer IS the cheap
   in-house worker model; pinning it is the policy. *Consequence:* relax this back to
   `auto`/premium and the local CLI re-opens the metered-pool burn the policy closes.

4. **Retry on transient network.** `api.cursor.com` connectivity on this box is
   INTERMITTENT (observed ~1-in-4 success on back-to-back calls; "Failed to reach"
   / "Connection lost, reconnecting"). The buffered path retries up to 3× on any
   transient marker; a genuine 30-min timeout is NOT retried. *Rejected:* claudecli's
   "retry only on a non-zero exit" rule — cursor-agent can exit non-zero on a clean
   usage error (don't retry) and can ALSO emit a transient mid-stream, so the retry
   keys on transient SUBSTRINGS, not just exit code. *Consequence:* without the
   substring-keyed retry, a single network flap bounces the whole leaf.

**Prompt via STDIN (verified), not argv.** `cursor-agent` reads the prompt from
stdin, so the weapon pipes a temp file (`type`/`cat`) exactly like `claudecli` —
zero argv quoting of the (often multi-KB, newline-heavy) prompt. Confirmed
2026-06-23: piping with no positional prompt returned the expected single-word
answer.

---

## 2026-06-23 — separate weapon from `claudecli`, NOT a `claudecli` flag

**Decision.** `cursorcli` is its own weapon with the SAME `invoke(prompt, opts)`
contract (`{ok, output, rawOutput, error}`, optional streaming `logPath`), so the
caravan dispatch fork can select it positionally — `claudecli.invoke` for a
`worker_type='local'` adventurer, `cursorcli.invoke` for `cursor_cli` — with no
branching inside either weapon.

**Rejected alternative.** A `claudecli.invoke(prompt, { engine: 'cursor' })` flag
that swaps the binary. Rejected: the two engines diverge on env (key injection,
proxy strip), model selection, the auth model, the retry predicate, and the tool
surface — a shared function would become a tangle of `if engine===` branches, and
`claudecli`'s `--dangerously-skip-permissions` / OAuth-via-`delete ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
logic is Anthropic-specific and wrong for Cursor.

**Why.** Mirroring the contract (not the implementation) is what makes the dispatch
fork a one-line `pick the weapon` choice while each weapon stays a clean, single-
engine subprocess wrapper.

**Consequence if violated.** Fold Cursor into `claudecli` and every future
engine-specific quirk (Cursor's, the next backend's) accretes as branches in one
function until neither engine's path is readable or independently testable.
```

```js
/**
 * cursorCLI weapon — invokes the LOCAL Cursor CLI (`cursor-agent --print --force`)
 * as a subprocess and returns stdout. The Cursor-side mirror of the `claudecli`
 * weapon: same invoke contract ({ ok, output, rawOutput, error }, optional
 * streaming logPath), so a future caravan dispatch path can pick it for a
 * `worker_type: "cursor_cli"` adventurer exactly where it picks `claudecli.invoke`
 * for a `local` one.
 *
 * WHY a separate weapon (not a claudecli flag): the local Cursor CLI has four
 * non-native invocation requirements a Claude-leaf path never has — they are
 * baked in here so every caller gets them for free (see engineering_decisions.md):
 *   1. CURSOR_API_KEY MUST be in the child env. Headless `--print` does NOT use
 *      the interactive `cursor-agent login` token; without the key it errors
 *      "Authentication required."
 *   2. The local HTTP proxy (e.g. <REDACTED-IP>:7897 from HTTP(S)_PROXY) breaks egress
 *      to api.cursor.com. Strip the proxy vars from the child env.
 *   3. Pin Cursor's CHEAP Composer model (`composer-2.5`), never the premium default
 *      and never `auto` (which can route to a premium frontier model and bill the
 *      metered pool — the "$200 bridge-for-Claude" burn). Enforced cheap-only via
 *      resolveCheapCursorModel (../cursor/model.js): premium ids throw unless
 *      CURSOR_ALLOW_PREMIUM=1. Override the cheap default via CURSOR_CHEAP_MODEL.
 *   4. api.cursor.com connectivity is intermittent on at least one box; retry on
 *      transient "Failed to reach" / "Connection lost".
 */

export const toc = {
  invoke: "Invoke the local Cursor CLI (cursor-agent --print) as a subprocess with a prompt; returns stdout / raw output. Cursor-side mirror of claudecli.invoke.",
};

import { exec, spawn } from "child_process";
import { writeFileSync, unlinkSync, mkdirSync, createWriteStream } from "fs";
import { join, dirname } from "path";
import { tmpdir } from "os";
import { randomUUID } from "crypto";
import { resolveCheapCursorModel } from "../cursor/model.js";

const TIMEOUT_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000; // 30 minutes — match claudecli; long curation/tagging batches exceed 5m.

/** The cursor-agent binary. PATH-resolved by default (the install dir is on PATH);
 *  override per box with CURSOR_AGENT_BIN if it isn't. */
const AGENT_BIN = process.env.CURSOR_AGENT_BIN || "cursor-agent";

// Default model is Cursor's cheap in-house Composer (CURSOR_CHEAP_MODEL). NOT `auto`
// — `auto` can route to a premium frontier model and bill Cursor's metered API pool,
// which is exactly the "Cursor as a bridge for Claude" burn this policy forbids. The
// per-call model is resolved + ENFORCED through resolveCheapCursorModel (premium throws
// unless CURSOR_ALLOW_PREMIUM=1). See libs/weapon/cursor/model.js.

/** Substrings that mark a transient (retryable) failure rather than a real result. */
const TRANSIENT = ["failed to reach", "connection lost", "reconnecting", "econnreset", "etimedout", "socket hang up"];
const isTransient = (s) => { const l = (s || "").toLowerCase(); return TRANSIENT.some((t) => l.includes(t)); };

/** Build the child env: inherit, inject CURSOR_API_KEY, strip the local proxy. */
function buildChildEnv() {
  const env = { ...process.env };
  // (1) headless --print needs the key explicitly; the login token is not used.
  if (!env.CURSOR_API_KEY && env.CURSOR_API_TOKEN) env.CURSOR_API_KEY = env.CURSOR_API_TOKEN;
  // (2) the local proxy breaks egress to api.cursor.com — remove it for the child.
  for (const k of ["HTTP_PROXY", "HTTPS_PROXY", "ALL_PROXY", "http_proxy", "https_proxy", "all_proxy"]) delete env[k];
  return env;
}

/**
 * Invoke `cursor-agent --print --force`. Two modes (mirrors claudecli):
 *  - Default (no logPath): buffered exec with retry, returns final stdout.
 *  - Streaming (opts.logPath set): spawn + tee stdout/stderr LIVE into a log file.
 *    opts.streamJson adds `--output-format stream-json` for a per-event log.
 *
 * @param {string} taskPrompt
 * @param {{ logPath?: string, streamJson?: boolean, model?: string, cwd?: string }} [opts]
 * @returns {Promise<{ ok: boolean, output: string, rawOutput: string, error?: string }>}
 */
export async function invoke(taskPrompt, opts = {}) {
  if (!taskPrompt || typeof taskPrompt !== "string" || !taskPrompt.trim()) {
    return { ok: false, output: "", rawOutput: "", error: "taskPrompt is required" };
  }
  const { logPath = null, streamJson = false, model: requestedModel, cwd = process.cwd() } = opts || {};
  // Enforce the cheap-worker policy: composer-* only (premium throws unless the
  // CURSOR_ALLOW_PREMIUM escape hatch is set). Defaults to CURSOR_CHEAP_MODEL.
  let model;
  try {
    model = resolveCheapCursorModel(requestedModel);
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, output: "", rawOutput: "", error: e.message };
  }

  // Prompt via temp file piped to STDIN (cursor-agent reads the prompt from stdin)
  // — same escaping-free pattern as claudecli; no argv quoting of the prompt.
  const tmpFile = join(tmpdir(), `cursorcli-${randomUUID()}.txt`);
  try {
    writeFileSync(tmpFile, taskPrompt.trim(), "utf8");
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, output: "", rawOutput: "", error: `Failed to write temp file: ${e.message}` };
  }

  const cat = process.platform === "win32" ? "type" : "cat";
  const fmt = streamJson ? "stream-json" : "text";
  const cmd = `${cat} "${tmpFile}" | ${AGENT_BIN} --print --force --model ${model} --output-format ${fmt}`;
  const env = buildChildEnv();

  // ── Streaming path — tee a leaf worker's live transcript into logPath ──
  if (logPath) {
    try { mkdirSync(dirname(logPath), { recursive: true }); } catch { /* ignore */ }
    let ws;
    try { ws = createWriteStream(logPath, { flags: "w" }); } catch { ws = null; }
    if (ws) {
      ws.write(`# cursor worker log — started ${new Date().toISOString()} (model=${model})\n`);
      ws.write(`# ===PROMPT_BEGIN===\n${taskPrompt.trim()}\n# ===PROMPT_END===\n`);
    }
    return new Promise((resolve) => {
      let out = "";
      const child = spawn(cmd, { cwd, env, shell: true, windowsHide: true });
      // UTF-8 decode at the stream level so multibyte chars split across a pipe
      // boundary aren't mangled into U+FFFD � (see claudecli for the full rationale).
      child.stdout?.setEncoding("utf8");
      child.stderr?.setEncoding("utf8");
      const killer = setTimeout(() => { try { child.kill(); } catch { /* ignore */ } }, TIMEOUT_MS);
      child.stdout?.on("data", (d) => { const s = d.toString(); out += s; if (ws) ws.write(s); });
      child.stderr?.on("data", (d) => { const s = d.toString(); if (ws) ws.write(s); });
      child.on("error", (e) => {
        clearTimeout(killer);
        if (ws) { try { ws.end(`\n# spawn error: ${e.message}\n`); } catch { /* ignore */ } }
        try { unlinkSync(tmpFile); } catch { /* ignore */ }
        resolve({ ok: false, output: "", rawOutput: out, error: e.message });
      });
      child.on("close", (code) => {
        clearTimeout(killer);
        if (ws) { try { ws.end(`\n# cursor worker log — exited code=${code} at ${new Date().toISOString()}\n`); } catch { /* ignore */ } }
        try { unlinkSync(tmpFile); } catch { /* ignore */ }
        resolve({ ok: code === 0, output: out.trim(), rawOutput: out });
      });
    });
  }

  // ── Default path — buffered exec with retry on transient network failure ──
  const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3;
  const runOnce = () =>
    new Promise((res) => {
      exec(cmd, { cwd, timeout: TIMEOUT_MS, maxBuffer: 10 * 1024 * 1024, env }, (err, stdout, stderr) => {
        res({ err, stdout: stdout || "", stderr: stderr || "" });
      });
    });

  let last;
  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= MAX_ATTEMPTS; attempt++) {
    last = await runOnce();
    const combined = `${last.stdout}\n${last.stderr}\n${last.err?.message || ""}`;
    const transient = isTransient(combined);
    if (!last.err && !transient) {
      try { unlinkSync(tmpFile); } catch { /* ignore */ }
      return { ok: true, output: last.stdout.trim(), rawOutput: last.stdout };
    }
    const isTimeout = last.err?.killed || last.err?.code === "ETIMEDOUT";
    if (isTimeout && !transient) break; // a genuine 30-min timeout is not retried
    if (attempt < MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
      console.warn(`[cursorcli] attempt ${attempt}/${MAX_ATTEMPTS} failed (${(last.err?.message || combined).split("\n")[0]}); retrying after backoff`);
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1500 * attempt));
    }
  }
  try { unlinkSync(tmpFile); } catch { /* ignore */ }
  const isTimeout = last.err?.killed || last.err?.code === "ETIMEDOUT";
  const msg = isTimeout
    ? "Cursor CLI timed out after 30 minutes."
    : `Cursor CLI error after ${MAX_ATTEMPTS} attempts: ${last.err?.message || "transient network failure (Failed to reach the Cursor API)"}`;
  return { ok: false, output: last.stdout.trim(), rawOutput: last.stdout, error: isTimeout ? "timeout" : msg };
}
```

```js
/**
 * DataForSEO weapon — Google SERP rank checks via DataForSEO live/advanced.
 *
 * Auth: DATAFORSEO_LOGIN + DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD env vars (or profile env_vars).
 * Optional: DATAFORSEO_DEFAULT_LOCATION (numeric location_code, defaults to
 *   2840 = United States).
 *
 * Endpoints used:
 *   POST /v3/serp/google/organic/live/advanced — full SERP for one keyword
 *
 * For batch operations DataForSEO accepts up to 100 tasks per call against
 * the same endpoint, so checkSerpRanks ships batches under that cap.
 */

import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";

export const toc = {
  checkSerpRank:
    "Check Google SERP rank of a target domain for a single keyword. Returns rank_absolute or null.",
  checkSerpRanks:
    "Batch SERP rank check for many (keyword, target_domain) pairs.",
  fetchSerp:
    "Return the full top-N organic SERP for a keyword (raw items list).",
  searchVolume:
    "Mass-screen demand: Google Ads search_volume + CPC + competition for a batch of keywords (<=1000). The cheap universal gate for 'does this term have any demand'. CPC is the commercial-intent proxy.",
  keywordIdeas:
    "Topic discovery: DataForSEO Labs keyword_suggestions for a seed phrase — returns long-tail phrases CONTAINING the seed, each with search_volume + CPC. Use to uncover the real question/topic cluster for an FAQ.",
  checkCredentials: "Check that DataForSEO credentials are configured.",
};

const BASE = "https://api.dataforseo.com/v3";
const MAX_BATCH = 100;
const DEFAULT_LOCATION = 2840; // United States
const DEFAULT_LANGUAGE = "en";

async function loadCreds(userId) {
  if (userId) {
    try {
      const db = await database.init("service");
      const { data } = await db
        .from("profiles")
        .select("env_vars")
        .eq("id", userId)
        .single();
      const ev = data?.env_vars || {};
      const login = ev.DATAFORSEO_LOGIN;
      const password = ev.DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD;
      const defLoc = ev.DATAFORSEO_DEFAULT_LOCATION;
      if (login && password) {
        return {
          login,
          password,
          defaultLocation: parseInt(defLoc || "0", 10) || DEFAULT_LOCATION,
        };
      }
    } catch {
      /* fall through */
    }
  }
  const login = process.env.DATAFORSEO_LOGIN;
  const password = process.env.DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD;
  if (!login || !password) return null;
  return {
    login,
    password,
    defaultLocation:
      parseInt(process.env.DATAFORSEO_DEFAULT_LOCATION || "0", 10) ||
      DEFAULT_LOCATION,
  };
}

function authHeader(login, password) {
  return "Basic " + Buffer.from(`${login}:${password}`).toString("base64");
}

function normalizeDomain(d) {
  if (!d) return "";
  let s = String(d).toLowerCase().trim();
  s = s.replace(/^https?:\/\//, "");
  s = s.replace(/^www\./, "");
  s = s.split("/")[0];
  return s;
}

function postSerp(payload, login, password) {
  return fetch(`${BASE}/serp/google/organic/live/advanced`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: authHeader(login, password),
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(payload),
  });
}

/**
 * Look up the rank of `target_domain` for `keyword`. Returns the lowest
 * (best) rank_absolute matching the domain (counting all organic items
 * down to depth=100), or null if not in the top 100.
 *
 * @param {{ keyword: string, target_domain: string, location_code?: number, depth?: number, userId?: string }} input
 */
export async function checkSerpRank(input = {}, userId) {
  const { keyword, target_domain, location_code, depth = 100 } = input;
  if (!keyword) throw new Error("keyword is required");
  if (!target_domain) throw new Error("target_domain is required");
  const creds = await loadCreds(userId);
  if (!creds) throw new Error("DATAFORSEO_LOGIN/PASSWORD not set");
  const target = normalizeDomain(target_domain);
  const payload = [
    {
      keyword,
      location_code: location_code || creds.defaultLocation,
      language_code: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE,
      depth: Math.min(Math.max(depth, 10), 100),
      device: "desktop",
      os: "windows",
    },
  ];
  const res = await postSerp(payload, creds.login, creds.password);
  if (!res.ok) {
    const text = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`DataForSEO ${res.status}: ${text.slice(0, 200)}`);
  }
  const json = await res.json();
  if (json.status_code !== 20000) {
    throw new Error(
      `DataForSEO status_code=${json.status_code}: ${json.status_message}`
    );
  }
  const items = json?.tasks?.[0]?.result?.[0]?.items || [];
  let best = null;
  for (const it of items) {
    if (it.type !== "organic") continue;
    const dom = normalizeDomain(it.domain);
    if (dom === target) {
      if (best == null || it.rank_absolute < best) best = it.rank_absolute;
    }
  }
  return {
    keyword,
    target_domain: target,
    rank_absolute: best,
    found: best != null,
    location_code: location_code || creds.defaultLocation,
  };
}

/**
 * Batch SERP rank check. Each pair is checked in its own DataForSEO live
 * task — DataForSEO accepts up to 100 tasks per HTTP call.
 *
 * @param {{ pairs: Array<{keyword: string, target_domain: string}>, location_code?: number, depth?: number, userId?: string }} input
 * @returns {Promise<{ results: Array<{keyword:string, target_domain:string, rank_absolute:number|null}>, errors: Array<{i:number, error:string}> }>}
 */
export async function checkSerpRanks(input = {}, userId) {
  const { pairs, location_code, depth = 100 } = input;
  if (!Array.isArray(pairs) || pairs.length === 0) {
    return { results: [], errors: [] };
  }
  const creds = await loadCreds(userId);
  if (!creds) throw new Error("DATAFORSEO_LOGIN/PASSWORD not set");

  const results = new Array(pairs.length).fill(null);
  const errors = [];

  for (let start = 0; start < pairs.length; start += MAX_BATCH) {
    const batch = pairs.slice(start, start + MAX_BATCH);
    const payload = batch.map((p) => ({
      keyword: p.keyword,
      location_code: location_code || creds.defaultLocation,
      language_code: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE,
      depth: Math.min(Math.max(depth, 10), 100),
      device: "desktop",
      os: "windows",
    }));
    let res;
    try {
      res = await postSerp(payload, creds.login, creds.password);
    } catch (e) {
      errors.push({ i: start, error: `network: ${e.message}` });
      continue;
    }
    if (!res.ok) {
      const text = await res.text().catch(() => "");
      errors.push({ i: start, error: `HTTP ${res.status}: ${text.slice(0, 120)}` });
      continue;
    }
    const json = await res.json();
    const tasks = json?.tasks || [];
    for (let i = 0; i < batch.length; i++) {
      const t = tasks[i];
      const items = t?.result?.[0]?.items || [];
      const target = normalizeDomain(batch[i].target_domain);
      let best = null;
      for (const it of items) {
        if (it.type !== "organic") continue;
        if (normalizeDomain(it.domain) === target) {
          if (best == null || it.rank_absolute < best) best = it.rank_absolute;
        }
      }
      results[start + i] = {
        keyword: batch[i].keyword,
        target_domain: target,
        rank_absolute: best,
        found: best != null,
      };
    }
  }
  return { results, errors };
}

/**
 * Return the top-N organic items for a keyword. Useful for competitive
 * landscape inspection (which other vendors are ranking?).
 *
 * @param {{ keyword: string, location_code?: number, depth?: number, userId?: string }} input
 */
export async function fetchSerp(input = {}, userId) {
  const { keyword, location_code, depth = 30 } = input;
  if (!keyword) throw new Error("keyword is required");
  const creds = await loadCreds(userId);
  if (!creds) throw new Error("DATAFORSEO_LOGIN/PASSWORD not set");
  const payload = [
    {
      keyword,
      location_code: location_code || creds.defaultLocation,
      language_code: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE,
      depth: Math.min(Math.max(depth, 10), 100),
      device: "desktop",
      os: "windows",
    },
  ];
  const res = await postSerp(payload, creds.login, creds.password);
  if (!res.ok) {
    const text = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`DataForSEO ${res.status}: ${text.slice(0, 200)}`);
  }
  const json = await res.json();
  if (json.status_code !== 20000) {
    throw new Error(
      `DataForSEO status_code=${json.status_code}: ${json.status_message}`
    );
  }
  const items = (json?.tasks?.[0]?.result?.[0]?.items || [])
    .filter((it) => it.type === "organic")
    .map((it) => ({
      rank_absolute: it.rank_absolute,
      domain: normalizeDomain(it.domain),
      url: it.url,
      title: it.title,
    }));
  return { keyword, items };
}

export async function checkCredentials(input = {}, userId) {
  const creds = await loadCreds(userId);
  if (!creds) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      msg: "DATAFORSEO_LOGIN/PASSWORD not set in profiles.env_vars or process.env",
    };
  }
  // Cheapest credentials check: GET /v3/appendix/user_data
  try {
    const res = await fetch(`${BASE}/appendix/user_data`, {
      headers: { Authorization: authHeader(creds.login, creds.password) },
    });
    if (!res.ok) {
      const text = await res.text();
      return { ok: false, msg: `HTTP ${res.status}: ${text.slice(0, 100)}` };
    }
    const json = await res.json();
    const tasks = json?.tasks || [];
    const balance =
      tasks?.[0]?.data?.money?.balance ?? tasks?.[0]?.result?.[0]?.money?.balance;
    return {
      ok: true,
      msg: `DataForSEO credentials valid${balance != null ? ` — balance: $${balance}` : ""}`,
    };
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, msg: e.message };
  }
}

function postLive(endpoint, payload, login, password) {
  return fetch(`${BASE}/${endpoint}`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: authHeader(login, password),
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify([payload]),
  });
}

/**
 * Mass-screen demand. Google Ads search_volume for a batch of keywords.
 * Returns [{ keyword, search_volume, cpc, competition }]. search_volume is
 * the avg monthly US searches; cpc (USD) is the commercial-intent proxy.
 *
 * @param {{ keywords: string[], location_code?: number, language_code?: string, userId?: string }} input
 */
export async function searchVolume(input = {}, userId) {
  const creds = await loadCreds(userId || input.userId);
  if (!creds) throw new Error("DATAFORSEO_LOGIN/PASSWORD not set");
  const keywords = (input.keywords || []).filter(Boolean).slice(0, 1000);
  if (!keywords.length) return [];
  const payload = {
    keywords,
    location_code: input.location_code || creds.defaultLocation,
    language_code: input.language_code || DEFAULT_LANGUAGE,
  };
  const res = await postLive(
    "keywords_data/google_ads/search_volume/live",
    payload,
    creds.login,
    creds.password,
  );
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}: ${(await res.text()).slice(0, 160)}`);
  const json = await res.json();
  const result = json?.tasks?.[0]?.result || [];
  return result.map((r) => ({
    keyword: r.keyword,
    search_volume: r.search_volume ?? 0,
    cpc: r.cpc ?? 0,
    competition: r.competition ?? null,
  }));
}

/**
 * Topic discovery. DataForSEO Labs keyword_suggestions — long-tail phrases
 * CONTAINING the seed, each with its own search_volume + cpc. Sorted by
 * volume desc. Use to uncover the real question/topic cluster for an FAQ.
 *
 * @param {{ seed: string, limit?: number, location_code?: number, language_code?: string, userId?: string }} input
 */
export async function keywordIdeas(input = {}, userId) {
  const creds = await loadCreds(userId || input.userId);
  if (!creds) throw new Error("DATAFORSEO_LOGIN/PASSWORD not set");
  const seed = String(input.seed || "").trim();
  if (!seed) return { seed: "", ideas: [] };
  const payload = {
    keyword: seed,
    location_code: input.location_code || creds.defaultLocation,
    language_code: input.language_code || DEFAULT_LANGUAGE,
    limit: input.limit || 50,
    order_by: ["keyword_info.search_volume,desc"],
  };
  const res = await postLive(
    "dataforseo_labs/google/keyword_suggestions/live",
    payload,
    creds.login,
    creds.password,
  );
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}: ${(await res.text()).slice(0, 160)}`);
  const json = await res.json();
  const items = json?.tasks?.[0]?.result?.[0]?.items || [];
  const ideas = items.map((it) => ({
    keyword: it.keyword,
    search_volume: it.keyword_info?.search_volume ?? 0,
    cpc: it.keyword_info?.cpc ?? 0,
    competition: it.keyword_info?.competition ?? null,
  }));
  return { seed, ideas };
}
```

```js
/**
 * doStep weapon — Plan B GM orchestration.
 *
 * When GM→MA loose orchestration fails (MA improvises, skips skill books, etc.),
 * GM switches to doStep. Each step dispatches a specific, narrow MA type via a
 * dedicated instruction file (CLAUDE-SCRIBE.md, CLAUDE-SAGE.md, etc.).
 *
 * The weapon:
 *   1. Validates stepId against the STEPS registry
 *   2. Reads the MA instruction file for that step
 *   3. Prepends the step-specific handshake
 *   4. Validates input artifact against the step's input schema
 *   5. Returns { prompt, stepId, maType, warnings } for GM to dispatch via Agent()
 *   6. Logs the call via weaponLog
 *
 * Step registry: 8 steps covering the full task execution lifecycle.
 * STEP_HANDSHAKE: ##GUILDOS-STEP-DISPATCH-s1r7t##
 */

import { readFileSync, existsSync } from "fs";
import { join } from "path";
import { logWeaponCall } from "../weaponLog/index.js";

const STEP_HANDSHAKE = "##GUILDOS-STEP-DISPATCH-s1r7t##";

const STEPS = {
  1: { maType: "scribe",    file: "CLAUDE-SCRIBE.md",    label: "Clarification",   inputRequired: ["task"] },
  2: { maType: "sage",      file: "CLAUDE-SAGE.md",      label: "Skill Selection", inputRequired: ["task", "clarification"] },
  3: { maType: "architect", file: "CLAUDE-ARCHITECT.md", label: "Planning",        inputRequired: ["task", "clarification", "skillBooks"] },
  4: { maType: "artificer", file: "CLAUDE-ARTIFICER.md", label: "Mockup",          inputRequired: ["task", "plan"] },
  5: { maType: "foreman",   file: "CLAUDE-FOREMAN.md",   label: "Development",     inputRequired: ["task", "plan"] },
  6: { maType: "inspector", file: "CLAUDE-INSPECTOR.md", label: "Verification",    inputRequired: ["task", "artifacts"] },
  7: { maType: "strategist",file: "CLAUDE-STRATEGIST.md","label": "Retry/Recovery",inputRequired: ["task", "failureReport"] },
  8: { maType: "herald",    file: "CLAUDE-HERALD.md",    label: "Reporting",       inputRequired: ["task", "results"] },
};

/**
 * Dispatch a step — validate input, assemble MA prompt, return ready for Agent().
 *
 * @param {{ stepId: number, task: string, initiativeId: string, inputArtifact?: object, agent?: string }} opts
 * @returns {{ prompt: string, stepId: number, maType: string, label: string, warnings: string[], handshake: string } | { error: string }}
 */
export function dispatch({ stepId, task, initiativeId, inputArtifact = {}, agent = "GM" }) {
  const input = { stepId, initiativeId, taskLength: task?.length ?? 0 };
  const warnings = [];

  // ── Validate stepId ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  if (!stepId || !STEPS[stepId]) {
    const result = {
      error: `DOSTEP_ERROR: unknown stepId "${stepId}". Valid steps: ${Object.keys(STEPS).join(", ")}. Each step maps to a specific MA type.`,
    };
    logWeaponCall({ weapon: "doStep", fn: "dispatch", agent, input, output: result, status: "error" });
    return result;
  }

  if (!initiativeId?.trim()) {
    const result = { error: "DOSTEP_ERROR: initiativeId is required — GM assigns it before calling doStep." };
    logWeaponCall({ weapon: "doStep", fn: "dispatch", agent, input, output: result, status: "error" });
    return result;
  }

  if (!task || task.trim().length < 5) {
    const result = { error: "DOSTEP_ERROR: task is required and must be at least 5 characters." };
    logWeaponCall({ weapon: "doStep", fn: "dispatch", agent, input, output: result, status: "error" });
    return result;
  }

  const step = STEPS[stepId];

  // ── Validate inputArtifact fields ────────────────────────────────────────
  // For steps > 1, prior step artifacts are expected in inputArtifact
  const missingFields = step.inputRequired
    .filter(f => f !== "task" && !(f in inputArtifact));

  if (missingFields.length > 0) {
    warnings.push(`Step ${stepId} (${step.label}) expects these input fields that are missing: [${missingFields.join(", ")}]. Proceeding with what's available.`);
  }

  // ── Read MA instruction file ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  const maFilePath = join(process.cwd(), step.file);
  let maInstructions = "";

  if (!existsSync(maFilePath)) {
    warnings.push(`${step.file} not found at ${maFilePath}. MA will run without specialized instructions.`);
  } else {
    try {
      maInstructions = readFileSync(maFilePath, "utf8");
    } catch (e) {
      warnings.push(`Failed to read ${step.file}: ${e.message}`);
    }
  }

  // ── Assemble prompt ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  const artifactBlock = Object.keys(inputArtifact).length > 0
    ? `## Input Artifacts\n\`\`\`json\n${JSON.stringify(inputArtifact, null, 2)}\n\`\`\``
    : "";

  const parts = [
    STEP_HANDSHAKE,
    "",
    maInstructions.trim(),
    "",
    "---",
    `## Step ${stepId} of 8 — ${step.label}`,
    `Initiative ID: ${initiativeId}`,
    "",
    "## Task",
    task.trim(),
    "",
    artifactBlock,
  ].filter(Boolean);

  const prompt = parts.join("\n");

  const result = {
    prompt,
    handshake: STEP_HANDSHAKE,
    stepId,
    maType: step.maType,
    label: step.label,
    maFile: step.file,
    maFileFound: existsSync(maFilePath),
    warnings,
    message: `Step ${stepId} (${step.label} → ${step.maType}) assembled. Dispatch via Agent(prompt). ${warnings.length > 0 ? `${warnings.length} warning(s).` : ""}`,
  };

  logWeaponCall({
    weapon: "doStep",
    fn: "dispatch",
    agent,
    input,
    output: { stepId, maType: step.maType, promptLength: prompt.length, warnings: warnings.length },
    status: "ok",
  });

  return result;
}

/**
 * List all registered steps.
 * @returns {Record<number, { maType, file, label, inputRequired }>}
 */
export function listSteps() {
  return Object.fromEntries(
    Object.entries(STEPS).map(([id, s]) => [id, {
      maType: s.maType,
      file: s.file,
      label: s.label,
      inputRequired: s.inputRequired,
    }])
  );
}

// ── Output schemas per step ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
const OUTPUT_SCHEMAS = {
  1: { required: ["stepId", "maType", "taskTitle", "scope", "successCriteria", "outputLocation", "readyToExecute"] },
  2: { required: ["stepId", "maType", "selectedSkillBooks", "executionOrder", "readyToExecute"] },
  3: { required: ["stepId", "maType", "phases", "artifacts", "readyToExecute"] },
  4: { required: ["stepId", "maType", "mockupArtifacts", "readyToExecute"] },
  5: { required: ["stepId", "maType", "completedActions", "artifacts", "readyToExecute"] },
  6: { required: ["stepId", "maType", "verificationResults", "passed", "readyToExecute"] },
  7: { required: ["stepId", "maType", "retryPlan", "readyToExecute"] },
  8: { required: ["stepId", "maType", "summary", "report"] },
};

/**
 * Validate the JSON output from an MA step.
 * Parses the last line of the MA response as JSON, checks required fields.
 *
 * @param {{ stepId: number, maResponse: string, agent?: string }} opts
 * @returns {{ valid: boolean, parsed?: object, missing?: string[], error?: string }}
 */
export function validateOutput({ stepId, maResponse, agent = "GM" }) {
  const schema = OUTPUT_SCHEMAS[stepId];
  if (!schema) {
    return { valid: false, error: `No output schema defined for stepId ${stepId}` };
  }

  // Extract the OUTERMOST JSON object from the response.
  // Strategy: find the last top-level { ... } block by scanning for
  // the last occurrence of a line that starts with `{` at depth 0.
  const text = maResponse.trim();
  let jsonStr = null;

  // Find all { positions, track depth, extract top-level blocks
  const topLevelBlocks = [];
  let depth = 0;
  let blockStart = -1;
  let inString = false;
  let escape = false;

  for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) {
    const ch = text[i];
    if (escape) { escape = false; continue; }
    if (ch === '\\' && inString) { escape = true; continue; }
    if (ch === '"') { inString = !inString; continue; }
    if (inString) continue;
    if (ch === '{') {
      if (depth === 0) blockStart = i;
      depth++;
    } else if (ch === '}') {
      depth--;
      if (depth === 0 && blockStart >= 0) {
        topLevelBlocks.push(text.slice(blockStart, i + 1));
        blockStart = -1;
      }
    }
  }

  // Use the last top-level block (MA output should be last)
  for (let k = topLevelBlocks.length - 1; k >= 0; k--) {
    try {
      JSON.parse(topLevelBlocks[k]);
      jsonStr = topLevelBlocks[k];
      break;
    } catch { /* keep trying */ }
  }

  if (!jsonStr) {
    logWeaponCall({ weapon: "doStep", fn: "validateOutput", agent, input: { stepId }, output: { error: "no JSON found" }, status: "error" });
    return { valid: false, error: "No valid JSON found in MA response. MA must return a JSON object on the last line." };
  }

  let parsed;
  try {
    parsed = JSON.parse(jsonStr);
  } catch (e) {
    return { valid: false, error: `JSON parse error: ${e.message}` };
  }

  const missing = schema.required.filter(f => !(f in parsed));
  if (missing.length > 0) {
    logWeaponCall({ weapon: "doStep", fn: "validateOutput", agent, input: { stepId }, output: { missing }, status: "error" });
    return { valid: false, parsed, missing, error: `Output missing required fields: [${missing.join(", ")}]` };
  }

  logWeaponCall({ weapon: "doStep", fn: "validateOutput", agent, input: { stepId }, output: { valid: true, fields: Object.keys(parsed) }, status: "ok" });
  return { valid: true, parsed };
}

export const toc = {
  dispatch: "Validate stepId + input, read MA instruction file, assemble gated prompt for Agent(). Input: {stepId, task, initiativeId, inputArtifact?}. Returns {prompt, stepId, maType, label, warnings} or {error}.",
  validateOutput: "Parse and validate MA step output JSON. Input: {stepId, maResponse}. Returns {valid, parsed, missing?, error?}. Checks required fields per step schema.",
  listSteps: "Return registry of all 8 steps: stepId → {maType, file, label, inputRequired}.",
};
```

```markdown
# Engineering Decisions — libs/weapon

## 2026-07-06 · Infra config is env-only (no literal fallbacks) — redacted out of source

- **Decision:** Live infrastructure identifiers consumed by weapons — SSH hosts,
  usernames, ports, private-key file paths, Supabase project URLs, the owner
  email — are read from `process.env.*` with **no literal fallback**, and the
  real values live in the gitignored `.env.local` (documented in `.env.example`).
  Applies to: `bioinvsyncAccess` (`BIOINVSYNC_*`), `ssh` +
  `bosterbio.comLiveSite` (`BOSTER_PROD_*`, `BOSTER_MAGENTO_ROOT`), `cjgeo`
  (`CJGEO_SUPABASE_URL`, `CJGEO_ENV_FILE`), `aws.ensureBudgetAlarm`
  (`GUILDOS_OWNER_EMAIL`). Username-bearing local paths derive from
  `os.homedir()` instead of a hardcoded `C:/Users/<name>/…`.
- **Rejected alternative:** the codebase's usual `process.env.X || "<literal>"`
  idiom. Rejected here because the literal fallback keeps the exact host/key/ref
  in the tracked source — it defeats the point of redaction. Instead each site
  guards on the missing env and throws a message naming the var to set.
- **Why:** the skill books/weapons are being prepared for wider (team, and
  potentially public) access. Source must carry no live hosts, credentials paths,
  or project refs. A guard-and-throw is a strictly better failure mode than a
  silent connection to a stale hardcoded host.
- **Consequence-if-violated:** re-adding a literal fallback (e.g. to "make the
  error go away") silently un-redacts the infra and reintroduces the exact leak
  this pass removed. If a weapon throws "… not configured", the fix is to set the
  var in `.env.local` (see `.env.example`) — NOT to inline the value.
- **Explicit exception:** `libs/proving-grounds/index.js` keeps its hardcoded
  `C:/Users/xsj70/GuildOS2/…` sink path on purpose — see that module's ED (both
  GuildOS and GuildOS2 ship a byte-identical copy and the path must resolve
  identically from both repos with no config). Do not env-var it.
```

```js
/**
 * eventLog weapon — append rows to the curated semantic `event_log` table.
 *
 * The guild's event stream: quest lifecycle transitions (assign / finish /
 * approve / escalate) + adoption/origination events (skill_adopted,
 * gio_implemented). Powers usage-pattern + skill/GIO adoption-impact analysis.
 * Named "event" not "activity" because some rows are pure state facts, not
 * actions someone performed.
 *
 * SEPARATE from caravan_logs (operational cron/caravan liveness, auto-truncated).
 * See supabase/migrations/20260708120000_create_event_log.sql for the rationale
 * and the two event classes.
 *
 * This is CROSS-CUTTING infra (called from libs/quest lifecycle, skillExchange,
 * the GIO→quest path), which is why it lives as a weapon rather than a bare
 * facade file — the registry is the sanctioned home for shared write helpers.
 * Persistence detail (client resolution) is delegated to the database facade.
 */
import { publicTables } from "@/libs/council/publicTables";
import { resolveServerClient } from "@/libs/council/database/resolveServer.js";

/**
 * Append one event row.
 *
 * @param {Object} evt
 * @param {string}  evt.kind          quest_assigned | quest_finished | quest_approved | quest_escalated | quest_created | quest_reassigned | gio_implemented | skill_adopted | ...
 * @param {string} [evt.actor]        agent id / guild / cron / user id
 * @param {"quest"|"skill"|"gio"} [evt.subjectType]
 * @param {string} [evt.subjectId]    quest uuid | skill name | gio id
 * @param {string} [evt.summary]      human-readable one-liner
 * @param {Object} [evt.detail]       analytics payload — for outcome rows: { skills_used, origin, gio_id, duration_ms, escalations }
 * @param {Object} [opts]
 * @param {import("@/libs/council/database/types.js").DatabaseClient} [opts.client] injected client (defaults to server/service resolution)
 */
export async function recordEvent(
  { kind, actor = null, subjectType = null, subjectId = null, summary = "", detail = {} } = {},
  { client: injected } = {},
) {
  if (!kind) throw new Error("recordEvent: `kind` is required");
  const db = await resolveServerClient(injected);
  return db
    .from(publicTables.eventLog)
    .insert({
      kind,
      actor,
      subject_type: subjectType,
      subject_id: subjectId,
      summary,
      detail: detail ?? {},
    })
    .select("id")
    .single();
}

/**
 * Fire-and-forget wrapper for hot lifecycle paths: log the event but NEVER let a
 * logging failure propagate into the quest transition that triggered it. Use this
 * at the lifecycle call-sites; use recordEvent directly only when the caller
 * genuinely wants the insert error surfaced.
 */
export async function recordEventSafe(evt, opts) {
  try {
    return await recordEvent(evt, opts);
  } catch (err) {
    console.error("[event_log] recordEvent failed (non-fatal):", err?.message || err);
    return { data: null, error: err };
  }
}
```

```js
/**
 * Figma weapon — Figma REST API connector for reading files, exporting assets,
 * and listing projects.
 *
 * Auth: FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN from profiles.env_vars or process.env.
 */

export const toc = {
  readFile: "Read a Figma file's document tree.",
  readNodes: "Read specific nodes from a Figma file by id.",
  readExport: "Export images of Figma nodes (PNG/SVG/etc).",
  searchProjects: "Search Figma projects within a team.",
  searchFiles: "Search Figma files within a project.",
  readComments: "Read comments on a Figma file.",
  readPages: "List all pages in a file (defaults to the Boster master file) — id, name, child count.",
  readPage: "Get the full node tree for a single named page.",
  exportFrames: "Export frames/components as image URLs by node id.",
  readComponents: "List all top-level frames/components across every page of a file.",
};
import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";
import { skillActionOk, skillActionErr } from "../../skill_book/actionResult.js";

const API_BASE = "https://api.figma.com/v1";

/**
 * Primary design file — Boster Design Master File. Default for the agent-facing
 * read* helpers below when no fileKey is given.
 * URL: https://www.figma.com/design/NMfOvoGgMVFPYM4nLtN8zD/Boster-Design-Master-File
 */
const PRIMARY_FILE_KEY = "NMfOvoGgMVFPYM4nLtN8zD";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Auth
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async function getToken(userId) {
  if (process.env.FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN) return process.env.FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN;
  if (!userId) return null;
  const db = await database.init("service");
  const { data } = await db
    .from("profiles")
    .select("env_vars")
    .eq("id", userId)
    .single();
  return data?.env_vars?.FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN ?? null;
}

async function figmaFetch(path, opts = {}, userId) {
  const token = await getToken(userId);
  if (!token) throw new Error("Missing FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN");
  const url = path.startsWith("http") ? path : `${API_BASE}${path}`;
  const res = await fetch(url, {
    ...opts,
    headers: {
      "X-Figma-Token": token,
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      ...opts.headers,
    },
  });
  if (!res.ok) {
    const body = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`Figma API ${res.status}: ${body.slice(0, 500)}`);
  }
  return res.json();
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Files
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Read a Figma file's metadata and structure.
 * @param {{ fileKey: string, depth?: number }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function readFile({ fileKey, depth } = {}, userId) {
  if (!fileKey) throw new Error("fileKey is required");
  const params = new URLSearchParams();
  if (depth != null) params.set("depth", String(depth));
  return figmaFetch(`/files/${fileKey}?${params}`, {}, userId);
}

/**
 * Read specific nodes from a Figma file.
 * @param {{ fileKey: string, nodeIds: string[] }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function readNodes({ fileKey, nodeIds } = {}, userId) {
  if (!fileKey) throw new Error("fileKey is required");
  if (!Array.isArray(nodeIds) || nodeIds.length === 0) throw new Error("nodeIds is required");
  const params = new URLSearchParams({ ids: nodeIds.join(",") });
  return figmaFetch(`/files/${fileKey}/nodes?${params}`, {}, userId);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Export
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Export renderings of nodes as images.
 * @param {{ fileKey: string, nodeIds: string[], format?: string, scale?: number }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 * @returns {Promise<{ images: Record<string, string> }>} — node ID to image URL map
 */
export async function readExport({ fileKey, nodeIds, format = "png", scale = 2 } = {}, userId) {
  if (!fileKey) throw new Error("fileKey is required");
  if (!Array.isArray(nodeIds) || nodeIds.length === 0) throw new Error("nodeIds is required");
  const params = new URLSearchParams({
    ids: nodeIds.join(","),
    format,
    scale: String(scale),
  });
  return figmaFetch(`/images/${fileKey}?${params}`, {}, userId);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Projects & Team
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * List projects in a team.
 * @param {{ teamId: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function searchProjects({ teamId } = {}, userId) {
  if (!teamId) throw new Error("teamId is required");
  return figmaFetch(`/teams/${teamId}/projects`, {}, userId);
}

/**
 * List files in a project.
 * @param {{ projectId: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function searchFiles({ projectId } = {}, userId) {
  if (!projectId) throw new Error("projectId is required");
  return figmaFetch(`/projects/${projectId}/files`, {}, userId);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Comments
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Read comments on a file.
 * @param {{ fileKey: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function readComments({ fileKey } = {}, userId) {
  if (!fileKey) throw new Error("fileKey is required");
  return figmaFetch(`/files/${fileKey}/comments`, {}, userId);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Credential check
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export async function checkCredentials(userId) {
  try {
    const token = await getToken(userId);
    if (token) {
      return { ok: true, msg: "FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN is set" };
    }
    return {
      ok: false,
      msg: "Missing FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN — generate a personal access token at figma.com/developers and add it to profile env_vars.",
    };
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, msg: `Error: ${e.message}` };
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Agent-facing read helpers (skillActionOk/Err envelope). Default fileKey is the
// Boster Design Master File. Driven by the `figma` skill book's howTos.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export async function readPages(a, b) {
  const [userId, input] = typeof a === "string" ? [a, b ?? {}] : [undefined, a ?? {}];
  const fileKey = input?.fileKey || PRIMARY_FILE_KEY;
  try {
    const data = await readFile({ fileKey, depth: 1 }, userId);
    const pages = (data?.document?.children || []).map((p) => ({
      id: p.id,
      name: p.name,
      childCount: p.children?.length ?? 0,
    }));
    return skillActionOk({ pages, fileKey });
  } catch (e) {
    return skillActionErr(e.message);
  }
}

export async function readPage(a, b) {
  const [userId, input] = typeof a === "string" ? [a, b ?? {}] : [undefined, a ?? {}];
  if (!input?.pageName) return skillActionErr("pageName required");
  const fileKey = input?.fileKey || PRIMARY_FILE_KEY;
  try {
    const meta = await readFile({ fileKey, depth: 1 }, userId);
    const pages = meta?.document?.children || [];
    const page = pages.find((p) => p.name.toLowerCase() === input.pageName.toLowerCase());
    if (!page) {
      const names = pages.map((p) => p.name).join(", ");
      return skillActionErr(`Page "${input.pageName}" not found. Available: ${names}`);
    }
    const nodes = await readNodes({ fileKey, nodeIds: [page.id] }, userId);
    const pageNode = nodes?.nodes?.[page.id]?.document ?? page;
    return skillActionOk({ page: pageNode, fileKey });
  } catch (e) {
    return skillActionErr(e.message);
  }
}

export async function exportFrames(a, b) {
  const [userId, input] = typeof a === "string" ? [a, b ?? {}] : [undefined, a ?? {}];
  if (!Array.isArray(input?.nodeIds) || input.nodeIds.length === 0)
    return skillActionErr("nodeIds (array) required");
  const fileKey = input?.fileKey || PRIMARY_FILE_KEY;
  try {
    const data = await readExport(
      { fileKey, nodeIds: input.nodeIds, format: input.format ?? "png", scale: input.scale ?? 2 },
      userId
    );
    return skillActionOk({ images: data?.images ?? {}, fileKey });
  } catch (e) {
    return skillActionErr(e.message);
  }
}

export async function readComponents(a, b) {
  const [userId, input] = typeof a === "string" ? [a, b ?? {}] : [undefined, a ?? {}];
  const fileKey = input?.fileKey || PRIMARY_FILE_KEY;
  try {
    const data = await readFile({ fileKey, depth: 2 }, userId);
    const components = [];
    for (const page of data?.document?.children || []) {
      for (const node of page.children || []) {
        components.push({ id: node.id, name: node.name, page: page.name, type: node.type });
      }
    }
    return skillActionOk({ components, fileKey });
  } catch (e) {
    return skillActionErr(e.message);
  }
}
```
