```js
/**
 * Flywheel weapon — control Flywheel-hosted WordPress sites.
 *
 * IMPORTANT — there is NO public Flywheel management API and NO MCP server.
 * The legacy Flywheel platform (app.getflywheel.com) exposes zero customer-
 * facing REST/GraphQL endpoints and no API-token UI (verified 2026-06-03 by
 * exhaustively sweeping MANAGE, the account dropdown, and every /profile tab —
 * ACCOUNT / SECURITY / SSH — none offer tokens or integrations). WP Engine's
 * API (wpengineapi.com) only serves accounts provisioned in the my.wpengine.com
 * portal; this Flywheel account is not migrated there, so it is unavailable.
 *
 * Therefore control is split two ways (HYBRID):
 *   1. Platform settings (backups, staging, notifications, SSH-key mgmt,
 *      privacy gating) — UI-ONLY, driven through CIC. This weapon supplies the
 *      deterministic deep-links; the `flywheel` skill book holds the click map.
 *   2. WordPress-level control (new admin user, plugins, users, content) —
 *      SCRIPTABLE over SSH/WP-CLI through the Flywheel SSH gateway. This weapon
 *      wraps that path via the existing `ssh` weapon.
 *
 * Prerequisite for the SSH/WP-CLI path: an SSH public key must be registered at
 * https://app.getflywheel.com/profile/ssh (none was present as of 2026-06-03 —
 * `addSshKey` howTo in the skill book covers it). The gateway authenticates by
 * key; the system `ssh` (BatchMode) the `ssh` weapon uses then works headless.
 */

import { executeCommand } from "@/libs/weapon/ssh";

export const toc = {
  dashboardUrls: "Build the deterministic Flywheel dashboard deep-links for a site (overview/advanced/backups/staging/wp-admin) + account pages, for CIC navigation.",
  sshCommand: "Return the raw `ssh <org>+<site>@<REDACTED-HOST>` connection command for a site.",
  sshTarget: "Return the {user, host} pair for the Flywheel SSH gateway, for passing to the ssh weapon.",
  wpCli: "Run an arbitrary WP-CLI command on a site over the Flywheel SSH gateway (requires a registered SSH key).",
  createWpAdmin: "Create a new WordPress administrator on a site via WP-CLI over SSH (capability #4).",
  getConnectionInfo: "Return the known SSH/SFTP connection facts (gateway host, SFTP host/port, account username).",
  listKnownSites: "Return the locally-recorded site registry (org slug, domains, staging domain).",
  checkCredentials: "Report whether system ssh is available + the gateway reachability hint.",
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Constants — public infrastructure, safe to hardcode. NO passwords here:
// the SFTP/SSH password is the Flywheel account password (set via the SECURITY
// tab, never stored by the agent); WP-CLI auth is by registered SSH key.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const DASHBOARD = "https://app.getflywheel.com";
const SSH_GATEWAY = "<REDACTED-HOST>"; // per-site gateway: <org>+<site>@<REDACTED-HOST>
const SFTP_HOST = "<REDACTED-HOST>";
const SFTP_PORT = 22;

/**
 * Locally-recorded sites. The org *slug* (used in dashboard URLs) can differ
 * from the SFTP account username — record both. Add new sites here as they are
 * onboarded; this is a convenience cache, not a source of truth (the dashboard
 * is). Verified 2026-06-03.
 */
const KNOWN = {
  account: { username: "cjxia", orgSlug: "sijiexia1" },
  sites: {
    "kyinno-bio-live-site": {
      org: "sijiexia1",
      domain: "www.kyinno.com",
      staging: "<REDACTED-HOST>",
      platform: "cloud",
    },
  },
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Deep-link builder (for CIC navigation)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Build the Flywheel dashboard deep-links for a site, plus the account pages.
 * @param {{ org?: string, site: string }} input
 *   org defaults to the recorded org for a known site, else KNOWN.account.orgSlug.
 * @returns {Record<string, string>}
 */
export function dashboardUrls({ org, site } = {}) {
  if (!site) throw new Error("site (slug) is required");
  const o = org || KNOWN.sites[site]?.org || KNOWN.account.orgSlug;
  const base = `${DASHBOARD}/${o}/${site}`;
  return {
    overview: base,
    plugins: `${base}/plugins`,
    performance: `${base}/performance`,
    stats: `${base}/stats`,
    backups: `${base}/backups`,
    staging: `${base}/staging_site`, // NOTE: tab path is /staging_site, not /staging
    advanced: `${base}/advanced`, // SSH command, staging toggle, email deliverability, multisite, DB
    // Account-level (not site-scoped):
    account: `${DASHBOARD}/profile`,
    security: `${DASHBOARD}/profile/security`, // change account password (== SFTP/SSH password) + 2FA
    sshKeys: `${DASHBOARD}/profile/ssh`, // add/remove SSH public keys
    sites: `${DASHBOARD}/sites`,
    organizations: `${DASHBOARD}/organizations`,
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// SSH / WP-CLI path
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** The gateway login string: `<org>+<site>@<REDACTED-HOST>`. */
export function sshCommand({ org, site } = {}) {
  const { user, host } = sshTarget({ org, site });
  return `ssh ${user}@${host}`;
}

/** {user, host} for the Flywheel SSH gateway — feed to the ssh weapon. */
export function sshTarget({ org, site } = {}) {
  if (!site) throw new Error("site (slug) is required");
  const o = org || KNOWN.sites[site]?.org || KNOWN.account.orgSlug;
  return { user: `${o}+${site}`, host: SSH_GATEWAY };
}

/**
 * Run a WP-CLI command on a site over the Flywheel SSH gateway.
 * Requires a registered SSH key (see skill book `addSshKey`).
 * @param {{ org?: string, site: string, args: string }} input
 *   args: the WP-CLI args *after* `wp`, e.g. "plugin list --status=active".
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function wpCli({ org, site, args } = {}, userId) {
  if (!args) throw new Error("args (the WP-CLI command after `wp`) is required");
  const { user, host } = sshTarget({ org, site });
  return executeCommand({ host, user, command: `wp ${args}` }, userId);
}

/**
 * Create a new WordPress administrator on a site (capability #4).
 * If password is omitted, WP-CLI generates one and prints it (parse stdout).
 * @param {{ org?: string, site: string, username: string, email: string, password?: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function createWpAdmin({ org, site, username, email, password } = {}, userId) {
  if (!username || !email) throw new Error("username and email are required");
  // Quote email; pass --role=administrator. --porcelain prints only the new user ID.
  let args = `user create ${username} ${email} --role=administrator`;
  if (password) args += ` --user_pass='${password}'`;
  args += " --porcelain";
  return wpCli({ org, site, args }, userId);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Facts
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** Known SSH/SFTP connection facts. The password is the Flywheel account password (not stored). */
export function getConnectionInfo() {
  return {
    sshGateway: SSH_GATEWAY,
    sshPerSiteFormat: `ssh <org>+<site>@${SSH_GATEWAY}`,
    sftpHost: SFTP_HOST,
    sftpPort: SFTP_PORT,
    sftpUsername: KNOWN.account.username,
    authNote:
      "SFTP/SSH password == your Flywheel account password (set at /profile/security). " +
      "Headless WP-CLI uses an SSH public key registered at /profile/ssh instead.",
  };
}

/** The locally-recorded site registry. */
export function listKnownSites() {
  return KNOWN;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Credential check
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export async function checkCredentials(userId) {
  try {
    const sites = Object.keys(KNOWN.sites).length;
    // Best-effort: is a key registered for the gateway? We can't know without a
    // site, so just confirm system ssh exists (the ssh weapon enforces the rest).
    const ssh = await executeCommand({ host: "<REDACTED-HOST>", user: "noop", command: "true", timeout: 6000 }, userId).catch(
      (e) => ({ ok: false, stderr: e.message }),
    );
    const keyHint = ssh?.ok
      ? "gateway reachable"
      : "no SSH key registered yet OR gateway unreachable (UI control still works via CIC)";
    return {
      ok: true,
      msg: `Flywheel: UI control via CIC (no API). ${sites} known site(s). SSH/WP-CLI: ${keyHint}.`,
    };
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, msg: `Flywheel weapon error: ${e.message}` };
  }
}
```

```js
/**
 * Extract unsubscribe candidates from a set of Gmail message IDs.
 *
 * Deterministic data-layer behavior — exists in the weapon because it's
 * the same parser logic on every call (OAuth refresh, raw-message fetch,
 * RFC 2369/8058 header parse, HTML anchor extraction by regex). Lives
 * outside the per-message MCP loop because: the MCP `read_email` returns
 * the full decoded body (often >100k chars) and busts agent context
 * before the agent can grep for an unsubscribe URL. This function reads
 * the same raw payload but returns only the unsubscribe candidates —
 * orders of magnitude smaller payload, keeps agent context clean.
 *
 * Auth: reuses the gongrzhe gmail-mcp credential files at
 *   ~/.gmail-mcp/gcp-oauth.keys.json  (client_id, client_secret)
 *   ~/.gmail-mcp/credentials.json     (refresh_token)
 * No new OAuth flow — the MCP refresh token already grants `gmail.readonly`.
 *
 * @param {string[]} messageIds  Gmail message IDs (not thread IDs)
 * @param {object}   [opts]
 * @param {string}   [opts.gmailDir]    override creds dir (default ~/.gmail-mcp)
 * @param {function} [opts.fetchImpl]   fetch override (tests)
 * @returns {Promise<Array<{
 *   id: string,
 *   from?: string,
 *   subject?: string,
 *   oneClick?: boolean,           // true if List-Unsubscribe-Post header present
 *   listUnsubUrls?: string[],     // RFC 2369 URLs from List-Unsubscribe
 *   listUnsubMailtos?: string[],  // mailto: tokens from List-Unsubscribe
 *   anchors?: Array<{href:string,text:string}>,  // HTML anchors matching UNSUB_RX
 *   error?: string
 * }>>}
 */
export async function extractUnsubscribeLinks(messageIds, opts = {}) {
  const fs = await import("node:fs");
  const path = await import("node:path");
  const os = await import("node:os");

  const fetchImpl =
    opts.fetchImpl || (typeof fetch !== "undefined" ? fetch : null);
  if (!fetchImpl) throw new Error("no fetch implementation available");

  const gmailDir = opts.gmailDir || path.join(os.homedir(), ".gmail-mcp");
  const keysPath = path.join(gmailDir, "gcp-oauth.keys.json");
  const credPath = path.join(gmailDir, "credentials.json");

  const keys = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(keysPath, "utf8"));
  const creds = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(credPath, "utf8"));
  const installed = keys.installed || keys.web || keys;

  const tokenRes = await fetchImpl("https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token", {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" },
    body: new URLSearchParams({
      client_id: installed.client_id,
      client_secret: installed.client_secret,
      refresh_token: creds.refresh_token,
      grant_type: "refresh_token",
    }).toString(),
  });
  if (!tokenRes.ok) {
    throw new Error(`gmail oauth refresh: ${tokenRes.status} ${await tokenRes.text()}`);
  }
  const { access_token: accessToken } = await tokenRes.json();

  const results = [];
  for (const id of messageIds) {
    try {
      const r = await fetchImpl(
        `https://gmail.googleapis.com/gmail/v1/users/me/messages/${id}?format=full`,
        { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` } }
      );
      if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`fetch ${id}: ${r.status} ${await r.text()}`);
      const msg = await r.json();
      const headers = msg.payload?.headers || [];
      const from = getHeader(headers, "From") || "?";
      const subject = getHeader(headers, "Subject") || "?";
      const listUnsub = parseListUnsub(getHeader(headers, "List-Unsubscribe"));
      const oneClick = !!getHeader(headers, "List-Unsubscribe-Post");
      const body = collectBody(msg.payload);
      const anchors = extractAnchors(body);
      results.push({
        id,
        from,
        subject,
        oneClick,
        listUnsubUrls: listUnsub.urls,
        listUnsubMailtos: listUnsub.mailtos,
        anchors: anchors.slice(0, 5),
      });
    } catch (e) {
      results.push({ id, error: e.message });
    }
  }
  return results;
}

const UNSUB_RX =
  /unsubscribe|opt[\s\-_]?out|email\s*preferences|manage\s+(your\s+)?preferences|preference\s*center|stop\s+(receiving|these)/i;

function getHeader(headers, name) {
  const h = (headers || []).find(
    (x) => x.name.toLowerCase() === name.toLowerCase()
  );
  return h ? h.value : null;
}

function decode(data) {
  if (!data) return "";
  return Buffer.from(
    data.replace(/-/g, "+").replace(/_/g, "/"),
    "base64"
  ).toString("utf8");
}

function collectBody(payload) {
  const out = [];
  const walk = (p) => {
    if (!p) return;
    if (p.mimeType === "text/html" && p.body?.data) out.push(decode(p.body.data));
    if (p.mimeType === "text/plain" && p.body?.data) out.push(decode(p.body.data));
    (p.parts || []).forEach(walk);
  };
  walk(payload);
  return out.join("\n");
}

function parseListUnsub(value) {
  if (!value) return { urls: [], mailtos: [] };
  const tokens = value.match(/<([^>]+)>/g) || [];
  const urls = [];
  const mailtos = [];
  for (const t of tokens) {
    const v = t.slice(1, -1);
    if (v.startsWith("mailto:")) mailtos.push(v);
    else urls.push(v);
  }
  return { urls, mailtos };
}

function extractAnchors(html) {
  const out = [];
  const re = /<a\b[^>]*?href\s*=\s*(["'])(.*?)\1[^>]*>([\s\S]*?)<\/a>/gi;
  let m;
  while ((m = re.exec(html)) !== null) {
    const href = m[2].trim();
    const text = m[3].replace(/<[^>]+>/g, " ").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
    if (!href || href.startsWith("#") || href.startsWith("mailto:?")) continue;
    if (UNSUB_RX.test(href) || UNSUB_RX.test(text)) {
      out.push({ href, text: text.slice(0, 80) });
    }
  }
  // Plain-text URLs near the word unsubscribe (for text/plain bodies)
  const plain = html.replace(/<[^>]+>/g, " ");
  const lines = plain.split(/\r?\n/);
  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
    if (!UNSUB_RX.test(lines[i])) continue;
    const ctx = lines.slice(Math.max(0, i - 1), i + 2).join(" ");
    const urlRe = /https?:\/\/[^\s)<>"']+/g;
    let u;
    while ((u = urlRe.exec(ctx)) !== null) {
      const url = u[0].replace(/[.,;:!?\)\]]+$/, "");
      if (!out.find((x) => x.href === url)) {
        out.push({
          href: url,
          text: `[plain] ${lines[i].slice(0, 80).trim()}`,
        });
      }
    }
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Pick the single best unsubscribe URL per result, ranked: header URL >
 * highest-scoring anchor > mailto. Returns a slim row array suitable for
 * a markdown table or CSV.
 *
 * @param {Array} results  output of extractUnsubscribeLinks
 * @returns {Array<{id,from,sender,subject,url,source,oneClick}>}
 */
export function pickBestUnsubscribeLink(results) {
  const rows = [];
  for (const r of results) {
    if (r.error) {
      rows.push({ id: r.id, from: "?", sender: "", subject: "(error)", url: r.error, source: "err", oneClick: false });
      continue;
    }
    const fromName = (r.from || "").replace(/<.*>/, "").replace(/"/g, "").trim();
    const sender = r.from?.match(/<([^>]+)>/)?.[1] || "";
    let url = r.listUnsubUrls?.[0];
    let source = "header";
    if (!url && r.anchors?.length) {
      const ranked = r.anchors
        .map((a) => {
          let score = 0;
          if (/unsubscribe/i.test(a.text)) score += 10;
          if (/unsubscribe/i.test(a.href)) score += 5;
          if (/opt[\s\-_]?out/i.test(a.text + a.href)) score += 5;
          if (/preferences/i.test(a.text)) score += 2;
          return { ...a, score };
        })
        .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score);
      url = ranked[0]?.href;
      source = "body";
    }
    if (!url && r.listUnsubMailtos?.length) {
      url = r.listUnsubMailtos[0];
      source = "mailto";
    }
    rows.push({
      id: r.id,
      from: fromName,
      sender,
      subject: (r.subject || "").slice(0, 80),
      url: url || "(none found)",
      source,
      oneClick: !!r.oneClick,
    });
  }
  return rows;
}
```

```js
/**
 * Gmail weapon — unsubscribe parsers only.
 *
 * The only runtime logic here is the pair of context-budget-beating
 * unsubscribe parsers. The MCP `read_email` returns the fully decoded body,
 * which on marketing emails is routinely 100k+ chars and exceeds the agent
 * context window before the agent can grep for what it needs. For
 * deterministic parses where the agent only wants a small slice of each
 * message (e.g. unsubscribe URLs), the weapon exports a CLI-callable function
 * that fetches the raw payload via the Gmail REST API directly and returns
 * just the slice. Same OAuth surface (gongrzhe gmail-mcp credential files),
 * no new auth, just a smaller return value.
 *
 * Everything else Gmail-related (MCP setup, OAuth scopes, the full
 * `mcp__gmail__*` tool catalog, triage/read/label procedures) is text and
 * lives in the gmail SKILL BOOK (`libs/skill_book/gmail/index.js`).
 */

export { extractUnsubscribeLinks, pickBestUnsubscribeLink } from "./extractUnsubscribeLinks.js";

export const toc = {
  // Most Gmail actions are MCP tools, not weapon exports. Agents discover
  // those via the MCP server at connection time. Exports below are the
  // context-budget exceptions only (see header comment for rationale).
  extractUnsubscribeLinks:
    "Fetch raw bodies of given message IDs via Gmail REST, return only the unsubscribe candidates per message (List-Unsubscribe header URLs/mailtos + body anchors matching the unsubscribe regex). Same OAuth as MCP; reuses ~/.gmail-mcp/credentials.json. CLI wrapper: scripts/_extract-unsubscribe-links.mjs.",
  pickBestUnsubscribeLink:
    "Reduce extractUnsubscribeLinks output to one best URL per message (header > best anchor > mailto), suitable for a markdown table.",
};
```

```js

export const toc = {
  readAccount: "Read the Google Merchant Center account info.",
  readProducts: "Read products from the Merchant Center feed.",
  readOrders: "Read orders from the Merchant Center.",
};
import { getGoogleCredentials } from "@/libs/council/profileEnvVars";
import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";

const BASE = "https://shoppingcontent.googleapis.com/content/v2.1";
const TOKEN_URL = "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token";
const SCOPE = "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/content";

async function resolveUserId(explicit) {
  if (explicit) return explicit;
  try {
    const { getAdventurerExecutionUserId } = await import("@/libs/adventurer/advance.js");
    const ctxId = getAdventurerExecutionUserId();
    if (ctxId) return ctxId;
  } catch { /* not in adventurer context */ }
  const { requireUser } = await import("@/libs/council/auth/server");
  const user = await requireUser();
  return user.id;
}

async function loadMerchantId(userId) {
  if (userId) {
    try {
      const db = await database.init("service");
      const { data } = await db.from("profiles").select("env_vars").eq("id", userId).single();
      const m = data?.env_vars?.GOOGLE_MERCHANT_ID;
      if (m) return m;
    } catch { /* fall through */ }
  }
  return process.env.GOOGLE_MERCHANT_ID || null;
}

async function getServiceAccountKey(userId) {
  const creds = await getGoogleCredentials(userId);
  const raw = creds.serviceAccountJson;
  if (!raw) throw new Error("GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT is not set in profiles.env_vars or process.env.");
  const key = typeof raw === "string" ? JSON.parse(raw) : raw;
  if (!key.client_email || !key.private_key) {
    throw new Error("GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT missing client_email or private_key.");
  }
  return key;
}

async function getAccessToken(userId) {
  const key = await getServiceAccountKey(userId);
  const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
  const header = { alg: "RS256", typ: "JWT" };
  const payload = {
    iss: key.client_email,
    scope: SCOPE,
    aud: key.token_uri || TOKEN_URL,
    iat: now,
    exp: now + 3600,
  };
  const enc = (obj) => Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(obj)).toString("base64url");
  const unsigned = `${enc(header)}.${enc(payload)}`;
  const crypto = await import("node:crypto");
  const sign = crypto.createSign("RSA-SHA256");
  sign.update(unsigned);
  const signature = sign.sign(key.private_key, "base64url");
  const jwt = `${unsigned}.${signature}`;

  const res = await fetch(key.token_uri || TOKEN_URL, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" },
    body: `grant_type=urn%3Aietf%3Aparams%3Aoauth%3Agrant-type%3Ajwt-bearer&assertion=${jwt}`,
  });
  if (!res.ok) {
    const text = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`Token exchange failed (${res.status}): ${text}`);
  }
  const data = await res.json();
  return data.access_token;
}

async function request(path, userId, params = {}) {
  const token = await getAccessToken(userId);
  const url = new URL(`${BASE}${path}`);
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(params)) {
    if (v !== undefined && v !== null) url.searchParams.set(k, String(v));
  }
  const res = await fetch(url.toString(), {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
  });
  if (!res.ok) {
    const text = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`Merchant Center ${path} failed (${res.status}): ${text}`);
  }
  return res.json();
}

export async function readAccount({ merchantId } = {}, userId) {
  const uid = await resolveUserId(userId);
  const mid = merchantId || await loadMerchantId(uid);
  if (!mid) throw new Error("merchantId required — set GOOGLE_MERCHANT_ID");
  return request(`/${mid}/accounts/${mid}`, uid);
}

export async function readProducts({ merchantId, maxResults = 10 } = {}, userId) {
  const uid = await resolveUserId(userId);
  const mid = merchantId || await loadMerchantId(uid);
  if (!mid) throw new Error("merchantId required — set GOOGLE_MERCHANT_ID");
  return request(`/${mid}/products`, uid, { maxResults });
}

export async function readOrders({ merchantId, maxResults = 10 } = {}, userId) {
  const uid = await resolveUserId(userId);
  const mid = merchantId || await loadMerchantId(uid);
  if (!mid) throw new Error("merchantId required — set GOOGLE_MERCHANT_ID");
  return request(`/${mid}/orders`, uid, { maxResults });
}

export async function checkCredentials(userId) {
  try {
    const uid = await resolveUserId(userId);
    const creds = await getGoogleCredentials(uid);
    if (!creds.serviceAccountJson) {
      return { ok: false, msg: "GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT not set in profiles.env_vars or process.env" };
    }
    const mid = await loadMerchantId(uid);
    if (!mid) {
      return { ok: false, msg: "GOOGLE_MERCHANT_ID not set in profiles.env_vars or process.env" };
    }
    await getAccessToken(uid);
    return { ok: true, msg: `Merchant Center credentials valid (merchant ${mid})` };
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, msg: e.message };
  }
}
```

<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: libs/weapon/guildKeys/engineering_decisions.md -->
```markdown
# guildKeys — Engineering Decisions

## 2026-07-04 — Per-owner revocable API keys REPLACE the single shared CARAVAN_SECRET for external tick pings

**Decision:** External authenticated pings to GuildOS API routes (`/api/quest/tick`,
`/api/caravan/tick`, …) authenticate with a **per-owner, individually-revocable
GuildOS API key** (`gos_…` bearer, minted in council-hall/api-keys), verified by
`guildKeys.verifyKey`. The key ACTS AS its owner — routes owner-gate the target
quest to the key's `owner_id`, identical to how a UI session gates to the user id.
The dual-auth resolver is `libs/council/auth/server.js → resolvePrincipal`
(API-key → legacy secret → session cookie, in that order).

**Rejected alternative:** Reusing the existing single shared `CARAVAN_SECRET` /
`CRON_SECRET` env value as the machine bearer (the native default — the caravan
get/lease and quest/mutate?batch routes already do exactly this with
`provided !== expected`, so the obvious move is to copy that one-liner into the
tick routes and be done).

**Why:** The shared-secret pattern is a single ownerless superuser token: it
can't be attributed to a guild, can't be rotated without coordinating every
consumer, can't be revoked individually, and grants access to ALL owners' quests.
GuildOS's thesis is heterogeneous guilds each on their own infra — that needs
keys that (a) belong to a specific owner so a machine ping is naturally scoped to
that owner's quests, (b) can be revoked one at a time, and (c) are stored as a
one-way hash so a DB leak doesn't expose live secrets. The legacy secret is kept
in `resolvePrincipal` ONLY as an ownerless bypass for back-compat with the
existing caravan/cron consumers; new external drivers should use a `gos_` key.

**Consequence-if-violated:** If a future agent "simplifies" the tick routes back
to a bare `CARAVAN_SECRET` compare, GuildOS loses per-guild attribution,
revocation, and owner-scoping — one leaked env value would grant tick access to
every owner's pipeline, and rotating it would silently break every guild at once.

## 2026-07-04 — Raw key lives in the GUILD env; only its hash lives in the GuildOS DB

**Decision:** The raw `gos_…` key is returned exactly ONCE (by `mintKey` / the
POST mint route) and is thereafter unrecoverable. GuildOS persists only
`sha256(raw)` in `public.guildos_api_keys`. The **guild** holds the raw key in
its own environment (`GUILDOS_API_KEY` in the guild's `.env.local`); the
**GuildOS quest DB** holds the hash. This split is the operator's stated model:
"the guild should hold it in env, while GuildOS quest holds it in database."

**Rejected alternative:** Storing the key (or a reversibly-encrypted form) in the
DB so the UI can re-display it, or reading it back for the guild — the native
convenience move so a user who lost the key can look it up.

**Why:** A key you can read back is a key a DB compromise hands over intact.
One-way hashing means the stored form is useless to an attacker and forces the
correct operational discipline (the secret lives only where it's used — the
guild's env). Recovery is deliberately impossible: lost key → revoke + re-mint.

**Consequence-if-violated:** Reintroducing recoverable storage turns a routine DB
read (or leak) into full credential disclosure for every guild, and erodes the
env-vs-database boundary that keeps the secret off the GuildOS control plane.
```

<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: libs/weapon/guildKeys/index.js -->
```js
/**
 * @file guildKeys — GuildOS machine API keys (mint / list / revoke / verify).
 *
 * The capability behind "external authenticated pings" to GuildOS API routes.
 * A key is a bearer token of the form `gos_<40 hex>`. Only its sha256 hash is
 * ever stored (table public.guildos_api_keys); the raw string is returned ONCE
 * at mint time and thereafter unrecoverable. Routes authenticate a request by
 * passing the incoming `Authorization: Bearer gos_…` value to `verifyKey`.
 *
 * Owner model: every key belongs to a user (owner_id). A machine ping
 * authenticated by that key acts AS that owner — routes owner-gate the target
 * quest to the key's owner_id, exactly as a UI session gates to the user id.
 */
import crypto from "node:crypto";
import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";
import { publicTables } from "@/libs/council/publicTables";

export const toc = {
  id: "guildKeys",
  owns:
    "GuildOS machine API keys: mint/list/revoke per-owner bearer tokens and verify an incoming Authorization bearer for external authenticated pings to API routes (tick, caravan, …).",
  mintKey: "Create a new API key for an owner; returns the raw key ONCE (store it in the guild env).",
  listKeys: "List an owner's keys (metadata only — never the raw key or hash).",
  revokeKey: "Revoke (soft-delete) one of an owner's keys by id.",
  verifyKey:
    "Authenticate an incoming raw bearer: returns { ok, ownerId, keyId, scopes } and stamps last_used_at. Used by API routes to accept machine pings.",
};

const KEY_PREFIX = "gos_";
const PREFIX_DISPLAY_LEN = KEY_PREFIX.length + 8; // e.g. "gos_a1b2c3d4"

/** sha256 hex of the raw key — the only form persisted. */
function hashKey(raw) {
  return crypto.createHash("sha256").update(String(raw)).digest("hex");
}

/** Generate a fresh key. Returns { raw, prefix, hash }. */
function generateKey() {
  const raw = KEY_PREFIX + crypto.randomBytes(20).toString("hex"); // gos_ + 40 hex
  return { raw, prefix: raw.slice(0, PREFIX_DISPLAY_LEN), hash: hashKey(raw) };
}

/**
 * Mint a new API key for an owner.
 * @param {object} input
 * @param {string} input.ownerId  auth.users.id the key acts as
 * @param {string} input.name     human label
 * @param {string[]} [input.scopes]  default ['tick']
 * @returns {Promise<{ ok:boolean, key?:{ id, name, prefix, scopes, created_at, raw }, error?:string }>}
 *          `raw` is present ONLY here — the one and only time it can be read.
 */
export async function mintKey({ ownerId, name, scopes } = {}) {
  if (!ownerId) return { ok: false, error: "ownerId is required" };
  const label = typeof name === "string" && name.trim() ? name.trim() : "Unnamed key";
  const scopeList = Array.isArray(scopes) && scopes.length ? scopes.map(String) : ["tick"];
  const { raw, prefix, hash } = generateKey();
  const svc = await database.init("service");
  const { data, error } = await svc
    .from(publicTables.guildosApiKeys)
    .insert({ owner_id: ownerId, name: label, key_prefix: prefix, key_hash: hash, scopes: scopeList })
    .select("id, name, key_prefix, scopes, created_at")
    .single();
  if (error) return { ok: false, error: error.message };
  return {
    ok: true,
    key: { id: data.id, name: data.name, prefix: data.key_prefix, scopes: data.scopes, created_at: data.created_at, raw },
  };
}

/**
 * List an owner's keys (no secret material).
 * @param {object} input
 * @param {string} input.ownerId
 * @param {boolean} [input.includeRevoked=false]
 */
export async function listKeys({ ownerId, includeRevoked = false } = {}) {
  if (!ownerId) return { ok: false, error: "ownerId is required", keys: [] };
  const svc = await database.init("service");
  let q = svc
    .from(publicTables.guildosApiKeys)
    .select("id, name, key_prefix, scopes, last_used_at, revoked_at, created_at")
    .eq("owner_id", ownerId)
    .order("created_at", { ascending: false });
  if (!includeRevoked) q = q.is("revoked_at", null);
  const { data, error } = await q;
  if (error) return { ok: false, error: error.message, keys: [] };
  return { ok: true, keys: data || [] };
}

/**
 * Revoke one of an owner's keys. Owner-scoped: a caller can only revoke its own.
 * @param {object} input
 * @param {string} input.ownerId
 * @param {string} input.id  key id
 */
export async function revokeKey({ ownerId, id } = {}) {
  if (!ownerId || !id) return { ok: false, error: "ownerId and id are required" };
  const svc = await database.init("service");
  const { data, error } = await svc
    .from(publicTables.guildosApiKeys)
    .update({ revoked_at: new Date().toISOString() })
    .eq("id", id)
    .eq("owner_id", ownerId)
    .is("revoked_at", null)
    .select("id")
    .maybeSingle();
  if (error) return { ok: false, error: error.message };
  if (!data) return { ok: false, error: "Key not found (or already revoked)" };
  return { ok: true, id: data.id };
}

/**
 * Authenticate an incoming raw bearer string. Accepts the raw key with or
 * without a leading "Bearer ". Returns the acting owner on success.
 * Stamps last_used_at (best-effort, non-blocking on failure).
 * @param {string} rawBearer
 * @returns {Promise<{ ok:boolean, ownerId?:string, keyId?:string, scopes?:string[], error?:string }>}
 */
export async function verifyKey(rawBearer) {
  const raw = String(rawBearer || "").replace(/^Bearer\s+/i, "").trim();
  if (!raw || !raw.startsWith(KEY_PREFIX)) return { ok: false, error: "not a GuildOS API key" };
  const svc = await database.init("service");
  const { data, error } = await svc
    .from(publicTables.guildosApiKeys)
    .select("id, owner_id, scopes, revoked_at")
    .eq("key_hash", hashKey(raw))
    .maybeSingle();
  if (error) return { ok: false, error: error.message };
  if (!data) return { ok: false, error: "unknown key" };
  if (data.revoked_at) return { ok: false, error: "key revoked" };
  // Stamp usage; do not fail the request if this write hiccups.
  svc
    .from(publicTables.guildosApiKeys)
    .update({ last_used_at: new Date().toISOString() })
    .eq("id", data.id)
    .then(() => {}, () => {});
  return { ok: true, ownerId: data.owner_id, keyId: data.id, scopes: data.scopes || [] };
}

/** True for a bearer string that looks like a GuildOS API key (cheap, no DB). */
export function isGuildKey(rawBearer) {
  return String(rawBearer || "").replace(/^Bearer\s+/i, "").trim().startsWith(KEY_PREFIX);
}
```

```js
export const toc = {
  searchContacts: "Search HighLevel CRM contacts.",
  readContact: "Read a single HighLevel contact by id.",
  searchOpportunities: "Search HighLevel pipeline opportunities.",
  writeContact: "Create or update a HighLevel contact.",
};
import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";

const BASE = "https://rest.gohighlevel.com/v1";

async function loadKey(userId) {
  if (userId) {
    try {
      const db = await database.init("service");
      const { data } = await db.from("profiles").select("env_vars").eq("id", userId).single();
      const k = data?.env_vars?.HIGHLEVEL_API_KEY;
      if (k) return k;
    } catch { /* fall through */ }
  }
  return process.env.HIGHLEVEL_API_KEY || null;
}

async function request(method, path, key, params = {}, body) {
  const url = new URL(`${BASE}${path}`);
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(params)) {
    if (v !== undefined && v !== null) url.searchParams.set(k, String(v));
  }
  const opts = {
    method,
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${key}`,
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
  };
  if (body !== undefined) opts.body = JSON.stringify(body);
  const res = await fetch(url.toString(), opts);
  if (!res.ok) {
    const text = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`HighLevel ${method} ${path} failed (${res.status}): ${text}`);
  }
  return res.json();
}

export async function searchContacts({ query, limit = 20 } = {}, userId) {
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) throw new Error("HIGHLEVEL_API_KEY not set");
  return request("GET", "/contacts/search", key, { query, limit });
}

export async function readContact({ id } = {}, userId) {
  if (!id) throw new Error('"id" is required');
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) throw new Error("HIGHLEVEL_API_KEY not set");
  return request("GET", `/contacts/${id}`, key);
}

export async function searchOpportunities({ pipelineId, limit = 20 } = {}, userId) {
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) throw new Error("HIGHLEVEL_API_KEY not set");
  const params = { limit };
  if (pipelineId) params.pipelineId = pipelineId;
  return request("GET", "/opportunities/search", key, params);
}

export async function writeContact({ email, firstName, lastName, phone } = {}, userId) {
  if (!email) throw new Error('"email" is required');
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) throw new Error("HIGHLEVEL_API_KEY not set");
  return request("POST", "/contacts/", key, {}, { email, firstName, lastName, phone });
}

export async function checkCredentials(input = {}, userId) {
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) return { ok: false, msg: "HIGHLEVEL_API_KEY not set in profiles.env_vars or process.env" };
  try {
    await request("GET", "/contacts/search", key, { limit: 1 });
    return { ok: true, msg: "HighLevel credentials valid" };
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, msg: e.message };
  }
}
```

```markdown
# IMAP weapon — Engineering Decisions

- **2026-07-06 · Weapon actions resolve their owner via `resolveImapUserId()` →
  `explicit || process.env.PIGEON_POST_OWNER_ID`, NOT a plain `userId` arg.**
  Rejected alternative: rely on the `userId` positional (the shape the original
  `readMessages(input, userId)` used). Why: `run-action.mjs` invokes *weapon*
  functions as `fn(input)` and does **not** forward any userId (only skill-book
  actions get `PIGEON_POST_OWNER_ID`). `IMAP_ACCOUNTS` lives in
  `profiles.env_vars` (keyed by owner id), *not* in `process.env`, so with no
  userId `loadAccounts()` silently returns `{}` and every call fails with "No
  IMAP credentials". Consequence if violated: strip the env fallback and all
  CLI-invoked IMAP actions break with an empty-account error that looks like a
  credentials-missing problem but isn't.

- **2026-07-06 · Invoke this weapon's CLI with `node --env-file=.env.local
  libs/adventurer/run-action.mjs imap …`.** Rejected alternative: bare `node
  libs/adventurer/run-action.mjs …`. Why: run-action only does
  `import "dotenv/config"` (loads `.env`, which does not carry our secrets);
  `PIGEON_POST_OWNER_ID` and the service-role keys live in `.env.local`. Without
  `--env-file=.env.local` the owner id is unset, `resolveImapUserId` finds
  nothing, and account resolution returns empty. Consequence if violated: the
  action "works" (exit 0) but returns zero accounts / zero results.
```

```js
/**
 * IMAP weapon — read email from IMAP mailboxes via imapflow.
 *
 * Credentials stored in env_vars as IMAP_ACCOUNTS (JSON map of email → password)
 * or IMAP_SERVER / IMAP_PORT for server overrides.
 *
 * Default server: imappro.zoho.com:993 (Zoho Mail Pro)
 */

export const toc = {
  readMessages: "Read messages from an IMAP mailbox (e.g. Zoho Mail Pro).",
  searchBySubject: "Server-side IMAP SEARCH for messages whose Subject contains a phrase; returns matching {uid, subject, from, date}. Use to locate a specific ticket email by title.",
  readBody: "Fetch and decode one message's body (text/plain preferred, html stripped as fallback) by uid. Use after searchBySubject to grab a ticket's actual reply content.",
  searchAccounts: "Search configured IMAP accounts for the user.",
};
import { ImapFlow } from "imapflow";
import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";

const DEFAULT_SERVER = "imappro.zoho.com";
const DEFAULT_PORT = 993;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Credential loading
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Load IMAP accounts from env_vars or process.env.
 * Returns map of { email: password }.
 */
async function loadAccounts(userId) {
  // Try user profile env_vars first
  if (userId) {
    try {
      const db = await database.init("service");
      const { data } = await db.from("profiles").select("env_vars").eq("id", userId).single();
      const raw = data?.env_vars?.IMAP_ACCOUNTS;
      if (raw) return JSON.parse(raw);
    } catch { /* fall through */ }
  }
  // Fall back to process.env
  if (process.env.IMAP_ACCOUNTS) {
    return JSON.parse(process.env.IMAP_ACCOUNTS);
  }
  return {};
}

function getServer(userId) {
  return {
    host: process.env.IMAP_SERVER ?? DEFAULT_SERVER,
    port: Number(process.env.IMAP_PORT ?? DEFAULT_PORT),
  };
}

/**
 * Resolve the userId whose profile holds IMAP_ACCOUNTS.
 * run-action.mjs invokes weapon functions as fn(input) WITHOUT forwarding a
 * userId, so an explicit userId is rarely present — fall back to the
 * PIGEON_POST_OWNER_ID the harness already loads from .env.local, which is the
 * same owner run-action uses for skill-book actions. Without this, loadAccounts
 * sees no userId, skips the DB, and finds no creds (IMAP_ACCOUNTS is not in
 * process.env — it lives in profiles.env_vars).
 */
function resolveImapUserId(explicit) {
  return explicit || process.env.PIGEON_POST_OWNER_ID || undefined;
}

/** Collect a Readable stream into a utf8 string. */
async function streamToString(stream) {
  if (!stream) return "";
  const chunks = [];
  for await (const chunk of stream) chunks.push(Buffer.isBuffer(chunk) ? chunk : Buffer.from(chunk));
  return Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8");
}

/**
 * Walk an imapflow bodyStructure to find the best text leaf part.
 * Prefers text/plain (or text/html when preferHtml), else the first text/* leaf.
 * Returns { part, type } or null (single-part message with no part specifier).
 */
function pickTextPart(node, preferHtml) {
  const wantFirst = preferHtml ? "text/html" : "text/plain";
  const wantSecond = preferHtml ? "text/plain" : "text/html";
  const leaves = [];
  (function walk(n) {
    if (!n) return;
    if (Array.isArray(n.childNodes) && n.childNodes.length) {
      n.childNodes.forEach(walk);
    } else if (typeof n.type === "string" && n.type.startsWith("text/")) {
      leaves.push({ part: n.part, type: n.type });
    }
  })(node);
  return (
    leaves.find((l) => l.type === wantFirst) ||
    leaves.find((l) => l.type === wantSecond) ||
    leaves[0] ||
    null
  );
}

/** Minimal HTML → text: drop scripts/styles, convert breaks, strip tags, decode a few entities. */
function stripHtml(html) {
  return String(html)
    .replace(/<(script|style)[\s\S]*?<\/\1>/gi, "")
    .replace(/<\s*br\s*\/?>/gi, "\n")
    .replace(/<\/\s*(p|div|tr|li|h[1-6])\s*>/gi, "\n")
    .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, "")
    .replace(/&nbsp;/gi, " ")
    .replace(/&amp;/gi, "&")
    .replace(/&lt;/gi, "<")
    .replace(/&gt;/gi, ">")
    .replace(/&quot;/gi, '"')
    .replace(/&#39;/gi, "'")
    .replace(/\n{3,}/g, "\n\n")
    .trim();
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Core
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Open an IMAP connection, run callback, then close.
 */
async function withClient(email, password, fn) {
  const { host, port } = getServer();
  const client = new ImapFlow({
    host,
    port,
    secure: true,
    auth: { user: email, pass: password },
    logger: false,
  });
  await client.connect();
  try {
    return await fn(client);
  } finally {
    await client.logout();
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Actions
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Read recent messages from an IMAP inbox.
 * @param {{ email: string, limit?: number, folder?: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function readMessages({ email, limit = 5, folder = "INBOX", userId } = {}, userIdArg) {
  if (!email) throw new Error('"email" is required');

  const accounts = await loadAccounts(resolveImapUserId(userId ?? userIdArg));
  const password = accounts[email];
  if (!password) throw new Error(`No IMAP credentials found for ${email}. Add to IMAP_ACCOUNTS env var.`);

  return withClient(email, password, async (client) => {
    const lock = await client.getMailboxLock(folder);
    try {
      const total = client.mailbox.exists;
      const start = Math.max(1, total - limit + 1);
      const messages = [];
      for await (const msg of client.fetch(`${start}:${total}`, {
        envelope: true,
        flags: true,
      })) {
        messages.push({
          uid: msg.uid,
          subject: msg.envelope.subject ?? "(no subject)",
          from: msg.envelope.from?.[0]?.address ?? "",
          date: msg.envelope.date?.toISOString() ?? null,
          seen: msg.flags.has("\\Seen"),
        });
      }
      return messages.reverse(); // newest first
    } finally {
      lock.release();
    }
  });
}

/**
 * Server-side IMAP SEARCH for messages whose Subject contains `subject`.
 * IMAP SUBJECT search is a case-insensitive substring match done on the server,
 * so it scales to large mailboxes without fetching everything. Returns up to
 * `limit` most-recent matches (newest first) with envelope metadata + uid; pass
 * a returned uid to readBody to grab the actual content.
 *
 * @param {{ email: string, subject: string, folder?: string, limit?: number, sinceDays?: number, userId?: string }} input
 */
export async function searchBySubject({ email, subject, folder = "INBOX", limit = 25, sinceDays, userId } = {}) {
  if (!email) throw new Error('"email" is required');
  if (!subject) throw new Error('"subject" is required');

  const uid = resolveImapUserId(userId);
  const accounts = await loadAccounts(uid);
  const password = accounts[email];
  if (!password) throw new Error(`No IMAP credentials found for ${email}. Add to IMAP_ACCOUNTS env var or the owner's profile.`);

  const criteria = { subject };
  if (sinceDays && Number(sinceDays) > 0) {
    criteria.since = new Date(Date.now() - Number(sinceDays) * 86400_000);
  }

  return withClient(email, password, async (client) => {
    const lock = await client.getMailboxLock(folder);
    try {
      const uids = await client.search(criteria, { uid: true });
      if (!uids || !uids.length) return [];
      // uids ascend with arrival; take the newest `limit`.
      const pick = uids.slice(-Math.max(1, limit));
      const messages = [];
      for await (const msg of client.fetch(pick, { envelope: true, flags: true }, { uid: true })) {
        messages.push({
          uid: msg.uid,
          subject: msg.envelope.subject ?? "(no subject)",
          from: msg.envelope.from?.[0]?.address ?? "",
          to: (msg.envelope.to ?? []).map((a) => a.address).filter(Boolean),
          date: msg.envelope.date?.toISOString() ?? null,
          seen: msg.flags.has("\\Seen"),
        });
      }
      return messages.reverse(); // newest first
    } finally {
      lock.release();
    }
  });
}

/**
 * Fetch and decode one message's body by uid. Prefers text/plain; falls back to
 * html (tags stripped) or, for odd single-part messages, the raw source with the
 * header block removed. imapflow's download() already decodes the
 * content-transfer-encoding (base64 / quoted-printable).
 *
 * @param {{ email: string, uid: number, folder?: string, preferHtml?: boolean, maxChars?: number, userId?: string }} input
 */
export async function readBody({ email, uid, folder = "INBOX", preferHtml = false, maxChars = 20000, userId } = {}) {
  if (!email) throw new Error('"email" is required');
  if (uid == null) throw new Error('"uid" is required');

  const owner = resolveImapUserId(userId);
  const accounts = await loadAccounts(owner);
  const password = accounts[email];
  if (!password) throw new Error(`No IMAP credentials found for ${email}. Add to IMAP_ACCOUNTS env var or the owner's profile.`);

  return withClient(email, password, async (client) => {
    const lock = await client.getMailboxLock(folder);
    try {
      const msg = await client.fetchOne(uid, { envelope: true, bodyStructure: true }, { uid: true });
      if (!msg) throw new Error(`No message with uid ${uid} in ${folder}`);

      const leaf = pickTextPart(msg.bodyStructure, preferHtml);
      let body = "";
      let usedPart = leaf?.part ?? null;
      let contentType = leaf?.type ?? null;

      if (leaf && leaf.part) {
        const dl = await client.download(uid, leaf.part, { uid: true });
        body = await streamToString(dl?.content);
      } else {
        // Single-part message (no part specifier) — download the full source and
        // drop the header block (everything up to the first blank line).
        const dl = await client.download(uid, undefined, { uid: true });
        const raw = await streamToString(dl?.content);
        const split = raw.indexOf("\r\n\r\n");
        body = split >= 0 ? raw.slice(split + 4) : raw;
        contentType = contentType || "text/plain";
      }

      if (contentType && contentType.includes("html")) body = stripHtml(body);
      body = body.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n").trim();

      return {
        uid: msg.uid,
        subject: msg.envelope.subject ?? "(no subject)",
        from: msg.envelope.from?.[0]?.address ?? "",
        date: msg.envelope.date?.toISOString() ?? null,
        contentType,
        part: usedPart,
        truncated: body.length > maxChars,
        body: body.slice(0, maxChars),
      };
    } finally {
      lock.release();
    }
  });
}

/**
 * List all IMAP accounts currently configured.
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function searchAccounts(input = {}, userId) {
  const accounts = await loadAccounts(resolveImapUserId(input?.userId ?? userId));
  return Object.keys(accounts).map((email) => ({ email }));
}

/**
 * Test connectivity for a single account.
 * @param {{ email: string }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function checkCredentials({ email, userId } = {}, userIdArg) {
  const accounts = await loadAccounts(resolveImapUserId(userId ?? userIdArg));
  if (email) {
    const password = accounts[email];
    if (!password) return { ok: false, msg: `No credentials for ${email}` };
    try {
      await withClient(email, password, async (client) => {
        await client.getMailboxLock("INBOX").then((l) => l.release());
      });
      return { ok: true, msg: `Connected to ${email}` };
    } catch (e) {
      return { ok: false, msg: e.message };
    }
  }
  // Test all
  const results = [];
  for (const [acct, password] of Object.entries(accounts)) {
    try {
      await withClient(acct, password, async (client) => {
        await client.getMailboxLock("INBOX").then((l) => l.release());
      });
      results.push({ email: acct, ok: true });
    } catch (e) {
      results.push({ email: acct, ok: false, error: e.message });
    }
  }
  return { results };
}
```

```js
export const toc = {
  searchCampaigns: "Search Instantly cold-email campaigns.",
  readCampaign: "Read a single Instantly campaign by id.",
  readAnalytics: "Read Instantly campaign analytics.",
  readLeads: "Read leads in an Instantly campaign.",
};

import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";

// Instantly API v2 — Bearer token auth.
// Key created 2026-04-19 via UI (GuildOS key, all:all scope).
// V1 API uses ?api_key= param but is deprecated; V2 uses Bearer Authorization header.

const BASE_V2 = "https://api.instantly.ai/api/v2";

async function loadKey(userId) {
  if (userId) {
    try {
      const db = await database.init("service");
      const { data } = await db.from("profiles").select("env_vars").eq("id", userId).single();
      const k = data?.env_vars?.INSTANTLY_API_KEY;
      if (k) return k;
    } catch { /* fall through */ }
  }
  return process.env.INSTANTLY_API_KEY || null;
}

async function request(path, key, params = {}, method = "GET", body) {
  const url = new URL(`${BASE_V2}${path}`);
  if (method === "GET") {
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(params)) {
      if (v !== undefined && v !== null) url.searchParams.set(k, String(v));
    }
  }
  const opts = {
    method,
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${key}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  };
  if (body) opts.body = JSON.stringify(body);
  const res = await fetch(url.toString(), opts);
  if (!res.ok) {
    const text = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`Instantly ${path} failed (${res.status}): ${text}`);
  }
  return res.json();
}

export async function searchCampaigns({ limit = 10, skip = 0 } = {}, userId) {
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) throw new Error("INSTANTLY_API_KEY not set");
  return request("/campaigns", key, { limit, starting_after: skip > 0 ? skip : undefined });
}

export async function readCampaign({ id } = {}, userId) {
  if (!id) throw new Error('"id" is required');
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) throw new Error("INSTANTLY_API_KEY not set");
  return request(`/campaigns/${id}`, key);
}

export async function readAnalytics({ campaignId } = {}, userId) {
  if (!campaignId) throw new Error('"campaignId" is required');
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) throw new Error("INSTANTLY_API_KEY not set");
  return request(`/campaigns/${campaignId}/analytics/overview`, key);
}

export async function readLeads({ campaignId, limit = 10, skip = 0 } = {}, userId) {
  if (!campaignId) throw new Error('"campaignId" is required');
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) throw new Error("INSTANTLY_API_KEY not set");
  return request("/leads", key, { campaign_id: campaignId, limit });
}

export async function checkCredentials(input = {}, userId) {
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) return { ok: false, msg: "INSTANTLY_API_KEY not set in profiles.env_vars or process.env" };
  try {
    const data = await request("/campaigns", key, { limit: 1 });
    return { ok: true, msg: `Instantly credentials valid — ${data?.items?.length ?? 0} campaigns accessible` };
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, msg: e.message };
  }
}
```

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * leafBrowser CLI — operator helpers for the leaf authenticated-browser profile.
 *
 *   node libs/weapon/leafBrowser/cli.mjs capture   # launch headed Chrome on the master profile to log in
 *   node libs/weapon/leafBrowser/cli.mjs status    # show master/chrome detection
 *
 * `capture` is the ONE manual step: Chrome opens on the master profile, you log
 * into the sites leaves must reach, then close it. Leaves get copies thereafter.
 */
import { spawn } from "child_process";
import { mkdirSync } from "fs";
import { captureMasterProfileCmd, hasMasterProfile, hasMasterCookie, captureMasterFromChrome, openInteractiveLogin, exportStorageState, findChrome } from "./index.js";

const cmd = process.argv[2] || "status";

// Headed, persistent interactive login (for sites that reject copied cookies,
// e.g. Gmail). Auto-seeds the account from the master profile's storageState so
// the page recognizes the operator (Gmail shows their email) BEFORE they log in.
// Run DETACHED — it stays open until the operator closes the window.
//   node libs/weapon/leafBrowser/cli.mjs login [url]
if (cmd === "login") {
  const url = process.argv[3] || "https://mail.google.com/";
  let seedStatePath = null;
  if (hasMasterProfile()) {
    const exp = await exportStorageState({ fromProfile: "master", outPath: ".browser-profiles/auth-seed.json" });
    if (exp.ok) { seedStatePath = exp.path; console.log(`Seeded account from master (${exp.cookieCount} cookies) → ${exp.path}`); }
    else console.log(`Seed export skipped: ${exp.reason}`);
  }
  const r = await openInteractiveLogin({ url, seedStatePath, resetProfile: true });
  console.log(JSON.stringify(r));
  process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1);
}

if (cmd === "status") {
  console.log(JSON.stringify({
    hasMasterProfile: hasMasterProfile(),
    hasMasterCookie: hasMasterCookie(),
    chrome: findChrome(),
    capture: captureMasterProfileCmd(),
  }, null, 2));
  process.exit(0);
}

// Non-interactive capture from the operator's LIVE Chrome profile (zero login
// step). Grabs the Cookies DB only when Chrome isn't holding it under its
// exclusive lock — close Chrome first if `hasMasterCookie` stays false.
if (cmd === "capture-from-chrome") {
  const r = captureMasterFromChrome();
  console.log(JSON.stringify(r, null, 2));
  console.log(r.ok ? "ARMED (session cookie captured)." : "NOT armed — Cookies still locked. Close Chrome once and re-run, or it self-arms on the next questTick after Chrome closes.");
  process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1);
}

if (cmd === "capture") {
  const info = captureMasterProfileCmd();
  if (!info.chrome) {
    console.error("Chrome not found — install Chrome or set its path. Detected: null");
    process.exit(1);
  }
  mkdirSync(info.masterDir, { recursive: true });
  console.log(`Launching Chrome on master profile:\n  ${info.masterDir}\nLog into the sites leaves need, then CLOSE Chrome to finish.`);
  const child = spawn(info.chrome, [`--user-data-dir=${info.masterDir}`], { stdio: "ignore", detached: false });
  child.on("close", (code) => {
    console.log(`Chrome closed (code=${code}). Master profile ready: ${hasMasterProfile()}`);
    process.exit(0);
  });
  child.on("error", (e) => { console.error("Failed to launch Chrome:", e.message); process.exit(1); });
} else {
  console.error(`Unknown command "${cmd}". Use: capture | status`);
  process.exit(1);
}
```

<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: libs/weapon/leafBrowser/engineering_decisions.md -->
```markdown
# leafBrowser — Engineering Decisions

## 2026-06-15 · leafBrowser is the SINGLE browser substrate; in-process screenshots route through it

**Decision.** leafBrowser owns ALL Playwright/Chromium launching in the repo, via
two surfaces over one auth model:
- `prepareLeafBrowser` — MCP injection for headless `claude --print` LEAVES
  (interactive page-driving by an LLM).
- `launchContext` / `screenshotUrl` — in-process render-to-PNG (no LLM), the
  primitive `questPurrview.autoVisualVerify`, `cicVerify`, and `poster_render`
  now delegate to. `launchContext` is the only `chromium.launch*` call site.

**Rejected alternative.** Leaving each weapon with its own
`await import("playwright"); chromium.launch({headless:true})` (the state before
this date: questPurrview.renderDeliverableScreenshot, cicVerify.screenshotFromUrl,
poster_render.renderPoster each launched independently), and letting the
"planned substrate" (leafBrowser) stay MCP-only.

**Why.** leafBrowser was built with ONLY the MCP-leaf surface, gated on a
captured master profile — so it was dormant (no profile → never called) while the
job that actually recurs is the *unauthenticated, in-process* "URL → verify PNG".
With no in-process surface on leafBrowser, three weapons grew parallel chromium
launchers and, under pressure, leaves hand-rolled `node -e require('playwright')`
and fell back to **html2canvas** (the operator's locked not-real-verification
path). Four+ launchers + a synthetic-canvas escape hatch = exactly the substrate
sprawl a single owner prevents (drifting auth policy, chromium-resolution, and
fail-closed semantics; the browsercontrol skill book even still claimed Chrome was
launched in only one place). Centralizing also makes the auth-profile model
reachable from the in-process path (`authed:true` → persistent context over a
profile copy), so the captured-profile work finally pays off for screenshots, not
just MCP leaves.

**Consequence if violated.** Re-introducing a local `chromium.launch` /
`puppeteer` / `html2canvas` in any weapon forks the substrate again: verify
screenshots stop sharing the fail-closed-on-blank guard and the ref→URL
resolution (the bug that made `proving-grounds/x/index.html` refs un-navigable and
silently empty), and synthetic-canvas "verifications" creep back in. New screenshot
needs MUST call `leafBrowser.screenshotUrl` (or `launchContext` if they drive the
page themselves).

**Scope note.** `CICPolice` (drives a *headed* browser to police CIC) and
`scripts/auth-capture.mjs` (manual storageState export for cloud Cursor agents)
are deliberately NOT folded in — different jobs, not the verify-screenshot
substrate. They are the only remaining direct Playwright launches and are headed /
operator-manual, not headless screenshot producers.

**Proven.** 2026-06-15 — `screenshotUrl({ ref:'proving-grounds/about-us-rewrite/index.html' })`
returned a 304 KB full-page PNG (real render, visually confirmed), including the
dev-server→`file://` fallback for static public refs.

## 2026-06-16 · Master capture = copy the operator's LIVE Chrome profile, non-interactively + self-arming

**Decision.** `captureMasterFromChrome` populates the master by copying the
operator's EXISTING logged-in Chrome profile (auth-only allowlist: `Local State` +
`Network/Cookies` + `Local Storage/leveldb` + `Preferences`) rather than the
interactive headed re-login (`captureMasterProfileCmd` / `cli.mjs capture`).
Dispatch gates on `hasMasterCookie()` (the session Cookies DB) — NOT
`hasMasterProfile()` — and `questTick` calls `ensureMasterFromChrome()` so the
pipeline self-arms with zero operator action.

**Rejected alternatives.** (1) The interactive capture (operator opens headed
Chrome, logs into every site, closes) — rejected because the operator is ALREADY
logged in in their main Chrome and explicitly wanted no manual step. (2) Gating on
`hasMasterProfile()` — rejected: after a partial copy, `Local State` exists so it
returns true while the profile has NO cookie, so a `[BROWSER]` leaf would dispatch
"authenticated" and silently bounce to `/signin`. (3) Force-closing / taskkilling
the operator's Chrome to free the cookie lock — rejected (memory
feedback_browser_control: never taskkill the operator's Chrome).

**Why / the load-bearing constraint.** Chrome's Network service holds
`Default/Network/Cookies` under an EXCLUSIVE OS lock while running — verified three
ways 2026-06-16: `CopyFile` → EBUSY, libuv read-handle → EBUSY, .NET
`FileShare.ReadWrite` → sharing violation; this box is non-admin (no VSS/`esentutl`)
and Chrome 149 refuses `--remote-debugging-port` on the default profile dir (no CDP
fallback). So the session cookie CANNOT be extracted while Chrome is live. The
copy is therefore (a) lock-tolerant (`lockTolerantCopy`: libuv read-handle bypasses
CopyFile's share-mode failure for files Chrome doesn't hold exclusively), (b)
NON-destructive (no `rmSync` wipe — a re-run that can't grab the live-locked cookie
must preserve a previously captured one), and (c) opportunistic (re-attempts only
the cookie each tick; succeeds the moment Chrome is next closed). Everything except
the cookie copies fine while Chrome runs; the cookie self-captures on the next
natural Chrome close — zero operator action.

**Consequence if violated.** Re-adding `rmSync(MASTER_DIR)` to the capture wipes a
good cookie whenever the next opportunistic run hits a live lock (the pipeline
would arm then disarm itself every cron tick). Gating dispatch back on
`hasMasterProfile()` dispatches `[BROWSER]` leaves against a cookieless profile
that just screenshots the sign-in wall (the exact deadlock on quest 988c9792).

**PROVEN end-to-end 2026-06-16.** Operator closed Chrome → `captureMasterFromChrome`
grabbed the now-unlocked `Network/Cookies` → a headless Playwright leaf rendered the
**authenticated** GuildOS `/caravan` (no `/signin` redirect; full dashboard —
`public/proving-grounds/caravan-authed.png`). So ABE cookie decryption works in a
copied profile launched by Playwright with system Chrome on the same user+machine,
and the cron-leaf auth-screenshot deadlock (quest 988c9792) is cleared.

**Google-account caveat (Gmail will NOT work via copied cookies).** Same run, target
`mail.google.com`: Google recognized the account from the copied session ("Hi Sijie,
<REDACTED-EMAIL>") but stopped at "Verifying it's you — complete sign-in using your
passkey" (`public/proving-grounds/gmail-inbox-delivered.png`), even headed + with
anti-automation flags (`--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled`, no
`--enable-automation`, `navigator.webdriver` spoofed). High-value Google accounts
require a passkey/2FA to authorize a session on a *new browser instance*
(device-bound-session-style hardening), which a profile/cookie copy cannot satisfy
(the passkey is hardware/TPM-bound, non-exportable) and which an agent must not
complete. **Consequence:** do not waste cycles trying to make Gmail (or other
passkey-gated Google surfaces) work through `leafBrowser` **cookie-COPY** reuse — it
is a Google-side wall, not a pipeline defect. The pipeline IS correct for normal
cookie/Supabase-session sites (proven on `/caravan`).

## 2026-06-16 · HAZARD — copying a rotating-refresh-token session can LOG OUT the source browser

**Observed.** After a leaf rendered the authenticated `/caravan` via the cookie-COPY
master (real, screenshotted), within ~the hour BOTH the copy AND the operator's MAIN
Chrome were logged out (`/caravan` → `/signin`). The operator noticed their own
localhost:3002 was signed out.

**Why.** GuildOS auth is Supabase, which **rotates the refresh token** on use. The
copied cookie carries the SAME refresh token as the source. When the leaf's copy
exercised the session and a refresh fired, Supabase rotated the token and invalidated
the prior one — which the operator's main browser still held → the operator got
signed out as collateral. (Plain ~1h access-token expiry can produce the same symptom;
rotation triggered by the copy's use is the likely accelerant.)

**Consequence / guidance.** Cookie-copy auth is **best-effort and can disturb the
source login** for any site with rotating sessions (Supabase, many OAuth sessions).
Do NOT present a cookie-copy render as a durable/shared logged-in state — it is a
point-in-time snapshot that can desync. For durable automation auth, prefer the
**dedicated-interactive-profile** model (log in ONCE in `.browser-profiles/interactive`
and have leaves reuse that profile DIRECTLY) — the session lives only there, so
refreshing/rotating it never touches the operator's main browser. Reserve cookie-copy
for read-mostly, short-lived, non-rotating targets.

## 2026-06-18 · PROVEN — Gmail works headlessly via native interactive login + same-profile reuse

The Gmail path below is now VERIFIED end-to-end, and it resolves the earlier
"Gmail is walled" caveat (which applies ONLY to cookie-COPY):
- **Clean login avoids the passkey wall.** A FRESH interactive login (empty profile,
  no seeded/copied cookies) advances `<REDACTED-EMAIL>` straight to the PASSWORD
  step — NOT the "complete sign-in using your passkey" challenge. The passkey wall
  only fires when Google sees a copied/seeded session it must re-verify on a "new
  device." So do NOT seed the profile when the goal is a real login; seed only to
  show the account chooser.
- **Same-profile headless reuse renders the inbox.** After the operator logged in
  (password) in the headed window on `.browser-profiles/interactive` and closed it
  gracefully, a HEADLESS Playwright launch on that SAME profile dir loaded
  `mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox` with the live inbox (Inbox 368, Compose, labels)
  — `public/proving-grounds/gmail-inbox-delivered.png`. No copy → no device-binding
  re-challenge. This is the durable Gmail-in-a-leaf path; quest 6b5133b8 = complete.

## 2026-06-18 · Leaf-MCP injection: `cmd /c npx` on Windows + `directProfileDir` (PROVEN)

**Decision.** `prepareLeafBrowser`'s mcp-config launches the Playwright MCP server as
`{ command:"cmd", args:["/c","npx",...] }` on win32 (not `{ command:"npx", args:[...] }`),
and accepts `directProfileDir` (use a profile IN PLACE, no copy) + `outputDir`.

**Why — the bug this fixes.** An MCP host (`claude --print --mcp-config`) spawns the
server command DIRECTLY, without a shell. On Windows `npx` is `npx.cmd`; a bare
`"npx"` is not found, the server never connects, and `claude --print` proceeds with
**no `mcp__playwright__*` tools** — silently (no fatal error). First leaf run hit
exactly this: the leaf reported "no Playwright MCP tools connected." Wrapping via
`cmd /c npx` resolves it. **Rejected alternative:** `command:"npx"` (worked on
macOS/Linux, silently broke every Windows leaf — and GuildOS runs on Windows).

**`directProfileDir`.** The default per-leaf COPY of master is wrong for Google
(copy → passkey re-challenge) and for rotating sessions (logs the operator out).
`directProfileDir` points `--user-data-dir` at the operator's native-login profile
(`.browser-profiles/interactive`) in place — single-flight, never copied, never
cleaned up by `cleanupLeafBrowser` (which only removes `LEAF_ROOT/<workerId>`).

**Consequence if violated.** Reverting to `command:"npx"` silently disables browser
for EVERY Windows leaf (the deadlock returns, with no error to diagnose). Copying the
interactive profile instead of using it directly re-triggers the Google passkey wall.

**PROVEN 2026-06-18.** A real `claude --print` leaf with this config navigated to
Gmail and screenshotted the operator's authenticated inbox (<REDACTED-EMAIL>, real
senders) → `public/proving-grounds/leaf-gmail-inbox.png`. This is the end-to-end
leaf-MCP proof the earlier "not yet proven" note (browsercontrol) was waiting on.

## 2026-06-16 · HAZARD — never FORCE-KILL an interactive-login Chrome window

Force-killing the Playwright login window (`Stop-Process -Force` / `taskkill /F`)
skips Chrome's graceful shutdown, which is what flushes the just-completed session
to the profile on disk → the operator's login is LOST (observed: a completed
`<REDACTED-EMAIL>` login vanished after a force-kill, profile showed "Signed
out" next launch). Close via `context.close()` (graceful) or let the operator close
the window. Only force-kill when you are about to WIPE that profile anyway.

Also: Google's account chooser offers no inline "Remove an account" while one of the
listed accounts holds an active session — so to drop a specific account (e.g. a
passkey-walled personal account, keeping a password-login work account) the reliable
move is to WIPE the dedicated profile (`.browser-profiles/interactive`; `master` is
separate and untouched) and have the operator log into only the wanted account. A
passkey-gated Google account cannot be automated headlessly at all; a password-login
(non-passkey) account can.

**The Gmail path (added 2026-06-16): native interactive login, reused directly.**
`openInteractiveLogin()` opens a HEADED persistent Playwright browser on a DEDICATED
profile (`.browser-profiles/interactive`) where the operator logs in BY HAND. Because
the session is MINTED in that browser+profile (not copied in), the device binding is
native → Google does not re-challenge, and it persists for days. **Load-bearing
rule: reuse that profile dir DIRECTLY — NEVER copy it** (a copy re-triggers the exact
passkey wall above; that is the whole reason the cookie-copy master fails for Gmail).
So Google/Gmail leaf targets must launch on `.browser-profiles/interactive` itself,
single-flight (Chrome locks a user-data-dir), NOT via the per-leaf copy path used for
the cookie-copy master. Do not "unify" interactive into the copy flow — it breaks it.
(The Gmail MCP remains a fine alternative when only email *content* is needed, no
browser screenshot.)

## 2026-06-16 · Cloudflare-protected targets (bosterbio): HEADED + ONE fresh context per page

**Discovery (measured this date, verifying the EK1695 / Biotium escalated quests).**
For `www.bosterbio.com` (Cloudflare "Just a moment…" JS challenge):
- `screenshotUrl`/`launchContext` with `headless:true` is **403'd every time** — both
  `isolated` AND `authed` (the bundled-Chromium headless fingerprint is the tell;
  even the operator's real profile + `cf_clearance` cookie does not save it).
- `headless:false` (headed, system Chrome via `executablePath`) **clears the
  challenge** — but only for the **FIRST navigation in a given context**. Cloudflare
  adaptively re-challenges the 2nd+ nav in the same session (observed: page A 200,
  page B/C 403 in one context). So the reliable pattern is **one fresh
  `launchContext` per page** (first-hit-per-context passes), with a poll-until-cleared
  wait (title ≠ "just a moment" AND bodyLen>~400, up to ~25–30 s) before screenshot.

**Rejected alternative.** Batching N bosterbio pages through one headless (or one
shared headed) context — produces a pile of "Just a moment…" challenge screenshots
that *look* like real captures (fail-closed catches blanks, but a 265-char challenge
page is not blank), i.e. silent false verification.

**Consequence if violated.** A verify/QA run that reuses a context or stays headless
will catalog Cloudflare interstitials as "verified" deliverables. Multi-step flows on
bosterbio (add-to-cart → cart) inherently need ≥2 navs → the 2nd gets challenged, so
**cart-submit cannot be auto-driven this way** (verify cart via the cart API, or a
single manual add). Pace + headed + fresh-context-per-page, or don't claim it.

## 2026-06-16 · The master profile authenticates PROD + bosterbio, NOT localhost — verify against prod URLs

**Discovery.** `captureMasterFromChrome` copies the operator's LIVE Chrome cookies, so
the master holds sessions for what they actually browse: `guild-os-ten.vercel.app`
(prod GuildOS), `<REDACTED-HOST>` (prod boster_nexus), `bosterbio.com`,
`cjgeoai.com`, Google. It does **NOT** hold `localhost:3002` / `localhost:3001`
cookies (the operator signs into local dev via CIC / a different context, not their
main Chrome). Verified 2026-06-16: `authed` render of `localhost:3002/caravan` →
302 `/signin`, but `guild-os-ten.vercel.app/caravan` → 200 authed (full dashboard);
same for `<REDACTED-HOST>` `/ooa-dashboard` + `/purchase-orders/open-items`.

**Consequence / guidance.** To visually verify an auth-gated app feature with
leafBrowser, target its **production URL**, not localhost — the cookie is there.
This means a feature must be **DEPLOYED to prod** to be leaf-verifiable; a local-only
build (uncommitted worktree changes, or a dev-only page like the OOA user-drill-down
and the Open-PO per-item status field, both confirmed ABSENT on prod 2026-06-16)
**cannot** be verified this way. The fix for a local-only target is either (a) deploy
it to prod then verify, or (b) capture a localhost login into the master (operator
logs into the local dev server in their main Chrome, then `ensureMasterFromChrome`)
AND have that dev server running. Do not assume `authed:true` reaches localhost.
## 2026-07-03 - Isolated verification launches prefer system Chrome; purrview disables lazy-scroll

**Decision.** `launchContext` uses the operator's system Chrome for isolated
headless screenshots when it can find it, and `questPurrview.autoVisualVerify`
calls `screenshotUrl` with `waitUntil:"domcontentloaded"` and `scrollLazyLoad:false`.

**Rejected alternative.** Keep isolated screenshots on Playwright's bundled
Chromium and let purrview use the screenshot primitive's default
`networkidle`+lazy-scroll behavior.

**Why.** On the Hermes visual-gate acceptance quest, bundled/default rendering
stalled the real `autoVisualVerify` path: the deliverable was a valid public
Supabase HTML page, but the purrview capture never returned. A bounded system
Chrome render of the same URL produced a real PNG in about two seconds. Purrview's
job is to capture enough real pixels for the independent vision judge, not to
crawl an arbitrary page forever.

**Consequence if violated.** Hermes-produced deliverables can reach `purrview`
with valid refs and still never get a `verify_screenshot_ref`, so the review gate
appears broken even though the worker output is correct.
```
