```js
/**
 * pim weapon — GuildOS-side Magento-row → canonical-PIM converter.
 *
 * Single public action: mapProductInfo(input, map?). Takes one Magento product
 * row (or an array of rows) and returns the canonical-PIM shape, applying the
 * locked DEFAULT_MAP (Type-A buckets + Type-B per-template attr_x assignment)
 * or a caller-supplied override. Same shape in → out (object→object, array→array).
 *
 * Full contract, table schemas, bucketing rules, and the mirror plan live in the
 * `pim` skill book → libs/skill_book/pim/index.js (action: mapProductInfo).
 * This weapon is mirrored verbatim into boster_nexus/libs/pim/mapProductInfo.js.
 */

const TRANSFORMS = {
  identity: (v) => v,
  trim: (v) => (v == null ? v : String(v).trim()),
  toNull: (v) => (v === "" || v === undefined ? null : v),
  splitList: (v) =>
    v == null || v === ""
      ? []
      : String(v)
          .split(/[,;|]/)
          .map((s) => s.trim())
          .filter(Boolean),
  // Image labels in Magento are pipe-separated only (commas appear inside labels).
  splitListPipe: (v) =>
    v == null || v === ""
      ? []
      : String(v)
          .split(/\|/)
          .map((s) => s.trim())
          .filter(Boolean),
  joinList: (v) => (Array.isArray(v) ? v.join(",") : v == null ? "" : String(v)),
  magentoStatusToCanonical: (v) => {
    const s = String(v ?? "").trim();
    if (s === "1") return "enabled";
    if (s === "2") return "disabled";
    if (s === "enabled" || s === "disabled" || s === "draft") return s;
    return "draft";
  },
  canonicalStatusToMagento: (v) => (v === "enabled" ? "1" : "0"),
  numeric: (v) =>
    v == null || v === ""
      ? null
      : Number.isFinite(Number(v))
        ? Number(v)
        : String(v),
  // Parse Magento's pipe-delimited custom_options string into a JSONB-friendly
  // array. Each option is a string of `k=v` pairs joined by `,`; sub-options
  // are joined by `|`. We do a best-effort parse — anything that looks
  // unparseable is preserved verbatim under `__raw` so the next stage can fix
  // it without data loss.
  parseCustomOptions: (v) => {
    if (v == null || v === "") return [];
    const out = [];
    for (const optStr of String(v).split(/\|/)) {
      if (!optStr.trim()) continue;
      const obj = {};
      for (const kv of optStr.split(/,(?=[a-z_]+=)/i)) {
        const m = kv.match(/^([a-z_][a-z0-9_]*)=(.*)$/i);
        if (m) obj[m[1]] = m[2];
      }
      if (Object.keys(obj).length === 0) obj.__raw = optStr;
      out.push(obj);
    }
    return out;
  },
};

// ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// mapProductInfo — Magento-row → canonical-PIM converter (the only public path).
//
// DEFAULT_MAP below is the locked source of truth at runtime (Type-A/Keep/
// Nameless/Relation buckets + per-template attr_x assignment). It is NOT loaded
// from JSON/TSV/DB; the TSVs in boster_nexus/docs/pim/ are reference only.
//
// Full contract, table schemas, bucketing rules, transforms, and the verbatim-
// mirror plan (→ boster_nexus/libs/pim/mapProductInfo.js): see the `pim` skill
// book at libs/skill_book/pim/index.js (action: mapProductInfo).
// ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Default PIM mapping. Encodes the two locked decision tables that live in
 * the boster_nexus repo (docs/pim/attr-mapping-1.tsv + attr-mapping-2.tsv).
 * THIS IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH AT RUNTIME — the TSV files are documentation.
 *
 * Shape:
 *   fields: { <magento_col>: { to, transform?, relation? } }
 *     - to:        canonical destination path; dotted path supported
 *                  (e.g. 'target_info.gene_name', 'metadata.source_created_at')
 *     - transform: key in TRANSFORMS above (trim, splitList, numeric, …)
 *     - relation:  'images' | 'options' — handled by relation post-processors
 *                  in the ingest pipeline (not by this function)
 *
 *   typeB: { <product_template>: { <magento_col>: <attr_index>, ... } }
 *     Per-template assignment of "nameless" Magento columns into the generic
 *     attr_1..attr_30 slots on the products row.
 *
 * NOTE: Index-vs-Keep bucket distinction (which columns get a DB index) is
 * NOT encoded in this map. Index/Keep columns are added to the products
 * table the SAME WAY at the schema level. The Index decision is metadata
 * that lives in docs/pim/attr-mapping-1-index-keep-nameless.tsv now and
 * will move to env vars on the new website later. The converter doesn't
 * need to know which fields are indexed.
 */

function applyTransformByName(name, value) {
  if (!name) return value;
  const fn = TRANSFORMS[name];
  if (!fn) throw new Error(`mapProductInfo: unknown transform '${name}'`);
  return fn(value);
}

function setNestedPath(target, dottedPath, value) {
  // Writes `value` at `dottedPath` inside `target`. Creates intermediate
  // objects as needed. Top-level paths fall through to a flat write.
  if (!dottedPath.includes(".")) {
    target[dottedPath] = value;
    return;
  }
  const parts = dottedPath.split(".");
  let cur = target;
  for (let i = 0; i < parts.length - 1; i++) {
    const k = parts[i];
    if (cur[k] == null || typeof cur[k] !== "object" || Array.isArray(cur[k])) {
      cur[k] = {};
    }
    cur = cur[k];
  }
  cur[parts[parts.length - 1]] = value;
}

function isPlainObject(v) {
  return v != null && typeof v === "object" && !Array.isArray(v);
}

/**
 * Convert one Magento product row → canonical-PIM product object.
 * Internal helper; mapProductInfo() handles single-vs-array shape dispatch.
 */
function mapOne(row, map) {
  if (!isPlainObject(row)) {
    throw new Error("mapProductInfo: each row must be a plain object (key→value)");
  }
  const out = {};
  const unmapped = {};
  const template = row.template || row.product_template || null;

  // First pass: Type-A + Relation columns (driven by map.fields).
  const handledKeys = new Set();
  for (const [srcKey, spec] of Object.entries(map.fields || {})) {
    handledKeys.add(srcKey);
    if (!(srcKey in row)) continue;
    let value = row[srcKey];
    if (value === "" || value === undefined) {
      value = null;
    }
    if (value !== null && spec.transform) {
      value = applyTransformByName(spec.transform, value);
    }
    setNestedPath(out, spec.to, value);
  }

  // Second pass: Type-B (Nameless) — per-template attr_N assignment.
  const typeBForTemplate = (map.typeB && template && map.typeB[template]) || null;
  if (typeBForTemplate) {
    for (const [srcKey, attrIndex] of Object.entries(typeBForTemplate)) {
      handledKeys.add(srcKey);
      if (!(srcKey in row)) continue;
      let value = row[srcKey];
      if (value === "" || value === undefined) value = null;
      out[`attr_${attrIndex}`] = value;
    }
  }

  // Third pass: anything left over goes into _unmapped (audit trail; not
  // written to the products table by downstream ingest unless a follow-up
  // map upgrade adopts it).
  for (const key of Object.keys(row)) {
    if (handledKeys.has(key)) continue;
    // Skip known-internal noise that Magento exports sometimes carry.
    if (key === "" || key.startsWith("_")) continue;
    unmapped[key] = row[key];
  }
  if (Object.keys(unmapped).length > 0) {
    Object.defineProperty(out, "_unmapped", {
      value: unmapped,
      enumerable: true,
    });
  }

  // Carry the template through explicitly for downstream routing even if the
  // map didn't include it (defensive — DEFAULT_MAP does include it).
  if (template && !out.product_template) out.product_template = template;

  return out;
}

/**
 * Convert Magento product info (single row or array of rows) to the
 * canonical-PIM shape using a declarative map. See contract block above.
 *
 * @param {object|object[]} input
 * @param {object} [map] - defaults to DEFAULT_MAP when omitted/null/undefined
 * @returns {object|object[]} - same shape as input
 */
export function mapProductInfo(input, map) {
  const resolvedMap = map && typeof map === "object" ? map : DEFAULT_MAP;
  if (!resolvedMap.fields || typeof resolvedMap.fields !== "object") {
    throw new Error("mapProductInfo: map.fields is required");
  }

  if (Array.isArray(input)) {
    return input.map((row) => mapOne(row, resolvedMap));
  }
  if (isPlainObject(input)) {
    return mapOne(input, resolvedMap);
  }
  throw new Error(
    "mapProductInfo: input must be a plain object or an array of objects",
  );
}
```

```js
/**
 * Poster Render weapon — deterministic PNG generation from an HTML/CSS template.
 *
 * Use case: brand-locked, run-stable image deliverables (decision cards,
 * one-page guides, social previews) where AI image-gen jitter is unacceptable.
 * Data goes in as JSON, exact same bytes come out for the same input.
 *
 * Pattern:
 *   - The TEMPLATE is a static HTML file in /public/poster-templates/<slug>/.
 *     It reads its `data` from the URL hash (`#data=<base64-encoded JSON>`)
 *     and renders client-side. Brand assets (logo, fonts, colors) live
 *     inside the template — agents never see them.
 *   - The WEAPON launches headless Chromium via Playwright, navigates to
 *     `http://localhost:<port>/poster-templates/<slug>/#data=<...>`, waits
 *     for a sentinel selector (`.poster-ready`), screenshots the
 *     `.poster-canvas` element, saves PNG.
 *
 * Browser launch goes through the single substrate (leafBrowser.launchContext)
 * — the only chromium-launch site in the repo. This weapon keeps its own
 * page-driving (data injection, sentinel wait, element shot); it just no longer
 * launches Chromium itself. See leafBrowser engineering_decisions.md 2026-06-15.
 *
 * ─── API surface ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * renderPoster({ template, data, outPath, port?, waitMs? })
 *   template — slug under /public/poster-templates/  (e.g. "wb-decision-card")
 *   data     — JSON-serializable payload the template reads from #data hash
 *   outPath  — absolute path to write the PNG
 *   port     — dev-server port (default 3002)
 *   waitMs   — extra ms to wait after `.poster-ready` (default 200)
 *
 * Returns { path, bytes, viewport: {w,h}, elapsed_ms, template, source_url }.
 *
 * ─── Caller discipline ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * Call from API routes (app/api/**) or skill-book actions. Do NOT call from
 * scripts in scripts/ — see memory feedback_skill_books_weapons_first.md
 * LOCKED 2026-05-22.
 */

import fs from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";
import { launchContext } from "../leafBrowser/index.js";

export const toc = {
  renderPoster:
    "Render a deterministic PNG from a static HTML/CSS template under /public/poster-templates/<slug>/. Data injected via URL hash. Headless Chromium via Playwright. Brand-locked, run-stable, no AI in the hot path.",
};

/**
 * Find the .poster-canvas element in the template page, screenshot it as PNG,
 * write to outPath.
 *
 * @param {{template:string, data:object, outPath:string, port?:number, waitMs?:number, viewport?:{w:number,h:number}}} input
 * @returns {Promise<{path:string, bytes:number, viewport:{w:number,h:number}, elapsed_ms:number, template:string, source_url:string}>}
 */
export async function renderPoster({
  template,
  data,
  outPath,
  port = 3002,
  waitMs = 200,
  viewport = { w: 1024, h: 1536 },
}) {
  if (!template || typeof template !== "string") throw new Error("template (slug) required");
  if (!outPath || typeof outPath !== "string") throw new Error("outPath required");
  if (data == null) throw new Error("data required");

  const t0 = Date.now();
  // Use explicit index.html — Next.js static serving under /public doesn't
  // auto-index trailing-slash paths (returns 404 for /poster-templates/foo/).
  // Data is injected via page.evaluate after load — URL hashes are flaky in
  // headless contexts (race between hash listener attachment and document
  // parse, browser-specific stripping).
  const sourceUrl = `http://localhost:${port}/poster-templates/${template}/index.html`;

  const launched = await launchContext({
    viewport: { width: viewport.w, height: viewport.h },
    deviceScaleFactor: 2, // sharper text on the resulting PNG
  });
  if (!launched.ok) throw new Error(`poster_render: browser launch failed — ${launched.reason}`);
  const { context, close } = launched;
  try {
    const page = await context.newPage();
    page.on("console", (msg) => {
      if (msg.type() === "error") {
        // eslint-disable-next-line no-console
        console.error("[poster_render template console.error]", msg.text());
      }
    });
    page.on("pageerror", (err) => {
      // eslint-disable-next-line no-console
      console.error("[poster_render template pageerror]", err.message);
    });
    // Use 'load' (not 'networkidle') — Next.js dev keeps a HMR WebSocket open
    // that prevents networkidle from ever firing.
    await page.goto(sourceUrl, { waitUntil: "load", timeout: 20000 });
    // Inject the data payload directly — calls the template's window.renderPoster
    // function with the JSON payload. Templates MUST expose
    // `window.renderPoster(data)` and toggle `.poster-canvas.poster-ready` when done.
    await page.evaluate((payload) => {
      if (typeof window.renderPoster !== "function") {
        throw new Error("template must expose window.renderPoster(data)");
      }
      window.renderPoster(payload);
    }, data);
    // Templates signal "I'm done laying out, fonts loaded, assets in" by
    // exposing a `.poster-ready` class on the canvas element.
    // state:'attached' — element-in-DOM is sufficient; we don't need visibility
    // checks (canvas may be larger than viewport, which marks it 'not visible'
    // by Playwright's default).
    await page.waitForSelector(".poster-canvas.poster-ready", { state: "attached", timeout: 15000 });
    if (waitMs > 0) await page.waitForTimeout(waitMs);

    const canvas = await page.$(".poster-canvas");
    if (!canvas) throw new Error("template did not expose .poster-canvas element");
    const buffer = await canvas.screenshot({ type: "png", omitBackground: false });

    await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(outPath), { recursive: true });
    await fs.writeFile(outPath, buffer);

    return {
      path: outPath,
      bytes: buffer.length,
      viewport,
      elapsed_ms: Date.now() - t0,
      template,
      source_url: sourceUrl,
    };
  } finally {
    await close();
  }
}
```

```js
export const toc = {
  readSearch: "Read PubCompare search results via Browserclaw CDP (public site, no auth).",
};
import { ensureCdpChrome, executeSteps } from "@/libs/weapon/browserclaw/cdp";

export async function readSearch({ query } = {}) {
  if (!query) throw new Error('"query" is required');
  await ensureCdpChrome();
  const result = await executeSteps([
    { action: "navigate", url: "https://pubcompare.ai", item: "pubcompare_home" },
    { action: "extract_text", selector: "input[type='search'],input[type='text']", item: "search_input" },
    {
      action: "fill",
      selector: "input[type='search'],input[type='text']",
      value: query,
      item: "fill_query",
    },
    { action: "keyboard", key: "Enter", item: "submit" },
    { action: "extract_text", selector: "body", item: "results" },
  ]);
  return result;
}

export async function checkCredentials() {
  try {
    await ensureCdpChrome();
    const result = await executeSteps([
      { action: "navigate", url: "https://pubcompare.ai", item: "pubcompare_check" },
      { action: "extract_text", selector: "body", item: "body" },
    ]);
    return { ok: true, msg: "PubCompare accessible" };
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, msg: e.message };
  }
}
```

```js
/**
 * questDesign weapon — design-stage transitions.
 *
 * Owns the local-Guildmaster's view of the design stage. The flow:
 *   1. Quest is created at stage='design' (via writeQuest default).
 *   2. housekeeping.runDesignStage iterates each deliverables row: NL expectation →
 *      ChatGPT image-gen → upload to Supabase Storage → write design_url →
 *      vision-judge image vs expectation → write design_approved + design_feedback.
 *   3. When every deliverables row has design_approved=true, runDesignStage calls
 *      questDesign.submit({questId}) which advances stage='design' →
 *      stage='html_markup' and writes the lockphrase comment that the
 *      next stage's tooling greps for.
 *
 * Design stage is local-only (no Cat / cursor) — see CLAUDE.md DSY section.
 *
 * Sister weapons: questHtmlMarkup (next stage), questExecution (after that),
 * questPurrview (after execute), questReview (final gate).
 */

import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";
import { publicTables } from "@/libs/council/publicTables";

export const toc = {
  submit:
    "Move a quest from design to html_markup. Hard-gated: stage must be design AND every deliverables row must have expectation, design_url, and design_approved=true. On success, leaves the lockphrase comment 'this quest now meets the criteria for html_markup'.",
};

export const GATE_VERSION = 1;
export const SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE = "this quest now meets the criteria for html_markup";

const CRITERIA_CHECKED = [
  "questId is a non-empty string",
  "quest exists",
  "quest.stage === 'design'",
  "deliverables rows exist for the quest",
  "every deliverable has expectation set",
  "every deliverable has design_url set",
  "every deliverable has design_approved === true",
  "stage write to html_markup verified by SELECT-back",
];

/**
 * Submit a quest from design → html_markup.
 *
 * @param {{ questId: string }} args
 * @returns {Promise<{ ok: boolean, stage?: string, lockphrase?: string,
 *                    deliverables_count?: number, criteria_checked?: string[],
 *                    failed?: string[], report?: object }>}
 */
export async function submit({ questId }) {
  if (typeof questId !== "string" || !questId.trim()) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["questId"],
      report: { msg: "questId is required (non-empty string).", fix: "Pass { questId: '<uuid>' }." },
    };
  }

  const db = await database.init("service");

  const { data: quest, error: qErr } = await db
    .from(publicTables.quests)
    .select("id, stage, title, assigned_to")
    .eq("id", questId)
    .single();
  if (qErr || !quest) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["quest_exists"],
      report: { msg: qErr?.message || "Quest not found.", fix: "Verify the questId.", questId },
    };
  }
  if (quest.stage !== "design") {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["stage"],
      report: {
        msg: `Quest stage is "${quest.stage}", expected "design".`,
        fix:
          quest.stage === "html_markup" || quest.stage === "execute"
            ? "Quest is already past design — no resubmission needed."
            : "Submission only opens from design.",
        current_stage: quest.stage,
      },
    };
  }

  const { data: deliverables, error: iErr } = await db
    .from(publicTables.deliverables)
    .select("id, item_key, expectation, design_url, design_approved, design_feedback")
    .eq("quest_id", questId);
  if (iErr) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["deliverables_read"],
      report: { msg: iErr.message, fix: "DB read against `deliverables` failed." },
    };
  }
  const deliverableList = deliverables || [];
  if (deliverableList.length === 0) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["no_deliverables"],
      report: {
        msg: "Quest has no deliverables declared.",
        fix: "Insert deliverables rows at quest creation via writeItemExpectations({ questId, expectations: [{item_key, expectation}, ...] }).",
      },
    };
  }

  const missingExpectation = deliverableList.filter(
    (i) => !i.expectation || (typeof i.expectation === "string" && !i.expectation.trim()),
  );
  if (missingExpectation.length > 0) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["expectation_missing"],
      report: {
        msg: `${missingExpectation.length} deliverable(s) have no expectation set.`,
        fix: `Set deliverables.expectation for: ${missingExpectation.map((i) => i.item_key).join(", ")}.`,
        item_keys_missing_expectation: missingExpectation.map((i) => i.item_key),
      },
    };
  }

  const missingDesign = deliverableList.filter((i) => !i.design_url);
  if (missingDesign.length > 0) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["design_url_missing"],
      report: {
        msg: `${missingDesign.length} deliverable(s) have no design_url set. Run housekeeping.runDesignStage to generate baseline images.`,
        fix: `Generate design baseline images for: ${missingDesign.map((i) => i.item_key).join(", ")} via the OpenAI image weapon, then upload to Supabase Storage and write the URL via writeItem.`,
        item_keys_missing_design: missingDesign.map((i) => i.item_key),
      },
    };
  }

  const notApproved = deliverableList.filter((i) => i.design_approved !== true);
  if (notApproved.length > 0) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["design_not_approved"],
      report: {
        msg: `${notApproved.length} deliverable(s) have design_approved !== true. Vision-judge each design and set design_approved + design_feedback before submitting.`,
        fix: `For each of [${notApproved.map((i) => i.item_key).join(", ")}], call the vision judge against the design_url, then writeItem with design_approved=true (or regenerate the image if it fails).`,
        item_keys_not_approved: notApproved.map((i) => ({
          item_key: i.item_key,
          design_approved: i.design_approved,
          design_feedback: i.design_feedback,
        })),
      },
    };
  }

  const { error: upErr } = await db
    .from(publicTables.quests)
    .update({ stage: "html_markup" })
    .eq("id", questId);
  if (upErr) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["stage_write"],
      report: { msg: upErr.message, fix: "Stage write failed at the DB layer." },
    };
  }
  const { data: verify } = await db
    .from(publicTables.quests)
    .select("stage")
    .eq("id", questId)
    .single();
  if (verify?.stage !== "html_markup") {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["stage_write_verify"],
      report: {
        msg: `Stage write did not persist; reads back as "${verify?.stage}".`,
        fix: "Stage write was silently rejected (likely RLS or trigger).",
      },
    };
  }

  const summary = `Gate v${GATE_VERSION} passed. ${deliverableList.length} deliverable(s) design-approved. ${SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE.slice(1)}.`;
  const { error: cErr } = await db.from(publicTables.questComments).insert({
    quest_id: questId,
    source: "questDesign",
    action: "submit_for_html_markup",
    summary,
    actor_name: quest.assigned_to || "Guildmaster",
    detail: {
      gate_version: GATE_VERSION,
      lockphrase: SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE,
      criteria_checked: CRITERIA_CHECKED,
      deliverables_count: deliverableList.length,
      item_keys: deliverableList.map((i) => i.item_key),
    },
  });
  if (cErr) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["lockphrase_comment_write"],
      report: {
        msg: `Stage moved to html_markup but lockphrase comment failed to write: ${cErr.message}.`,
        fix: `Manually insert a quest_comments row with source='questDesign', action='submit_for_html_markup', summary including "${SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE}".`,
        partial: true,
        stage: "html_markup",
      },
    };
  }

  return {
    ok: true,
    stage: "html_markup",
    deliverables_count: deliverableList.length,
    lockphrase: SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE,
    criteria_checked: CRITERIA_CHECKED,
  };
}
```

<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: libs/weapon/questExecution/engineering_decisions.md -->
```markdown
# Engineering decisions — `libs/weapon/questExecution` (and the gate weapons)

Rationale layer (per CLAUDE.md §6). The WHY behind the stage-transition gates
shared by `questExecution`, `questPurrview`, and `questReview` — not API docs, not
procedure. Append; supersede in place when a decision changes.

---

## 2026-06-13 — every stage transition is a lockphrase-bearing comment, written weapon-atomically with the stage write

**Decision.** A stage transition writes `quests.stage` AND inserts a
`quest_comments` row carrying a gate-specific **lockphrase**
(`SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE` at `questExecution/index.js:40`, `APPROVE_LOCKPHRASE` at
`questPurrview/index.js:96`, `FINAL_GATE_PASS_LOCKPHRASE` at
`questReview/index.js:56`) together. The next consumer (`confirmSubmission`,
`confirmApproval`) **greps for the prior gate's lockphrase** before proceeding; it
never trusts a bare `.stage` value.

**Rejected alternative.** A simple stage-column check (`quest.stage === 'execute'`)
with no orthogonal audit comment.

**Why.** A bare stage write is invisible to auditing and forgeable by raw SQL or a
rogue call. The lockphrase comment IS the proof the gate ran: it makes every
transition tamper-evident, and couples the audit trail to the stage so a partial
transition (stage moved, comment missing) is detected and rejected by the next
gate rather than sailing through.

**Consequence if violated.** Rogue/partial stage writes bypass gates entirely — a
quest reaches review with unfinished objectives and the review gates become
theater (the leak class the operator repeatedly flags).

---

## 2026-06-13 — each gate stamps a `GATE_VERSION` into its audit comment

**Decision.** Every gate exports a `GATE_VERSION` constant and writes it to the
audit comment's `detail.gate_version` (`questExecution:34`, `questPurrview:86`,
`questReview:49`, `questDesign:28`). Quest comments are immutable; the version lets
a future reader know which gate logic a past approval passed.

**Rejected alternative.** Omit versioning (no forward tracking of gate changes).

**Why.** When a gate's criteria change, old quests carry comments from the old
gate. Without a version stamp, a past approval is ambiguous — did it clear the
current gate or a weaker predecessor? — making targeted re-validation impossible.

**Consequence if violated.** Gate-logic evolution becomes invisible in the trail;
re-validation after a gate change is guesswork.

---

## 2026-06-13 — visual verification is the reviewer's responsibility, NOT the worker's

**Decision.** The worker's `submit()` gate requires only a non-null deliverable
`ref` ("I made it exists"). The `verify_screenshot_ref` requirement lives
downstream at `questPurrview.approve()` ("it's real and satisfies the spec"), with
`autoVisualVerify()` capturing the screenshot for headless quests.

**Rejected alternative.** Symmetric gates (worker also blocks on a screenshot), or
the worker captures the screenshot itself.

**Why.** A headless worker leaf has no CIC / user-channel browser to capture a live
screenshot — only the CIC-capable reviewer (or local Claude at review) can. Putting
the screenshot gate on the worker would either block every headless quest or push
the worker to fake it; deferring it to purrview keeps the worker autonomous while
preserving a real visual gate.

**Consequence if violated.** Either headless workers stall on an unobtainable
screenshot, or unverified deliverables flow into review as "trusted" and the visual
gate goes toothless.

---

## 2026-06-13 — open unblocking questions at submit route to `escalated`, not `purrview`

**Decision.** If `submit()` finds any open unblocking question
(`qtype='unblocking', answered=false`), it routes the quest to `escalated` (with an
explanatory comment) instead of advancing to `purrview`.

**Rejected alternative.** Always `submit() → purrview` (gate only on objectives +
deliverables) and let the review path notice the questions later.

**Why.** A quest with unanswered user-facing questions is not "ready for review" —
it's waiting on the user. Parking it in purrview misrepresents its state;
escalating signals the user that input is needed now. (Companion to the
`questmaster` planner-side escalate ED — same principle at the submit boundary.)

**Consequence if violated.** Quests sit in purrview awaiting answers, breaking the
contract that purrview = "worker done, please review."
```

```js
/**
 * questExecution weapon — worker-side quest stage transitions.
 *
 * Owns the WORKER's view: how an adventurer ships a quest from execute → purrview.
 * The agent CANNOT advance a quest by writing `stage` directly. The only
 * supported path is `submit({ questId })`, which refuses to move the quest unless
 * every gate passes.
 *
 * New steps/items model (post 20260515120000_steps_items_refactor):
 *   - readiness is the `steps` + `items` state, NOT the retired
 *     items.expectation / per-item item_comments / tier-check columns.
 *   - A quest is submittable when every step up to AND including the Checkpoint
 *     (the step whose view_results='Checkpoint') is status='done', and every
 *     asset those steps name in output[].asset exists as an `items` row with a
 *     non-null `ref`.
 *
 * Sister weapon: `questPurrview` owns the QUESTMASTER's view (confirmSubmission
 * for the read-side handoff check, approve/bounce for the write-side transitions
 * out of purrview).
 *
 * Auth: uses the service-role DB facade (`database.init("service")`).
 * No external API. Reads `steps`, `items`, `quests`; writes `quests`, `quest_comments`.
 */

import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";
import { publicTables } from "@/libs/council/publicTables";
import { getQuestDetails } from "@/libs/weapon/questmaster/index.js";

export const toc = {
  submit:
    "Move a quest from execute to purrview. Hard-gated on the new steps/items model: every step up to and including the Checkpoint is status='done', and the items those steps produce exist with a non-null ref. On success, leaves the lockphrase comment that questPurrview.confirmSubmission checks for.",
};

export const GATE_VERSION = 2;
/**
 * Stable phrase embedded in the success comment.
 * `questPurrview.confirmSubmission` greps for it verbatim.
 * Do not change without coordinating with every consumer.
 */
export const SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE = "this quest now meets the criteria for purrview";

const CRITERIA_CHECKED = [
  "questId is a non-empty string",
  "quest exists",
  "quest.stage === 'execute'",
  "objectives rows exist for the quest",
  "every objective is status='done'",
  "every deliverable has a non-null ref",
  "stage write to purrview verified by SELECT-back",
];

/**
 * Submit a quest for Questmaster review.
 *
 * On full pass: writes `stage = "purrview"`, posts a `submit_for_purrview` audit
 * comment containing the lockphrase + full criteria list, returns
 * `{ ok: true, stage: "purrview", ... }`.
 *
 * On any failure: stage stays at `execute`, returns
 * `{ ok: false, failed: [<gate-id>], report: { msg, fix, ...details } }`.
 *
 * @param {{ questId: string }} args
 */
export async function submit({ questId }) {
  // Gate 1 — questId
  if (typeof questId !== "string" || !questId.trim()) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["questId"],
      report: {
        msg: "questId is required (non-empty string).",
        fix: "Pass { questId: '<uuid>' } as the argument.",
      },
    };
  }

  const db = await database.init("service");

  // Gates 2 + 3 — read the quest (also pulls assignee so we can stamp
  // actor_name on the submit comment).
  const { data: quest, error: qErr } = await db
    .from(publicTables.quests)
    .select("id, stage, title, assignee")
    .eq("id", questId)
    .single();
  if (qErr || !quest) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["quest_exists"],
      report: {
        msg: qErr?.message || "Quest not found.",
        fix: "Verify the questId. Confirm the quest exists with: SELECT id, stage FROM quests WHERE id = '<uuid>'.",
        questId,
      },
    };
  }
  if (quest.stage !== "execute") {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["stage"],
      report: {
        msg: `Quest stage is "${quest.stage}", expected "execute". Submission only valid from execute.`,
        fix:
          quest.stage === "purrview" || quest.stage === "review"
            ? "Quest is already past execute — no resubmission needed. If you have new artifacts, post them as comments and ping the Questmaster."
            : "If the quest is in closing/complete, contact the Guildmaster — submission only opens from execute.",
        current_stage: quest.stage,
      },
    };
  }

  // Gate 3b — open unblocking questions BLOCK submission → route to escalated.
  // If the agent has unanswered questions TO the user (qtype='unblocking',
  // answered=false), the quest is waiting on the user — it is NOT ready for
  // purrview/review. A quest can never pass review with the agent's own
  // questions unanswered, so we transition it to 'escalated' (awaiting the user)
  // instead of advancing. (operator rule 2026-06-13: "with N unblocking
  // questions unanswered, it should not progress to review but to escalated".)
  const { data: openUnblocking } = await db
    .from(publicTables.questQuestions)
    .select("id, body")
    .eq("quest_id", questId)
    .eq("qtype", "unblocking")
    .eq("answered", false);
  if (openUnblocking && openUnblocking.length > 0) {
    await db.from(publicTables.quests).update({ stage: "escalated" }).eq("id", questId);
    const { recordQuestComment } = await import("@/libs/quest/index.js");
    await recordQuestComment(questId, {
      source: "questExecution",
      action: "escalated_open_questions",
      summary: `Routed to escalated, not purrview: ${openUnblocking.length} open unblocking question(s) await the user. A quest cannot pass review while the agent's own questions to the user are unanswered.`,
      actor_name: quest.assignee || null,
      detail: { open_unblocking_count: openUnblocking.length, question_ids: openUnblocking.map((q) => q.id) },
    }, { client: db });
    return {
      ok: true,
      stage: "escalated",
      escalated: true,
      open_unblocking: openUnblocking.length,
      report: {
        msg: `${openUnblocking.length} open unblocking question(s) await the user — quest routed to escalated instead of purrview.`,
        fix: "The user must answer the unblocking questions (quest_questions, qtype='unblocking'). Once answered, the worker digests them and re-submits.",
      },
    };
  }

  // Gate 4 — objectives rows exist
  const { data: steps, error: sErr } = await db
    .from(publicTables.objectives)
    .select("id, n, name, status")
    .eq("quest_id", questId)
    .order("n", { ascending: true });
  if (sErr) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["steps_read"],
      report: {
        msg: sErr.message,
        fix: "DB read against `steps` failed. Check service-role auth and table name (libs/council/publicTables.js: steps).",
      },
    };
  }
  const stepList = steps || [];
  if (stepList.length === 0) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["no_steps"],
      report: {
        msg: "Quest has no steps rows. The materialized SMART plan is empty — there's nothing to execute or submit.",
        fix: "Steps are written at quest creation by questmaster.createQuest. If they're missing, the quest was created incorrectly — escalate to the Guildmaster.",
      },
    };
  }

  // Gate 5 — every objective is status='done'
  const unfinished = stepList.filter((s) => s.status !== "done");
  if (unfinished.length > 0) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["steps_not_done"],
      report: {
        msg: `${unfinished.length} step(s) up to the Checkpoint are not status='done'.`,
        fix: `Finish each step via worker.executeStep until its status flips to 'done'. Unfinished (non-done) steps: ${unfinished
          .map((s) => `n${s.n} "${s.name}" (${s.status})`)
          .join(", ")}.`,
        unfinished_steps: unfinished.map((s) => ({ n: s.n, name: s.name, status: s.status })),
      },
    };
  }

  // Gate 6 — every deliverable has a non-null ref (the produced artifact).
  // Deliverables are the canonical list of what the quest must produce; the
  // reviewer grades them, not objective output[] (dropped in BCS migration).
  const details = await getQuestDetails({ questId });
  if (details?.error) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["quest_unreadable_via_ui_path"],
      report: {
        msg: `getQuestDetails failed: ${details.error}. The reviewer's page would not render.`,
        fix: "Fix getQuestDetails / the read path so the quest page can load.",
      },
    };
  }
  const uiDeliverables = Array.isArray(details?.deliverables) ? details.deliverables : [];
  const missingRef = uiDeliverables.filter(
    (d) => d.ref == null || (typeof d.ref === "string" && d.ref.trim() === ""),
  );
  if (missingRef.length > 0) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["deliverables_missing_ref"],
      report: {
        msg: `${missingRef.length} deliverable(s) have no ref (produced artifact): ${missingRef.map((d) => d.name).join(", ")}.`,
        fix: "Ship each deliverable via worker.shipItemArtifact / libs/quest writeDeliverable. UPSERT on (quest_id, name) replaces in place.",
        missing: missingRef.map((d) => d.name),
      },
    };
  }

  // NOTE: VISUAL VERIFICATION is the PURRVIEW agent's responsibility, NOT the
  // worker's — a headless worker leaf has no CIC/user-channel browser to capture
  // a verify screenshot. The submit gate therefore requires only a produced `ref`
  // (above). The verify_screenshot_ref requirement lives at the purrview→review
  // gate (questPurrview.approve), where the CIC-capable reviewer sets it. See
  // docs/quest-lifecycle.md (visual-verification responsibility).

  // All gates pass — write lockphrase comment FIRST (the DB trigger
  // enforce_stage_gate requires it before the stage write succeeds).
  const summary = `Gate v${GATE_VERSION} passed. ${stepList.length} objective(s) done, ${uiDeliverables.length} deliverable(s) verified. ${SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE.slice(1)}.`;
  const { recordQuestComment } = await import("@/libs/quest/index.js");
  // submit_for_purrview is a PASS_THROUGH gate action (the chokepoint always
  // inserts it fresh — the DB enforce_stage_gate trigger requires the lockphrase
  // comment before the stage write, and auditStageBypass times its freshness).
  const { error: commentErr } = await recordQuestComment(questId, {
    source: "questExecution",
    action: "submit_for_purrview",
    summary,
    actor_name: quest.assignee || null,
    detail: {
      gate_version: GATE_VERSION,
      lockphrase: SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE,
      criteria_checked: CRITERIA_CHECKED,
      steps_count: stepList.length,
      assets: uiDeliverables.map((d) => d.name),
    },
  }, { client: db });
  if (commentErr) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["lockphrase_comment_write"],
      report: {
        msg: `Lockphrase comment failed to write: ${commentErr.message}. Stage NOT advanced (comment-before-stage order).`,
        fix: `Debug the quest_comments insert. The DB trigger enforce_stage_gate blocks stage→purrview without this comment.`,
      },
    };
  }

  // Advance stage (the trigger allows it because the lockphrase comment exists).
  const { error: upErr } = await db
    .from(publicTables.quests)
    .update({ stage: "purrview" })
    .eq("id", questId);
  if (upErr) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["stage_write"],
      report: {
        msg: upErr.message,
        fix: "Quest stage write failed at the DB layer. Check service-role auth or the enforce_stage_gate trigger — this is a system-level failure, not an agent fix.",
      },
    };
  }
  const { data: verify } = await db
    .from(publicTables.quests)
    .select("stage")
    .eq("id", questId)
    .single();
  if (verify?.stage !== "purrview") {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["stage_write_verify"],
      report: {
        msg: `Stage write did not persist; reads back as "${verify?.stage}".`,
        fix: "Stage write was silently rejected (likely RLS or the enforce_stage_gate trigger). Check that the lockphrase comment exists.",
      },
    };
  }

  return {
    ok: true,
    stage: "purrview",
    steps_count: stepList.length,
    assets_count: uiDeliverables.length,
    lockphrase: SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE,
    criteria_checked: CRITERIA_CHECKED,
  };
}
```

<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: libs/weapon/questHtmlMarkup/index.js -->
```js
/**
 * questHtmlMarkup weapon — html_markup stage transitions.
 *
 * The html_markup stage is the second of two new pre-execute stages. Its purpose
 * is to translate the AI-approved design baseline into a static-HTML proving-ground
 * page (one per deliverables row, hosted under app/(town)/proving-ground/<questId>/<item_key>/).
 * That page is the canonical implementation reference handed to the worker at
 * stage='execute'.
 *
 * Three transitions:
 *
 *   submit({questId})
 *     Called by housekeeping.runHtmlMarkupStage after writing all proving-ground
 *     pages and self-judging them. Gates: stage='html_markup' AND every deliverables row
 *     has html_markup_url set. Writes lockphrase but does NOT advance — the user
 *     reviews on the GM Desk before approving.
 *
 *   approve({questId})
 *     User-triggered from GM Desk. Advances stage='html_markup' → 'execute'.
 *     Gates: stage='html_markup' AND submit lockphrase comment exists.
 *
 *   bounce({questId, reason, item_keys?})
 *     User-triggered from GM Desk. Bounces back to 'design'. If item_keys is
 *     provided, clears design_approved on those deliverables so runDesignStage retries
 *     just those; otherwise clears all.
 */

import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";
import { publicTables } from "@/libs/council/publicTables";

export const toc = {
  submit:
    "Mark a quest's html_markup stage ready for user review. Gates: stage=html_markup AND every deliverables row has html_markup_url. Does not auto-advance — leaves the lockphrase for user-side approve.",
  approve:
    "User-triggered transition html_markup → execute. Gates: stage=html_markup AND submit lockphrase exists. Lockphrase: 'this quest now meets the criteria for execute'.",
  bounce:
    "User-triggered transition html_markup → design. Optionally clears design_approved on cited item_keys so runDesignStage targets only those deliverables. Lockphrase: 'this quest has been bounced from html_markup back to design'.",
};

export const GATE_VERSION = 1;
export const SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE = "this quest's html markup is ready for user review";
export const APPROVE_LOCKPHRASE = "this quest now meets the criteria for execute";
export const BOUNCE_LOCKPHRASE = "this quest has been bounced from html_markup back to design";

const SUBMIT_CRITERIA = [
  "questId is a non-empty string",
  "quest exists",
  "quest.stage === 'html_markup'",
  "deliverables rows exist for the quest",
  "every deliverable has html_markup_url set",
];

/** Internal: read quest + deliverables in one shot. */
async function loadQuestAndDeliverables(db, questId, expectedStage) {
  const { data: quest, error: qErr } = await db
    .from(publicTables.quests)
    .select("id, stage, title, assigned_to")
    .eq("id", questId)
    .single();
  if (qErr || !quest) {
    return { ok: false, failed: ["quest_exists"], msg: qErr?.message || "Quest not found." };
  }
  if (quest.stage !== expectedStage) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["stage"],
      msg: `Quest stage is "${quest.stage}", expected "${expectedStage}".`,
      current_stage: quest.stage,
    };
  }
  const { data: deliverables, error: iErr } = await db
    .from(publicTables.deliverables)
    .select("id, item_key, expectation, design_url, design_approved, html_markup_url")
    .eq("quest_id", questId);
  if (iErr) return { ok: false, failed: ["deliverables_read"], msg: iErr.message };
  return { ok: true, quest, deliverables: deliverables || [] };
}

/**
 * Stage stays at html_markup; just stamps "ready for user review."
 */
export async function submit({ questId }) {
  if (typeof questId !== "string" || !questId.trim()) {
    return { ok: false, failed: ["questId"], report: { msg: "questId is required." } };
  }
  const db = await database.init("service");
  const r = await loadQuestAndDeliverables(db, questId, "html_markup");
  if (!r.ok) return { ok: false, failed: r.failed, report: { msg: r.msg, current_stage: r.current_stage } };

  const missingMarkup = r.deliverables.filter((i) => !i.html_markup_url);
  if (missingMarkup.length > 0) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["html_markup_url_missing"],
      report: {
        msg: `${missingMarkup.length} deliverable(s) have no html_markup_url set.`,
        fix: `Run housekeeping.runHtmlMarkupStage to generate proving-ground pages for: ${missingMarkup.map((i) => i.item_key).join(", ")}.`,
        item_keys_missing_markup: missingMarkup.map((i) => i.item_key),
      },
    };
  }
  if (r.deliverables.length === 0) {
    return { ok: false, failed: ["no_deliverables"], report: { msg: "Quest has no deliverables." } };
  }

  const summary = `${r.deliverables.length} proving-ground page(s) written. ${SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE.slice(1)}.`;
  const { error: cErr } = await db.from(publicTables.questComments).insert({
    quest_id: questId,
    source: "questHtmlMarkup",
    action: "ready_for_user_review",
    summary,
    actor_name: r.quest.assigned_to || "Guildmaster",
    detail: {
      gate_version: GATE_VERSION,
      lockphrase: SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE,
      criteria_checked: SUBMIT_CRITERIA,
      deliverables_count: r.deliverables.length,
      item_keys: r.deliverables.map((i) => i.item_key),
      html_markup_urls: r.deliverables.map((i) => ({ item_key: i.item_key, url: i.html_markup_url })),
    },
  });
  if (cErr) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["lockphrase_comment_write"],
      report: {
        msg: `Lockphrase comment failed: ${cErr.message}.`,
        fix: `Manually insert quest_comments with source='questHtmlMarkup', action='ready_for_user_review', summary including "${SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE}".`,
      },
    };
  }
  return {
    ok: true,
    stage: "html_markup",
    deliverables_count: r.deliverables.length,
    lockphrase: SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE,
  };
}

/**
 * Advance html_markup → execute. User-triggered (GM Desk button).
 * Requires the submit lockphrase to exist as evidence the markup was actually
 * generated.
 */
export async function approve({ questId }) {
  if (typeof questId !== "string" || !questId.trim()) {
    return { ok: false, failed: ["questId"], report: { msg: "questId is required." } };
  }
  const db = await database.init("service");
  const r = await loadQuestAndDeliverables(db, questId, "html_markup");
  if (!r.ok) return { ok: false, failed: r.failed, report: { msg: r.msg, current_stage: r.current_stage } };

  // Confirm submit lockphrase exists (gate handshake — user shouldn't approve a
  // quest whose markup was never actually written).
  const { data: stories } = await db
    .from(publicTables.questComments)
    .select("summary")
    .eq("quest_id", questId)
    .eq("source", "questHtmlMarkup")
    .eq("action", "ready_for_user_review")
    .limit(1);
  const hasSubmit = (stories || []).some((s) => (s.summary || "").includes(SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE));
  if (!hasSubmit) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["submit_lockphrase_missing"],
      report: {
        msg: `No '${SUBMIT_LOCKPHRASE}' comment found. Run questHtmlMarkup.submit first.`,
        fix: "Call questHtmlMarkup.submit({questId}) after housekeeping.runHtmlMarkupStage finishes; that posts the lockphrase.",
      },
    };
  }

  const { error: upErr } = await db
    .from(publicTables.quests)
    .update({ stage: "execute" })
    .eq("id", questId);
  if (upErr) {
    return { ok: false, failed: ["stage_write"], report: { msg: upErr.message } };
  }
  const { data: v } = await db.from(publicTables.quests).select("stage").eq("id", questId).single();
  if (v?.stage !== "execute") {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["stage_write_verify"],
      report: { msg: `Stage write did not persist; reads back as "${v?.stage}".` },
    };
  }

  const summary = `User approved the html_markup. ${APPROVE_LOCKPHRASE.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + APPROVE_LOCKPHRASE.slice(1)}.`;
  await db.from(publicTables.questComments).insert({
    quest_id: questId,
    source: "questHtmlMarkup",
    action: "approve",
    summary,
    actor_name: "user",
    detail: { lockphrase: APPROVE_LOCKPHRASE, deliverables_count: r.deliverables.length },
  });

  return { ok: true, stage: "execute", lockphrase: APPROVE_LOCKPHRASE, deliverables_count: r.deliverables.length };
}

/**
 * Bounce html_markup → design. User-triggered (GM Desk button).
 * Optionally clears design_approved on cited item_keys so runDesignStage retries
 * just those deliverables. With no item_keys, clears all (full re-design).
 */
export async function bounce({ questId, reason, item_keys = null }) {
  if (typeof questId !== "string" || !questId.trim()) {
    return { ok: false, failed: ["questId"], report: { msg: "questId is required." } };
  }
  if (typeof reason !== "string" || !reason.trim()) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      failed: ["reason"],
      report: { msg: "reason is required (non-empty string)." },
    };
  }
  const db = await database.init("service");
  const r = await loadQuestAndDeliverables(db, questId, "html_markup");
  if (!r.ok) return { ok: false, failed: r.failed, report: { msg: r.msg, current_stage: r.current_stage } };

  // Clear design_approved on the deliverables being re-designed so runDesignStage
  // picks them up again.
  const targetKeys = Array.isArray(item_keys) && item_keys.length > 0
    ? item_keys
    : r.deliverables.map((i) => i.item_key);
  await db
    .from(publicTables.deliverables)
    .update({ design_approved: null, design_feedback: null })
    .eq("quest_id", questId)
    .in("item_key", targetKeys);

  const { error: upErr } = await db
    .from(publicTables.quests)
    .update({ stage: "design" })
    .eq("id", questId);
  if (upErr) {
    return { ok: false, failed: ["stage_write"], report: { msg: upErr.message } };
  }

  const summary = `User bounced from html_markup. ${BOUNCE_LOCKPHRASE.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + BOUNCE_LOCKPHRASE.slice(1)}. Reason: ${reason}`;
  await db.from(publicTables.questComments).insert({
    quest_id: questId,
    source: "questHtmlMarkup",
    action: "bounce",
    summary,
    actor_name: "user",
    detail: {
      lockphrase: BOUNCE_LOCKPHRASE,
      reason,
      cleared_design_approved_for: targetKeys,
    },
  });

  return {
    ok: true,
    stage: "design",
    lockphrase: BOUNCE_LOCKPHRASE,
    reason,
    cleared_design_approved_for: targetKeys,
  };
}
```

```markdown
# questMutator — engineering decisions

## 2026-07-03 — Audit comment doubles as the idempotency store
**Decision:** Batch idempotency (`idempotency_key`) is implemented by querying the
`guild_update` audit comment (`quest_comments.detail->>idempotency_key`), not a
dedicated idempotency table. Replay returns the results stored in the resolved
audit row; an *unresolved* matching row (a prior attempt that died mid-batch) is
re-applied into the same row (at-least-once).
**Rejected alternative:** A new `mutation_batches` table + migration.
**Why:** The comment-first pattern (questmaster.questUpdate) already mandates an
audit row per batch, written BEFORE mutations render and resolved after — the
replay record and the audit record are the same fact, so one row serves both.
No migration, no second write path, and the audit trail is visible on the quest
page where operators already look.
**Consequence-if-violated:** Splitting them reintroduces a migration + a second
source of truth that can disagree with the visible audit trail; dropping the
unresolved-row re-apply turns a mid-batch crash into a permanently blocked key.

## 2026-07-03 — Lease auth = stateless HMAC token + live worker_id check (no token table)
**Decision:** `mintLeaseToken` signs `{questId, workerId}` with
CARAVAN_SECRET/CRON_SECRET (`glt1.<payload>.<hmac>`); `applyQuestMutations`
additionally requires `quests.worker_id === workerId` at apply time. No expiry
claim and no server-side token storage.
**Rejected alternative:** Persisted lease tokens (table + revocation), or JWT
with expiry.
**Why:** The lease itself is the revocation mechanism — rescueStuckCaravans /
release clears `quests.worker_id`, which instantly invalidates every token for
that lease. Expiry would duplicate (and could contradict) the lease clock that
`worker_claimed_at` + rescue already own.
**Consequence-if-violated:** A token table drifts from the real lease state and
needs its own reaper; honoring tokens without the live `worker_id` re-check lets
a rescued/re-leased quest be written by a zombie worker.

## 2026-07-03 — Fail-fast batch validation (validate ALL, then apply)
**Decision:** Every mutation in a batch is whitelist-validated before ANY row is
touched; a single malformed mutation 400s the whole batch with per-index errors.
Runtime DB errors after validation are per-mutation (HTTP 207).
**Rejected alternative:** Best-effort per-mutation apply (the sibling
`/api/quest/mutate?action=batch` behavior).
**Why:** External guilds retry batches by idempotency key; a typo'd batch that
half-lands would be re-sent and re-half-land forever. Validation errors are
deterministic, so rejecting upfront costs nothing and keeps retries clean.
**Consequence-if-violated:** Partially-applied typo batches whose retries can
never converge, and audit rows that don't describe what actually happened.

## 2026-07-03 — quest_comments/quest_questions/quest_assets are remove-forbidden; comment update = `resolved` only
**Decision:** `remove` is rejected on quest_comments, quest_questions, and
quest_assets; quest_comments `update` may only touch `resolved`.
**Rejected alternative:** Symmetric add/update/remove on every whitelisted table.
**Why:** Comments and assets are the audit/verification surface the purrview
pipeline gates on — a worker that can delete or rewrite them can erase its own
trail. Questions carry the operator's authority rule (workers may ANSWER, never
delete/resolve user questions — questmaster.ruleUserQuestionAuthority).
**Consequence-if-violated:** The "single auditable write channel" thesis breaks;
verification can be gamed by the very workers it verifies.

## 2026-07-03 — Separate endpoint (/api/quest/update), legacy batch kept
**Decision:** The LOCKED operator contract lives at its own route; the older
machine channel `/api/quest/mutate?action=batch` (different shape: semantic
types, no lease check, no idempotency) is left untouched.
**Rejected alternative:** Reshaping the batch handler in place.
**Why:** The Hermes plugin (`hermes/plugins/guildos/caravan_client.py
mutate_quest`) already speaks the batch shape in production; breaking it to
avoid a second route trades a working integration for tidiness. Migration of
hermes to the new contract is a follow-up, after which batch can be retired.
**Consequence-if-violated:** Silent Hermes write failures the moment this
deploys.

## 2026-07-03 — `CARAVAN_API_DOC` is the ONE source for the natural-language protocol
**Decision:** The self-describing guild-worker protocol (lease lifecycle +
write-back contract + worked example + mutation whitelist) is a single exported
constant `CARAVAN_API_DOC`, computed once at module load. Its prose is
hand-written but the per-table column whitelist is DERIVED from
`describeContract()`/`MUTATION_TABLES` via `renderWhitelistMarkdown()`. The
endpoint `GET /api/caravan/help` renders this constant verbatim, and every
`/api/caravan/get` + `/lease` response carries the short `CARAVAN_HELP_POINTER`
to it.
**Rejected alternative:** Hand-authoring the human-readable contract in the
help route (or in a docs/*.md file) — the obvious "just write the endpoint's
text inline" move.
**Why:** The machine whitelist (`MUTATION_TABLES`) is the actual privilege
guard and changes over time (a new appendable column, a new whitelisted table).
A hand-typed doc drifts silently the moment the whitelist changes, and a
net-new external guild that trusts the doc would then send rejected payloads.
Deriving the whitelist section from the same structure the validator uses makes
the doc physically incapable of disagreeing with enforcement.
**Consequence-if-violated:** Two copies of the contract that diverge — the doc
tells an external guild one set of columns, the validator enforces another; the
"self-describing so a brand-new guild can learn the protocol with no other
context" guarantee is false and produces confident-but-rejected write-backs.
```
