```js
/**
 * @file questMutator — the write-back half of the guild dispatch contract.
 *
 * External guilds (Hermes/Codex, Cursor, remote machines) lease quests via the
 * pull-based caravan flow (GET /api/caravan/get → POST /api/caravan/lease) and
 * report progress through THIS weapon (surfaced at POST /api/quest/update).
 * It is the single auditable write channel the purrview/verification pipeline
 * can gate: every batch is lease-checked, column-whitelisted, idempotent, and
 * traceable to a worker_id via a `guild_update` audit comment.
 *
 * PAYLOAD CONTRACT (operator-specified, LOCKED 2026-07-03) — per-quest JSON:
 *   {
 *     "quest_id":  "<uuid>",
 *     "mutations": [
 *       {
 *         "type":   "<whitelisted subitem table>",   // quest_comments | objectives | deliverables | quest_assets | quest_questions
 *         "action": "add" | "update" | "remove",
 *         "ref_id": "<uuid of the subitem row; null for add>",
 *         "values": { "<actual column names of that table>": <value> }
 *       }
 *     ]
 *   }
 * Optional batch fields: idempotency_key (retry-safe replay), worker_id (master-
 * secret auth path only — the lease-token path derives it from the token).
 *
 * Append semantics: a values entry shaped {"op":"append","value":"..."} on an
 * appendable text column does a server-side read-modify-write (existing text +
 * "\n" + value) instead of overwriting. Update-only (add has nothing to append to).
 *
 * NOTE the naming collision: quest_comments has its own `action` COLUMN
 * (progress_note / update_request / …) distinct from the mutation-level
 * `action` field (add/update/remove). They never share a namespace: the
 * mutation action is envelope-level, the column lives inside `values`.
 *
 * SELF-DESCRIBING: the natural-language rendering of this contract — for a
 * net-new external guild that has never seen this file — lives in the exported
 * `CARAVAN_API_DOC` constant below (served at GET /api/caravan/help) and is
 * derived from describeContract()/MUTATION_TABLES, never hand-duplicated.
 */

import crypto from "node:crypto";
import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";
import { publicTables } from "@/libs/council/publicTables";
import { logWeaponCall } from "../weaponLog/index.js";

// ── table whitelist ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const UUID_RE = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i;

/** Mirrors questmaster.patchObjective's status vocabulary — keep aligned. */
const OBJECTIVE_STATUSES = new Set(["pending", "running", "active", "done", "review"]);
/** Mirrors /api/quest/mutate DELIVERABLE_KINDS — keep aligned. */
const DELIVERABLE_KINDS = new Set(["text", "html", "image", "video", "document"]);

/** verify_screenshot_ref = the polymorphic "Purrview Verification": EITHER a public
 *  Supabase Storage URL (screenshot, for visual kinds) OR a `PASS …`/`FAIL …` text
 *  verdict (for a text deliverable). Same rule as /api/quest/mutate + libs/quest —
 *  keep aligned. (null/"" = clear.) */
function validVerifyScreenshotRef(val) {
  if (val == null || val === "") return true;
  const s = String(val).trim();
  return /^https:\/\/.*\.supabase\.co\/storage\//i.test(s) || /^(PASS|FAIL)\b/i.test(s);
}

/**
 * The per-table mutation whitelist. `type` in the payload is the ACTUAL table
 * name (operator contract), mapped through publicTables for the real query.
 * Columns not listed here (id, quest_id, n, created_at, …) are unreachable —
 * that is the privilege boundary, not an omission.
 *
 * Per-table shape:
 *   addColumns / updateColumns — writable column sets per action (false = action forbidden)
 *   addRequired               — columns that must be present + non-empty on add
 *   addDefaults(workerId)     — server-injected defaults on add
 *   appendable                — text columns accepting the {"op":"append"} wrapper (update only)
 *   validate(col, val)        — per-column value guard; returns an error string or null
 */
export const MUTATION_TABLES = {
  quest_comments: {
    table: publicTables.questComments,
    addColumns: new Set(["summary", "actor_name", "source", "action", "resolved", "verdict", "detail"]),
    addRequired: ["summary"],
    addDefaults: (workerId) => ({ actor_name: workerId, source: "worker", resolved: false }),
    // Comments are an audit surface: workers may resolve/unresolve, never rewrite text.
    updateColumns: new Set(["resolved"]),
    removeAllowed: false,
    appendable: new Set(),
    validate(col, val) {
      if (col === "resolved" && typeof val !== "boolean") return "resolved must be a boolean";
      if (col === "detail" && (val == null || typeof val !== "object" || Array.isArray(val))) return "detail must be an object";
      return null;
    },
  },
  objectives: {
    table: publicTables.objectives,
    // `n` is server-assigned (max+1) on add — UNIQUE(quest_id, n) makes a
    // caller-supplied n a race hazard between concurrent workers.
    addColumns: new Set(["name", "status", "progress", "delta", "notes"]),
    addRequired: ["name"],
    addDefaults: () => ({ status: "active", delta: "new" }),
    updateColumns: new Set(["name", "status", "progress", "delta", "notes"]),
    removeAllowed: true,
    appendable: new Set(["progress", "delta", "notes"]),
    validate(col, val) {
      if (col === "status" && !OBJECTIVE_STATUSES.has(val)) return `invalid status '${val}' (allowed: ${[...OBJECTIVE_STATUSES].join(", ")})`;
      return null;
    },
  },
  deliverables: {
    table: publicTables.deliverables,
    addColumns: new Set(["name", "kind", "ref", "status", "verify_screenshot_ref"]),
    addRequired: ["name"],
    addDefaults: () => ({ kind: "text", status: "active" }),
    updateColumns: new Set(["name", "kind", "ref", "status", "verify_screenshot_ref"]),
    removeAllowed: true,
    appendable: new Set(),
    validate(col, val) {
      if (col === "kind" && !DELIVERABLE_KINDS.has(val)) return `invalid kind '${val}' (allowed: ${[...DELIVERABLE_KINDS].join(", ")})`;
      if (col === "verify_screenshot_ref" && !validVerifyScreenshotRef(val)) return "verify_screenshot_ref must be a public Supabase Storage URL (https://*.supabase.co/storage/*)";
      return null;
    },
  },
  quest_assets: {
    table: publicTables.questAssets,
    addColumns: new Set(["label", "ref", "kind", "source"]),
    addRequired: ["label", "ref"],
    addDefaults: (workerId) => ({ kind: "text", source: "worker", actor_name: workerId }),
    updateColumns: new Set(["label", "ref", "kind"]),
    // Assets are reviewable "where to look" pointers — removing one erases audit trail.
    removeAllowed: false,
    appendable: new Set(),
    validate: () => null,
  },
  quest_questions: {
    table: publicTables.questQuestions,
    addColumns: new Set(["qtype", "direction", "body", "unblocks_objective_ids"]),
    addRequired: ["body"],
    addDefaults: (workerId) => ({ qtype: "unblocking", direction: "to_user", answered: false, actor_name: workerId }),
    // Workers may ANSWER questions but never delete or resolve user questions
    // (questmaster.ruleUserQuestionAuthority) — so update is answer-only, remove forbidden.
    updateColumns: new Set(["answer", "answered"]),
    removeAllowed: false,
    appendable: new Set(["answer"]),
    validate(col, val) {
      if (col === "answered" && typeof val !== "boolean") return "answered must be a boolean";
      if (col === "qtype" && !["user", "unblocking"].includes(val)) return `invalid qtype '${val}' (allowed: user, unblocking)`;
      return null;
    },
  },
};

const MAX_MUTATIONS_PER_BATCH = 20; // matches the sibling /api/quest/mutate?action=batch cap
const AUDIT_ACTION = "guild_update";

// ── lease tokens ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const TOKEN_PREFIX = "glt1"; // guild lease token, version 1

function tokenSecret() {
  return process.env.CARAVAN_SECRET || process.env.CRON_SECRET || "";
}

const b64url = (buf) => Buffer.from(buf).toString("base64url");

function sign(payloadB64, secret) {
  return crypto.createHmac("sha256", secret).update(payloadB64).digest("base64url");
}

/**
 * Mint a stateless per-lease token binding (questId, workerId). Returned to the
 * guild by POST /api/caravan/lease. No expiry field: the token is only honored
 * while quests.worker_id still equals workerId, so a rescue/release invalidates
 * it naturally.
 *
 * @param {{ questId:string, workerId:string }} opts
 * @returns {string|null} token, or null when no signing secret is configured
 */
export function mintLeaseToken({ questId, workerId } = {}) {
  const secret = tokenSecret();
  if (!secret || !questId || !workerId) return null;
  const payload = b64url(JSON.stringify({ q: questId, w: workerId }));
  return `${TOKEN_PREFIX}.${payload}.${sign(payload, secret)}`;
}

/**
 * Verify a lease token's signature and unpack its claims. Does NOT check the
 * live lease — applyQuestMutations does that against quests.worker_id.
 *
 * @param {string} token
 * @returns {{ ok:true, questId:string, workerId:string } | { ok:false, error:string }}
 */
export function verifyLeaseToken(token) {
  const secret = tokenSecret();
  if (!secret) return { ok: false, error: "no signing secret configured (CARAVAN_SECRET/CRON_SECRET)" };
  const parts = String(token || "").split(".");
  if (parts.length !== 3 || parts[0] !== TOKEN_PREFIX) return { ok: false, error: "malformed lease token" };
  const [, payload, sig] = parts;
  const expected = sign(payload, secret);
  const a = Buffer.from(sig);
  const b = Buffer.from(expected);
  if (a.length !== b.length || !crypto.timingSafeEqual(a, b)) return { ok: false, error: "invalid lease token signature" };
  try {
    const { q, w } = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(payload, "base64url").toString("utf8"));
    if (!q || !w) return { ok: false, error: "lease token missing claims" };
    return { ok: true, questId: q, workerId: w };
  } catch {
    return { ok: false, error: "unreadable lease token payload" };
  }
}

/** True when the caller presented the raw machine master secret. */
export function isMasterSecret(provided) {
  const secret = tokenSecret();
  if (!secret || !provided) return false;
  const a = Buffer.from(String(provided));
  const b = Buffer.from(secret);
  return a.length === b.length && crypto.timingSafeEqual(a, b);
}

// ── validation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/** Is this values entry the {"op":"append","value":"..."} wrapper? */
function isAppendWrapper(v) {
  return v != null && typeof v === "object" && !Array.isArray(v) && v.op === "append";
}

/**
 * Validate ONE mutation against the whitelist. Pure — no I/O. Returns an error
 * string, or null when valid.
 */
export function validateMutation(mut) {
  if (!mut || typeof mut !== "object" || Array.isArray(mut)) return "mutation must be an object";
  const spec = MUTATION_TABLES[mut.type];
  if (!spec) return `unknown type '${mut.type}' (allowed: ${Object.keys(MUTATION_TABLES).join(", ")})`;
  const action = mut.action;
  if (!["add", "update", "remove"].includes(action)) return `invalid action '${action}' (allowed: add, update, remove)`;

  if (action === "add") {
    if (mut.ref_id != null) return "ref_id must be null for add";
    if (!mut.values || typeof mut.values !== "object" || Array.isArray(mut.values)) return "values object is required for add";
    for (const col of Object.keys(mut.values)) {
      if (!spec.addColumns.has(col)) return `column '${col}' is not writable on add to ${mut.type} (allowed: ${[...spec.addColumns].join(", ")})`;
      if (isAppendWrapper(mut.values[col])) return `append is only valid on update (column '${col}')`;
      const err = spec.validate(col, mut.values[col]);
      if (err) return err;
    }
    for (const req of spec.addRequired) {
      const v = mut.values[req];
      if (v == null || (typeof v === "string" && !v.trim())) return `'${req}' is required to add a ${mut.type} row`;
    }
    return null;
  }

  // update / remove target an existing row
  if (typeof mut.ref_id !== "string" || !UUID_RE.test(mut.ref_id)) return `ref_id must be a ${mut.type} row uuid for ${action}`;

  if (action === "remove") {
    if (!spec.removeAllowed) return `remove is not allowed on ${mut.type}`;
    return null;
  }

  // update
  if (!mut.values || typeof mut.values !== "object" || Array.isArray(mut.values)) return "values object is required for update";
  const cols = Object.keys(mut.values);
  if (cols.length === 0) return "values must contain at least one column for update";
  for (const col of cols) {
    if (!spec.updateColumns.has(col)) return `column '${col}' is not writable on update to ${mut.type} (allowed: ${[...spec.updateColumns].join(", ")})`;
    const v = mut.values[col];
    if (isAppendWrapper(v)) {
      if (!spec.appendable.has(col)) return `column '${col}' does not support append (appendable on ${mut.type}: ${[...spec.appendable].join(", ") || "none"})`;
      if (typeof v.value !== "string" || !v.value) return `append to '${col}' requires a non-empty string value`;
      continue;
    }
    const err = spec.validate(col, v);
    if (err) return err;
  }
  return null;
}

// ── apply ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/** One-line digest of a batch for the audit comment summary. */
function batchDigest(mutations) {
  return mutations.map((m) => `${m.action} ${m.type}${m.ref_id ? ` ${String(m.ref_id).slice(0, 8)}` : ""}`).join("; ");
}

async function applyOne(client, questId, workerId, mut) {
  const spec = MUTATION_TABLES[mut.type];

  if (mut.action === "add") {
    // quest_comments adds go through THE chokepoint (libs/quest
    // recordQuestComment) so telemetry redirect + dedup policy apply to guild
    // writes exactly as to internal ones.
    if (mut.type === "quest_comments") {
      const { recordQuestComment } = await import("@/libs/quest/index.js");
      const payload = { ...spec.addDefaults(workerId), ...mut.values };
      const res = await recordQuestComment(questId, payload, { client });
      if (res?.error) return { ok: false, error: res.error.message || String(res.error) };
      if (res?.redirected) return { ok: true, redirected: true };
      return { ok: true, id: res?.data?.id, ...(res?.deduped ? { deduped: true } : {}) };
    }
    const row = { quest_id: questId, ...spec.addDefaults(workerId), ...mut.values };
    if (mut.type === "objectives") {
      const { data: maxRow } = await client
        .from(spec.table).select("n").eq("quest_id", questId)
        .order("n", { ascending: false }).limit(1).maybeSingle();
      row.n = (maxRow?.n || 0) + 1;
    }
    const { data, error } = await client.from(spec.table).insert(row).select("id").single();
    if (error) return { ok: false, error: error.message };
    return { ok: true, id: data?.id };
  }

  if (mut.action === "remove") {
    const { data, error } = await client
      .from(spec.table).delete().eq("id", mut.ref_id).eq("quest_id", questId).select("id");
    if (error) return { ok: false, error: error.message };
    if ((data?.length || 0) !== 1) return { ok: false, error: `${mut.type} row not found in this quest` };
    return { ok: true, id: mut.ref_id };
  }

  // update — resolve append wrappers with a fresh read of the target row.
  const appendCols = Object.keys(mut.values).filter((c) => isAppendWrapper(mut.values[c]));
  let existing = null;
  {
    const selectCols = ["id", ...appendCols].join(", ");
    const { data, error } = await client
      .from(spec.table).select(selectCols).eq("id", mut.ref_id).eq("quest_id", questId).maybeSingle();
    if (error) return { ok: false, error: error.message };
    if (!data) return { ok: false, error: `${mut.type} row not found in this quest` };
    existing = data;
  }
  const update = {};
  for (const [col, v] of Object.entries(mut.values)) {
    if (isAppendWrapper(v)) {
      const prior = existing[col] == null ? "" : String(existing[col]);
      update[col] = prior ? `${prior}\n${v.value}` : v.value;
    } else {
      update[col] = v;
    }
  }
  const { data, error } = await client
    .from(spec.table).update(update).eq("id", mut.ref_id).eq("quest_id", questId).select("id").maybeSingle();
  if (error) return { ok: false, error: error.message };
  if (!data) return { ok: false, error: `${mut.type} row not found in this quest` };
  return { ok: true, id: mut.ref_id, fields: Object.keys(update) };
}

/**
 * Apply a lease-checked, whitelisted, idempotent mutation batch to one quest.
 *
 * Fail-fast validation: EVERY mutation is validated before ANY is applied, so a
 * typo'd batch never half-lands. Runtime DB errors after validation are
 * reported per-mutation (httpStatus 207) — the audit comment records both.
 *
 * @param {object} opts
 * @param {string} opts.questId         target quest uuid
 * @param {string} opts.workerId        must equal quests.worker_id (the live lease)
 * @param {Array<object>} opts.mutations LOCKED-contract mutation list
 * @param {string} [opts.idempotencyKey] replay-safe batch key (per quest)
 * @param {object} [opts.client]        injected supabase client (tests)
 * @returns {Promise<{ok:boolean, httpStatus:number, results?:Array, auditCommentId?:string, replayed?:boolean, error?:string, errors?:Array}>}
 */
export async function applyQuestMutations({ questId, workerId, mutations, idempotencyKey = null, client: injected } = {}) {
  const fail = (httpStatus, error, extra = {}) => {
    const out = { ok: false, httpStatus, error, ...extra };
    logWeaponCall({ weapon: "questMutator", fn: "applyQuestMutations", input: { questId, workerId, count: Array.isArray(mutations) ? mutations.length : 0 }, output: out, status: "fail" });
    return out;
  };

  if (typeof questId !== "string" || !UUID_RE.test(questId)) return fail(400, "quest_id must be a quest uuid");
  if (typeof workerId !== "string" || !workerId.trim()) return fail(400, "worker_id is required");
  if (!Array.isArray(mutations) || mutations.length === 0) return fail(400, "mutations array is required and must be non-empty");
  if (mutations.length > MAX_MUTATIONS_PER_BATCH) return fail(400, `max ${MAX_MUTATIONS_PER_BATCH} mutations per batch`);
  if (idempotencyKey != null && (typeof idempotencyKey !== "string" || !idempotencyKey.trim() || idempotencyKey.length > 128)) {
    return fail(400, "idempotency_key must be a non-empty string (max 128 chars)");
  }

  // Fail-fast: validate the WHOLE batch before touching the database.
  const errors = mutations
    .map((m, i) => ({ i, error: validateMutation(m) }))
    .filter((e) => e.error);
  if (errors.length) return fail(400, "batch failed validation — nothing was applied", { errors });

  const client = injected || (await database.init("service"));

  // Lease gate: the caller may only mutate a quest it currently holds.
  const { data: quest, error: qErr } = await client
    .from(publicTables.quests).select("id, worker_id").eq("id", questId).maybeSingle();
  if (qErr) return fail(500, qErr.message);
  if (!quest) return fail(404, "quest not found");
  if (quest.worker_id !== workerId.trim()) {
    return fail(409, "lease not held: quests.worker_id does not match this worker (re-lease via /api/caravan/get + /api/caravan/lease)");
  }

  // Idempotency: the guild_update audit comment doubles as the replay record.
  if (idempotencyKey) {
    const { data: prior } = await client
      .from(publicTables.questComments)
      .select("id, resolved, detail")
      .eq("quest_id", questId)
      .eq("action", AUDIT_ACTION)
      .eq("detail->>idempotency_key", idempotencyKey)
      .order("created_at", { ascending: false })
      .limit(1)
      .maybeSingle();
    if (prior?.resolved && Array.isArray(prior?.detail?.results)) {
      const out = { ok: prior.detail.batch_ok !== false, httpStatus: 200, replayed: true, auditCommentId: prior.id, results: prior.detail.results };
      logWeaponCall({ weapon: "questMutator", fn: "applyQuestMutations", input: { questId, workerId, idempotencyKey }, output: { replayed: true }, status: "ok" });
      return out;
    }
    // An unresolved prior audit row = a previous attempt died mid-batch. Fall
    // through and re-apply (at-least-once), reusing that audit row.
    if (prior?.id) {
      const results = [];
      for (const mut of mutations) results.push({ type: mut.type, action: mut.action, ...(await applyOne(client, questId, workerId, mut)) });
      const allOk = results.every((r) => r.ok);
      await client.from(publicTables.questComments)
        .update({ resolved: true, detail: { ...(prior.detail || {}), results, batch_ok: allOk, reapplied: true } })
        .eq("id", prior.id);
      const out = { ok: allOk, httpStatus: allOk ? 200 : 207, reapplied: true, auditCommentId: prior.id, results };
      logWeaponCall({ weapon: "questMutator", fn: "applyQuestMutations", input: { questId, workerId, idempotencyKey }, output: { reapplied: true, allOk }, status: allOk ? "ok" : "fail" });
      return out;
    }
  }

  // Comment-first (questmaster.questUpdate pattern): the audit record lands
  // BEFORE any mutation renders, then is resolved with results after.
  const { recordQuestComment } = await import("@/libs/quest/index.js");
  const { data: audit, error: aErr } = await recordQuestComment(questId, {
    summary: `Guild update from ${workerId}: ${mutations.length} mutation(s) — ${batchDigest(mutations)}`.slice(0, 1900),
    actor_name: workerId,
    source: "worker",
    action: AUDIT_ACTION,
    resolved: false,
    detail: { idempotency_key: idempotencyKey, worker_id: workerId, mutation_count: mutations.length },
  }, { client });
  if (aErr || !audit?.id) return fail(500, aErr?.message || "audit comment insert returned no id");

  const results = [];
  for (const mut of mutations) results.push({ type: mut.type, action: mut.action, ...(await applyOne(client, questId, workerId, mut)) });
  const allOk = results.every((r) => r.ok);

  await client.from(publicTables.questComments)
    .update({ resolved: true, detail: { idempotency_key: idempotencyKey, worker_id: workerId, mutation_count: mutations.length, results, batch_ok: allOk } })
    .eq("id", audit.id);

  const out = { ok: allOk, httpStatus: allOk ? 200 : 207, auditCommentId: audit.id, results };
  logWeaponCall({ weapon: "questMutator", fn: "applyQuestMutations", input: { questId, workerId, count: mutations.length, idempotencyKey }, output: { allOk, applied: results.filter((r) => r.ok).length }, status: allOk ? "ok" : "fail" });
  return out;
}

/** Machine-readable contract description (served by GET /api/quest/update). */
export function describeContract() {
  const tables = {};
  for (const [type, spec] of Object.entries(MUTATION_TABLES)) {
    tables[type] = {
      add: spec.addColumns.size ? { columns: [...spec.addColumns], required: spec.addRequired } : false,
      update: spec.updateColumns.size ? { columns: [...spec.updateColumns], appendable: [...spec.appendable] } : false,
      remove: spec.removeAllowed,
    };
  }
  return {
    endpoint: "POST /api/quest/update",
    auth: "Authorization: Bearer <lease_token from POST /api/caravan/lease> — or the caravan master secret plus worker_id in the body",
    body: { quest_id: "<uuid>", worker_id: "<required on the master-secret path>", idempotency_key: "<optional, retry-safe>", mutations: [{ type: "<table>", action: "add|update|remove", ref_id: "<uuid|null>", values: { "<column>": "<value> | {\"op\":\"append\",\"value\":\"...\"}" } }] },
    maxMutationsPerBatch: MAX_MUTATIONS_PER_BATCH,
    tables,
  };
}

// ── self-describing protocol doc (single source of truth) ───────────────────────

/**
 * Short natural-language pointer surfaced on EVERY caravan response (get + lease)
 * so any guild — internal Claude, Hermes/Codex, or a net-new external guild with
 * no other context — discovers the write-back protocol automatically at lease time.
 * The full doc lives one hop away at GET /api/caravan/help (CARAVAN_API_DOC).
 */
export const CARAVAN_HELP_POINTER =
  "To report progress on these quests, POST mutations to /api/quest/update. " +
  "Full caravan API + payload docs (natural language): GET /api/caravan/help";

/** Render the per-table mutation whitelist as a markdown list, derived from
 *  describeContract() so it can never drift from MUTATION_TABLES (the real guard). */
function renderWhitelistMarkdown() {
  const { tables } = describeContract();
  const lines = [];
  for (const [type, t] of Object.entries(tables)) {
    lines.push(`### \`${type}\``);
    if (t.add) {
      lines.push(`- **add** — writable columns: ${t.add.columns.map((c) => `\`${c}\``).join(", ")}` +
        (t.add.required.length ? ` · required: ${t.add.required.map((c) => `\`${c}\``).join(", ")}` : ""));
    } else {
      lines.push(`- **add** — not allowed`);
    }
    if (t.update) {
      lines.push(`- **update** — writable columns: ${t.update.columns.map((c) => `\`${c}\``).join(", ")}` +
        (t.update.appendable.length ? ` · append-capable: ${t.update.appendable.map((c) => `\`${c}\``).join(", ")}` : " · (no append-capable columns)"));
    } else {
      lines.push(`- **update** — not allowed`);
    }
    lines.push(`- **remove** — ${t.remove ? "allowed" : "not allowed"}`);
    lines.push("");
  }
  return lines.join("\n").trimEnd();
}

/**
 * THE single source of truth for the human/LLM-readable caravan protocol, served
 * verbatim by GET /api/caravan/help. Computed once at module load. Prose is
 * hand-written; the table/column whitelist is DERIVED from describeContract() (so
 * it stays honest against MUTATION_TABLES). Do NOT hand-duplicate this contract
 * elsewhere — render this constant.
 */
export const CARAVAN_API_DOC = [
  "# GuildOS Caravan API — Guild Worker Protocol",
  "",
  "You are a guild worker — an LLM agent or a human programmer — that GuildOS has",
  "assigned quests to. This document is everything you need to pull that work, do",
  "it, and report progress back. No other context is required.",
  "",
  "A **quest** is a unit of work. It owns child rows you will read and write:",
  "`objectives` (the plan/checklist), `deliverables` (what you must produce),",
  "`quest_comments` (the audit/progress thread), `quest_assets` (where-to-look",
  "pointers), and `quest_questions` (clarifications). The quest IS the durable",
  "record — you progress work by mutating these rows, not by returning a result.",
  "",
  "All caravan endpoints authenticate with a bearer token:",
  "`Authorization: Bearer <CARAVAN_SECRET>` (the shared machine secret your guild",
  "was issued). The write-back endpoint additionally accepts a per-lease token",
  "(below), which is the preferred credential for reporting progress.",
  "",
  "## The lease lifecycle",
  "",
  "GuildOS dispatches work with a two-phase pull-based lease. Poll it on your own",
  "cadence:",
  "",
  "### 1. Pull your assigned quests — `GET /api/caravan/get`",
  "",
  "```",
  "GET /api/caravan/get?class=<caravanClass>&workerguildname=<yourGuild>&limit=25",
  "Authorization: Bearer <CARAVAN_SECRET>",
  "```",
  "",
  "Returns the quests currently available to your guild, each with an execute-ready",
  "payload (title, description, objectives, deliverables). This TEMP-leases each",
  "returned quest to your guild: if you never complete step 2, the temp lease goes",
  "stale and the quest returns to the pool for another worker. Add `dry=1` to",
  "preview without leasing.",
  "",
  "### 2. Claim the ones you'll actually run — `POST /api/caravan/lease`",
  "",
  "```",
  "POST /api/caravan/lease",
  "Authorization: Bearer <CARAVAN_SECRET>",
  "Content-Type: application/json",
  "",
  '{ "guildName": "<yourGuild>",',
  '  "payload": [ { "quest_id": "<uuid>", "worker_id": "<your worker/agent name>" } ] }',
  "```",
  "",
  "Commit which quests your workers will run. Every temp-leased quest you do NOT",
  "list here is released back to the pool. The response carries a `leases[]` array;",
  "each entry has a **`lease_token`** — SAVE IT. That token authenticates your",
  "write-backs for that one quest, so you don't need to resend the master secret.",
  "",
  "### 3. Do the work.",
  "",
  "### 4. Report progress — `POST /api/quest/update`  (repeat as you go)",
  "",
  "This is the ONLY write channel back to a quest. Call it as often as you make",
  "progress: update an objective's status, append a note, attach a deliverable,",
  "answer a question. Every batch is lease-checked, column-whitelisted, idempotent,",
  "and audit-logged.",
  "",
  "```",
  "POST /api/quest/update",
  "Authorization: Bearer <lease_token>      # from step 2 (preferred)",
  "Content-Type: application/json",
  "```",
  "",
  "Auth — two accepted forms:",
  "- **Lease token** (`glt1.…`, from step 2): scoped to one quest. `quest_id` in the",
  "  body must match the token's quest.",
  "- **Master secret** (`CARAVAN_SECRET`): the trusted machine channel. On this path",
  "  you must also send your `worker_id` (body field or `X-Worker-Id` header). It",
  "  must match the live lease (`quests.worker_id`) or the write is rejected 409.",
  "",
  "## The write-back payload contract (LOCKED)",
  "",
  "One JSON body targets ONE quest and carries a list of mutations:",
  "",
  "```json",
  "{",
  '  "quest_id": "<uuid>",',
  '  "idempotency_key": "<optional, retry-safe — replaying the same key never double-applies>",',
  '  "worker_id": "<required ONLY on the master-secret path>",',
  '  "mutations": [',
  "    {",
  '      "type":   "<whitelisted child table>",',
  '      "action": "add" | "update" | "remove",',
  '      "ref_id": "<uuid of the row to update/remove; null for add>",',
  '      "values": { "<actual column name>": <value> }',
  "    }",
  "  ]",
  "}",
  "```",
  "",
  "- **`type`** is the ACTUAL child-table name (see the whitelist below). Anything",
  "  not whitelisted — including the `quests` table itself and columns like `id`,",
  "  `quest_id`, `n`, `created_at` — is unreachable by design; that is the privilege",
  "  boundary, not an omission.",
  "- **`action`**: `add` (ref_id must be null, `values` supplies the new row),",
  "  `update` (ref_id targets an existing row), `remove` (ref_id targets an existing",
  "  row; only allowed on some tables).",
  "- **Append semantics**: on an append-capable text column, pass",
  '  `{ "op": "append", "value": "..." }` instead of a plain value to do a',
  "  server-side read-modify-write (existing text + newline + your value) rather",
  "  than overwriting. Append is valid on `update` only (an `add` has nothing to",
  "  append to).",
  "- **`idempotency_key`** (optional, ≤128 chars): make a batch retry-safe. Replaying",
  "  a completed key returns the stored result without re-applying; a key whose prior",
  "  attempt died mid-batch is safely re-applied (at-least-once).",
  `- At most ${MAX_MUTATIONS_PER_BATCH} mutations per batch.`,
  "- Validation is fail-fast: if ANY mutation is invalid the whole batch is rejected",
  "  (400) and nothing is applied. Runtime per-row failures after validation come",
  "  back as HTTP 207 with a per-mutation `results[]`.",
  "",
  "> ⚠️ **Column-name gotcha:** the `quest_comments` text lives in the **`summary`**",
  "> column, NOT `body`. Writing progress notes to `body` silently misses the column",
  "> whitelist and is rejected. Use `summary`.",
  "",
  "## Worked example",
  "",
  "Append a line to objective `c184eba3-…`'s delta and drop a progress note, in one",
  "idempotent batch, authenticated by the lease token:",
  "",
  "```json",
  "{",
  '  "quest_id": "c73eeeac-dfa9-4c8b-8ac5-86fe55c4ada7",',
  '  "idempotency_key": "worker-run-42",',
  '  "mutations": [',
  "    {",
  '      "type": "objectives",',
  '      "action": "update",',
  '      "ref_id": "c184eba3-4a8b-4a9f-b8a0-7fc7690313d6",',
  '      "values": { "delta": { "op": "append", "value": "Meooow" } }',
  "    },",
  "    {",
  '      "type": "quest_comments",',
  '      "action": "add",',
  '      "ref_id": null,',
  '      "values": { "summary": "hello world", "action": "progress_note" }',
  "    }",
  "  ]",
  "}",
  "```",
  "",
  "## Mutation whitelist — writable columns per table",
  "",
  "(Server-injected defaults like `actor_name`, `source`, `status`, and objective",
  "`n` are filled for you on add; you don't send them.)",
  "",
  renderWhitelistMarkdown(),
  "",
  "## Reporting patterns",
  "",
  "- **Made progress on an objective** → `update` its `status`",
  `  (${[...OBJECTIVE_STATUSES].join(" | ")}) and append to \`progress\`/\`delta\`/\`notes\`.`,
  "- **Produced a deliverable** → `add` a `deliverables` row (`name`, `kind`, `ref`),",
  "  or `update` an existing one; set `verify_screenshot_ref` to a public Supabase",
  "  Storage URL (visual proof) or a `PASS …`/`FAIL …` text verdict.",
  "- **Need a decision from the user** → `add` a `quest_questions` row (`body`).",
  "- **Left something to look at** → `add` a `quest_assets` row (`label`, `ref`).",
  "- **Narrating what you did** → `add` a `quest_comments` row (`summary`).",
  "",
  "That's the whole protocol. Pull, claim, work, report — the quest is the record.",
].join("\n");

import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach } from "vitest";

// ── mocks (pattern mirrors libs/caravan/index.test.js) ───────────────────────

const { mockDb } = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  mockDb: { from: vi.fn() },
}));

vi.mock("@/libs/council/database", () => ({
  database: { init: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(mockDb) },
}));

vi.mock("@/libs/council/publicTables", () => ({
  publicTables: {
    quests: "quests",
    questComments: "quest_comments",
    objectives: "objectives",
    deliverables: "deliverables",
    questAssets: "quest_assets",
    questQuestions: "quest_questions",
  },
}));

vi.mock("../weaponLog/index.js", () => ({ logWeaponCall: vi.fn() }));

const recordQuestComment = vi.hoisted(() => vi.fn());
vi.mock("@/libs/quest/index.js", () => ({ recordQuestComment }));

import {
  validateMutation,
  mintLeaseToken,
  verifyLeaseToken,
  isMasterSecret,
  applyQuestMutations,
  MUTATION_TABLES,
  CARAVAN_API_DOC,
  CARAVAN_HELP_POINTER,
} from "./index.js";

const QUEST = "c73eeeac-dfa9-4c8b-8ac5-86fe55c4ada7";
const OBJ = "c184eba3-4a8b-4a9f-b8a0-7fc7690313d6";

beforeEach(() => {
  vi.clearAllMocks();
  process.env.CARAVAN_SECRET = "test-secret";
});

// ── validateMutation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

describe("validateMutation", () => {
  it("accepts the operator's worked example", () => {
    expect(validateMutation({
      type: "quest_comments", action: "add", ref_id: null,
      values: { summary: "hello world", actor_name: "hermes-worker-1", source: "hermes", action: "progress_note", resolved: true },
    })).toBeNull();
    expect(validateMutation({
      type: "objectives", action: "update", ref_id: OBJ,
      values: { delta: { op: "append", value: "Meooow" } },
    })).toBeNull();
  });

  it("rejects unknown tables and unknown columns", () => {
    expect(validateMutation({ type: "quests", action: "update", ref_id: OBJ, values: { stage: "complete" } }))
      .toMatch(/unknown type/);
    expect(validateMutation({ type: "objectives", action: "update", ref_id: OBJ, values: { quest_id: QUEST } }))
      .toMatch(/not writable/);
    expect(validateMutation({ type: "objectives", action: "add", ref_id: null, values: { name: "x", n: 1 } }))
      .toMatch(/not writable/);
  });

  it("rejects remove on protected tables, allows it on objectives/deliverables", () => {
    expect(validateMutation({ type: "quest_comments", action: "remove", ref_id: OBJ })).toMatch(/not allowed/);
    expect(validateMutation({ type: "quest_questions", action: "remove", ref_id: OBJ })).toMatch(/not allowed/);
    expect(validateMutation({ type: "quest_assets", action: "remove", ref_id: OBJ })).toMatch(/not allowed/);
    expect(validateMutation({ type: "objectives", action: "remove", ref_id: OBJ })).toBeNull();
    expect(validateMutation({ type: "deliverables", action: "remove", ref_id: OBJ })).toBeNull();
  });

  it("enforces append rules: update-only, appendable columns, string value", () => {
    expect(validateMutation({ type: "objectives", action: "add", ref_id: null, values: { name: "x", notes: { op: "append", value: "y" } } }))
      .toMatch(/append is only valid on update/);
    expect(validateMutation({ type: "objectives", action: "update", ref_id: OBJ, values: { name: { op: "append", value: "y" } } }))
      .toMatch(/does not support append/);
    expect(validateMutation({ type: "objectives", action: "update", ref_id: OBJ, values: { delta: { op: "append", value: "" } } }))
      .toMatch(/non-empty string/);
  });

  it("enforces required add columns, ref_id shape, and value guards", () => {
    expect(validateMutation({ type: "quest_comments", action: "add", ref_id: null, values: { actor_name: "w" } }))
      .toMatch(/'summary' is required/);
    expect(validateMutation({ type: "objectives", action: "add", ref_id: OBJ, values: { name: "x" } }))
      .toMatch(/ref_id must be null/);
    expect(validateMutation({ type: "objectives", action: "update", ref_id: "not-a-uuid", values: { notes: "x" } }))
      .toMatch(/uuid/);
    expect(validateMutation({ type: "objectives", action: "update", ref_id: OBJ, values: { status: "bogus" } }))
      .toMatch(/invalid status/);
    expect(validateMutation({ type: "deliverables", action: "update", ref_id: OBJ, values: { verify_screenshot_ref: "file:///c/shot.png" } }))
      .toMatch(/Supabase Storage/);
    expect(validateMutation({ type: "quest_comments", action: "update", ref_id: OBJ, values: { resolved: "yes" } }))
      .toMatch(/boolean/);
  });
});

// ── lease tokens ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

describe("lease tokens", () => {
  it("round-trips mint → verify", () => {
    const token = mintLeaseToken({ questId: QUEST, workerId: "hermes-worker-1" });
    expect(token).toMatch(/^glt1\./);
    const claims = verifyLeaseToken(token);
    expect(claims).toEqual({ ok: true, questId: QUEST, workerId: "hermes-worker-1" });
  });

  it("rejects tampered and malformed tokens", () => {
    const token = mintLeaseToken({ questId: QUEST, workerId: "hermes-worker-1" });
    const [p, payload] = token.split(".");
    const forged = `${p}.${Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({ q: QUEST, w: "attacker" })).toString("base64url")}.${token.split(".")[2]}`;
    expect(verifyLeaseToken(forged).ok).toBe(false);
    expect(verifyLeaseToken(`${p}.${payload}.AAAA`).ok).toBe(false);
    expect(verifyLeaseToken("garbage").ok).toBe(false);
    expect(verifyLeaseToken("").ok).toBe(false);
  });

  it("isMasterSecret matches only the exact secret", () => {
    expect(isMasterSecret("test-secret")).toBe(true);
    expect(isMasterSecret("test-secreT")).toBe(false);
    expect(isMasterSecret("")).toBe(false);
  });
});

// ── applyQuestMutations ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/** Chainable supabase mock: each from(table) call pops the next queued result. */
function buildClient(queue) {
  const calls = [];
  const from = vi.fn((table) => {
    const step = queue.shift() || { data: null, error: null };
    const call = { table, filters: [], op: null, payload: null };
    calls.push(call);
    const chain = {
      select: () => chain,
      eq: (k, v) => { call.filters.push([k, v]); return chain; },
      is: () => chain,
      order: () => chain,
      limit: () => chain,
      maybeSingle: () => Promise.resolve(step),
      single: () => Promise.resolve(step),
      insert: (row) => { call.op = "insert"; call.payload = row; return chain; },
      update: (row) => { call.op = "update"; call.payload = row; return chain; },
      delete: () => { call.op = "delete"; return chain; },
      then: (resolve) => resolve(step),
    };
    return chain;
  });
  return { client: { from }, calls };
}

describe("applyQuestMutations", () => {
  it("400s the whole batch when any mutation is invalid (nothing applied)", async () => {
    const { client } = buildClient([]);
    const res = await applyQuestMutations({
      questId: QUEST, workerId: "w1", client,
      mutations: [
        { type: "quest_comments", action: "add", ref_id: null, values: { summary: "ok" } },
        { type: "objectives", action: "update", ref_id: OBJ, values: { quest_id: "evil" } },
      ],
    });
    expect(res.ok).toBe(false);
    expect(res.httpStatus).toBe(400);
    expect(res.errors).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(res.errors[0].i).toBe(1);
    expect(client.from).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("409s when the caller does not hold the lease", async () => {
    const { client } = buildClient([{ data: { id: QUEST, worker_id: "someone-else" }, error: null }]);
    const res = await applyQuestMutations({
      questId: QUEST, workerId: "w1", client,
      mutations: [{ type: "quest_comments", action: "add", ref_id: null, values: { summary: "hi" } }],
    });
    expect(res.httpStatus).toBe(409);
    expect(res.error).toMatch(/lease not held/);
  });

  it("applies a valid batch: audit-first, append read-modify-write, resolve after", async () => {
    recordQuestComment.mockResolvedValueOnce({ data: { id: "audit-1" }, error: null }); // audit comment
    const { client, calls } = buildClient([
      { data: { id: QUEST, worker_id: "hermes-worker-1" }, error: null },      // lease read
      { data: { id: OBJ, delta: "old" }, error: null },                        // append pre-read
      { data: { id: OBJ }, error: null },                                      // objective update
      { data: [], error: null },                                               // audit resolve
    ]);
    recordQuestComment.mockResolvedValueOnce({ data: { id: "cmt-1" }, error: null }); // comment add via chokepoint

    const res = await applyQuestMutations({
      questId: QUEST, workerId: "hermes-worker-1", client,
      mutations: [
        { type: "objectives", action: "update", ref_id: OBJ, values: { delta: { op: "append", value: "Meooow" } } },
        { type: "quest_comments", action: "add", ref_id: null, values: { summary: "hello world" } },
      ],
    });

    expect(res.ok).toBe(true);
    expect(res.httpStatus).toBe(200);
    expect(res.auditCommentId).toBe("audit-1");
    expect(res.results).toHaveLength(2);
    // audit comment written FIRST (comment-first), with guild_update action
    expect(recordQuestComment.mock.calls[0][1].action).toBe("guild_update");
    expect(recordQuestComment.mock.calls[0][1].actor_name).toBe("hermes-worker-1");
    // append produced old + "\n" + new
    const objUpdate = calls.find((c) => c.table === "objectives" && c.op === "update");
    expect(objUpdate.payload.delta).toBe("old\nMeooow");
    // comment add went through the chokepoint with worker defaults
    expect(recordQuestComment.mock.calls[1][1].summary).toBe("hello world");
    // audit row resolved with results at the end
    const auditResolve = calls.find((c) => c.table === "quest_comments" && c.op === "update");
    expect(auditResolve.payload.resolved).toBe(true);
    expect(auditResolve.payload.detail.batch_ok).toBe(true);
  });

  it("replays a resolved idempotent batch without re-applying", async () => {
    const stored = [{ type: "quest_comments", action: "add", ok: true, id: "cmt-1" }];
    const { client, calls } = buildClient([
      { data: { id: QUEST, worker_id: "w1" }, error: null },                                    // lease read
      { data: { id: "audit-1", resolved: true, detail: { idempotency_key: "k1", results: stored, batch_ok: true } }, error: null }, // replay lookup
    ]);
    const res = await applyQuestMutations({
      questId: QUEST, workerId: "w1", idempotencyKey: "k1", client,
      mutations: [{ type: "quest_comments", action: "add", ref_id: null, values: { summary: "hello world" } }],
    });
    expect(res.replayed).toBe(true);
    expect(res.results).toEqual(stored);
    expect(recordQuestComment).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(calls.filter((c) => c.op === "insert")).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it("assigns n = max+1 on objective add", async () => {
    recordQuestComment.mockResolvedValueOnce({ data: { id: "audit-1" }, error: null });
    const { client, calls } = buildClient([
      { data: { id: QUEST, worker_id: "w1" }, error: null }, // lease read
      { data: { n: 4 }, error: null },                       // max-n read
      { data: { id: "new-obj" }, error: null },              // insert
      { data: [], error: null },                             // audit resolve
    ]);
    const res = await applyQuestMutations({
      questId: QUEST, workerId: "w1", client,
      mutations: [{ type: "objectives", action: "add", ref_id: null, values: { name: "New objective" } }],
    });
    expect(res.ok).toBe(true);
    const insert = calls.find((c) => c.table === "objectives" && c.op === "insert");
    expect(insert.payload.n).toBe(5);
    expect(insert.payload.quest_id).toBe(QUEST);
    expect(insert.payload.status).toBe("active");
  });
});

// ── contract sanity ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

describe("MUTATION_TABLES", () => {
  it("never whitelists privileged columns", () => {
    for (const spec of Object.values(MUTATION_TABLES)) {
      for (const col of ["id", "quest_id", "created_at", "updated_at", "n"]) {
        expect(spec.addColumns.has(col)).toBe(false);
        expect(spec.updateColumns.has(col)).toBe(false);
      }
    }
  });
});

// ── self-describing protocol doc (GET /api/caravan/help) ────────────────────────

describe("CARAVAN_API_DOC", () => {
  it("documents the whole lifecycle + write-back contract in one derived constant", () => {
    // Lease lifecycle endpoints.
    for (const ep of ["/api/caravan/get", "/api/caravan/lease", "/api/quest/update"]) {
      expect(CARAVAN_API_DOC).toContain(ep);
    }
    // Contract essentials: whitelisted tables, append semantics, idempotency, lease token.
    for (const table of Object.keys(MUTATION_TABLES)) expect(CARAVAN_API_DOC).toContain(table);
    expect(CARAVAN_API_DOC).toMatch(/"op":\s*"append"/);
    expect(CARAVAN_API_DOC).toContain("idempotency_key");
    expect(CARAVAN_API_DOC).toContain("lease_token");
    // The quest_comments text-column gotcha is called out explicitly.
    expect(CARAVAN_API_DOC).toMatch(/`summary`/);
    expect(CARAVAN_API_DOC).toMatch(/NOT `body`/);
    // The worked example (reused from the header/tests) is embedded verbatim.
    expect(CARAVAN_API_DOC).toContain("c73eeeac-dfa9-4c8b-8ac5-86fe55c4ada7");
    // Whitelist is derived, not hand-typed: an objective append column shows up.
    expect(CARAVAN_API_DOC).toContain("append-capable");
  });

  it("the help pointer names the help endpoint", () => {
    expect(CARAVAN_HELP_POINTER).toContain("/api/caravan/help");
    expect(CARAVAN_HELP_POINTER).toContain("/api/quest/update");
  });
});
```

<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: libs/weapon/questPurrview/engineering_decisions.md -->
```markdown
# Engineering decisions — `libs/weapon/questPurrview`

Rationale layer (per CLAUDE.md §6). The WHY behind purrview's visual-verification
gate. Append; supersede in place when a decision changes.

---

## 2026-07-03 — a PASS milestone verdict (`approve`, `final_gate_pass`) is written `resolved=true`

**Decision.** `questPurrview.approve` (and `questReview.final_gate_pass`, same
class) now writes its `quest_comments` row with `resolved: true`. **Rejected
alternative:** the prior behavior — inherit the column default `resolved=false`
"for audit." **Why:** an approval is a *terminal* pass verdict, not an open
to-do. Multiple `resolved=false` scans classify a comment as pending FEEDBACK by
its **source prefix** alone — `registry.js` rung-8 digest
(`unresolvedDigestibleCommentsByQuest`) and `caravan/index.js`
`resolveGateForward.hasFeedback` (`src.startsWith("questpurrview")` /
`.startsWith("review")`). An unresolved PASS row therefore reads back as
"unaddressed feedback," which either mis-routes a done quest or is only masked by
the milestone short-circuit firing first. Writing PASS rows `resolved=true` keeps
them out of those scans entirely (the verdict-based guard in the rung-8 counter
stays as defense-in-depth for legacy rows). **Safe because:** the approve /
final_gate_pass UPSERT keys on `(quest_id, action)` — NOT on `resolved` — and
`milestoneByQuest` does not filter `resolved`, so the milestone floor
(approved → review, final_gate_passed → closing) is unaffected. **Consequence if
violated:** revert to `resolved=false` and a PASS verdict re-enters the feedback
scans, resurfacing the approve-treated-as-feedback class of bug the rung-8
`isCatFeedback` (verdict==='fail') guard was added to kill.

---

## 2026-07-04 — `approve` flips each passed deliverable `active → done`

**Decision.** On a passing gate, `questPurrview.approve` now writes
`deliverables.status = 'done'` for every active deliverable it just verified,
right before advancing the stage to `review`. **Rejected alternative:** leaving
the pass verdict to live ONLY on the `quest_comments` approve row and never
touching `deliverables.status` (the prior behavior). **Why:** the rest of purrview
was already written *as if* passed deliverables become `done` — both
`preflightStageTransition` and `autoVisualVerify` filter to `status==='active'`
with the comment "a non-active row (e.g. status 'done') is out of scope — it needs
no verdict and no verification link." But nothing in the pipeline ever set `done`,
so that filter was dead: a passed asset stayed `active` forever, got re-verified
from scratch on any re-entry to purrview, and showed perpetually active on the
board (observed on quest `c73b68a9` — infographic judged `match`, approved, still
`active`). Objectives get lifecycle transitions (`questmaster` sets
`running`/`done`); deliverables had none. **Consequence if violated:** the
active-only filter stays a no-op — passed deliverables re-enter every future
purrview verdict count, and the UI never shows a deliverable as finished.

---

## 2026-06-13 — the judge claim must carry the quest's acceptance criteria, not just the deliverable name

**Decision.** Both judge paths (`runReviewLoop` for images, `approve` Gate 3 for
every deliverable) build the vision-judge claim via `buildJudgeClaim()`, which
folds the quest **title + description** into the claim ("must satisfy these
requirements; judge mismatch on wrong style/language/missing-or-forbidden
elements"). `confirmSubmission` returns `title`/`description` so the claim source
is available.

**Rejected alternative.** Claim = `deliverable.name` (the post-migration default)
or a generic "is this a real, non-blank render".

**Why.** A contextless judge told only the name verifies that *an artifact
exists*, not that it *satisfies this brief*. A correctly-rendered but WRONG
deliverable (wrong art style, wrong language, violence present, missing the
required story mutation) sails through. The acceptance criteria must reach the
judge or the gate is theater.

**Consequence if violated.** Purrview "passes" wrong work — the exact leak the
operator flagged ("purrview has been rather leaky"). Reverting to a name-only
claim silently reopens it.

---

## 2026-06-13 — document deliverables are rendered in FULL (all pages), not page 1

**Decision.** `renderDeliverableScreenshot` loops every PDF page (capped 15)
stacked into one tall screenshot.

**Rejected alternative.** `pdf.getPage(1)` — render only page 1.

**Why.** The deliverable here is a multi-chapter book (`kind=document`). Verifying
it by page 1 means chapters 2..N are never seen by the gate — a blind spot that
passes a book with a fine cover and broken interior.

**Consequence if violated.** Multi-page documents are "verified" by their cover.

---

## 2026-06-13 — auto visual-verify fails CLOSED on render error

**Decision.** `renderDeliverableScreenshot` throws when navigation errors AND the
page rendered empty, instead of screenshotting and uploading a blank/partial page.

**Rejected alternative.** Swallow nav failures (`.catch(()=>{})`) and screenshot
whatever is there.

**Why.** A blank/error screenshot that gets uploaded can satisfy a weak gate; a
thrown error leaves `verify_screenshot_ref` unset, so `approve` cannot pass. Fail
closed, not open, on a verification surface.

**Consequence if violated.** A never-loaded deliverable self-certifies via an
empty screenshot.

---

## 2026-06-15 — buildJudgeClaim must distinguish per-deliverable roles in multi-deliverable quests

**Decision.** `buildJudgeClaim` now tells the vision judge that this image is ONE
specific deliverable (by name), and that a quest may produce multiple deliverables
with different roles. The judge evaluates content against the deliverable's stated
role within the quest description, not against the entire quest scope.

**Rejected alternative.** Feed the full quest description without per-deliverable
framing (the pre-fix default).

**Why.** Multi-deliverable quests produce artifacts with distinct purposes (e.g. a
proposal document + a customer follow-up email). The vision judge, given only the
full quest description, rejects supplementary deliverables because they "don't
match the quest requirements" — it compares an email against the full proposal
spec. This caused 100% false-negative on the email deliverable for quest
1613dd7d (Antibody Continuity Program) despite the email being correct and
complete for its role.

**Consequence if violated.** Supplementary deliverables in multi-deliverable quests
will always fail the vision gate, forcing manual workarounds or single-deliverable
quest designs.

---

## 2026-06-15 — approve/bounce write ONE structured verdict comment, not one row per asset

**Decision.** `approve` and `bounce` no longer call a `writeVerdictComments` helper
that inserted one `action='asset_verdict'` `quest_comments` row per deliverable.
The full per-asset verdict set rides in the SINGLE lockphrase comment's
`detail.perItemVerdicts` (machine-readable — what `countPriorBounces` reads) plus a
compact roll-up in its `summary`, and the row now carries the top-level `verdict`
column (`'pass'` for approve, `'fail'` for bounce). `writeVerdictComments` was
deleted. `countPriorBounces` keeps `'asset_verdict'` in its action filter so legacy
rows still read.

**Rejected alternative.** Keep emitting a separate per-asset verdict row alongside
the lockphrase comment (the pre-fix shape, and what an agent re-derives by default —
"one audit row per asset").

**Why.** The lockphrase comment ALREADY carried the full `perItemVerdicts` array, so
the per-asset rows were pure duplication — N extra rows per pass on top of the
lockphrase, the weapon-side half of the verify comment-bloat (#2 source; see the
questmaster `recordVerifyPass` ED). Collapsing also removes a latent double-count:
each prior bounce previously contributed twice to `countPriorBounces` (once via its
`asset_verdict` row, once via the bounce row's `perItemVerdicts`), so a prior bounce
now counts exactly ONCE and the `>= 2` chronic threshold finally means "3rd bounce"
as its comment claims. The lockphrase string MUST remain in `summary` — the DB
trigger `enforce_stage_gate` greps it before allowing the forward stage write.

**Consequence if violated.** Reintroduce `writeVerdictComments` and the per-pass row
count jumps back to N+1, re-flooding the thread; the chronic-bounce counter silently
double-counts again. Drop the lockphrase from `summary` and the stage transition is
blocked at the DB layer.

---

## 2026-07-03 — pre-submit render-sanity is ADVISE-MODE, not a gate (SIO #1)

**Decision.** `adviseRenderSanity` runs a set of CHEAP HTTP-fetch heuristics over
each deliverable ref (localhost/loopback ref, unreachable/HTTP-error, HTML served
with the wrong content-type or as an attachment, escaped-source body, blank body,
restrictive CSP) and ANNOTATES the thread with fixable-error notes — but it NEVER
changes a verdict. It is called from `confirmSubmission` in a swallowed try/catch,
so a slow fetch or a thrown error inside it can never block the submit gate. It
writes one **upserted** `advise_render_check` comment plus a `render_advise`
telemetry row (`would_have_bounced`) on the caravan log channel for hit-rate.

**Rejected alternative.** Make it a HARD gate that blocks submit when a heuristic
fires (the "obvious" way to stop bad deliverables reaching purrview). Also rejected:
do a full headless RASTER (screenshot + non-blank check) at submit time.

**Why.** The operator's de-risked mandate was advise-FIRST: a heuristic is a
proxy, and a false positive that *blocks* submit is strictly worse than the 2-3x
bounce it replaces — it would strand correct deliverables with no override. Advise
mode gets the fixable notes onto the thread with zero blast radius; the telemetry
counter lets the operator MEASURE the true would-have-caught rate before deciding
whether to promote advise→gate. Raster is deferred because the blank-render case is
already caught downstream by `autoVisualVerify` (fail-closed-on-blank) + the vision
judge — a cheap fetch adds the checks the current pipeline only discovers AFTER an
expensive render→judge→bounce (localhost refs, wrong content-type, escaped source),
which is exactly the friction in quests ac48ab69 / 7ec94b9d / 3f5860e4 / 4065db7e.
Render-shape checks (content-type/escaped/blank/CSP) are gated on `kind==='html'`
because a PNG served as image/png or a PDF as application/pdf is correct, not a
defect. The upsert (see `advise_render_check` in `libs/quest` `UPSERT_ACTIONS`)
keeps the advisory from itself becoming per-pass comment bloat.

**Consequence if violated.** Turn advise into a gate before the telemetry justifies
it and a false-positive heuristic hard-blocks a correct deliverable with no operator
visibility — reintroducing the very stall the SIO set out to remove. Emit the
advisory as an appended (non-upserted) comment and the render-advise annotation
re-floods the thread it was meant to keep clean.

## 2026-07-03 — Purrview Verification is polymorphic by deliverable Type; text kinds verify by reading, not by screenshot

**Decision.** The `verify_screenshot_ref` column is now the **"Purrview Verification"**
value and is polymorphic by the deliverable's `kind`:
- **VISUAL** kinds (html/image/document/video) → a Supabase Storage **screenshot URL**,
  vision-judged by `openai_images.judge` (Gate 3, unchanged).
- **TEXT** kind → a **`PASS …`/`FAIL …` text verdict**. The reviewer READS the content
  and states the outcome; `PASS` passes, anything else bounces. No screenshot, no
  vision-judge. The three writers that validated the field as a Supabase URL
  (`/api/quest/mutate`, `questMutator`, `libs/quest.writeDeliverable`) now also accept
  a `^(PASS|FAIL)\b` verdict. The `approve` Gate 3 branches on the value shape.
Purrview also now scopes to **ACTIVE** deliverables only (`status ?? 'active'`).

**Rejected alternatives.** (a) Force a screenshot for text too — a headless render of
"72" or a paragraph is verification theater and, when the render channel was
auth-gated, produced a *login-screen* screenshot that the judge (correctly) failed,
escalating dozens of finished text quests. (b) Add a separate `verify_text_verdict`
column — needless migration + a second nullable field the UI and every gate must
special-case; the field is already "the proof this deliverable is verified", so keep
it single and polymorphic. (c) Rename the DB column to `purrview_verification` — a
cross-tree rename for a label change; the user-facing concept is relabeled in the UI
while the column name stays for compatibility.

**Why.** A simple text answer is verified by reading it, not photographing it. Coupling
ALL verification to a screenshot made the whole gate hostage to the browser/auth
channel — the "cat disabled during purrview → image shows a login screen" false-fail
class that stranded finished quests in `escalated`.

**Consequence if violated.** Re-requiring a screenshot for text kinds (or re-tightening
any of the three validators back to URL-only) reopens the login-screen false-fail and
re-strands text quests; dropping the active-only scope makes purrview re-verify
archived/superseded rows.

---

### 2026-07-03 · Judge on deliverable KIND, not just the verification VALUE SHAPE (residual login-screen hole)

**Decision.** The purrview verify gate now branches on `deliverable.kind` (via
`isTextKind`), not only on the shape of `verify_screenshot_ref`. For a text-like kind
(text/json/markdown/csv): (a) the approve Gate 3 REFUSES to vision-judge a screenshot
value — it demands a `PASS/FAIL` read verdict; and (b) `preflightStageTransition`
(shared by approve+bounce) REJECTS any per-item verdict on a text deliverable that
carries an `openai_images.judge*` origin (`isImageJudgeOrigin`). The questmaster
review-leaf prompt (buildLeafReviewPrompt 3b/3c) was also corrected: it had falsely
claimed `autoVisualVerify` renders text to "a full-page browser shot" — the code
SKIPS text; the prompt led leaves to screenshot + image-judge text anyway.

**Rejected alternative.** Rely on the value-shape branch alone (the prior fix). That
only helps when a text deliverable's verification is ALREADY a `PASS/FAIL` string.
Nothing stopped a stray render PNG from being SET as a text deliverable's
`verify_screenshot_ref` (or a leaf computing an image-judge verdict directly and
calling bounce) — then `classifyPurrviewVerification` returns `screenshot` and the
image judge false-fails it. Quest fa1accaf ("compute 8×9", deliverable "72", kind
text) was approved 18:46 then re-worked and bounced 19:47 as "shows a login screen,
not 72", then escalated — the exact residual.

**Why.** The KIND is the source of truth for HOW a deliverable is verified; the
value shape is downstream and forgeable. Gating on shape lets a mis-typed value route
text through the pixel judge.

**Consequence if violated.** Reverting to value-shape-only judging (or dropping the
text_deliverable_image_judged guard) reopens the false login-screen bounce for text
deliverables that carry a screenshot value, re-stranding finished text quests in
execute→escalated after a spurious purrview kickback.

---

## 2026-07-08 — `bounce` targets `plan`, not `execute` (plan = digest)

**Decision.** `bounce` writes `stage='plan'` (was `execute`), and `BOUNCE_LOCKPHRASE`
became "this quest has been bounced back to plan". The caravan purrview VERIFY leaf
likewise routes a mismatch through the new `questmaster.moveQuestToPlan` (not
`moveQuestToExecute`).

**Rejected alternative.** Keep `bounce → execute` (the native/historical target). A
bounce "feels like" sending the worker back to redo production. Rejected per operator
directive 2026-07-08 (plan = digest): the fail feedback is a digestible input that must
be reconciled into the objectives/deliverables at the plan altitude BEFORE re-production.

**Why.** The lifecycle ladder now maps a quest carrying unresolved cat-fail feedback to
`plan` (see `libs/caravan/engineering_decisions.md` 2026-07-08). Writing `execute`
directly only created a one-tick disagreement that the derail rescuer immediately
corrected back to `plan` — an extra hop and a misleading "back to execute" audit trail.
Writing `plan` directly matches the ladder. The transition is DB-safe: the
`enforce_stage_gate` trigger gates only FORWARD moves (→purrview/review/closing); →plan
is ungated.

**Consequence if violated.** Re-target `execute` and every bounce incurs a redundant
derail-kickback hop (execute→plan) and the "bounced back to execute" wording contradicts
where the quest actually lands, confusing both the worker and the audit log.
```
