```js
/**
 * recall weapon — ranked, source-tagged snippet retrieval across GuildOS corpora.
 *
 * Generalises gearUp's token-overlap scoring into a retrieval primitive that
 * searches docs/, skill-book TOCs + howTos, and agent memory. Returns the
 * smallest relevant snippets within an optional token budget.
 *
 * Corpora (v1 — all searched by default):
 *   docs     — every .md file under docs/
 *   registry — skill-book + weapon TOC entries (from tocScan)
 *   memory   — agent memory .md files under the Claude memory dir
 *
 * Retrieval method: BM25-style token overlap with IDF weighting.
 * Each document is chunked by markdown ## headers into sections.
 */

import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
import { join, resolve, basename, relative } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { scanSkillBookTocsFromDisk, scanWeaponTocsFromDisk, SKILL_BOOKS_DIR } from "../skillBooks/tocScan.js";
import { logWeaponCall } from "../weaponLog/index.js";

const __dirname = fileURLToPath(new URL(".", import.meta.url));
const PROJECT_ROOT = resolve(__dirname, "..", "..", "..");
const DOCS_DIR = join(PROJECT_ROOT, "docs");
const MEMORY_DIR = join(
  process.env.USERPROFILE || process.env.HOME || "",
  ".claude", "projects", "C--Users-xsj70-GuildOS", "memory"
);

// ── tokenizer (shared with gearUp) ─────────────────────────────────────────

function tokenize(text) {
  return text
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}\s]/gu, " ")
    .split(/\s+/)
    .filter(t => t.length >= 3);
}

// ── section chunker ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Split markdown text into sections by ## (or #) headers.
 * Each section has { heading, text, startLine }.
 */
function chunkMarkdown(text) {
  const lines = text.split("\n");
  const sections = [];
  let current = { heading: "(top)", text: "", startLine: 0 };

  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
    const line = lines[i];
    if (/^#{1,3}\s+/.test(line)) {
      // flush previous
      if (current.text.trim()) sections.push(current);
      current = { heading: line.replace(/^#{1,3}\s+/, "").trim(), text: "", startLine: i };
    } else {
      current.text += line + "\n";
    }
  }
  if (current.text.trim()) sections.push(current);
  return sections;
}

// ── corpus loaders ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function loadDocsCorpus() {
  const snippets = [];
  let entries;
  try { entries = readdirSync(DOCS_DIR); } catch { return snippets; }
  for (const name of entries) {
    if (!name.endsWith(".md")) continue;
    const p = join(DOCS_DIR, name);
    try { if (!statSync(p).isFile()) continue; } catch { continue; }
    let src;
    try { src = readFileSync(p, "utf8"); } catch { continue; }
    const sections = chunkMarkdown(src);
    for (const sec of sections) {
      snippets.push({
        sourceId: "docs",
        docPath: `docs/${name}`,
        section: sec.heading,
        text: sec.text.trim(),
        tokenEstimate: Math.ceil(sec.text.trim().length / 4),
      });
    }
  }
  return snippets;
}

function loadRegistryCorpus() {
  const snippets = [];
  // Skill book TOC entries
  for (const row of scanSkillBookTocsFromDisk()) {
    snippets.push({
      sourceId: "registry",
      docPath: `libs/skill_book/${row.skillBook}/index.js`,
      section: `${row.skillBook}.${row.action}`,
      text: row.description,
      tokenEstimate: Math.ceil((row.description || "").length / 4),
    });
  }
  // Weapon TOC entries
  for (const row of scanWeaponTocsFromDisk()) {
    snippets.push({
      sourceId: "registry",
      docPath: `libs/weapon/${row.weapon}/index.js`,
      section: `${row.weapon}.${row.action}`,
      text: row.description,
      tokenEstimate: Math.ceil((row.description || "").length / 4),
    });
  }
  // Skill book howTo bodies — read the full file and extract function bodies
  // that contain howTo strings. Too heavy for v1; TOC descriptions suffice
  // since they're what gearUp already scores against.
  return snippets;
}

function loadMemoryCorpus() {
  const snippets = [];
  let entries;
  try { entries = readdirSync(MEMORY_DIR); } catch { return snippets; }
  for (const name of entries) {
    if (!name.endsWith(".md") || name === "MEMORY.md") continue;
    const p = join(MEMORY_DIR, name);
    try { if (!statSync(p).isFile()) continue; } catch { continue; }
    let src;
    try { src = readFileSync(p, "utf8"); } catch { continue; }

    // Strip frontmatter
    let body = src;
    if (body.startsWith("---")) {
      const end = body.indexOf("---", 3);
      if (end > 0) body = body.slice(end + 3).trim();
    }
    if (!body) continue;

    snippets.push({
      sourceId: "memory",
      docPath: `memory/${name}`,
      section: name.replace(/\.md$/, ""),
      text: body,
      tokenEstimate: Math.ceil(body.length / 4),
    });
  }
  return snippets;
}

// ── IDF-weighted BM25-style scorer ──────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Build IDF map from a corpus of snippets.
 * IDF(term) = log(N / (1 + df(term))) where df = docs containing term.
 */
function buildIdf(snippets) {
  const N = snippets.length || 1;
  const df = {};
  for (const s of snippets) {
    const seen = new Set(tokenize(s.text + " " + s.section));
    for (const t of seen) {
      df[t] = (df[t] || 0) + 1;
    }
  }
  const idf = {};
  for (const [term, count] of Object.entries(df)) {
    idf[term] = Math.log(N / (1 + count));
  }
  return idf;
}

/**
 * Score a snippet against query tokens using IDF-weighted token overlap.
 */
function scoreSnippet(queryTokens, snippet, idf) {
  const haystack = (snippet.text + " " + snippet.section).toLowerCase();
  let score = 0;
  for (const tok of queryTokens) {
    if (haystack.includes(tok)) {
      score += (idf[tok] || 1);
    }
  }
  return score;
}

// ── main recall function ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const CORPUS_LOADERS = {
  docs: loadDocsCorpus,
  registry: loadRegistryCorpus,
  memory: loadMemoryCorpus,
};

const DEFAULT_TOP_K = 10;
const DEFAULT_TOKEN_BUDGET = 4000;

/**
 * Retrieve the most relevant snippets for a query across GuildOS corpora.
 *
 * @param {{ query: string, corpora?: string[], topK?: number, tokenBudget?: number, agent?: string }} opts
 * @returns {{ snippets: Array<{sourceId, docPath, section, score, text, tokenEstimate}>, totalCandidates: number, tokenUsed: number }}
 */
export function recall({ query, corpora, topK = DEFAULT_TOP_K, tokenBudget = DEFAULT_TOKEN_BUDGET, agent = "leaf" }) {
  if (!query || typeof query !== "string") {
    const result = { snippets: [], error: "query required", totalCandidates: 0, tokenUsed: 0 };
    logWeaponCall({ weapon: "recall", fn: "recall", agent, input: { queryLength: 0 }, output: result, status: "error" });
    return result;
  }

  // Load corpora
  const corporaToSearch = corpora && Array.isArray(corpora) && corpora.length > 0
    ? corpora.filter(c => CORPUS_LOADERS[c])
    : Object.keys(CORPUS_LOADERS);

  let allSnippets = [];
  for (const c of corporaToSearch) {
    allSnippets = allSnippets.concat(CORPUS_LOADERS[c]());
  }

  // Filter empty snippets
  allSnippets = allSnippets.filter(s => s.text && s.text.length > 0);

  const queryTokens = tokenize(query);
  const idf = buildIdf(allSnippets);

  // Score all snippets
  const scored = allSnippets.map(s => ({
    ...s,
    score: scoreSnippet(queryTokens, s, idf),
  }));

  // Sort by score desc, drop zeros
  scored.sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score);
  const nonZero = scored.filter(s => s.score > 0);

  // Apply topK and token budget
  const result = [];
  let tokenUsed = 0;
  for (const s of nonZero) {
    if (result.length >= topK) break;
    if (tokenBudget > 0 && tokenUsed + s.tokenEstimate > tokenBudget && result.length > 0) break;
    result.push(s);
    tokenUsed += s.tokenEstimate;
  }

  const output = { snippets: result, totalCandidates: allSnippets.length, tokenUsed };
  logWeaponCall({
    weapon: "recall",
    fn: "recall",
    agent,
    input: { queryLength: query.length, corpora: corporaToSearch, topK, tokenBudget },
    output: { matchCount: result.length, totalCandidates: allSnippets.length, tokenUsed },
    status: "ok",
  });
  return output;
}

/**
 * List available corpora and their sizes (snippet counts).
 * Useful for understanding what's searchable.
 *
 * @param {{ agent?: string }} opts
 * @returns {{ corpora: Array<{id: string, snippetCount: number, totalTokens: number}> }}
 */
export function listCorpora({ agent = "leaf" } = {}) {
  const corpora = [];
  for (const [id, loader] of Object.entries(CORPUS_LOADERS)) {
    const snippets = loader();
    const totalTokens = snippets.reduce((sum, s) => sum + s.tokenEstimate, 0);
    corpora.push({ id, snippetCount: snippets.length, totalTokens });
  }
  logWeaponCall({
    weapon: "recall",
    fn: "listCorpora",
    agent,
    input: {},
    output: { corporaCount: corpora.length },
    status: "ok",
  });
  return { corpora };
}

export const toc = {
  recall: "Retrieve the most relevant ranked, source-tagged snippets for a query across GuildOS corpora (docs/, skill-book+weapon registry, agent memory). BM25-style IDF-weighted token overlap. Input: {query, corpora?:['docs','registry','memory'], topK?:10, tokenBudget?:4000}. Output: {snippets:[{sourceId, docPath, section, score, text, tokenEstimate}], totalCandidates, tokenUsed}.",
  listCorpora: "List available retrieval corpora and their sizes. Input: {}. Output: {corpora:[{id, snippetCount, totalTokens}]}.",
};

```markdown
# reportGuildStatus — engineering decisions

_2026-07-09 · Official guild-status contract vs. GuildOS2's status inference._
**Decision:** ship an OFFICIAL `GET /api/guild-status` endpoint that a guild serves to
report its own status, and make the GuildOS2 card prefer it. **Rejected alternative:**
keep improving the card's inference (loopback `/api/status` ping + `guild_activity` DB
rows). **Why:** inference is a first-party hack — it only works because GuildOS2 knows the
prebuilt guild's internals (the `/api/status` shape, the `guild-*.log` mtime convention).
A third-party guild GuildOS2 didn't build can't be inferred; it must be *asked*. An
explicit self-report contract is the only thing that generalizes to arbitrary guilds.
**Consequence if violated:** revert to inference and every third-party guild shows "not
detected" forever regardless of how healthy it actually is.

_2026-07-09 · Card prefers guild-status, FALLS BACK to /api/status — never the reverse._
**Decision:** the card tries `/api/guild-status` first and only drops to the legacy
`/api/status` ping when the new endpoint is absent/invalid. **Rejected alternative:**
replace the `/api/status` ping outright. **Why:** thousands of already-downloaded guilds
serve only `/api/status`; a hard cutover would blank their cards on GuildOS2's next
deploy. Prefer-new-fallback-old makes adoption a pure guild-side opt-in with zero
coordinated release. **Consequence if violated:** dropping the fallback strands every
guild that hasn't installed the template yet.

_2026-07-09 · The template route is PORTABLE (no @/libs imports) — self-contained on purpose._
**Decision:** `template/route.js` inlines its cron/worker getters (env + a
`public/proving-grounds/guild-*.log` scan) rather than importing the prebuilt guild's
`libs/guild/settings.js` / `workers.js`. **Rejected alternative:** import the existing
helpers (DRY). **Why:** the file is SHIPPED to strangers via the skill exchange and
copied into arbitrary repos — an `@/libs/guild/...` import would break the instant it
lands anywhere but the reference guild. Self-contained = drops into any Next guild
unchanged, and because it reuses the exact `guild-*.log` 3-min-window convention it still
reports the SAME numbers `/api/status` does in the prebuilt guild. **Consequence if
violated:** re-adding the import makes the template un-installable outside this one repo —
defeating the entire "third-party reportable" goal.

_2026-07-09 · `online: true` is tautological, and that's correct._
**Decision:** the endpoint always returns `online: true`. **Rejected alternative:** try to
compute liveness inside the handler. **Why:** if the handler executed, the process is up —
"online" is proven by the 200 itself. The card decides reachability from whether the fetch
succeeded; the field is just an explicit echo. Real cross-machine liveness (when the
loopback ping can't reach a remote guild) stays with `guild_activity` DB rows, unchanged.
**Consequence if violated:** adding fake liveness logic inside the handler invents a
signal that can only ever say "true," adding confusion without information.

_2026-07-09 · Protocol tag + `extra` bag = forward-compatible schema._
**Decision:** responses carry `protocol: "guildos2.guild-status/1"` and an `extra` object;
the card matches on the `guildos2.guild-status/` prefix and ignores unknown fields.
**Rejected alternative:** a fixed field list the card validates strictly. **Why:** the user
asked for "possibly others in the future" — new fields (queue depth, last-tick time, agent
kind) must not require a lockstep card+guild release. Prefix-match + ignore-unknown lets
either side move first. **Consequence if violated:** strict validation turns every future
field into a breaking change across two independently-deployed apps.
```

```js
/**
 * @file reportGuildStatus — the OFFICIAL guild self-reporting skill.
 *
 * WHAT IT SOLVES. The GuildOS2 "My Guilds" report card historically INFERRED a guild's
 * status from indirect signals (a loopback ping to /api/status, guild_activity DB rows).
 * Inference can't cover a third-party guild whose internals GuildOS2 doesn't know. This
 * skill ships an OFFICIAL contract — `GET /api/guild-status` — that any guild serves to
 * report its OWN status (online, cron active, active worker count, extensible). Once a
 * guild serves it, the card reads status directly and stops guessing.
 *
 * TWO HALVES:
 *   1. THE TEMPLATE (the shipped artifact) — `template/route.js` is the drop-in API
 *      endpoint an external guild installs (see template/README.md). This is what makes
 *      the guild reportable; the skill exists to distribute it.
 *   2. THE CLIENT (this weapon's `check` action) — GET a guild's /api/guild-status and
 *      return the parsed contract. Useful for verifying an install or polling a guild.
 *
 * SCOPE. This is a GUILD-FACING installable skill, the sibling of GuildOS2QuestUpdate
 * (write-back), leaseQuest, and caravan-get in the external-guild "skills to install"
 * set. It is NOT this repo's native quest machinery.
 *
 * CONTRACT (protocol "guildos2.guild-status/1"):
 *   GET {base}/api/guild-status  →  200
 *   { ok, protocol, guild, online, ts, cron:{active,intervalMinutes},
 *     workers:{active,max,armed,total}, path?, port?, extra? }
 * The card treats any 200 whose `protocol` starts "guildos2.guild-status/" as
 * authoritative. Unknown fields are ignored, so the schema grows without breaking cards.
 */

export const description =
  "The official guild self-reporting skill: ships the GET /api/guild-status API template " +
  "a guild installs so the GuildOS2 report card reads its status directly (online, cron " +
  "active, active workers) instead of inferring it. Also a client (check) to GET a guild's " +
  "status. Guild-facing installable skill, sibling of GuildOS2QuestUpdate.";

export const toc = {
  check: {
    description:
      "GET a guild's /api/guild-status and return the parsed guildos2.guild-status contract " +
      "(online, cron, workers). Use to verify an install or poll a guild's live status.",
    input: {
      base: "guild base URL, e.g. http://localhost:48452 (required unless port given)",
      port: "shorthand for http://localhost:<port> when base is omitted",
    },
    output: {
      ok: "boolean — endpoint answered with a valid guildos2.guild-status body",
      status: "the parsed contract (guild, online, cron, workers, ...)",
      httpStatus: "HTTP status code",
    },
  },
};

const PROTOCOL_PREFIX = "guildos2.guild-status/";

/**
 * check — GET {base}/api/guild-status and validate it's the official contract. Thin,
 * honest passthrough (the GuildOS2QuestUpdate lesson): return the guild's body verbatim,
 * only assert the protocol tag so a stray 200 from an unrelated route isn't mistaken for
 * a real guild status.
 */
export async function check({ base, port } = {}) {
  const root = (base || (port ? `http://localhost:${port}` : "")).replace(/\/+$/, "");
  if (!root) return { ok: false, error: "provide base (or port) of the guild to check" };
  const url = `${root}/api/guild-status`;

  let res, json;
  try {
    res = await fetch(url, { cache: "no-store", headers: { accept: "application/json" } });
    json = await res.json().catch(() => ({}));
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, error: `GET ${url} failed: ${e.message}`, hint: "is the guild running on this base/port?" };
  }
  if (!res.ok) {
    return { ok: false, httpStatus: res.status, error: `guild-status returned HTTP ${res.status}`, detail: json };
  }
  if (typeof json?.protocol !== "string" || !json.protocol.startsWith(PROTOCOL_PREFIX)) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      httpStatus: res.status,
      error: "response is not a guildos2.guild-status contract (missing/wrong protocol tag)",
      hint: "the guild may serve an unrelated /api/guild-status, or hasn't installed the template",
      detail: json,
    };
  }
  return { ok: true, httpStatus: res.status, status: json };
}

```markdown
# report guild status — API template

**Rule: copy `route.js` into your guild, don't author a status endpoint from scratch.**

This ships the OFFICIAL `GET /api/guild-status` contract so the GuildOS2 "My Guilds"
report card can read your guild's status DIRECTLY (online, cron active, active workers)
instead of inferring it from indirect signals. Serving this endpoint is what makes a
third-party guild fully reportable.

## Install (Next.js App Router guild)

1. **Copy the route:**
   `cp libs/weapon/reportGuildStatus/template/route.js app/api/guild-status/route.js`
2. **Start (or restart) your guild.** It's now live at
   `http://localhost:<PORT>/api/guild-status`.
3. **Verify:** open that URL in a browser (you get a readable status card) or
   `curl -s http://localhost:<PORT>/api/guild-status` (you get the JSON contract).

That's the whole install for the prebuilt-guild shape — `route.js` is portable and
self-contained (no `@/libs` imports; it reads env + the `public/proving-grounds/guild-*.log`
worker logs the tick already writes), so it reports the same numbers the card expects with
zero extra wiring.

## Non-Node / custom harness

Serve the SAME JSON at `GET /api/guild-status`. Minimum required body:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "protocol": "guildos2.guild-status/1",
  "guild": "my-guild",
  "online": true,
  "ts": "2026-07-09T12:00:00.000Z",
  "cron": { "active": true, "intervalMinutes": 5 },
  "workers": { "active": 0, "max": 4, "armed": true, "total": 0 }
}
```

The card keys off `protocol` starting `"guildos2.guild-status/"` and reads the fields it
knows; add more under the top level or an `extra` object freely — unknown fields are
ignored, so the schema grows without breaking older cards.

## Adapt the signals

If your harness tracks cron/workers differently than the prebuilt guild, edit the three
getters in the `ADAPT` block of `route.js` (`cronState`, `maxWorkers`, `workerCounts`) —
keep the response shape identical.

## How the card uses it

GuildOS2's card pings `GET /api/guild-status` FIRST. If it answers with the protocol
body, that IS the status (no inference). If the endpoint is absent (older guild), the
card falls back to its legacy `/api/status` ping — so installing this is safe and
backward-compatible.
```

```js
// app/api/guild-status/route.js
//
// OFFICIAL GuildOS2 guild-status contract. GET /api/guild-status returns a guild's
// own self-reported health so the GuildOS2 "My Guilds" report card can read status
// DIRECTLY instead of inferring it from indirect signals. Every guild — first-party
// or third-party — that serves this endpoint is fully reportable.
//
// Contract (protocol "guildos2.guild-status/1"), JSON body:
//   {
//     ok:        true,
//     protocol:  "guildos2.guild-status/1",
//     guild:     "<this guild's name>",
//     online:    true,               // the endpoint answered → the guild is up
//     ts:        "<ISO now>",
//     cron:      { active: bool, intervalMinutes: number },
//     workers:   { active: number, max: number, armed: bool, total: number },
//     path:      "<repo dir>",       // optional, nice-to-have
//     port:      <number|null>,      // optional
//     extra:     { ... }             // reserved for future fields; card ignores unknowns
//   }
//
// The card treats ANY 200 with `protocol` starting "guildos2.guild-status/" as the
// authoritative source and stops inferring. Add fields under the top level or `extra`
// freely — the card reads what it knows and ignores the rest, so this schema grows
// without breaking older cards.
//
// This file is PORTABLE: it has no @/libs import, reads its signals from env + the
// worker-log directory, and drops into any Next.js (App Router) guild unchanged. If
// your harness tracks cron/workers differently, replace the three getters in the
// "ADAPT" block below with your own source of truth — the response shape must stay.

import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
import { readdirSync, statSync } from "fs";
import { basename, join } from "path";

export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";

const PROTOCOL = "guildos2.guild-status/1";

// A worker counts as active while its transcript was written within this window. The
// prebuilt guild tees each leaf's transcript to public/proving-grounds/guild-*.log and
// touches it as the leaf runs, so a fresh mtime == a live worker. Same 3-min window the
// tick's concurrency cap uses, so the card and the cap agree.
const ACTIVE_WINDOW_MS = 3 * 60 * 1000;

// ─── ADAPT: wire these to your harness's real signals ──────────────────────────
// The three primitives the card needs. The defaults match the prebuilt guild; if your
// harness knows cron/worker state a different way, swap these bodies (keep the shapes).

/** Cron intent: is the guild configured to tick, and how often. */
function cronState() {
  return {
    active: process.env.CRON_ACTIVE === "1",
    intervalMinutes: Number(process.env.CRON_INTERVAL_MINUTES) || 5,
  };
}

/** Max concurrent worker leaves. Blank → 2; 0 = dry-run (no real leaves). */
function maxWorkers() {
  const raw = (process.env.GUILD_MAX_WORKERS ?? "").trim();
  if (raw === "") return 2;
  const n = Number(raw);
  return Number.isFinite(n) && n >= 0 ? Math.floor(n) : 2;
}

/** Active + total workers, derived from the leaf-transcript logs. */
function workerCounts() {
  const dir = join(process.cwd(), "public", "proving-grounds");
  let names = [];
  try { names = readdirSync(dir); } catch { return { active: 0, total: 0 }; }
  const now = Date.now();
  let active = 0, total = 0;
  for (const name of names) {
    if (!/^guild-.*\.log$/i.test(name)) continue;
    total++;
    try { if (now - statSync(join(dir, name)).mtimeMs < ACTIVE_WINDOW_MS) active++; } catch { /* skip */ }
  }
  return { active, total };
}
// ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function buildStatus() {
  const cron = cronState();
  const cap = maxWorkers();
  const { active, total } = workerCounts();
  return {
    ok: true,
    protocol: PROTOCOL,
    guild: (process.env.GUILD_NAME || basename(process.cwd()) || "guild").trim(),
    online: true, // if this handler ran, the guild is up
    ts: new Date().toISOString(),
    cron,
    workers: { active, max: cap, armed: cap > 0, total },
    path: process.cwd(),
    port: Number(process.env.PORT) || null,
    extra: {}, // reserved — add future fields here without breaking the card
  };
}

// A tiny self-contained HTML card so opening this URL in a browser shows a readable
// report (not raw JSON). Machines send Accept: application/json (or ?format=json) and
// get JSON; a browser sends Accept: text/html and gets the card.
function html(s) {
  const dot = (on) => on ? "#22c55e" : "#6b7280";
  const yn = (on) => on ? "yes" : "no";
  return `<!doctype html><meta charset="utf-8"><title>${s.guild} — guild status</title>
<style>
  body{font:14px/1.5 system-ui,sans-serif;background:#0b0b12;color:#e5e7eb;margin:0;padding:32px}
  .card{max-width:520px;margin:0 auto;background:#14141f;border:1px solid #26263a;border-radius:14px;padding:24px}
  h1{font-size:20px;margin:0 0 4px}.sub{color:#9ca3af;margin:0 0 20px;font-size:12px}
  .row{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;padding:10px 0;border-top:1px solid #26263a}
  .k{color:#9ca3af}.v{font-weight:600}
  .dot{display:inline-block;width:9px;height:9px;border-radius:50%;margin-right:7px;vertical-align:middle}
  code{color:#a5b4fc;font-size:12px}
</style>
<div class="card">
  <h1><span class="dot" style="background:${dot(s.online)}"></span>${s.guild}</h1>
  <p class="sub">protocol ${s.protocol} · ${s.ts}</p>
  <div class="row"><span class="k">Online</span><span class="v">${yn(s.online)}</span></div>
  <div class="row"><span class="k">Cron active</span><span class="v"><span class="dot" style="background:${dot(s.cron.active)}"></span>${yn(s.cron.active)} · every ${s.cron.intervalMinutes} min</span></div>
  <div class="row"><span class="k">Active workers</span><span class="v">${s.workers.active} / ${s.workers.max}${s.workers.armed ? "" : " (dry-run)"}</span></div>
  <div class="row"><span class="k">Worker logs (total)</span><span class="v">${s.workers.total}</span></div>
  <div class="row"><span class="k">Port</span><span class="v">${s.port ?? "—"}</span></div>
  <div class="row"><span class="k">Path</span><span class="v"><code>${s.path}</code></span></div>
</div>`;
}

export function GET(req) {
  const s = buildStatus();
  const url = new URL(req.url);
  const wantsHtml =
    url.searchParams.get("format") === "html" ||
    (url.searchParams.get("format") !== "json" &&
      (req.headers.get("accept") || "").includes("text/html"));
  if (wantsHtml) {
    return new NextResponse(html(s), { headers: { "content-type": "text/html; charset=utf-8" } });
  }
  return NextResponse.json(s);
}
```

```js

export const toc = {
  readDomainOverview: "Read the SEMRush overview for a domain.",
  searchKeywords: "Search SEMRush keyword data for a domain or seed.",
  readBacklinks: "Read SEMRush backlinks for a domain.",
};
import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";

const BASE = "https://api.semrush.com";

async function loadKey(userId) {
  if (userId) {
    try {
      const db = await database.init("service");
      const { data } = await db.from("profiles").select("env_vars").eq("id", userId).single();
      const k = data?.env_vars?.SEMRUSH_API_KEY;
      if (k) return k;
    } catch { /* fall through */ }
  }
  return process.env.SEMRUSH_API_KEY || null;
}

async function request(params, key) {
  const url = new URL(BASE);
  url.searchParams.set("key", key);
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(params)) {
    if (v !== undefined && v !== null) url.searchParams.set(k, String(v));
  }
  const res = await fetch(url.toString());
  if (!res.ok) {
    const text = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`SEMRush API failed (${res.status}): ${text}`);
  }
  return res.text();
}

export async function readDomainOverview({ domain, database: db = "us" } = {}, userId) {
  if (!domain) throw new Error('"domain" is required');
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) throw new Error("SEMRUSH_API_KEY not set");
  const raw = await request({ type: "domain_ranks", domain, database: db, export_columns: "Dn,Rk,Or,Ot,Oc,Ad,At,Ac" }, key);
  return { raw };
}

export async function searchKeywords({ phrase, database: db = "us", limit = 10 } = {}, userId) {
  if (!phrase) throw new Error('"phrase" is required');
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) throw new Error("SEMRUSH_API_KEY not set");
  const raw = await request({
    type: "phrase_related",
    phrase,
    database: db,
    display_limit: limit,
    export_columns: "Ph,Nq,Cp,Co,Nr",
  }, key);
  return { raw };
}

export async function readBacklinks({ target, limit = 10 } = {}, userId) {
  if (!target) throw new Error('"target" is required');
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) throw new Error("SEMRUSH_API_KEY not set");
  const raw = await request({
    type: "backlinks",
    target,
    target_type: "root_domain",
    display_limit: limit,
    export_columns: "page_ascore,source_url,target_url,anchor,external_num,internal_num,first_seen,last_seen",
  }, key);
  return { raw };
}

export async function checkCredentials(input = {}, userId) {
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) return { ok: false, msg: "SEMRUSH_API_KEY not set in profiles.env_vars or process.env" };
  try {
    await request({ type: "domain_ranks", domain: "semrush.com", database: "us", export_columns: "Dn" }, key);
    return { ok: true, msg: "SEMRush credentials valid" };
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, msg: e.message };
  }
}

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * siteAnalytics CLI — bare-node dispatcher for the GA4 + GSC provisioning weapon.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node libs/weapon/siteAnalytics/cli.mjs check
 *   node libs/weapon/siteAnalytics/cli.mjs consent [--port 4100]
 *   node libs/weapon/siteAnalytics/cli.mjs enable-apis
 *   node libs/weapon/siteAnalytics/cli.mjs ga4-accounts
 *   node libs/weapon/siteAnalytics/cli.mjs ga4-properties --account <id>
 *   node libs/weapon/siteAnalytics/cli.mjs ga4-create-property --account <id> --name "protectandgrow.blog"
 *   node libs/weapon/siteAnalytics/cli.mjs ga4-create-stream --property <id|properties/id> --name "Web" --uri https://protectandgrow.blog
 *   node libs/weapon/siteAnalytics/cli.mjs gsc-sites
 *   node libs/weapon/siteAnalytics/cli.mjs gsc-token --site https://protectandgrow.blog/ [--method META]
 *   node libs/weapon/siteAnalytics/cli.mjs gsc-add --site https://protectandgrow.blog/
 *   node libs/weapon/siteAnalytics/cli.mjs gsc-verify --site https://protectandgrow.blog/ [--method META]
 *   node libs/weapon/siteAnalytics/cli.mjs gsc-sitemap --site https://protectandgrow.blog/ --sitemap https://protectandgrow.blog/sitemap.xml
 */

import * as w from "./index.js";

function parseFlags(argv) {
  const f = {};
  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
    if (argv[i].startsWith("--")) {
      const k = argv[i].slice(2);
      const v = argv[i + 1] && !argv[i + 1].startsWith("--") ? argv[++i] : true;
      f[k] = v;
    }
  }
  return f;
}

const out = (x) => console.log(JSON.stringify(x, null, 2));

async function main() {
  const [cmd, ...rest] = process.argv.slice(2);
  const f = parseFlags(rest);
  switch (cmd) {
    case "check":
      out(w.checkCredentials());
      break;
    case "consent":
      out(await w.runConsent({ port: f.port ? Number(f.port) : 4100 }));
      break;
    case "token":
      out({ access_token: (await w.accessToken()).slice(0, 24) + "…(ok)" });
      break;
    case "enable-apis":
      out(await w.enableApis({}));
      break;
    case "ga4-accounts":
      out(await w.ga4ListAccounts());
      break;
    case "ga4-properties":
      out(await w.ga4ListProperties({ accountId: f.account }));
      break;
    case "ga4-create-property":
      out(await w.ga4CreateProperty({ accountId: f.account, displayName: f.name, ...(f.tz ? { timeZone: f.tz } : {}) }));
      break;
    case "ga4-create-stream":
      out(await w.ga4CreateDataStream({ propertyId: f.property, displayName: f.name || "Web stream", defaultUri: f.uri }));
      break;
    case "ga4-report": {
      const dimensions = f.dimensions ? String(f.dimensions).split(",").map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean) : [];
      const metrics = f.metrics
        ? String(f.metrics).split(",").map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)
        : ["sessions", "totalUsers", "screenPageViews"];
      let dimensionFilter;
      if (f.path) dimensionFilter = { fieldName: "pagePath", matchType: f.matchType || "CONTAINS", value: f.path };
      out(await w.ga4RunReport({
        propertyId: f.property,
        startDate: f.start,
        endDate: f.end,
        dimensions,
        metrics,
        dimensionFilter,
        ...(f.limit ? { limit: Number(f.limit) } : {}),
      }));
      break;
    }
    case "gsc-sites":
      out(await w.gscListSites());
      break;
    case "gsc-token":
      out(await w.gscGetVerificationToken({ siteUrl: f.site, method: f.method || "META" }));
      break;
    case "gsc-add":
      out(await w.gscAddSite({ siteUrl: f.site }));
      break;
    case "gsc-verify":
      out(await w.gscVerify({ siteUrl: f.site, method: f.method || "META" }));
      break;
    case "gsc-sitemap":
      out(await w.gscSubmitSitemap({ siteUrl: f.site, sitemapUrl: f.sitemap }));
      break;
    case "gsc-sitemaps":
      out(await w.gscListSitemaps({ siteUrl: f.site }));
      break;
    case "gsc-query": {
      const dimensions = f.dimensions ? String(f.dimensions).split(",").map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean) : [];
      const filters = [];
      if (f.page) filters.push({ dimension: "page", operator: f.op || "contains", expression: f.page });
      if (f.q) filters.push({ dimension: "query", operator: f.op || "contains", expression: f.q });
      if (f.country) filters.push({ dimension: "country", operator: "equals", expression: f.country });
      out(await w.gscSearchAnalytics({
        siteUrl: f.site,
        startDate: f.start,
        endDate: f.end,
        dimensions,
        filters,
        ...(f.rowLimit ? { rowLimit: Number(f.rowLimit) } : {}),
        ...(f.type ? { searchType: f.type } : {}),
        ...(f.dataState ? { dataState: f.dataState } : {}),
      }));
      break;
    }
    default:
      console.error("Unknown command:", cmd);
      console.error("Commands: check, consent, enable-apis, ga4-accounts, ga4-properties, ga4-create-property, ga4-create-stream, ga4-report, gsc-sites, gsc-token, gsc-add, gsc-verify, gsc-sitemap, gsc-sitemaps, gsc-query");
      console.error('  gsc-query --site sc-domain:bosterbio.com --start 2025-12-04 --end 2026-06-02 [--dimensions date|page] [--page /services/] [--q <query>] [--op contains|equals] [--type web] [--dataState final|all] [--rowLimit N]');
      console.error('  ga4-report --property 362731773 --start 2025-12-04 --end 2026-06-02 [--dimensions date|pagePath] [--metrics sessions,totalUsers,screenPageViews] [--path /services/] [--matchType CONTAINS|EXACT|BEGINS_WITH] [--limit N]');
      process.exit(1);
  }
}

main().catch((e) => {
  console.error("ERROR:", e.message);
  if (e.body) console.error(JSON.stringify(e.body, null, 2));
  process.exit(1);
});
```

```markdown
# Engineering decisions — `libs/weapon/siteAnalytics`

Rationale layer (per CLAUDE.md §6). Append; supersede in place when a decision
changes.

---

## 2026-06-06 — reuse the gmail-mcp OAuth client (GCP 962388978165) with extra scopes, not a separate GCP project

**Decision.** Site Analytics reuses the Desktop OAuth client from the gmail-mcp
install (`~/.gmail-mcp/gcp-oauth.keys.json`, GCP project 962388978165) and requests
four added scopes (analytics.edit, webmasters, siteverification, cloud-platform)
beyond Gmail's.

**Rejected alternative.** Create a dedicated GCP project + OAuth client for site
analytics.

**Why.** One GCP project means one consent flow and one credentials file. The
gmail-mcp client already exists wherever Gmail is set up; extending its scopes is
strictly cheaper than standing up a second project, and the added scopes are safe
grants on the same token (no credential sharing risk).

**Consequence if violated.** Every new user must provision a second GCP project +
OAuth credentials + key file — duplicated infra and a confusing setup. (OAuth
gotcha: the redirect must be a bare `http://localhost:<port>`.)
```

<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: libs/weapon/siteAnalytics/index.js -->
```js
/**
 * siteAnalytics weapon — provision GA4 + Google Search Console for a website
 * via the Google REST Admin APIs, with a loopback-OAuth consent flow.
 *
 * WHY THIS EXISTS: the official google-analytics-mcp (and community GA/GSC MCP
 * servers) are READ-ONLY (reporting). None can CREATE a GA4 property, create a
 * data stream, add a Search Console site, verify ownership, or submit a
 * sitemap. That provisioning work is API-only. This weapon is that API surface.
 *
 * AUTH: reuses the existing Desktop OAuth client from the gmail-mcp install
 * (~/.gmail-mcp/gcp-oauth.keys.json — GCP project 962388978165). One consent
 * mints a refresh token carrying the four scopes below; it is stored, gitignored,
 * at ~/.site-analytics/credentials.json and auto-refreshed thereafter.
 *
 * The CIC tier closes exactly two gaps the API cannot: (1) the one-time consent
 * "Allow" click, (2) GA4 top-level ACCOUNT creation (ToS acceptance — the Admin
 * API can only create properties UNDER an existing account).
 *
 * All functions are plain ESM with global fetch + node: builtins so the CLI
 * (cli.mjs) runs under bare `node` with no Next.js app context.
 */

import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync } from "node:fs";
import { homedir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import http from "node:http";
import { createServer } from "node:http";

export const toc = {
  runConsent:
    "One-time loopback-OAuth consent. Starts a localhost server, builds the Google auth URL (scopes: analytics.edit, webmasters, siteverification, cloud-platform), writes it to ~/.site-analytics/auth-url.txt, waits for the redirect, exchanges the code, and saves the refresh token. Drive the printed URL through the logged-in Chrome via CIC to click Allow.",
  accessToken: "Refresh the stored refresh token into a live access token. All API calls use this.",
  checkCredentials: "Report whether the gmail OAuth client + a stored site-analytics refresh token are present.",
  enableApis:
    "Enable the required Google APIs (analyticsadmin, searchconsole, siteverification) on the GCP project via the Service Usage API. Needs the cloud-platform scope.",
  ga4ListAccounts: "List GA4 accounts the consented user can administer (accounts.list).",
  ga4ListProperties: "List GA4 properties under an account (properties.list?filter=parent:accounts/{id}).",
  ga4CreateProperty: "Create a GA4 property under an account (properties.create). Returns the property resource incl. name=properties/{id}.",
  ga4CreateDataStream:
    "Create a WEB data stream on a property (properties.dataStreams.create). Returns the stream incl. webStreamData.measurementId (G-XXXXXXX).",
  ga4RunReport:
    "Pull GA4 on-site traffic — the Data API runReport (sessions, users, pageviews, events, conversions). Params: propertyId, startDate, endDate (YYYY-MM-DD), dimensions[] (e.g. ['date'] for a time series, ['pagePath']), metrics[] (default sessions/totalUsers/screenPageViews), dimensionFilter ({fieldName,matchType,value} convenience, e.g. pagePath CONTAINS /services/, or a raw FilterExpression), limit, offset, orderBys. The read counterpart to GSC's gscSearchAnalytics for the on-site/behavioral side.",
  gscAddSite: "Add a URL-prefix site to Search Console (webmasters sites.add — PUT /sites/{siteUrl}).",
  gscListSites: "List Search Console sites the user owns (webmasters sites.list).",
  gscGetVerificationToken:
    "Get a Site Verification token for a method (siteVerification token.getToken). For META, returns the meta tag content to embed in <head>.",
  gscVerify: "Verify ownership after the token is live on the site (siteVerification webResource.insert).",
  gscSubmitSitemap: "Submit a sitemap for a verified site (webmasters sitemaps.submit — PUT /sites/{site}/sitemaps/{sitemapUrl}).",
  gscSearchAnalytics:
    "Query the Search Analytics (Performance) report — the ACTUAL traffic data (clicks, impressions, CTR, position). Params: siteUrl, startDate, endDate (YYYY-MM-DD), dimensions[] (e.g. ['date'] for a time series, ['page'] for per-URL), filters[] ({dimension,operator,expression} — e.g. page contains /services/), rowLimit, searchType, dataState. Paginates and returns rows + summed totals. For the TRUE de-duplicated aggregate (matches the GSC web-UI cards) query with dimensions=[].",
};

// ---- constants -------------------------------------------------------------

const GMAIL_KEYS = join(homedir(), ".gmail-mcp", "gcp-oauth.keys.json");
const STORE_DIR = join(homedir(), ".site-analytics");
const TOKEN_FILE = join(STORE_DIR, "credentials.json");
const AUTH_URL_FILE = join(STORE_DIR, "auth-url.txt");

const PROJECT_NUMBER = "962388978165"; // from ~/.gmail-mcp client_id prefix
const TOKEN_URL = "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token";
const AUTH_BASE = "https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth";

export const SCOPES = [
  "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/analytics.edit",
  "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/analytics.readonly", // GA4 Data API (runReport) — Admin's analytics.edit is NOT sufficient for reporting
  "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/webmasters",
  "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/siteverification",
  "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform",
];

const GA4_ADMIN = "https://analyticsadmin.googleapis.com/v1beta";
const GA4_DATA = "https://analyticsdata.googleapis.com/v1beta";
const GSC_API = "https://www.googleapis.com/webmasters/v3";
const SITEVERIFY_API = "https://www.googleapis.com/siteVerification/v1";
const SERVICEUSAGE = "https://serviceusage.googleapis.com/v1";

// ---- credential plumbing ---------------------------------------------------

function loadClient() {
  if (!existsSync(GMAIL_KEYS)) {
    throw new Error(`OAuth client not found at ${GMAIL_KEYS}. The gmail-mcp install provides it.`);
  }
  const raw = JSON.parse(readFileSync(GMAIL_KEYS, "utf8"));
  const c = raw.installed || raw.web;
  if (!c?.client_id || !c?.client_secret) throw new Error("gcp-oauth.keys.json missing client_id/client_secret.");
  return { clientId: c.client_id, clientSecret: c.client_secret };
}

function ensureStore() {
  if (!existsSync(STORE_DIR)) mkdirSync(STORE_DIR, { recursive: true });
}

export function loadToken() {
  if (!existsSync(TOKEN_FILE)) return null;
  return JSON.parse(readFileSync(TOKEN_FILE, "utf8"));
}

function saveToken(tok) {
  ensureStore();
  writeFileSync(TOKEN_FILE, JSON.stringify(tok, null, 2), { mode: 0o600 });
}

export function checkCredentials() {
  const clientOk = existsSync(GMAIL_KEYS);
  const tok = loadToken();
  return {
    ok: clientOk && !!tok?.refresh_token,
    clientPresent: clientOk,
    tokenPresent: !!tok?.refresh_token,
    scopes: tok?.scope || null,
    projectNumber: PROJECT_NUMBER,
  };
}

/** Refresh the stored refresh token into a live access token. */
export async function accessToken() {
  const tok = loadToken();
  if (!tok?.refresh_token) throw new Error("No refresh token. Run runConsent first.");
  const { clientId, clientSecret } = loadClient();
  const body = new URLSearchParams({
    client_id: clientId,
    client_secret: clientSecret,
    refresh_token: tok.refresh_token,
    grant_type: "refresh_token",
  });
  const res = await fetch(TOKEN_URL, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" },
    body: body.toString(),
  });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Token refresh failed (${res.status}): ${await res.text()}`);
  const data = await res.json();
  return data.access_token;
}

// ---- generic Google REST helper -------------------------------------------

async function gapi(method, url, { body, token, query } = {}) {
  const at = token || (await accessToken());
  let full = url;
  if (query) {
    const qs = new URLSearchParams(query).toString();
    full += (url.includes("?") ? "&" : "?") + qs;
  }
  const res = await fetch(full, {
    method,
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${at}`,
      ...(body ? { "Content-Type": "application/json" } : {}),
    },
    ...(body ? { body: JSON.stringify(body) } : {}),
  });
  const text = await res.text();
  let json = null;
  try { json = text ? JSON.parse(text) : {}; } catch { json = { raw: text }; }
  if (!res.ok) {
    const msg = json?.error?.message || text || res.statusText;
    const err = new Error(`${method} ${url} → ${res.status}: ${msg}`);
    err.status = res.status;
    err.body = json;
    throw err;
  }
  return json;
}

// ---- OAuth consent (loopback) ---------------------------------------------

/**
 * Start a loopback server, build the consent URL, write it to AUTH_URL_FILE,
 * and resolve once the redirect delivers a code (which we exchange + store).
 * Run this BACKGROUNDED; meanwhile drive AUTH_URL_FILE's URL through CIC.
 */
export async function runConsent({ port = 4100, scopes = SCOPES } = {}) {
  ensureStore();
  const { clientId, clientSecret } = loadClient();
  // NOTE: the gmail Desktop OAuth client registers only "http://localhost".
  // Google's loopback rule ignores the PORT but not an arbitrary PATH, so the
  // redirect must be bare http://localhost:<port> (root) — not /oauth2callback.
  const redirectUri = `http://localhost:${port}`;
  const authUrl =
    `${AUTH_BASE}?` +
    new URLSearchParams({
      client_id: clientId,
      redirect_uri: redirectUri,
      response_type: "code",
      scope: scopes.join(" "),
      access_type: "offline",
      prompt: "consent",
      include_granted_scopes: "true",
    }).toString();
  writeFileSync(AUTH_URL_FILE, authUrl, "utf8");
  console.log("AUTH_URL:", authUrl);
  console.log("Listening on", redirectUri);

  return await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const server = createServer(async (req, res) => {
      try {
        const u = new URL(req.url, redirectUri);
        const code = u.searchParams.get("code");
        const oerr = u.searchParams.get("error");
        if (!code && !oerr) {
          // favicon or stray request — ignore, keep listening
          res.writeHead(204).end();
          return;
        }
        if (oerr) {
          res.writeHead(400, { "Content-Type": "text/html" }).end(`<h2>OAuth error: ${oerr}</h2>`);
          server.close();
          reject(new Error(`OAuth error: ${oerr}`));
          return;
        }
        if (!code) { res.writeHead(400).end("missing code"); return; }
        // exchange
        const tokenRes = await fetch(TOKEN_URL, {
          method: "POST",
          headers: { "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" },
          body: new URLSearchParams({
            code, client_id: clientId, client_secret: clientSecret,
            redirect_uri: redirectUri, grant_type: "authorization_code",
          }).toString(),
        });
        const tok = await tokenRes.json();
        if (!tokenRes.ok || !tok.refresh_token) {
          res.writeHead(500, { "Content-Type": "text/html" })
            .end(`<h2>Token exchange failed</h2><pre>${JSON.stringify(tok)}</pre>`);
          server.close();
          reject(new Error(`Token exchange failed: ${JSON.stringify(tok)}`));
          return;
        }
        saveToken(tok);
        res.writeHead(200, { "Content-Type": "text/html" })
          .end("<h2>✅ siteAnalytics authorized. You can close this tab.</h2>");
        server.close();
        resolve({ ok: true, scope: tok.scope, stored: TOKEN_FILE });
      } catch (e) {
        try { res.writeHead(500).end(String(e)); } catch {}
        server.close();
        reject(e);
      }
    });
    server.on("error", reject);
    server.listen(port);
  });
}

// ---- Service Usage (enable APIs) ------------------------------------------

export async function enableApis({ apis, projectNumber = PROJECT_NUMBER } = {}) {
  const services = apis || [
    "analyticsadmin.googleapis.com",
    "analyticsdata.googleapis.com", // GA4 Data API (runReport / reporting)
    "searchconsole.googleapis.com",
    "siteverification.googleapis.com",
  ];
  const out = [];
  for (const svc of services) {
    const r = await gapi(
      "POST",
      `${SERVICEUSAGE}/projects/${projectNumber}/services/${svc}:enable`,
      { body: {} },
    );
    out.push({ service: svc, result: r });
  }
  return out;
}

// ---- GA4 Admin -------------------------------------------------------------

export async function ga4ListAccounts() {
  const r = await gapi("GET", `${GA4_ADMIN}/accounts`);
  return r.accounts || [];
}

export async function ga4ListProperties({ accountId }) {
  const r = await gapi("GET", `${GA4_ADMIN}/properties`, {
    query: { filter: `parent:accounts/${accountId}`, pageSize: "200" },
  });
  return r.properties || [];
}

export async function ga4CreateProperty({
  accountId, displayName, timeZone = "America/New_York", currencyCode = "USD",
}) {
  return await gapi("POST", `${GA4_ADMIN}/properties`, {
    body: {
      parent: `accounts/${accountId}`,
      displayName,
      timeZone,
      currencyCode,
    },
  });
}

export async function ga4CreateDataStream({ propertyId, displayName, defaultUri }) {
  // propertyId may be "properties/123" or "123"
  const pid = String(propertyId).startsWith("properties/") ? propertyId : `properties/${propertyId}`;
  return await gapi("POST", `${GA4_ADMIN}/${pid}/dataStreams`, {
    body: {
      type: "WEB_DATA_STREAM",
      displayName,
      webStreamData: { defaultUri },
    },
  });
}

// ---- GA4 Data API (reporting) ---------------------------------------------

/** Accept a convenience {fieldName,matchType,value} or a raw GA4 FilterExpression. */
function normalizeGa4Filter(f) {
  if (!f || typeof f !== "object") return undefined;
  if (f.filter || f.andGroup || f.orGroup || f.notExpression) return f; // already a FilterExpression
  if (f.fieldName) {
    return {
      filter: {
        fieldName: f.fieldName,
        stringFilter: { matchType: f.matchType || "CONTAINS", value: f.value, caseSensitive: !!f.caseSensitive },
      },
    };
  }
  return f;
}

/**
 * Pull GA4 on-site traffic via the Data API runReport — the read counterpart to
 * gscSearchAnalytics (GSC is search-side; this is on-site/behavioral).
 *
 * @param {{
 *   propertyId: string,                 // 'properties/362731773' or '362731773'
 *   startDate: string, endDate: string, // 'YYYY-MM-DD' (also 'NdaysAgo'/'today' accepted by GA4)
 *   dimensions?: Array<string|{name:string}>,   // e.g. ['date'], ['pagePath']
 *   metrics?: Array<string|{name:string}>,       // default sessions/totalUsers/screenPageViews
 *   dimensionFilter?: { fieldName?: string, matchType?: string, value?: string, caseSensitive?: boolean } | object,
 *   limit?: number, offset?: number, orderBys?: object[], keepEmptyRows?: boolean,
 * }} p
 * @returns {Promise<{ rows: Array<Record<string, string|number>>, totals: Record<string, number>, rowCount: number, dimensionHeaders: string[], metricHeaders: string[] }>}
 */
export async function ga4RunReport({
  propertyId, startDate, endDate,
  dimensions = [], metrics = ["sessions", "totalUsers", "screenPageViews"],
  dimensionFilter, limit = 100000, offset = 0, orderBys, keepEmptyRows = false,
} = {}) {
  if (!propertyId) throw new Error("propertyId is required (e.g. 'properties/362731773').");
  if (!startDate || !endDate) throw new Error("startDate and endDate (YYYY-MM-DD) are required.");
  const pid = String(propertyId).startsWith("properties/") ? propertyId : `properties/${propertyId}`;

  const body = {
    dateRanges: [{ startDate, endDate }],
    dimensions: dimensions.map((d) => (typeof d === "string" ? { name: d } : d)),
    metrics: metrics.map((m) => (typeof m === "string" ? { name: m } : m)),
    limit: String(Math.max(1, Math.min(Number(limit) || 100000, 250000))),
    offset: String(Math.max(0, Number(offset) || 0)),
    keepEmptyRows: !!keepEmptyRows,
  };
  if (orderBys) body.orderBys = orderBys;
  const filt = normalizeGa4Filter(dimensionFilter);
  if (filt) body.dimensionFilter = filt;

  const r = await gapi("POST", `${GA4_DATA}/${pid}:runReport`, { body });

  const dimNames = (r.dimensionHeaders || []).map((h) => h.name);
  const metNames = (r.metricHeaders || []).map((h) => h.name);
  const rows = (r.rows || []).map((row) => {
    const o = {};
    (row.dimensionValues || []).forEach((v, i) => { o[dimNames[i] || `dim${i}`] = v.value; });
    (row.metricValues || []).forEach((v, i) => { o[metNames[i] || `met${i}`] = Number(v.value); });
    return o;
  });
  const totals = {};
  if (r.totals && r.totals[0]) {
    (r.totals[0].metricValues || []).forEach((v, i) => { totals[metNames[i] || `met${i}`] = Number(v.value); });
  }
  return { rows, totals, rowCount: r.rowCount ?? rows.length, dimensionHeaders: dimNames, metricHeaders: metNames };
}

// ---- Search Console + Site Verification -----------------------------------

const enc = (s) => encodeURIComponent(s);

export async function gscListSites() {
  const r = await gapi("GET", `${GSC_API}/sites`);
  return r.siteEntry || [];
}

export async function gscAddSite({ siteUrl }) {
  await gapi("PUT", `${GSC_API}/sites/${enc(siteUrl)}`);
  return { ok: true, siteUrl };
}

export async function gscGetVerificationToken({ siteUrl, method = "META" }) {
  // For META, identifier should be the site origin (no trailing slash needed).
  const r = await gapi("POST", `${SITEVERIFY_API}/token`, {
    body: {
      verificationMethod: method,
      site: { type: "SITE", identifier: siteUrl },
    },
  });
  return r; // { token: "<meta ... content=...> or content value", method }
}

export async function gscVerify({ siteUrl, method = "META" }) {
  return await gapi("POST", `${SITEVERIFY_API}/webResource`, {
    query: { verificationMethod: method },
    body: { site: { type: "SITE", identifier: siteUrl } },
  });
}

export async function gscSubmitSitemap({ siteUrl, sitemapUrl }) {
  await gapi("PUT", `${GSC_API}/sites/${enc(siteUrl)}/sitemaps/${enc(sitemapUrl)}`);
  return { ok: true, siteUrl, sitemapUrl };
}

export async function gscListSitemaps({ siteUrl }) {
  const r = await gapi("GET", `${GSC_API}/sites/${enc(siteUrl)}/sitemaps`);
  return r.sitemap || [];
}

/**
 * Query the Search Analytics (Performance) report — the actual traffic data.
 * This is the read counterpart to the provisioning calls above. The consented
 * OAuth user must have access to the property (any permissionLevel).
 *
 * @param {{
 *   siteUrl: string,                // 'sc-domain:bosterbio.com' or 'https://www.bosterbio.com/'
 *   startDate: string,              // 'YYYY-MM-DD'
 *   endDate: string,                // 'YYYY-MM-DD'
 *   dimensions?: string[],          // [] = single aggregate row; ['date'] = daily series; ['page'] = per-URL
 *   filters?: Array<{ dimension: string, operator?: string, expression: string }>,
 *   rowLimit?: number,              // per page, max 25000 (paginates beyond)
 *   searchType?: string,            // 'web' | 'image' | 'video' | 'news' | 'discover' | 'googleNews'
 *   dataState?: string,             // 'final' | 'all' (all includes fresh, partial data)
 *   aggregationType?: string,       // 'auto' | 'byPage' | 'byProperty'
 * }} p
 * @returns {Promise<{ rows: Array<{keys?:string[],clicks:number,impressions:number,ctr:number,position:number}>, totals:{clicks:number,impressions:number}, rowCount:number }>}
 */
export async function gscSearchAnalytics({
  siteUrl, startDate, endDate,
  dimensions = [], filters = [],
  rowLimit = 25000, searchType = "web", dataState = "final", aggregationType,
} = {}) {
  if (!siteUrl) throw new Error("siteUrl is required (e.g. 'sc-domain:bosterbio.com').");
  if (!startDate || !endDate) throw new Error("startDate and endDate (YYYY-MM-DD) are required.");

  const pageLimit = Math.min(Math.max(Number(rowLimit) || 25000, 1), 25000);
  const base = { startDate, endDate, type: searchType, dataState, rowLimit: pageLimit };
  if (dimensions.length) base.dimensions = dimensions;
  if (aggregationType) base.aggregationType = aggregationType;
  if (filters.length) {
    base.dimensionFilterGroups = [{
      groupType: "and",
      filters: filters.map((f) => {
        let operator = f.operator || "contains";
        let expression = f.expression;
        // GSC API quirk: the `contains` operator with a LEADING SLASH silently
        // matches zero rows (even though the page URLs contain it). Replicate the
        // web-UI "URLs containing /path/" by switching to an anchored regex.
        if (operator === "contains" && typeof expression === "string" && expression.startsWith("/")) {
          const escaped = expression.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");
          operator = "includingRegex";
          expression = `.*${escaped}.*`;
        }
        return { dimension: f.dimension, operator, expression };
      }),
    }];
  }

  // Page through results via startRow until a short page returns.
  const rows = [];
  let startRow = 0;
  for (;;) {
    const page = await gapi("POST", `${GSC_API}/sites/${enc(siteUrl)}/searchAnalytics/query`, {
      body: { ...base, startRow },
    });
    const got = page.rows || [];
    rows.push(...got);
    if (got.length < pageLimit || !dimensions.length) break; // aggregate query = single row
    startRow += got.length;
    if (startRow >= 100000) break; // safety cap
  }

  const totals = rows.reduce(
    (a, r) => ({ clicks: a.clicks + (r.clicks || 0), impressions: a.impressions + (r.impressions || 0) }),
    { clicks: 0, impressions: 0 },
  );
  return { rows, totals, rowCount: rows.length };
}

<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: libs/weapon/skillBooks/buildIndex.mjs -->
```js
/**
 * skillBooks weapon — skill-index generator (Option B, 2026-07-05).
 *
 * Rebuilds each `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` as a THIN INDEX that points back
 * to the single content source in `libs/` — instead of the verbatim per-action
 * `.md` copies (which duplicate the skill-book prose and drift). The split:
 *   - INDEX  (.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md): frontmatter name+description
 *     (discovery — preserved as-is) + `## Actions` list + a pointer to libs +
 *     `## Weapons` pointers. Portable per runtime.
 *   - CONTENT (libs/skill_book/<name>/index.js `howTo` prose, libs/weapon/<name>):
 *     the single source of truth, read on-demand when a skill fires.
 *
 * Idempotent: reads the CURRENT SKILL.md frontmatter (to preserve the hand-tuned
 * discovery description) + the folded-weapon list (from the existing `weapons/`
 * dir), pulls the Actions list fresh from libs via tocScan, rewrites SKILL.md,
 * and deletes the now-redundant per-action `.md` + `weapons/` copies.
 *
 * Skips folders with no libs source (the harness-native meta skills:
 * question-gate, skill-book-router, success-gate) — those are authored directly.
 *
 * Usage:  node libs/weapon/skillBooks/buildIndex.mjs [--dry]
 */

import { readdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, statSync, rmSync } from "node:fs";
import { join, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { scanSkillBookTocsFromDisk, scanWeaponTocsFromDisk } from "./tocScan.js";

const __dirname = fileURLToPath(new URL(".", import.meta.url));
const ROOT = resolve(__dirname, "..", "..", "..");
const SKILLS = join(ROOT, ".claude", "skills");
const SB = join(ROOT, "libs", "skill_book");
const WP = join(ROOT, "libs", "weapon");
const DRY = process.argv.includes("--dry");

// action→desc grouped by owner, from the libs content source (single source of truth).
const sbRows = scanSkillBookTocsFromDisk();
const wpRows = scanWeaponTocsFromDisk();
const sbToc = groupBy(sbRows, "skillBook");
const wpToc = groupBy(wpRows, "weapon");

function groupBy(rows, key) {
  const m = {};
  for (const r of rows) (m[r[key]] ||= []).push({ action: r.action, description: r.description });
  return m;
}
function pick(src, field) {
  const m = src.match(new RegExp(`${field}\\s*:\\s*(["'\`])((?:\\\\.|(?!\\1).)*)\\1`, "m"));
  return m ? m[2].replace(/\\(.)/g, "$1") : null;
}
function frontmatter(src) {
  const fm = src.match(/^---\s*\n[\s\S]*?\n---\s*(\n|$)/);
  return fm ? fm[0].replace(/\s*$/, "\n") : null;
}
function exists(p) { try { statSync(p); return true; } catch { return false; } }

let built = 0, skipped = 0, deleted = 0;
const report = [];

for (const name of readdirSync(SKILLS)) {
  const dir = join(SKILLS, name);
  if (!exists(dir) || !statSync(dir).isDirectory()) continue;
  const skillMd = join(dir, "SKILL.md");
  if (!exists(skillMd)) continue;

  // Resolve the libs content source + action list.
  let sourceKind, sourcePath, title, actions, runHint;
  if (exists(join(SB, name, "index.js"))) {
    sourceKind = "skill_book";
    sourcePath = `libs/skill_book/${name}/index.js`;
    const s = readFileSync(join(SB, name, "index.js"), "utf8");
    title = pick(s, "title") || name;
    actions = sbToc[name] || [];
    runHint = `node libs/adventurer/run-action.mjs --howto ${name} <action>`;
  } else if (exists(join(WP, name, "index.js"))) {
    sourceKind = "weapon";
    sourcePath = `libs/weapon/${name}/index.js`;
    const s = readFileSync(join(WP, name, "index.js"), "utf8");
    title = pick(s, "title") || name;
    actions = wpToc[name] || [];
    runHint = `node libs/adventurer/run-action.mjs ${name} <action> '<inputJson>'`;
  } else {
    skipped++;                          // no libs source → native meta skill, leave alone
    continue;
  }

  // Preserve the hand-tuned discovery frontmatter; fall back to a minimal one.
  const cur = readFileSync(skillMd, "utf8");
  const fm = frontmatter(cur) || `---\nname: ${name}\ndescription: ${title}\n---\n`;

  // Folded weapons = existing weapons/<W>.md basenames (preserve the fold).
  const weaponsDir = join(dir, "weapons");
  const folded = exists(weaponsDir)
    ? readdirSync(weaponsDir).filter(f => f.endsWith(".md")).map(f => f.replace(/\.md$/, ""))
    : [];

  const lines = [];
  lines.push(fm.trimEnd(), "");
  lines.push(`# ${title}`, "");
  lines.push(
    `> **Index only.** This skill is a discovery pointer. The full procedure for each`,
    `> action lives in the single content source \`${sourcePath}\`. Load it on demand:`,
    `> \`${runHint}\` (or read the source directly).`,
    ""
  );
  if (actions.length) {
    lines.push("## Actions", "");
    for (const a of actions) {
      const d = (a.description || "").replace(/\n+/g, " ").trim();
      lines.push(`- **${a.action}**${d ? ` — ${d}` : ""}`);
    }
    lines.push("");
  }
  if (folded.length) {
    lines.push("## Weapons", "");
    lines.push(`Folded-in executable weapons (code + toc in \`libs/weapon/\`; invoke via run-action):`, "");
    for (const w of folded) {
      const wt = (wpToc[w] || []).slice(0, 3).map(x => x.action).join(", ");
      lines.push(`- **${w}** — \`libs/weapon/${w}/\`${wt ? ` (e.g. ${wt})` : ""}`);
    }
    lines.push("");
  }
  const out = lines.join("\n").replace(/\n{3,}/g, "\n\n");

  if (DRY) {
    report.push(`[dry] ${name}: ${actions.length} actions, ${folded.length} weapons`);
    built++;
    continue;
  }

  writeFileSync(skillMd, out, "utf8");
  // Delete the now-redundant content copies: every .md except SKILL.md, and weapons/.
  for (const f of readdirSync(dir)) {
    const p = join(dir, f);
    if (f === "SKILL.md") continue;
    if (f === "weapons" && exists(p) && statSync(p).isDirectory()) { rmSync(p, { recursive: true, force: true }); deleted++; continue; }
    if (f.endsWith(".md")) { rmSync(p, { force: true }); deleted++; }
  }
  built++;
  report.push(`${name}: index rebuilt (${actions.length} actions, ${folded.length} weapons)`);
}

console.log(report.join("\n"));
console.log(`\n${DRY ? "[DRY] " : ""}Rebuilt ${built} skill indexes · skipped ${skipped} (no libs source) · removed ${deleted} redundant copies`);
```

/**
 * skillBooks weapon — ownership-map CLI entrypoint.
 *
 * Source of truth = the frontmatter `description` + `## Actions`/`## Weapons`
 * bullets in each `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (refactor 2026-07-04).
 * Discovery = directory scan (no hand-maintained hub-file lookup).
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node libs/weapon/skillBooks/cli-ownership.mjs            → markdown to stdout
 *   node libs/weapon/skillBooks/cli-ownership.mjs --json     → JSON to stdout
 *   node libs/weapon/skillBooks/cli-ownership.mjs --audit    → list entries with thin descriptions
 *
 * Runtime (`dumpOwnershipMap`) + CLI share `tocScan.scanClaudeSkillsFromDisk`
 * so their outputs cannot drift.
 */

import { scanClaudeSkillsFromDisk } from "./tocScan.js";

const args = process.argv.slice(2);
const wantJson = args.includes("--json");
const wantAudit = args.includes("--audit");

const rows = scanClaudeSkillsFromDisk();

if (wantAudit) {
  const thin = rows.filter(r => !r.description || r.description.length <= 30);
  const empty = rows.filter(r => !r.description);
  console.log(`Total TOC entries: ${rows.length}`);
  console.log(`Skill books represented: ${new Set(rows.map(r => r.skillBook)).size}`);
  console.log(`Thin descriptions (≤30 chars): ${thin.length}`);
  console.log(`Empty descriptions: ${empty.length}`);
  console.log("");
  if (thin.length) {
    console.log("--- Thin / empty entries (fix in source skill book) ---");
    for (const r of thin.slice(0, 60)) {
      console.log(`  ${r.skillBook}.${r.action} → ${JSON.stringify(r.description || "")}`);
    }
    if (thin.length > 60) console.log(`  ... and ${thin.length - 60} more`);
  }
  process.exit(0);
}

if (wantJson) {
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ rows, generatedAt: new Date().toISOString() }, null, 2));
  process.exit(0);
}

const lines = [
  "# Ownership map (generated from .claude/skills SKILL.md)",
  "",
  `> Auto-generated by \`libs/weapon/skillBooks/cli-ownership.mjs\` via directory-scan. Source of truth = the frontmatter \`description\` + \`## Actions\`/\`## Weapons\` bullets in each \`.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md\`. Discovery = filesystem walk, no hub-file maintenance required. To fix an entry, edit its description in that SKILL.md.`,
  "",
  `Generated: ${new Date().toISOString()} · ${rows.length} entries across ${new Set(rows.map(r => r.skillBook)).size} skills`,
  "",
  "| Skill | Action | Owns / describes |",
  "|---|---|---|",
];
for (const r of rows) {
  const desc = (r.description || "").replace(/\|/g, "\\|").replace(/\n/g, " ").trim() || "_(no description)_";
  lines.push(`| \`${r.skillBook}\` | \`${r.action}\` | ${desc} |`);
}
console.log(lines.join("\n"));
process.exit(0);

```js
/**
 * skillBooks weapon — CLI entrypoint.
 *
 * The skillBooks weapon is a function module (`gearUp`), normally
 * called from app/agent context. The skill-book-router skill needs to invoke
 * it as a process. Naive `node -e` fails on the `@/` path alias and the
 * registry's Next-style extensionless imports (documented failure mode in
 * guildmaster.evolutionLoop). That resolution bootstrap is always-on plumbing
 * hidden from the agent, so per blacksmith.refForgeDiscipline it lives WITH
 * the weapon, not as a satellite script. The skill calls this; this calls the
 * weapon. One-way reference, weapon stays the source of truth.
 *
 * Usage: node libs/weapon/skillBooks/cli.mjs "<pending action description>"
 */

import { register } from "node:module";
import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
import { resolve } from "node:path";

const projectRoot = resolve(import.meta.dirname, "..", "..", "..");
register("data:text/javascript," + encodeURIComponent(`
  import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url";
  import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
  const root = ${JSON.stringify(projectRoot.replace(/\\/g, "/"))};
  // Next.js bundler tolerates extensionless file AND directory imports
  // (e.g. "@/libs/council/profileEnvVars" or "@/libs/weapon/zoho").
  // Plain Node ESM does not — mimic the standard resolution candidates.
  const CANDIDATES = [".js", ".mjs", ".cjs", "/index.js", "/index.mjs"];
  function toPath(url) {
    try { return decodeURIComponent(new URL(url).pathname).replace(/^\\/([A-Za-z]:)/, "$1"); }
    catch { return null; }
  }
  export async function resolve(specifier, context, next) {
    let spec = specifier;
    if (spec.startsWith("@/")) spec = pathToFileURL(root + "/" + spec.slice(2)).href;
    try {
      return await next(spec, context);
    } catch (err) {
      if (!err || (err.code !== "ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT" && err.code !== "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND")) throw err;
      const base = (err.url || spec).replace(/\\/$/, "");
      const basePath = toPath(base);
      if (basePath) {
        for (const ext of CANDIDATES) {
          if (existsSync(basePath + ext)) return await next(base + ext, context);
        }
      }
      throw err;
    }
  }
`), pathToFileURL(projectRoot + "/"));

const rawArgs = process.argv.slice(2);
const withContext = rawArgs.includes("--with-context");
const taskDescription = rawArgs.filter(a => a !== "--with-context").join(" ").trim();

if (!taskDescription) {
  console.error('Usage: node libs/weapon/skillBooks/cli.mjs "<pending action description>" [--with-context]');
  process.exit(2);
}

const { gearUp } = await import("@/libs/weapon/skillBooks/index.js");

const gearResult = gearUp({
  taskDescription,
  withContext,
  agent: "skill-book-router",
});
// gearUp returns a Promise when withContext=true, plain object otherwise
const { suggestions = [], error, contextSnippets } = withContext ? await gearResult : gearResult;

if (error) {
  console.error(`scan error: ${error}`);
  process.exit(1);
}

if (suggestions.length === 0) {
  console.log("NO_MATCH — no skill book scored against this task. Proceed normally.");
  process.exit(0);
}

const top = suggestions.slice(0, 5);
console.log(`MATCHES (${top.length} of ${suggestions.length} scored — .claude/skills) for: ${taskDescription}\n`);
for (const s of top) {
  console.log(`# ${s.skillBook}  [SKILL]  (totalScore=${s.totalScore})`);
  for (const a of s.actions.sort((x, y) => y.score - x.score).slice(0, 4)) {
    console.log(`  - ${a.action} [${a.score}]: ${a.toc.slice(0, 160)}`);
  }
  console.log("");
}
const t0 = top[0];
console.log(
  `NEXT: read .claude/skills/${t0.skillBook}/SKILL.md, then open the matching action file ` +
    `.claude/skills/${t0.skillBook}/<action>.md for its howTo. If the action needs runtime ` +
    `logic, its executable weapon is invocable via ` +
    `node --no-warnings libs/adventurer/run-action.mjs ${t0.skillBook} <action> '<inputJson>'. ` +
    `If none of the above fits the pending action, proceed normally.`,
);

// When --with-context, append recall snippets as supplemental context
if (contextSnippets && contextSnippets.length > 0) {
  console.log(`\n── CONTEXT SNIPPETS (from docs + memory) ──\n`);
  for (const s of contextSnippets) {
    console.log(`[${s.sourceId}] ${s.docPath} § ${s.section}  (score=${s.score.toFixed(2)}, ~${s.tokenEstimate}tok)`);
    const lines = s.text.split("\n").slice(0, 3);
    for (const l of lines) console.log(`  ${l}`);
    if (s.text.split("\n").length > 3) console.log(`  …`);
    console.log("");
  }
}

process.exit(0);
```

<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: libs/weapon/skillBooks/engineering_decisions.md -->
```markdown
# Engineering decisions — `libs/weapon/skillBooks`

Rationale layer (per CLAUDE.md §6). The WHY behind this module's design — not API
docs, not procedure. Append; supersede in place when a decision changes.

---

## 2026-06-13 — `gearUp` scans skill books AND weapons (directory-driven)

**Decision.** `gearUp` ranks weapon `toc` actions alongside skill-book actions,
each suggestion tagged `kind: "skill_book" | "weapon"`. Weapon TOCs are read
from disk via `scanWeaponTocsFromDisk()` (`tocScan.js`), mirroring the existing
skill-book scan — directory-driven, so a new weapon folder is picked up with zero
edits here.

**Rejected alternative.** Scanning only skill books (the original), or maintaining
a hand-written weapon hub to scan.

**Why.** Capabilities live in BOTH trees, but discovery only covered one half —
so weapon actions (e.g. `openai_images.generate`) were invisible to the registry
scan, and agents that needed them had to already know the id/action or go
guessing. Disk-driven scan avoids a dual-maintained hub (same architecture call
as the skill-book scanner).

**Consequence if violated.** Half the capability surface is undiscoverable via the
preflight scan → agents maze on weapon-backed tasks (the 2026-06-13 image-gen
maze; full rationale in `libs/adventurer/engineering_decisions.md`).

---

## 2026-07-05 — `.claude/skills` is a GENERATED thin INDEX, not a content copy (supersedes the copy approach in the 2026-07-04 entry below)

**Decision.** Each `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is a thin INDEX: preserved
frontmatter (name + hand-tuned discovery `description`) + a `## Actions` list
generated from the libs `toc` + a pointer to the libs content source +
`## Weapons` pointers. The per-action `<action>.md` content files (verbatim howTo
copies) and the `weapons/<W>.md` docs were DELETED. Content lives ONLY in
`libs/skill_book/<name>/index.js` (howTo prose) and `libs/weapon/<name>`
(executable). `libs/weapon/skillBooks/buildIndex.mjs` regenerates every index from
libs, preserving frontmatter and the folded-weapon list; blacksmith's forge +
patchSkillBook now write to libs then run buildIndex.

**Rejected alternative.** (a) Keep the verbatim per-action `.md` copies in
`.claude/skills` (what the initial 2026-07-04 build did). (b) Copy the skills into
each runtime (e.g. Cursor equivalents) per guild.

**Why.** The verbatim copies duplicated the skill-book prose in two places →
guaranteed drift, dual maintenance. The index-and-point model keeps ONE content
source (libs) and makes the discovery layer a generated, disposable artifact.
Bonus: porting to another runtime/guild (Cursor `.mdc`, `AGENTS.md`) becomes a
second `buildIndex` output target over the SAME repo — port the thin index, not
the content. Footprint dropped 593 → 83 md files (~502 copies removed) with
discovery (gearUp/ownership: 698 rows/83 skills) unchanged.

**Consequence if violated.** If a future agent hand-writes howTo prose back into
`.claude/skills/<name>/*.md`, it re-forks the content and buildIndex will DELETE it
on the next run (silent data loss of the hand-edit). Edit howTo in `libs/`, then
regenerate. The frontmatter `description` is the ONE field authored in
`.claude/skills` (buildIndex preserves it) — it's the per-runtime discovery index.

---

## 2026-07-04 — `.claude/skills` is the canonical discovery registry; libs/ keeps the executable code

**Decision.** Discovery/routing now scans the `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`
tree, not the JS `toc` blocks. `scanClaudeSkillsFromDisk` (`tocScan.js`) parses
each SKILL.md's frontmatter `description` + `## Actions`/`## Weapons`/`## Functions`
bullets into the same `{skillBook, action, description}` rows the rest of the
system already consumes; `gearUp`, `dumpOwnershipMap`, `cli-ownership.mjs`, and the
preflight hook's `listSkillBooks` all read this one source. The former
`libs/skill_book/*/index.js` `toc` scan and the separate `libs/weapon/*` `toc`
scan (`scanSkillBookTocsFromDisk` / `scanWeaponTocsFromDisk`) are retained but no
longer wired into discovery. Every skill book + weapon was mirrored into
`.claude/skills` (folded weapons live under their owner skill's `weapons/`;
standalone weapons are their own skill folder).

**Rejected alternative.** (a) Keep discovery on the JS `toc` blocks and treat
`.claude/skills` as docs-only. (b) Go the whole way — delete `libs/skill_book`
prose and have adventurer EXECUTION parse the `.md` files too.

**Why.** The operator wants GuildOS capabilities to BE native Claude Code skills
(auto-loaded by the harness from `.claude/skills`), so the SKILL.md tree must be
the source of truth — one registry, not two that drift. But executable actions
(`libs/skill_book/<name>` `adventurerActions` loaded by `getSkillBook`; every
weapon's integration code invoked by `run-action`) are CODE, not markdown — they
cannot move into `.md`. So the split is deliberate: **markdown = discovery +
howTo prose; libs/ = executable code.** A folded weapon has a discovery doc under
its owner skill AND its real code in `libs/weapon`.

**Consequence if violated.** If a future agent "simplifies" by pointing discovery
back at the JS `toc` blocks, new skills authored only as `.claude/skills` folders
(the blacksmith's new forge target) become invisible to `gearUp`/preflight. If it
instead deletes `libs/skill_book`/`libs/weapon` to "finish the migration,"
adventurer/quest execution and every weapon call break — the `.md` files are not
executable. Keep both trees; keep discovery on `.claude/skills`.

**Follow-on (2026-07-05) — the preflight hook must NOT re-dump the registry.**
Once skills live in `.claude/skills`, the Claude Code harness ALREADY lists every
skill's name+description in the system prompt (native progressive disclosure —
free; the body loads only when the Skill tool invokes it). So
`.claude/hooks/preflight.mjs` was trimmed to STOP injecting the full per-skill
description dump (it had ballooned to ~5k tokens/turn — ~4,979 for the registry
block alone). It now injects only the gate text + a pointer to the native list +
the `gearUp` CLI + weapon IDs (~1.2k tok/turn total, down from ~5.8k). **Do NOT
re-add `bookLines = books.map(b => \`- ${b.id}: ${b.description}\`)` to the hook
output** — that re-duplicates the free native list and is pure per-turn waste. The
`listSkillBooks()` count is still read (cheap, for the header); only the dump is
gone. Realizing "skill-picking is free" was the whole point of moving to
`.claude/skills` — the hook dump silently defeated it.

---

## (standing) — TOC is the two-tier discovery mechanism; keep `description` thin

**Decision.** A `toc` entry's `description` is the **strategic** layer `gearUp`
scans across the whole registry in one pass; the `howTo` is the **tactical**
layer loaded only for the chosen action. Keep descriptions short and
intent-bearing (verb + noun + when-to-use), not procedure.

**Rejected alternative.** Fat descriptions that inline the how, or rationale; a
parallel discovery doc.

**Why.** Cheap reliable discovery = O(all descriptions) once + O(one howTo) after.
Bloating the description inflates every scan and blurs the strategic/tactical
split; putting rationale here (vs `engineering_decisions.md`) makes the scan
noisier without helping discovery.

**Consequence if violated.** `gearUp` ranking degrades (noise tokens), and the
two-tier efficiency that makes the preflight scan affordable erodes.
