```js
/**
 * skillBooks weapon — discovery and capability layer over the skill book registry.
 *
 * Used by GM-dispatched SAs to:
 *   - scanSMARTPlans({ userMessage }) → which [SMART]-prefixed actions match a user message
 *   - gearUp({ taskDescription }) → "gear up at the town stalls before the quest"; rank skill books for a task
 *
 * Both are noise-absorbing functions: they read all TOCs internally and surface
 * only the matches with their TOC descriptions. The full howTos are never returned.
 */

import { SKILL_BOOKS } from "@/libs/skill_book/index.js";
import { scanClaudeSkillsFromDisk } from "./tocScan.js";
import { logWeaponCall } from "../weaponLog/index.js";

const SMART_PREFIX = "[SMART]";

// ── helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function tocLine(entry) {
  if (typeof entry === "string") return entry;
  if (typeof entry?.description === "string") return entry.description;
  return "";
}

function tokenize(text) {
  return text
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}\s]/gu, " ")
    .split(/\s+/)
    .filter(t => t.length >= 3);
}

function scoreMatch(userTokens, tocText) {
  const haystack = tocText.toLowerCase();
  let hits = 0;
  for (const tok of userTokens) {
    if (haystack.includes(tok)) hits++;
  }
  return hits;
}

// ── scanSMARTPlans ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Scan every [SMART]-prefixed TOC entry across all skill books. Score matches
 * against the user message by simple token overlap. Return ranked candidates.
 *
 * @param {{ userMessage: string, agent?: string }} opts
 * @returns {{ matches: Array<{ skillBook, action, toc, score }> }}
 */
export function scanSMARTPlans({ userMessage, agent = "GM" }) {
  if (!userMessage || typeof userMessage !== "string") {
    const result = { matches: [], error: "userMessage required" };
    logWeaponCall({ weapon: "skillBooks", fn: "scanSMARTPlans", agent, input: { messageLength: 0 }, output: result, status: "error" });
    return result;
  }

  const userTokens = tokenize(userMessage);
  const candidates = [];

  for (const [bookId, book] of Object.entries(SKILL_BOOKS)) {
    const toc = book?.toc;
    if (!toc) continue;
    for (const [actionKey, entry] of Object.entries(toc)) {
      const line = tocLine(entry);
      if (!line.trim().startsWith(SMART_PREFIX)) continue;
      const score = scoreMatch(userTokens, line);
      candidates.push({ skillBook: bookId, action: actionKey, toc: line, score });
    }
  }

  // Sort by score desc, drop zeros
  const matches = candidates
    .filter(c => c.score > 0)
    .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score);

  const result = { matches, totalScanned: candidates.length };
  logWeaponCall({
    weapon: "skillBooks",
    fn: "scanSMARTPlans",
    agent,
    input: { messageLength: userMessage.length, userTokens: userTokens.length },
    output: { matchCount: matches.length, totalScanned: candidates.length },
    status: "ok",
  });
  return result;
}

// ── gearUp ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Gear up the adventurer for the quest. Reads every skill book's TOC and ranks
 * the most relevant skill books for a task description by token overlap —
 * the equivalent of stopping at the town square's stalls before heading out
 * the gates: which books, which weapons, which supplies for this run?
 *
 * @param {{ taskDescription: string, withContext?: boolean, contextBudget?: number, agent?: string }} opts
 * @returns {{ suggestions: Array<{ skillBook, actions: Array<{action, toc, score}>, totalScore }>, contextSnippets?: Array }}
 */
export function gearUp({ taskDescription, withContext = false, contextBudget = 2000, agent = "GM" }) {
  if (!taskDescription || typeof taskDescription !== "string") {
    return { suggestions: [], error: "taskDescription required" };
  }

  const tokens = tokenize(taskDescription);
  const perBook = {};

  // Canonical discovery source (refactor 2026-07-04): the `.claude/skills/<name>/`
  // tree. Each folder's SKILL.md frontmatter description + `## Actions` / `## Weapons`
  // / `## Functions` bullets are scanned as the toc. This is the single scan that
  // replaces BOTH the old SKILL_BOOKS-hub loop and the separate libs/weapon disk
  // scan — folded weapons already live under their owning skill's `## Weapons`, and
  // standalone weapons are their own skill folder, so one scan covers everything.
  // Executable JS still lives in libs/; a matched skill is READ (SKILL.md +
  // <action>.md), and if it has runtime logic the leaf invokes the paired weapon.
  for (const r of scanClaudeSkillsFromDisk()) {
    const score = scoreMatch(tokens, r.description || "");
    if (score <= 0) continue;
    const key = r.skillBook;
    if (!perBook[key]) perBook[key] = { skillBook: key, kind: "skill", actions: [], totalScore: 0 };
    // The `(skill)` synthetic row carries the frontmatter description — surface it
    // as the skill's own line but don't list it as an invokable action.
    if (r.action !== "(skill)") perBook[key].actions.push({ action: r.action, toc: r.description, score });
    perBook[key].totalScore += score;
  }

  const suggestions = Object.values(perBook).sort((a, b) => b.totalScore - a.totalScore);

  logWeaponCall({
    weapon: "skillBooks",
    fn: "gearUp",
    agent,
    input: { taskLength: taskDescription.length, tokens: tokens.length, withContext },
    output: { skillCount: suggestions.length },
    status: "ok",
  });

  // Optional: enrich with recall context snippets from docs + memory corpora.
  // Skips the 'registry' corpus (gearUp already covers TOC scoring) to avoid
  // duplicating information; pulls from docs/ and memory/ for supplemental context.
  // When withContext=true, returns a Promise; otherwise returns a plain object
  // (backward-compatible with all existing sync callers).
  if (withContext) {
    return import("../recall/index.js").then(({ recall }) => {
      let contextSnippets;
      try {
        const { snippets } = recall({
          query: taskDescription,
          corpora: ["docs", "memory"],
          topK: 5,
          tokenBudget: contextBudget,
          agent,
        });
        contextSnippets = snippets;
      } catch { contextSnippets = []; }
      return { suggestions, contextSnippets };
    }).catch(() => ({ suggestions, contextSnippets: [] }));
  }

  return { suggestions };
}

// ── dumpOwnershipMap ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Dump every TOC entry across every skill book as a flat ownership map. The
 * single source of truth for "which concept lives in which skill book action"
 * is the description text of the TOC entries themselves — this action just
 * concatenates them and emits a markdown table (or JSON for programmatic use).
 *
 * Replaces the hand-maintained CLAUDE.md "Ownership map" table (removed in
 * commit df4b5b5). When a description is too thin to stand in for ownership
 * info, fix the description in the source skill book — do NOT add a parallel
 * ownership doc.
 *
 * @param {{ format?: 'markdown'|'json', agent?: string }} opts
 * @returns {{ rows, markdown, format }} — rows always present; markdown only when format='markdown'
 */
export function dumpOwnershipMap({ format = "markdown", agent = "GM" } = {}) {
  // Directory-driven scan of the canonical `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` tree
  // (refactor 2026-07-04). Adding a new skill folder = it shows up here
  // automatically. Rows come back in the same {skillBook, action, description}
  // shape the markdown renderer already expects.
  const rows = scanClaudeSkillsFromDisk();

  let markdown;
  if (format === "markdown") {
    const lines = [
      "# Ownership map (generated from .claude/skills SKILL.md)",
      "",
      `> Auto-generated by \`libs/weapon/skillBooks.dumpOwnershipMap\`. Source of truth = the frontmatter \`description\` + \`## Actions\`/\`## Weapons\` bullets in each \`.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md\`. To fix an entry, edit its description in that SKILL.md — do NOT edit this map.`,
      "",
      "| Skill book | Action | Owns / describes |",
      "|---|---|---|",
    ];
    for (const r of rows) {
      const desc = (r.description || "").replace(/\|/g, "\\|").replace(/\n/g, " ").trim() || "_(no description)_";
      lines.push(`| \`${r.skillBook}\` | \`${r.action}\` | ${desc} |`);
    }
    markdown = lines.join("\n");
  }

  const result = { rows, format };
  if (markdown) result.markdown = markdown;

  logWeaponCall({
    weapon: "skillBooks",
    fn: "dumpOwnershipMap",
    agent,
    input: { format },
    output: { rowCount: rows.length, bookCount: new Set(rows.map(r => r.skillBook)).size },
    status: "ok",
  });

  return result;
}

export const toc = {
  scanSMARTPlans: "Scan all skill book TOCs for [SMART]-prefixed actions matching a user message. Returns ranked matches. Input: {userMessage}. Output: {matches: [{skillBook, action, toc, score}]}.",
  gearUp: "Gear up the adventurer for a quest — rank the most relevant skill books (and their actions) for a given task description by token-overlap against every TOC entry. The town-square step before any run: which books / weapons / supplies for this job? Input: {taskDescription}. Output: {suggestions: [{skillBook, actions, totalScore}]}.",
  dumpOwnershipMap: "Generate the ownership map by reading every TOC across every skill book. Replaces the hand-maintained CLAUDE.md table. Input: {format?: 'markdown'|'json'}. Output: {rows, markdown?, format}. To fix an ownership entry, edit its description in the source skill book — never edit a parallel doc.",
  buildSkillIndex: "Regenerate the .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md discovery indexes from the libs content source (index-and-point model). Preserves each skill's frontmatter + folded-weapon list, rebuilds the Actions list from the libs toc, and deletes the redundant per-action content copies. Run after editing any skill-book/weapon content. CLI: node libs/weapon/skillBooks/buildIndex.mjs [--dry].",
};

<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: libs/weapon/skillBooks/tocScan.js -->
```js
/**
 * Skill book TOC scanner — directory-driven, NOT registry-driven.
 *
 * Reads `libs/skill_book/<name>/index.js` directly from disk and extracts each
 * skill book's top-level `toc: { ... }` (or `export const toc = { ... }`) block
 * via brace-balanced regex parsing.
 *
 * Why directory-driven (per user architecture call 2026-05-28):
 *   The hand-maintained `libs/skill_book/index.js` hub (which imports each
 *   skill book individually) requires an edit every time a new skill book is
 *   added. That's dual-maintenance with the per-skill-book TOC descriptions
 *   and "just bad architecture all around" — the user opposes it.
 *
 *   Auto-discovery via fs.readdirSync removes that maintenance burden. Adding
 *   a new skill book = create the folder + `index.js` with a `toc` block; the
 *   scanner picks it up on the next call. No hub-file edit needed.
 *
 * Used by:
 *   - `dumpOwnershipMap` in this weapon's `index.js`
 *   - `cli-ownership.mjs` CLI (bare-node invocation)
 *
 * Both code paths share this function so the runtime + CLI outputs cannot
 * drift.
 */

import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
import { join, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

// Walk from this file (libs/weapon/skillBooks/tocScan.js) up three levels to
// reach the project root, then into libs/skill_book.
const __dirname = fileURLToPath(new URL(".", import.meta.url));
const PROJECT_ROOT = resolve(__dirname, "..", "..", "..");
export const SKILL_BOOKS_DIR = join(PROJECT_ROOT, "libs", "skill_book");
export const WEAPONS_DIR = join(PROJECT_ROOT, "libs", "weapon");
// Canonical registry (refactor 2026-07-04): the `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`
// tree is the source of truth for capability DISCOVERY. Each skill book + weapon
// was mirrored here (TOC → SKILL.md frontmatter + `## Actions`; folded weapons →
// `## Weapons`). Executable JS actions still live in libs/skill_book|libs/weapon
// and are loaded by getSkillBook for adventurer/quest EXECUTION — but gearUp /
// ownership / preflight discovery now scan THIS tree, not the JS `toc` blocks.
export const CLAUDE_SKILLS_DIR = join(PROJECT_ROOT, ".claude", "skills");

/**
 * @returns {Array<{name: string, path: string}>} per-folder index.js paths
 */
export function listSkillBookFiles(dir = SKILL_BOOKS_DIR) {
  const out = [];
  let entries;
  try { entries = readdirSync(dir); } catch { return out; }
  for (const name of entries) {
    const p = join(dir, name);
    let s;
    try { s = statSync(p); } catch { continue; }
    if (!s.isDirectory()) continue;
    const idx = join(p, "index.js");
    try { statSync(idx); out.push({ name, path: idx }); } catch {}
  }
  return out;
}

// Walk forward from `openIdx` (pointing at '{') to its matching '}',
// respecting strings, template literals, and comments.
function extractBalancedBlock(src, openIdx) {
  let depth = 0;
  let i = openIdx;
  const n = src.length;
  while (i < n) {
    const ch = src[i];
    if (ch === "/" && src[i + 1] === "/") {
      const nl = src.indexOf("\n", i);
      i = nl < 0 ? n : nl + 1;
      continue;
    }
    if (ch === "/" && src[i + 1] === "*") {
      const end = src.indexOf("*/", i + 2);
      i = end < 0 ? n : end + 2;
      continue;
    }
    if (ch === "'" || ch === '"' || ch === "`") {
      const quote = ch;
      i++;
      while (i < n) {
        if (src[i] === "\\") { i += 2; continue; }
        if (src[i] === quote) { i++; break; }
        if (quote === "`" && src[i] === "$" && src[i + 1] === "{") {
          let d = 1; i += 2;
          while (i < n && d > 0) {
            if (src[i] === "{") d++;
            else if (src[i] === "}") d--;
            i++;
          }
          continue;
        }
        i++;
      }
      continue;
    }
    if (ch === "{") depth++;
    else if (ch === "}") {
      depth--;
      if (depth === 0) return src.slice(openIdx, i + 1);
    }
    i++;
  }
  return null;
}

function parseTocBlock(inner, out) {
  let i = 0;
  const n = inner.length;
  while (i < n) {
    while (i < n) {
      const ch = inner[i];
      if (/\s/.test(ch) || ch === ",") { i++; continue; }
      if (ch === "/" && inner[i + 1] === "/") { const nl = inner.indexOf("\n", i); i = nl < 0 ? n : nl + 1; continue; }
      if (ch === "/" && inner[i + 1] === "*") { const e = inner.indexOf("*/", i + 2); i = e < 0 ? n : e + 2; continue; }
      break;
    }
    if (i >= n) break;
    let action = "";
    if (inner[i] === "'" || inner[i] === '"') {
      const q = inner[i]; i++;
      while (i < n && inner[i] !== q) { if (inner[i] === "\\") i++; action += inner[i] || ""; i++; }
      i++;
    } else {
      while (i < n && /[A-Za-z0-9_$]/.test(inner[i])) { action += inner[i]; i++; }
    }
    while (i < n && /\s/.test(inner[i])) i++;
    if (inner[i] !== ":") {
      while (i < n && inner[i] !== ",") i++;
      continue;
    }
    i++;
    while (i < n && /\s/.test(inner[i])) i++;
    let description = "";
    if (inner[i] === "'" || inner[i] === '"' || inner[i] === "`") {
      const q = inner[i]; i++;
      while (i < n) {
        if (inner[i] === "\\") { description += inner[i + 1] || ""; i += 2; continue; }
        if (inner[i] === q) { i++; break; }
        description += inner[i]; i++;
      }
    } else if (inner[i] === "{") {
      const block = extractBalancedBlock(inner, i);
      if (block) {
        const dm = block.match(/description\s*:\s*(["'`])((?:\\.|(?!\1).)*)\1/);
        if (dm) description = dm[2].replace(/\\(.)/g, "$1");
        i += block.length;
      }
    }
    if (action) out.push({ action, description: description.trim() });
    while (i < n && inner[i] !== ",") {
      if (inner[i] === "{") {
        const b = extractBalancedBlock(inner, i);
        if (b) { i += b.length; continue; }
      }
      i++;
    }
    if (inner[i] === ",") i++;
  }
}

function extractTocEntries(source) {
  const out = [];
  const re = /\btoc\s*[:=]\s*\{/g;
  let m;
  while ((m = re.exec(source)) !== null) {
    const start = m.index + m[0].length - 1;
    const block = extractBalancedBlock(source, start);
    if (!block) continue;
    parseTocBlock(block.slice(1, -1), out);
    break; // only first toc block per file
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Scan every `libs/skill_book/<name>/index.js` and emit ownership rows.
 * Directory-driven — adding a new skill book folder requires zero edits
 * anywhere else.
 *
 * @returns {Array<{skillBook: string, action: string, description: string}>}
 */
export function scanSkillBookTocsFromDisk() {
  const files = listSkillBookFiles();
  const rows = [];
  for (const f of files) {
    let src;
    try { src = readFileSync(f.path, "utf8"); }
    catch { continue; }
    const entries = extractTocEntries(src);
    for (const e of entries) {
      rows.push({ skillBook: f.name, action: e.action, description: e.description });
    }
  }
  rows.sort((a, b) => (a.skillBook + a.action).localeCompare(b.skillBook + b.action));
  return rows;
}

/**
 * Scan every `libs/weapon/<name>/index.js` and emit its `toc` entries — the
 * weapon-side mirror of scanSkillBookTocsFromDisk. Weapons expose their actions
 * via the same `toc` convention (action → description string), so gearUp can
 * rank weapon actions alongside skill-book actions. Directory-driven: a new
 * weapon folder is picked up with zero edits here.
 *
 * @returns {Array<{weapon: string, action: string, description: string}>}
 */
export function scanWeaponTocsFromDisk() {
  const files = listSkillBookFiles(WEAPONS_DIR);
  const rows = [];
  for (const f of files) {
    let src;
    try { src = readFileSync(f.path, "utf8"); }
    catch { continue; }
    for (const e of extractTocEntries(src)) {
      rows.push({ weapon: f.name, action: e.action, description: e.description });
    }
  }
  rows.sort((a, b) => (a.weapon + a.action).localeCompare(b.weapon + b.action));
  return rows;
}

// ── .claude/skills scanner (canonical discovery source, refactor 2026-07-04) ──

/**
 * List every `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
 * @returns {Array<{name: string, path: string, dir: string}>}
 */
export function listClaudeSkillFiles(dir = CLAUDE_SKILLS_DIR) {
  const out = [];
  let entries;
  try { entries = readdirSync(dir); } catch { return out; }
  for (const name of entries) {
    const p = join(dir, name);
    let s;
    try { s = statSync(p); } catch { continue; }
    if (!s.isDirectory()) continue;
    const md = join(p, "SKILL.md");
    try { statSync(md); out.push({ name, path: md, dir: p }); } catch {}
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Parse a SKILL.md into { name, description, actions: [{action, description}] }.
 * - Frontmatter `description:` (plain or `>-`/`|` block) → the skill-level line.
 * - Bullets under `## Actions`, `## Weapons`, `## Functions` → per-action lines.
 *   Recognises `- [key](file) — desc`, `- **key** — desc`, and `- key — desc`
 *   (em-dash `—` or ` - ` hyphen separator).
 */
export function parseSkillMd(src, skillName) {
  const out = { name: skillName, description: "", actions: [] };

  // Frontmatter block between the first two `---` fences.
  const fm = src.match(/^---\s*\n([\s\S]*?)\n---\s*(\n|$)/);
  if (fm) {
    const block = fm[1];
    // description: value  |  description: >-\n   folded lines...
    const dm = block.match(/^description:\s*(>-|>|\|-|\|)?\s*(.*)$/m);
    if (dm) {
      if (dm[1]) {
        // Folded/literal scalar: gather subsequent more-indented lines.
        const after = block.slice(block.indexOf(dm[0]) + dm[0].length).split("\n");
        const parts = [];
        for (const ln of after) {
          if (/^\S/.test(ln)) break;          // dedent → next key, stop
          parts.push(ln.trim());
        }
        out.description = parts.join(" ").trim();
      } else {
        out.description = dm[2].replace(/^["']|["']$/g, "").trim();
      }
    }
  }

  // Body bullets. Only inside relevant `##` sections.
  const body = fm ? src.slice(fm.index + fm[0].length) : src;
  const lines = body.split("\n");
  let inSection = false;
  for (const raw of lines) {
    const line = raw.replace(/\r$/, "");
    const h = line.match(/^##\s+(.+?)\s*$/);
    if (h) {
      inSection = /^(actions|weapons|functions)\b/i.test(h[1].trim());
      continue;
    }
    if (!inSection) continue;
    const b = line.match(/^\s*[-*]\s+(.*)$/);
    if (!b) continue;
    let rest = b[1];
    // Extract the label: [key](link) | **key** | `key` | key
    let key = "";
    let mk;
    if ((mk = rest.match(/^\[([^\]]+)\]\([^)]*\)/))) key = mk[1];
    else if ((mk = rest.match(/^\*\*([^*]+)\*\*/))) key = mk[1];
    else if ((mk = rest.match(/^`([^`]+)`/))) key = mk[1];
    else if ((mk = rest.match(/^([A-Za-z0-9_$.\-]+)/))) key = mk[1];
    // Description = everything after the first em-dash or " - " separator.
    let desc = "";
    const sep = rest.search(/\s(?:—|–|-)\s/);
    if (sep >= 0) desc = rest.slice(sep).replace(/^\s(?:—|–|-)\s/, "").trim();
    key = key.trim();
    if (key) out.actions.push({ action: key, description: desc || rest.trim() });
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Scan every `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and emit ownership rows in the
 * SAME shape as scanSkillBookTocsFromDisk (`{skillBook, action, description}`),
 * so gearUp / dumpOwnershipMap consume it with no shape change. Emits one
 * skill-level row (`action: "(skill)"`, the frontmatter description) plus one
 * row per `## Actions`/`## Weapons`/`## Functions` bullet.
 *
 * @returns {Array<{skillBook: string, action: string, description: string}>}
 */
export function scanClaudeSkillsFromDisk() {
  const files = listClaudeSkillFiles();
  const rows = [];
  for (const f of files) {
    let src;
    try { src = readFileSync(f.path, "utf8"); }
    catch { continue; }
    const parsed = parseSkillMd(src, f.name);
    if (parsed.description) {
      rows.push({ skillBook: f.name, action: "(skill)", description: parsed.description });
    }
    for (const a of parsed.actions) {
      rows.push({ skillBook: f.name, action: a.action, description: a.description });
    }
  }
  rows.sort((a, b) => (a.skillBook + a.action).localeCompare(b.skillBook + b.action));
  return rows;
}

```markdown
# Engineering Decisions — libs/weapon/skillExchange

## 2026-07-06 · Content format is MARKDOWN, with HTML-comment file sentinels — not JSON

- **Decision:** `compileSkill` packages a skill's files into a MARKDOWN document.
  File boundaries are HTML-comment sentinels — `<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: <path> -->` …
  `<!-- /GUILDOS-FILE -->` — with the code inside a cosmetic ```` ``` ```` fence.
  `decompileSkill` keys ONLY on the sentinels, never on the fences.
- **Rejected alternative:** JSON (`{ files: [{ path, content }] }`).
- **Why:** a skill is prose + code. JSON forces every weapon file into an escaped
  string where a single unescaped char breaks the WHOLE parse, and LLMs corrupt long
  JSON readily (unterminated strings in big code blobs) — the exchange content is
  explicitly expected to be human/LLM-edited. Markdown holds code verbatim and a
  mangled section degrades locally. Determinism (JSON's one advantage) is recovered
  by parsing on the SENTINELS, not the fences — so a weapon whose OWN source contains
  ```` ``` ```` fences still round-trips byte-identically (verified on the `imap` skill).
- **Consequence-if-violated:** switching to JSON (or relying on the code fences for
  boundaries) reintroduces the escaping-fragility this design exists to avoid — the
  first weapon containing a fenced example in its source would break decompilation.

## 2026-07-06 · Referenced weapons are auto-detected AND explicitly passable

- **Decision:** `compileSkill` gathers same-name `libs/skill_book/<name>` +
  `libs/weapon/<name>` + the `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, THEN unions in weapons
  referenced from that source (regex on `libs/weapon/<X>` / `run-action <X>`), plus
  any the caller lists in `weapons:`.
- **Rejected alternative:** requiring the caller to enumerate every referenced weapon.
- **Why:** most skills fold their weapon under the same name (auto-covered); cross-name
  references (a skill book that drives another weapon) are common enough that silent
  omission would ship a skill missing its dependency. Auto-detect + explicit override
  covers both without forcing the caller to know the dependency graph.
- **Consequence-if-violated:** dropping auto-detect means published skills silently miss
  the weapons they call; a puller decompiles a skill that references files that were
  never packaged. Binary files are intentionally skipped (listed in `skipped`) to keep
  `content` text-only — do not embed them as base64.
```

<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: libs/weapon/skillExchange/index.js -->
```js
/**
 * skillExchange weapon — package a local skill (its skill book + referenced
 * weapons) into ONE markdown `content` blob for the GuildOS2 Skill Exchange, and
 * unpackage a pulled blob back into local files. Also a thin client for the
 * exchange API (discover / publish / pull).
 *
 * WHY MARKDOWN (not JSON): a skill is prose + code. JSON would force every weapon
 * file into an escaped string where one stray char breaks the whole parse, and LLM
 * edits corrupt long JSON readily. Markdown holds code verbatim in fenced blocks.
 * Round-trip stays deterministic because file boundaries are HTML-comment SENTINELS
 * (`<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: path -->` … `<!-- /GUILDOS-FILE -->`), NOT the code fences —
 * so a weapon whose own source contains ``` fences round-trips cleanly.
 *
 * Loads under plain node (no "@/" alias) — invoked via run-action / directly.
 */
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, readdirSync, statSync, existsSync, mkdirSync } from "node:fs";
import { join, resolve, dirname, relative, extname, sep } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
// libs/weapon/skillExchange -> repo root is three levels up.
const REPO_ROOT = resolve(__dirname, "..", "..", "..");

export const toc = {
  compileSkill: "Package a local skill book + its referenced weapons into one markdown `content` blob (for publishing to the Skill Exchange).",
  decompileSkill: "Unpackage a Skill Exchange markdown `content` blob back into local skill-book/weapon files (adopt a pulled skill locally).",
  publishSkill: "compileSkill + POST it to the GuildOS2 Skill Exchange (/api/skills).",
  publishAllSkills: "Compile + publish EVERY local skill (union of libs/skill_book/* and libs/weapon/* dirs) to the exchange — the bulk local→DB migration/sync.",
  pullSkill: "GET a skill from the exchange by id and decompileSkill it into local files.",
  discoverSkills: "POST a purpose to /api/skills/discover and return the recommended skills.",
  redactForPublic: "Strip a compiled blob for PUBLIC release: neutralize private IPs, internal/client hostnames, Supabase project refs, SSH/SFTP paths, Tailscale hosts, and third-party email addresses. Returns { content, hits }.",
  scanForSecrets: "Adversarial post-strip gate: re-scan text for any surviving IP / email / internal-host / project-ref. Returns the list of survivors — a non-empty result MUST block a public push.",
};

// ── public-release redaction (used ONLY when pushing to the PUBLIC library repo) ──
// The exchange blob embeds raw source, which carries the operator's private infra
// map, client identities, and (in the email/inbox skills) THIRD-PARTY personal data.
// redactForPublic neutralizes the security/PII-critical classes; scanForSecrets is the
// hard gate that must return [] before anything is committed to a public repo. Client
// BRAND identifiability (folder names, code identifiers) is intentionally NOT stripped
// here — that is an accepted-residual product decision, not a security leak.

// Specific known-sensitive hosts/refs/nicknames, redacted verbatim (substring, case-
// insensitive) before the generic passes. Includes BARE host nicknames and server
// path segments that carry no dot/@ and so escape the structural regexes below.
const PRIVATE_HOSTS = [
  "<REDACTED-HOST>", "<REDACTED-HOST>", "<REDACTED-HOST>", "<REDACTED-HOST>",
  "<REDACTED-HOST>", "<REDACTED-HOST>", "<REDACTED-HOST>", "<REDACTED-HOST>",
  "<REDACTED-HOST>", "<REDACTED-HOST>", "<REDACTED-HOST>", "<REDACTED-HOST>", "<REDACTED-HOST>",
];
const PROJECT_REFS = ["<REDACTED-PROJECT-REF>", "<REDACTED-PROJECT-REF>", "<REDACTED-PROJECT-REF>"];
// Literal shared-secret VALUES that are dictionary words (so they slip past shape-based
// key/token scans). Low-secret by declaration, but still must not ship in a public repo.
const SHARED_SECRETS = ["<REDACTED-SHARED-SECRET>"];

const RE_IPV4 = /\b(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1?\d?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1?\d?\d)\b/g;
const RE_EMAIL = /\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b/g;
const RE_SUPABASE_SUB = /\bhttps?:\/\/[a-z0-9]{20}\.supabase\.co/g;
const RE_TAILSCALE = /\b[a-z0-9-]+\.ts\.net\b/gi;
const RE_TS_CGNAT = /\b100\.(?:6[4-9]|[7-9]\d|1[01]\d|12[0-7])\.\d{1,3}\.\d{1,3}\b/g; // 100.64/10 CGNAT
const RE_AWS_INSTANCE = /\bi-[0-9a-f]{8,17}\b/g; // AWS instance ids
const escapeRe = (s) => s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");

/**
 * Redact a compiled-skill markdown blob for public release.
 * @returns {{ content: string, hits: Record<string, number> }}
 */
export function redactForPublic(content) {
  if (typeof content !== "string") throw new Error("redactForPublic: content string required");
  const hits = {};
  const bump = (k, n = 1) => { hits[k] = (hits[k] || 0) + n; };
  let out = content;
  for (const h of PRIVATE_HOSTS) { const re = new RegExp(escapeRe(h), "gi"); out = out.replace(re, (m) => { bump("host"); return "<REDACTED-HOST>"; }); }
  for (const r of PROJECT_REFS) { const re = new RegExp(escapeRe(r), "g"); out = out.replace(re, () => { bump("project-ref"); return "<REDACTED-PROJECT-REF>"; }); }
  for (const s of SHARED_SECRETS) { const re = new RegExp(escapeRe(s), "gi"); out = out.replace(re, () => { bump("shared-secret"); return "<REDACTED-SHARED-SECRET>"; }); }
  out = out.replace(RE_SUPABASE_SUB, () => { bump("supabase-url"); return "https://<REDACTED-PROJECT-REF>.supabase.co"; });
  out = out.replace(RE_TAILSCALE, () => { bump("tailscale"); return "<REDACTED-TAILSCALE-HOST>"; });
  out = out.replace(RE_TS_CGNAT, () => { bump("ip"); return "<REDACTED-IP>"; });
  out = out.replace(RE_AWS_INSTANCE, () => { bump("aws-instance"); return "<REDACTED-INSTANCE-ID>"; });
  out = out.replace(RE_EMAIL, () => { bump("email"); return "<REDACTED-EMAIL>"; });
  out = out.replace(RE_IPV4, () => { bump("ip"); return "<REDACTED-IP>"; });
  return { content: out, hits };
}

/**
 * Adversarial re-scan of already-redacted text. Any survivor is a leak → block push.
 * @returns {Array<{ kind: string, value: string }>}
 */
export function scanForSecrets(content) {
  const survivors = [];
  const collect = (re, kind) => { let m; re.lastIndex = 0; while ((m = re.exec(content))) survivors.push({ kind, value: m[0] }); };
  collect(RE_IPV4, "ip");
  collect(RE_EMAIL, "email");
  collect(RE_SUPABASE_SUB, "supabase-url");
  collect(RE_TAILSCALE, "tailscale");
  collect(RE_AWS_INSTANCE, "aws-instance");
  for (const h of PRIVATE_HOSTS) collect(new RegExp(escapeRe(h), "gi"), "host");
  for (const r of PROJECT_REFS) collect(new RegExp(escapeRe(r), "g"), "project-ref");
  for (const s of SHARED_SECRETS) collect(new RegExp(escapeRe(s), "gi"), "shared-secret");
  return survivors;
}

// ── file gathering ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// Only text files are embedded; binaries (images in template dirs, etc.) are
// skipped so `content` stays a clean text document. Listed in the return `skipped`.
const TEXT_EXT = new Set([".js", ".mjs", ".cjs", ".ts", ".tsx", ".jsx", ".md", ".json", ".sql", ".sh", ".ps1", ".txt", ".html", ".css", ".yml", ".yaml", ".env", ".template"]);
const LANG = { ".js": "js", ".mjs": "js", ".cjs": "js", ".ts": "ts", ".tsx": "tsx", ".jsx": "jsx", ".md": "markdown", ".json": "json", ".sql": "sql", ".sh": "bash", ".ps1": "powershell", ".html": "html", ".css": "css", ".yml": "yaml", ".yaml": "yaml" };

function walk(dir) {
  const out = [];
  if (!existsSync(dir)) return out;
  for (const entry of readdirSync(dir)) {
    const p = join(dir, entry);
    if (entry === "node_modules" || entry === ".git") continue;
    const st = statSync(p);
    if (st.isDirectory()) out.push(...walk(p));
    else out.push(p);
  }
  return out;
}

function toRepoRel(absPath) {
  return relative(REPO_ROOT, absPath).split("\\").join("/");
}

// Scan gathered source for references to OTHER weapons (cross-name deps), e.g.
// `libs/weapon/browserclaw/…` or `run-action.mjs figma …`. Best-effort union.
function detectReferencedWeapons(sourceTexts, selfName) {
  const found = new Set();
  const re1 = /libs\/weapon\/([a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+)/g;
  const re2 = /run-action(?:\.mjs)?\s+([a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+)/g;
  for (const text of sourceTexts) {
    let m;
    while ((m = re1.exec(text))) found.add(m[1]);
    while ((m = re2.exec(text))) found.add(m[1]);
  }
  found.delete(selfName);
  return [...found].filter((w) => {
    const p = join(REPO_ROOT, "libs", "weapon", w);
    try { return statSync(p).isDirectory(); } catch { return false; }
  });
}

// Resolve a skill's discovery description with a fallback chain: the .claude/skills
// SKILL.md frontmatter (best — the real discovery surface) → a `description:` field
// in the skill_book/weapon index.js → the weapon registry entry (tagline + summary).
// Folded sub-weapons have no SKILL.md, so the registry is their description source.
function resolveDescription(name, skillMdPath, override) {
  if (override) return override.trim();
  if (existsSync(skillMdPath)) {
    const d = descFromSkillMd(readFileSync(skillMdPath, "utf8"));
    if (d) return d;
  }
  for (const base of [join(REPO_ROOT, "libs", "skill_book", name, "index.js"), join(REPO_ROOT, "libs", "weapon", name, "index.js")]) {
    if (existsSync(base)) {
      const m = readFileSync(base, "utf8").match(/\bdescription:\s*["'`]([^"'`]{12,})["'`]/);
      if (m) return m[1].trim();
    }
  }
  const reg = join(REPO_ROOT, "libs", "weapon", "registry.js");
  if (existsSync(reg)) {
    const t = readFileSync(reg, "utf8");
    const idx = t.indexOf(`id: "${name}"`);
    if (idx >= 0) {
      const slice = t.slice(idx, idx + 2500);
      const tag = slice.match(/tagline:\s*"([^"]+)"/)?.[1] || "";
      const sum = slice.match(/summary:\s*"([^"]+)"/)?.[1] || "";
      const d = [tag, sum].filter(Boolean).join(" ").trim();
      if (d) return d;
    }
  }
  return "";
}

// Pull the frontmatter `description:` out of a .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md.
function descFromSkillMd(text) {
  const fm = text.match(/^---\n([\s\S]*?)\n---/);
  if (!fm) return "";
  const m = fm[1].match(/description:\s*>-?\s*\n([\s\S]*?)(?:\n[a-zA-Z_]+:|\n*$)/) || fm[1].match(/description:\s*(.+)/);
  return (m ? m[1] : "").replace(/\n\s+/g, " ").trim();
}

// ── compile ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Package a skill into one markdown blob.
 * @param {object} input
 * @param {string} input.name            skill name (matches libs/skill_book/<name> and/or libs/weapon/<name>)
 * @param {string[]} [input.weapons]     extra weapon dir names to include (cross-name references)
 * @param {boolean} [input.autodetect=true] scan source for referenced weapons and include them
 * @param {string} [input.description]   override the description (else read from SKILL.md)
 * @returns {{ ok, name, description, content, files, skipped, weapons }}
 */
export function compileSkill({ name, weapons = [], autodetect = true, description } = {}) {
  if (!name) throw new Error('"name" is required');

  const skillBookDir = join(REPO_ROOT, "libs", "skill_book", name);
  const weaponDir = join(REPO_ROOT, "libs", "weapon", name);
  const skillMdPath = join(REPO_ROOT, ".claude", "skills", name, "SKILL.md");
  if (!existsSync(skillBookDir) && !existsSync(weaponDir)) {
    throw new Error(`no skill "${name}" found (neither libs/skill_book/${name} nor libs/weapon/${name} exists)`);
  }

  // First pass: gather same-name files + explicit extra weapons.
  const weaponSet = new Set(weapons);
  let absFiles = [...walk(skillBookDir), ...walk(weaponDir)];
  if (existsSync(skillMdPath)) absFiles.push(skillMdPath);
  for (const w of weaponSet) absFiles.push(...walk(join(REPO_ROOT, "libs", "weapon", w)));

  // Auto-detect referenced weapons from the source we have, then add their files.
  if (autodetect) {
    const texts = absFiles.filter((f) => TEXT_EXT.has(extname(f))).map((f) => { try { return readFileSync(f, "utf8"); } catch { return ""; } });
    for (const w of detectReferencedWeapons(texts, name)) {
      if (!weaponSet.has(w)) { weaponSet.add(w); absFiles.push(...walk(join(REPO_ROOT, "libs", "weapon", w))); }
    }
  }

  // De-dup, split text vs skipped (binary).
  const seen = new Set();
  const files = [], skipped = [];
  for (const f of absFiles) {
    const rel = toRepoRel(f);
    if (seen.has(rel)) continue;
    seen.add(rel);
    (TEXT_EXT.has(extname(f)) ? files : skipped).push(rel);
  }
  files.sort();

  const desc = (resolveDescription(name, skillMdPath, description) || `${name} — GuildOS ${existsSync(skillBookDir) ? "skill" : "weapon"}`).trim();

  // Build the markdown document.
  const parts = [
    `# ${name}`,
    "",
    `<!-- GUILDOS-SKILL name="${name}" -->`,
    "",
    "<!-- GUILDOS-DESC -->",
    desc || "(no description)",
    "<!-- /GUILDOS-DESC -->",
    "",
    "## Files",
    "",
  ];
  for (const rel of files) {
    const abs = join(REPO_ROOT, rel);
    const body = readFileSync(abs, "utf8");
    const lang = LANG[extname(abs)] || "";
    parts.push(`<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: ${rel} -->`, "```" + lang, body.replace(/\n$/, ""), "```", "<!-- /GUILDOS-FILE -->", "");
  }
  if (skipped.length) parts.push(`<!-- GUILDOS-SKIPPED-BINARY: ${skipped.join(", ")} -->`, "");

  return { ok: true, name, description: desc, content: parts.join("\n"), files, skipped, weapons: [...weaponSet] };
}

// ── decompile ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const FILE_RE = /<!--\s*GUILDOS-FILE:\s*(.+?)\s*-->\r?\n([\s\S]*?)\r?\n<!--\s*\/GUILDOS-FILE\s*-->/g;

// Strip the outermost ```lang / ``` fence pair the compiler wrapped a file in.
function stripFence(body) {
  const lines = body.split(/\r?\n/);
  if (lines.length && /^```[\w.+-]*$/.test(lines[0])) lines.shift();
  if (lines.length && /^```$/.test(lines[lines.length - 1])) lines.pop();
  return lines.join("\n");
}

/**
 * Unpackage a compiled blob back into local files.
 * @param {object} input
 * @param {string} input.content         the markdown blob (from a pull)
 * @param {string} [input.targetRoot]    where to write (default: this repo root)
 * @param {boolean} [input.dryRun=false] parse + report without writing
 * @returns {{ ok, name, description, files }}
 */
export function decompileSkill({ content, targetRoot = REPO_ROOT, dryRun = false } = {}) {
  if (!content || typeof content !== "string") throw new Error('"content" (string) is required');
  const name = content.match(/<!--\s*GUILDOS-SKILL\s+name="(.+?)"\s*-->/)?.[1] || null;
  const description = content.match(/<!--\s*GUILDOS-DESC\s*-->\r?\n([\s\S]*?)\r?\n<!--\s*\/GUILDOS-DESC\s*-->/)?.[1]?.trim() || "";

  const written = [];
  let m;
  FILE_RE.lastIndex = 0;
  while ((m = FILE_RE.exec(content))) {
    const rel = m[1].trim();
    // Path-boundary guard — never let a blob write outside targetRoot.
    const root = resolve(targetRoot);
    const abs = resolve(root, rel);
    if (abs !== root && !abs.startsWith(root + sep)) {
      throw new Error(`refusing to write outside targetRoot: ${rel}`);
    }
    const fileBody = stripFence(m[2]);
    if (!dryRun) {
      mkdirSync(dirname(abs), { recursive: true });
      writeFileSync(abs, fileBody.endsWith("\n") ? fileBody : fileBody + "\n", "utf8");
    }
    written.push(rel);
  }
  if (!written.length) throw new Error("no GUILDOS-FILE blocks found — not a valid compiled skill blob");
  return { ok: true, name, description, files: written };
}

// ── exchange client (thin) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function exchangeConfig({ baseUrl, apiKey } = {}) {
  const url = (baseUrl || process.env.GUILDOS2_BASE_URL || "http://localhost:3007").replace(/\/+$/, "");
  const key = apiKey || process.env.GUILDOS2_API_KEY;
  if (!key) throw new Error("GUILDOS2_API_KEY not set (needed to reach the Skill Exchange)");
  return { url, key };
}

/** compileSkill + POST it to the exchange. author defaults to this guild's name. */
export async function publishSkill({ name, weapons, author, baseUrl, apiKey } = {}) {
  const { url, key } = exchangeConfig({ baseUrl, apiKey });
  const pkg = compileSkill({ name, weapons });
  const guild = author || process.env.LOCAL_GUILD_NAME || "GuildOS";
  const resp = await fetch(`${url}/api/skills`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${key}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({ name: pkg.name, description: pkg.description, content: pkg.content, author: guild }),
  });
  const data = await resp.json().catch(() => ({}));
  if (!resp.ok) throw new Error(`publish failed (${resp.status}): ${data.error || ""}`);
  return { ok: true, published: data.skill, files: pkg.files };
}

/**
 * Enumerate every local skill (union of libs/skill_book/* and libs/weapon/* dir
 * names) and compile+publish each to the exchange. The bulk local→DB migration;
 * idempotent (republish upserts by name). Skills whose compile fails (e.g. a name
 * with no packageable files) are reported, not fatal.
 * @param {object} [input]
 * @param {string} [input.author]  guild name for every row (default LOCAL_GUILD_NAME|"GuildOS")
 * @param {string[]} [input.only]  restrict to these skill names (else all)
 * @returns {{ ok, total, published:[], skipped:[], errors:[] }}
 */
export async function publishAllSkills({ author, only, baseUrl, apiKey } = {}) {
  const { url, key } = exchangeConfig({ baseUrl, apiKey });
  const guild = author || process.env.LOCAL_GUILD_NAME || "GuildOS";
  const dirsIn = (p) => { const d = join(REPO_ROOT, p); return existsSync(d) ? readdirSync(d).filter((e) => { try { return statSync(join(d, e)).isDirectory(); } catch { return false; } }) : []; };
  let names = [...new Set([...dirsIn("libs/skill_book"), ...dirsIn("libs/weapon")])].sort();
  if (Array.isArray(only) && only.length) names = names.filter((n) => only.includes(n));

  const published = [], skipped = [], errors = [];
  for (const name of names) {
    let pkg;
    try {
      pkg = compileSkill({ name });
    } catch (e) {
      skipped.push({ name, reason: e.message });
      continue;
    }
    try {
      const resp = await fetch(`${url}/api/skills`, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${key}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
        body: JSON.stringify({ name: pkg.name, description: pkg.description, content: pkg.content, author: guild }),
      });
      const data = await resp.json().catch(() => ({}));
      if (!resp.ok) errors.push({ name, status: resp.status, error: data.error || "" });
      else published.push({ name: pkg.name, id: data.skill?.id, files: pkg.files.length, bytes: pkg.content.length });
    } catch (e) {
      errors.push({ name, error: e.message });
    }
  }
  return { ok: errors.length === 0, total: names.length, published, skipped, errors };
}

/** GET a skill by id and decompile it locally. */
export async function pullSkill({ id, targetRoot, dryRun = false, baseUrl, apiKey } = {}) {
  if (!id) throw new Error('"id" is required');
  const { url, key } = exchangeConfig({ baseUrl, apiKey });
  const resp = await fetch(`${url}/api/skills/${id}`, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${key}` } });
  const data = await resp.json().catch(() => ({}));
  if (!resp.ok) throw new Error(`pull failed (${resp.status}): ${data.error || ""}`);
  const out = decompileSkill({ content: data.skill.content, targetRoot, dryRun });
  return { ok: true, ...out, from: { id, name: data.skill.name, author: data.skill.author } };
}

/** POST a purpose to /api/skills/discover; returns the recommendations. */
export async function discoverSkills({ purpose, topK, baseUrl, apiKey } = {}) {
  if (!purpose) throw new Error('"purpose" is required');
  const { url, key } = exchangeConfig({ baseUrl, apiKey });
  const resp = await fetch(`${url}/api/skills/discover`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${key}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({ purpose, ...(topK ? { topK } : {}) }),
  });
  const data = await resp.json().catch(() => ({}));
  if (!resp.ok) throw new Error(`discover failed (${resp.status}): ${data.error || ""}`);
  return { ok: true, recommendations: data.recommendations || [] };
}

```js

export const toc = {
  searchCampaigns: "Search Smartlead cold-email campaigns.",
  readCampaign: "Read a single Smartlead campaign.",
  readLeads: "Read leads in a Smartlead campaign.",
  readAnalytics: "Read Smartlead campaign analytics.",
};
import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";

const BASE = "https://server.smartlead.ai/api/v1";

async function loadKey(userId) {
  if (userId) {
    try {
      const db = await database.init("service");
      const { data } = await db.from("profiles").select("env_vars").eq("id", userId).single();
      const k = data?.env_vars?.SMARTLEAD_API_KEY;
      if (k) return k;
    } catch { /* fall through */ }
  }
  return process.env.SMARTLEAD_API_KEY || null;
}

async function request(path, key, params = {}) {
  const url = new URL(`${BASE}${path}`);
  url.searchParams.set("api_key", key);
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(params)) {
    if (v !== undefined && v !== null) url.searchParams.set(k, String(v));
  }
  const res = await fetch(url.toString());
  if (!res.ok) {
    const text = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`Smartlead ${path} failed (${res.status}): ${text}`);
  }
  return res.json();
}

export async function searchCampaigns({ limit = 10, offset = 0 } = {}, userId) {
  const key = await loadKey(userId);

```markdown
# Engineering decisions — `libs/weapon/ssh`

Rationale layer (per CLAUDE.md §6). Append; supersede in place when a decision
changes.

---

## 2026-06-09 — SSH hardcodes `BatchMode=yes` + `StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new`

**Decision.** Every SSH invocation passes `-o BatchMode=yes` (never prompt for a
password) and `-o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new` (trust-on-first-use,
auto-populating known_hosts).

**Rejected alternative.** Allow interactive password prompts and/or strict host-key
verification (the ssh defaults).

**Why.** The weapon is agent-invoked automation. An interactive prompt hangs the
agent indefinitely; strict host-key checking blocks every first-time connection.
The operating assumption is that passwordless keys are pre-configured by the
operator, so BatchMode + accept-new is the correct automation semantic.

**Consequence if violated.** First connection to a new host hangs on the unknown-host
prompt, or any host needing a password never connects — both as silent agent stalls.
```

<!-- GUILDOS-FILE: libs/weapon/ssh/index.js -->
```js
/**
 * SSH weapon — execute commands on remote machines.
 *
 * Uses system SSH (no npm deps). Requires passwordless SSH keys to be set up.
 * Known hosts are configured in profiles.env_vars as SSH_HOSTS JSON.
 */

export const toc = {
  executeCommand: "Execute a shell command on a remote host via SSH.",
  searchHosts: "Search configured SSH hosts.",
  readRemoteFile: "Read a file from a remote host over SSH.",
};
import { execFile } from "node:child_process";
import { promisify } from "node:util";
import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";

const execFileAsync = promisify(execFile);
const DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 30_000;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Host registry
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Known host presets. Additional hosts can be added via SSH_HOSTS env var.
 */
// Host/user for boster_production are redacted from source — set BOSTER_PROD_HOST /
// BOSTER_PROD_USER (and optionally BOSTER_PROD_PORT) in .env.local. The preset is
// omitted from the registry when its host env is unset; use SSH_HOSTS or a raw host.
const KNOWN_HOSTS = {
  carbon: { host: "carbon", user: null, description: "Carbon SSH server (local network)" },
  ...(process.env.BOSTER_PROD_HOST
    ? {
        boster_production: {
          host: process.env.BOSTER_PROD_HOST,
          user: process.env.BOSTER_PROD_USER || undefined,
          port: Number(process.env.BOSTER_PROD_PORT) || 2223,
          description: "Boster production server — Magento 2, MariaDB",
        },
      }
    : {}),
};

/**
 * Resolve a host alias or raw host string to connection details.
 * @param {string} hostOrAlias
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
async function resolveHost(hostOrAlias, userId) {
  // Check presets
  const preset = KNOWN_HOSTS[hostOrAlias];
  if (preset) return preset;

  // Check user-defined hosts from env_vars
  if (userId) {
    try {
      const db = await database.init("service");
      const { data } = await db.from("profiles").select("env_vars").eq("id", userId).single();
      const hostsJson = data?.env_vars?.SSH_HOSTS;
      if (hostsJson) {
        const hosts = JSON.parse(hostsJson);
        if (hosts[hostOrAlias]) return hosts[hostOrAlias];
      }
    } catch { /* no custom hosts */ }
  }

  // Raw host string
  return { host: hostOrAlias, user: null, description: null };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Execute
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Execute a command on a remote host via SSH.
 * @param {{ host: string, command: string, user?: string, timeout?: number }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 * @returns {Promise<{ ok: boolean, stdout: string, stderr: string, exitCode: number|null }>}
 */
export async function executeCommand({ host, command, user, timeout } = {}, userId) {
  if (!host) throw new Error("host is required");
  if (!command) throw new Error("command is required");

  const resolved = await resolveHost(host, userId);
  const sshUser = user || resolved.user;
  const target = sshUser ? `${sshUser}@${resolved.host}` : resolved.host;
  const timeoutMs = timeout || DEFAULT_TIMEOUT;

  const args = [
    "-o", "ConnectTimeout=10",
    "-o", "StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new",
    "-o", "BatchMode=yes",
  ];
  if (resolved.port) {
    args.push("-p", String(resolved.port));
  }
  args.push(target, command);

  try {
    const { stdout, stderr } = await execFileAsync("ssh", args, {
      timeout: timeoutMs,
      maxBuffer: 5 * 1024 * 1024,
    });
    return { ok: true, stdout: stdout.slice(0, 10000), stderr: stderr.slice(0, 2000), exitCode: 0 };
  } catch (e) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      stdout: (e.stdout || "").slice(0, 10000),
      stderr: (e.stderr || e.message || "").slice(0, 2000),
      exitCode: e.code ?? null,
    };
  }
}

/**
 * Search available SSH hosts (presets + user-defined).
 * @param {object} [input]
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function searchHosts(input = {}, userId) {
  const hosts = { ...KNOWN_HOSTS };

  if (userId) {
    try {
      const db = await database.init("service");
      const { data } = await db.from("profiles").select("env_vars").eq("id", userId).single();
      const hostsJson = data?.env_vars?.SSH_HOSTS;
      if (hostsJson) {
        const custom = JSON.parse(hostsJson);
        Object.assign(hosts, custom);
      }
    } catch { /* no custom hosts */ }
  }

  return {
    hosts: Object.entries(hosts).map(([alias, info]) => ({
      alias,
      host: info.host,
      user: info.user,
      description: info.description,
    })),
  };
}

/**
 * Read a file from a remote host.
 * @param {{ host: string, path: string, user?: string, tail?: number }} input
 * @param {string} [userId]
 */
export async function readRemoteFile({ host, path, user, tail } = {}, userId) {
  if (!path) throw new Error("path is required");
  const cmd = tail ? `tail -n ${tail} ${path}` : `cat ${path}`;
  return executeCommand({ host, command: cmd, user }, userId);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Credential check
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export async function checkCredentials(userId) {
  try {
    // Check if ssh is available
    const { stdout } = await execFileAsync("ssh", ["-V"], { timeout: 5000 }).catch((e) => ({
      stdout: "",
      stderr: e.stderr || e.message,
    }));
    const hosts = await searchHosts({}, userId);
    return {
      ok: true,
      msg: `SSH available. ${hosts.hosts.length} known hosts configured.`,
    };
  } catch (e) {
    return { ok: false, msg: `SSH not available: ${e.message}` };
  }
}
```

export const toc = {
  readBalance: "Read the Stripe account balance.",
  readCharges: "Read recent Stripe charges.",
  readCustomers: "Read Stripe customers.",
  readSubscriptions: "Read Stripe subscriptions.",
  readProducts: "Read Stripe products (filter by active).",
  readPrices: "Read Stripe prices (filter by product and active).",
  searchProducts: "Search Stripe products with a Stripe query string.",
};
import { database } from "@/libs/council/database";

const BASE = "https://api.stripe.com/v1";

async function loadKey(userId) {
  if (userId) {
    try {
      const db = await database.init("service");
      const { data } = await db.from("profiles").select("env_vars").eq("id", userId).single();
      const k = data?.env_vars?.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY;
      if (k) return k;
    } catch { /* fall through */ }
  }
  return process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY || null;
}

async function request(path, key, params = {}) {
  const url = new URL(`${BASE}${path}`);
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(params)) {
    if (v !== undefined && v !== null) url.searchParams.set(k, String(v));
  }
  const res = await fetch(url.toString(), {
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Basic ${Buffer.from(`${key}:`).toString("base64")}`,
    },
  });
  if (!res.ok) {
    const text = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`Stripe ${path} failed (${res.status}): ${text}`);
  }
  return res.json();
}

export async function readBalance(input = {}, userId) {
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) throw new Error("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY not set");
  return request("/balance", key);
}

}

export async function readSubscriptions({ limit = 10, status } = {}, userId) {
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) throw new Error("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY not set");
  return request("/subscriptions", key, { limit, status });
}

export async function readProducts({ limit = 10, active } = {}, userId) {
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) throw new Error("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY not set");
  return request("/products", key, { limit, active });
}

export async function readPrices({ limit = 10, product, active } = {}, userId) {
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) throw new Error("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY not set");
  return request("/prices", key, { limit, product, active });
}

export async function searchProducts({ query, limit = 10 } = {}, userId) {
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) throw new Error("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY not set");
  if (!query) throw new Error("searchProducts requires a query (Stripe query string)");
  return request("/products/search", key, { query, limit });
}

export async function checkCredentials(input = {}, userId) {
  const key = await loadKey(userId);
  if (!key) return { ok: false, msg: "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY not set in profiles.env_vars or process.env" };
  try {
    await request("/balance", key);

    return { ok: false, msg: e.message };
  }
}

```markdown
# Engineering decisions — `libs/weapon/supabase`

Rationale layer (per CLAUDE.md §6). Append; supersede in place when a decision
changes.

---

## 2026-06-09 — `bulkUpload` rejects the pooler port 6543 and requires direct port 5432

**Decision.** `bulkUpload` hard-errors if pointed at port 6543 (the Supabase
PgBouncer pooler); it accepts ONLY port 5432 (direct frontend connection).

**Rejected alternative.** Accept both ports and let the caller use whatever
`SUPABASE_DB_URL` happens to carry.

**Why.** PostgreSQL's `COPY` meta-command needs the stateful frontend protocol.
PgBouncer-class poolers use stateless session pooling, which breaks `COPY` — the
failure surfaces as a cryptic "syntax error", which callers misattribute to data
shape and chase for hours. A hard guard names the real (transport-layer) cause.

**Consequence if violated.** Bulk ingests fail with misleading parse errors; the
bug is blamed on the data instead of the connection.

---

## 2026-06-15 — DDL / migrations go through the Management API (`runSql`/`applyMigrations`), not psql / `supabase db push`

**Decision.** Schema changes against the remote DB are applied with `runSql` /
`applyMigrations`, which POST SQL to the Supabase **Management API**
(`api.supabase.com/v1/projects/{ref}/database/query`) authenticated by
`SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` (a personal access token). `applyMigrations` also records
each version in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`.

**Rejected alternative.** Tell the user to run `supabase db push` (the "obvious"
path), or shell out to the CLI / psql by default.

**Why.** Three native paths fail or are unavailable on this box: (1) the service
REST key (`SUPABASE_SECRETE_KEY`) **cannot run DDL** — PostgREST only does
row-level reads/writes; (2) `supabase db push` needs the Supabase CLI *and* the DB
password, and the CLI's default direct host `db.<ref>.supabase.co` is
**unreachable here** (tls error EOF — IPv4-only/network quirk); (3) even with the
password, the CLI works only when forced onto the session pooler via
`--db-url aws-0-<region>.pooler.supabase.com:5432`. The Management API + PAT
sidesteps all of that: no CLI, no DB password, no direct host. This is the
recurring "run db push to apply migrations" ask — it kept resurfacing because the
default path is broken on this machine; the PAT path is the durable fix.

**Consequence if violated.** A future agent re-derives "no DDL path exists" (an
archived quest literally recorded that dead end), declines the task, or hand-rolls
an inline Management-API curl instead of using the codified action — re-paying the
discovery cost every time. If a migration is applied via `runSql` but the
`schema_migrations` ledger row is skipped, a later `supabase db push` re-attempts
it (harmless only if idempotent).
```
